title: Report: Emmanuel Acho comments spark NFL investigation of Dom DiSandro
summary: Every NFL team has a head of security.
full_text: Every NFL team has a head of security. For many if not most if not all NFL teams, the head of security is also a fixer. The topic became relevant during training camp, when the 49ers managed to keep under wraps for 11 days the fact that coach Kyle Shanahan had suffered multiple injuries (including a severe concussion) in a car accident. Some speculated that team security worked directly with law enforcement to keep the relevant information from being discovered or disclosed. The situation took on a different vibe when a police report placed the blame for the accident on the driver of the car. It was quickly dismissed by Shanahan as a clerical error; he accepted full responsibility for the crash. That twist prompted former NFL player Emmanuel Acho to discuss the situation on the Speakeasy podcast. Acho pointed to a specific example from his own playing career, regarding the manner in which a car accident was handled. And while he didn't mention the team, Acho spent time with the Browns, Eagles, and Giants. Acho explained that, one day after practice, his car rear-ended another car. (Generally speaking, it's always your fault when you hit someone from behind. It's part of the obligation to maintain a safe distance behind the car in front of you.) "I [contacted] one of our security people," Acho said. "He says, 'Acho, when the cop shows up, send the cop away. I’m going to send you another cop . And that other cop is going to say it wasn't your fault. It was their fault.' I was like, 'Wait, they do that?'" Acho then explained that a second cop did indeed arrive, and that the second cop found that the other driver was at fault. Acho added that, once the other driver found out that he played for the Eagles, she claimed that she and her daughter were injured. "Our head of security had to offer them two home tickets plus signed jerseys," Acho said, "and then were like, 'Oh, no, we're fine.'" Derrick Gunn, who has covered the Eagles for a very long time, posted this tweet on Wednesday: "The NFL is still investigating Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro based on comments made by Emmanuel Acho on his Speakeasy Podcast back in early August. . . . Acho who played for 3 NFL teams never mentioned a name . But it has been widely speculated he was referring to Big Dom." In fairness, the NFL should be investigating the Browns and Giants, too, if the league is indeed investigating DiSandro. And, frankly, the league should be investigating every security director for every franchise. If it's happening at one team, it's likely happening at others. It's potentially a cultural reality throughout the NFL. In that respect, it would be no different than the Saints' bounty scandal. Many teams were doing similar things. The league, instead of addressing it as a cultural problem, decided to drop the hammer on the one team the NFL had caught red-handed, in the hopes of scaring all other teams straight. That's not how cultural problems should be addressed. If, over time, the various franchises have developed a certain way of protecting players against the potential consequences of their mistakes and if the league has never before tried to put a stop to the things that team security will do to keep players out of trouble, it would be wrong to suddenly whack one person from one team for doing something that others are doing. None of that will matter, if the league is determined to make an example out of DiSandro in an effort to get other teams to stop doing the same thing. If it turns out that Acho was indeed referring to Big Dom.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams land in Melbourne some 28 hours before kickoff
summary: The Rams landed in Melbourne at 7 a.m. local time ahead of their season opener against the 49ers.
full_text: ' The Rams landed in Melbourne at 7 a.m. local time ahead of their season opener against the 49ers. They left Tuesday night PT and flew the nearly 8,000 miles in 16 hours. The game kicks off at 8:35 p.m. ET on Thursday, which is 10:35 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 11, in Melbourne. Thus, the Rams landed roughly 28 hours before kickoff. The NFL posted video of their arrival, with coach Sean McVay and wide receiver Puka Nacua among those walking down the jetway. Unlike the 49ers, who landed in Melbourne almost a week ago, the Rams chose to stay on Pacific Time. They will go to sleep in the late afternoon Melbourne time, wake up in the middle of the night and play the game on Friday morning before heading straight back to Los Angeles afterward.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bryce Young: Contract's out of my control, I'm just about football
summary: Panthers owner David Tepper weighed in on quarterback Bryce Young's future on Wednesday.
full_text: Panthers owner David Tepper weighed in on quarterback Bryce Young's future on Wednesday. When the Panthers drafted Young first overall in 2023, Tepper said he thought Young gave the team a chance to win multiple Super Bowls and he said Wednesday that he still feels that way "with the right weapons and the right situation" around the quarterback. That feeling did not lead the team to sign Young to a contract extension ahead of his fourth season, which is something Young says will not be on his mind when he takes the field against the Bears this weekend. "For me, it's just about football; all that stuff happens. It's outside my control," Young said, via the team's website. "All that stuff, other people and upstairs and agents, all that. It's season time. We're going into Week 1; that's all that matters. We have all the inspiration. There's a great challenge ahead of us, and our first opponent, so that's all that I have the capacity to be focused on." The Panthers did exercise their option on Young's contract for 2027, so he's not in the final year of his contract but it does feel like his performance this season will play a major role in determining how long Young remains with the teams.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drew Lock on TD pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba: Definitely never practiced that play
summary: One of the realities of life as an NFL backup quarterback is that you get fewer opportunities in practice and that means there are some plays that you never get to rehearse ahead of time.
full_text: ' One of the realities of life as an NFL backup quarterback is that you get fewer opportunities in practice and that means there are some plays that you never get to rehearse ahead of time. That's the situation Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock found himself in after replacing the injured Sam Darnold during Wednesday night's game against the Patriots. With the Seahawks down 10-3 and facing a fourth-and-1 from the New England 45-yard line with under 12 minutes to play, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury sent in a play that Lock had never gotten the chance to try out on the practice field. It was a play-action pass to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba that picked up the first down and then much more once Smith-Njigba turned around to find room to run all the way to the end zone. "It is like a classic football play," Lock said, via the team's website. "But, no. No, definitely never ran it . Looked kind of funny before the snap. I didn't really seem like they had anybody ready to match Jaxon based on what I knew we were about it run. He's the third read in that play, and when 11 is just standing there, you got to give him the pill." The Seahawks struggled to move the ball most of the night, but Drake Maye kept giving the ball away for the Patriots and Lock came up with key completions to Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp to set up Seattle's go-ahead field goal. He finished the night 16-of-22 for 187 yards and said after the game that he trusted in the defense to keep the game within reach. "Knowing the type of defense that we have, there is no rush to push the ball down the field," Lock said. "Let's find ways to get the ball in our guys' hands. Now, when the ones down field are there, I've never been one to be afraid of those, but having the mindset of taking football, getting it in our guys' hands. You got the best defense in the world, in my opinion, let's keep the ball moving forward and see what the scoreboard looks like at the end of this." The Seahawks can be happy with how the scoreboard looks thanks in large part to how well Lock handled being thrown into the fire on the second series of the 2026 season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joey Porter Jr. is "up in the air" for Sunday
summary: With Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon and Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez getting their new contracts, another 2023 draft pick at the same position is still waiting for his reward.
full_text: With Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon and Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez getting their new contracts, another 2023 draft pick at the same position is still waiting for his reward. Per a source with knowledge of the negotiations, nothing is imminent. However, the two sides have been talking. Porter, the first pick in round two (and the 32nd overall that year because the Dolphins had been stripped of their first-round pick), is due to make $3.924 million in 2026, the final year of his deal. If he doesn't get a new contract by Sunday, it's "up in the air," we're told, as to whether he'll play. Complicating matters is the Steelers' policy against negotiating once the regular season begins. So if a contract isn't done by Sunday, ii won't be this year — unless the Steelers deviate from their outdated policy. The two sides obviously disagree on the amount to be paid for a cornerback who has yet to make it to a Pro Bowl. And it's unclear whether the gap can be bridged. Absent a deal, will Porter play? It will be hard for the team to question the legitimacy of a back problem (he was limited in practice on Wednesday), and he could sit indefinitely in protest of the prospect of playing for less than $4 million. Another issue is the fact that Porter's father, Joey Porter Sr., who played in the NFL for 13 seasons and who is definitely involved in the situation. Joey Sr.'s knowledge of how the sausage gets made becomes a factor in whether a deal gets done, and whether Joey Jr. will take the best offer on the table before the season starts. However it goes, it needs to go somewhere — or nowhere — quickly. And if they don't finalize a contract, it could get awkward and potentially ugly.
author: Mike Florio

title: Carson Wentz is Vikings' No. 2 quarterback, J.J. McCarthy is No. 3
summary: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced today that Wentz will back up Kyler Murray.
full_text: '' J.J. McCarthy has fallen from the Vikings' franchise quarterback of the future to a third-stringer. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced today that Carson Wentz will be the No. 2 quarterback in Sunday's regular-season opener against the Packers. McCarthy is No. 3 on the depth chart. O'Connell suggested that Wentz's experience makes him the better backup right now, but insisted that the Vikings will continue to work on developing McCarthy. "I'm looking at that right now as a week-to-week thing, and Carson has almost 100 career starts," O'Connell said. "J.J. is still going to get a bunch of great work. . . . This gives us the best chance to win this Sunday." Kyler Murray was named the starter a month ago after winning a quarterback competition with McCarthy that never seemed like much of a competition. Now that McCarthy hasn't even beaten out Wentz for the competition to be No. 2, it's safe to say the Vikings are ready to move on from McCarthy, despite O'Connell's insistence that McCarthy is still going to get great work. McCarthy's four-year, $21.8 million rookie contract is guaranteed, so that's the primary reason the Vikings are keeping him. The Vikings took McCarthy with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft and hoped he would be their quarterback for many years to come. Instead, he missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury and then did not play well when given the opportunity to start in 2025. Now McCarthy is opening 2026 buried on the depth chart. It's entirely possible that he has played his last game as a Viking.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 122 of the Seahawks' 200 receiving yards, and Seattle's only TD
summary: "It's not all on me," Smith-Njigba said. "It's a team effort."
full_text: '' On an NFL opening night when the Seahawks' offense was otherwise stalling, wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba kept it going. Smith-Njigba caught a short pass on fourth-and-1 and raced downfield for a 45-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter, scoring the Seahawks' only touchdown in the 13-10 win over the Patriots. Afterward, he credited the play call, quarterback Drew Lock and his teammates' blocking more than his own effort. "I was happy it was a pass play," Smith-Njigba said. "My job was to find a zone and Drew did a great job finding me, and afterward just do what I do, try to get upfield and protect the ball. Great upfield blocking by our tight ends." The Seahawks' passing game went 8-for-11 for 122 yards and a touchdown when throwing to Smith-Njigba and 9-for-13 for 78 yards and no touchdowns when throwing to everyone else on the team. Despite that, Smith-Njigba credited teammates Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed, who had a combined three catches for 39 yards. "It's not all on me. We have Cooper Kupp making big plays, we have Sheed making big plays," Smith-Njigba said. "It's a team effort." It is a team effort, but Smith-Njigba showed who the best player on the team is.
author: Michael David Smith

title: George Kittle, Nick Bosa have no injury designations for Thursday's game
summary: The 49ers are set to welcome two of their biggest stars back to the lineup for their first game of the 2026 season.
full_text: The 49ers are set to welcome two of their biggest stars back to the lineup for their first game of the 2026 season. Neither tight end George Kittle nor defensive end Nick Bosa received injury designations on the team's final injury report ahead of their game against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia. Kittle is returning from a torn Achilles while Bosa has been working his way back from a torn ACL. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said this week that the team would be "smart" with both players given the extent of their injuries, so they may not play a full complement of snaps on Thursday. Defensive lineman James Thompson is listed as questionable while defensive lineman Alfred Collins has been ruled out after suffering a torn patellar tendon in practice earlier this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay: Flight was great, guys seem fresh, we'll be ready to rock
summary: The Rams' flight to Melbourne landed on Thursday morning local time, which left them with about 28 hours to acclimate to Australia before their game against the 49ers gets underway.
full_text: ''' The Rams' flight to Melbourne landed on Thursday morning local time, which left them with about 28 hours to acclimate to Australia before their game against the 49ers gets underway. The choice to arrive so close to the game — the 49ers have been in Melbourne for days — has been scrutinized all week, but head coach Sean McVay said at a press conference after arriving that he thinks his team will be ready to go when it is time to kick things off. "Flight was great ," McVay said, via Olivia Garvey of NBC Los Angeles. "We’re well rested, we feel good. It really was. Matthew [Stafford] and I were just talking about that on the way over here. Able to sleep through the night, guys were comfortable, they seem fresh. Get a good night rest tonight and be ready to rock tomorrow." In addition to giving one team an early boost in the NFC West race, the difference in the approaches to the game will make the result a referendum on how teams should plan for trips to play in any future Australian games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Anderson on facing the Bills: An AFC Championship matchup
summary: A perusal of the many published predictions for the 2026 season finds a lot of support for the Bills and Texans as two of the strongest teams in the AFC.
full_text: A perusal of the many published predictions for the 2026 season finds a lot of support for the Bills and Texans as two of the strongest teams in the AFC. One of them is likely to exit Week 1 with an 0-1 record, however. The two teams will meet in Houston on Sunday afternoon in a matchup that Texans defensive end Will Anderson believes will be a preview of one of the games that both teams hope to be playing in come January. “This is an AFC Championship matchup," Anderson said in a Wednesday press conference. "Two really good teams. We have a ton of respect for them. Josh Allen leading the way, really great offensive line. James Cook, best running back in the league. . . . The type of atmosphere that I’m feeling like it’s gonna be on Sunday is gonna be that AFC Championship-type feel." The Texans pass rush got the best of Allen and the Bills last November. Anderson had 2.5 sacks in that game and the Texans will be looking for something similar as they try to get an early leg up in the race for the actual AFC Championship Game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Vrabel: You can't throw three interceptions, Drake Maye knows that
summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel pointed to quarterback Drake Maye's turnovers as the difference after losing to the Seahawks.
full_text: '' Patriots coach Mike Vrabel pointed to quarterback Drake Maye's turnovers as the difference after losing to the Seahawks. "You can't throw three interceptions. Drake knows that," Vrabel said. The Patriots lost the game 13-10 and lost the turnover battle 3-0, as all three turnovers in the game were Maye interceptions. Given that, it's no surprise that the Patriots lost: Last season, teams that were minus-3 or worse in turnover margin went 3-38. "We can't turn the ball over and we have to create more turnovers," Vrabel said. "There's a few things we have to eliminate that get you beat in this league." The Patriots' loss was sealed when Maye threw an interception into the end zone with 21 seconds left. Vrabel defended the decision to try to score a game-winning touchdown rather than settle for a game-tying field goal, but he acknowledged the throw wasn't what the Patriots wanted. "We're trying to be aggressive and win the football game, but not reckless," Vrabel said. "It's never just about one guy. I think everybody knows that." It's not about one guy, but the Patriots' loss to the Seahawks was primarily attributable to one guy: Maye wasn't good enough.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Drake Maye: My bad decisions cost us the game
summary: "That wasn't how I play football and how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots," Maye said after losing to the Seahawks.
full_text: ''' Patriots quarterback Drake Maye took the blame after throwing three interceptions in a 13-10 loss to the Seahawks to open the NFL season on Wednesday night. "I thought we had the game under control," Maye said. "I lost patience and it cost us. There were decisions that cost us the game, on my part, on my end. I vow to myself to be better and realize it's a long season, but at the same time you can't have those. It was unacceptable and I know I have to get back to work, because that wasn't how I play football and how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots." With the Patriots trailing by a field goal and in field goal range in the final minute, Maye knew a turnover was the one thing the Patriots couldn't afford. And yet he threw a pass into the end zone that Seattle's Josh Jobe intercepted, sealing the Patriots' loss. "It was just unacceptable. We had a chance to send it to overtime, at the worst, and the only thing you could do was turn the ball over, and that's what I did." Maye had a tremendous 2025 season, finishing second in MVP voting and leading the Patriots to the Super Bowl. But they lost the Super Bowl to the Seahawks, and los to the Seahawks again in Week 1, and Maye knows he needs to be better.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ernest Jones: When you think about Seattle, we want you to think about defense
summary: The Seahawks didn't put any points on the board until the fourth quarter on Wednesday night, but waiting to get the scoring started didn't keep them from coming up with a win.
full_text: The Seahawks didn't put any points on the board until the fourth quarter on Wednesday night, but waiting to get the scoring started didn't keep them from coming up with a win. Their defense forced four punts while spotting the Patriots a 10-0 lead and then came up with interceptions on New England's final three possessions to help pave the way to a 13-10 comeback win that played out with quarterback Sam Darnold out of the game to be evaluated for a hip injury. The Seahawks also sacked Drake Maye three times in the second half and generally sent notice to the NFL that the unit that propelled them to the Super Bowl last season remain in fine shape. "When you think about Seattle, we want you to think about our defense , and what we are going to bring each and every day," linebacker Ernest Jones said, via the team's website. The Seahawks pulled off Wednesday's performance without safeties Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada, so they'll have even more weapons at their disposal in the weeks to come and that's not great news for the opposing offenses on their schedule.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers restructure DL Tershawn Wharton's contract
summary: The Panthers have created some more cap room ahead of Week 1.
full_text: The Panthers have created some more cap room ahead of Week 1. Per Spotrac, they have restructured defensive lineman Tershawn Wharton's contract. They converted $12.2 million of his base salary into a signing bonus, which opened up $9.7 million in cap space for the coming season. Wharton is in the second season of a three-year deal and the team added three void years to further spread out the remaining cap hit in coming seasons. While Wharton is helping the team's salary cap situation, he won't be helping them against the Bears on Sunday. Wharton had neck surgery this offseason and is on the physically unable to perform list to open the regular season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Harrison Smith: I kind of knew I'd be back the whole time
summary: Vikings fans saluted Harrison Smith's entire career when he walked off the field at the end of Week 18 last season, but thoughts that it was the final time the safety would be on the field were premature.
full_text: ' Vikings fans saluted Harrison Smith's entire career when he walked off the field at the end of Week 18 last season, but thoughts that it was the final time the safety would be on the field were premature. Smith was out of contract throughout the offseason and preseason, but remained in touch with head coach Kevin O'Connell and agreed to return for a 15th season a few days ago. While that came as a pleasant surprise to many in Minnesota, it was something that Smith had in mind for quite a while. "I think I kind of knew it the whole time . I just didn't know, exactly, the timing," Smith said, via the team's website. Neither Smith nor O'Connell is ready to say that the safety will play against the Packers in Week 1. Smith has worked out with a return in mind, but acknowledged the big difference between that training and what he'll be called to do on the field. "I'm in good shape. I've been working out," Smith said. "But there's nothing like playing football. It's just the reality of it. Heart rate, outside factors, thinking a lot while you're moving. It's hard to simulate that. I kind of do it the best I can. There's something about being on the grass and thinking while you're moving. You can feel a little stuck sometimes and just getting the fluidity back. That's kind of what I've been able to do the last few years — be very fluid out there while I'm thinking." Smith wasn't on the injury report for Wednesday, but further word on his status for Sunday will likely come closer to kickoff.
author: Josh Alper

title: PFT's Week 1 2026 NFL picks
summary: My not-for-betting purposes look at all 16 opening-weekend games.
full_text: The 2026 season returns tonight, and we'll be doing things a little bit differently when it comes to the weekly effort to predict what may happen in the upcoming slate of games. For decades, I've had my own thoughts about who will, or won't, win in a given weekend. Thanks to the fact that my dad was a bookie, and given his incessant messaging that it's impossible for the bettor to win over the long haul, I've had no inclination to wager on games. When the floodgates for legalized, normalized, and monetized sports betting opened eight years ago, my relationship with the burgeoning industry became complicated, to say the least. There's plenty of money to be made in sports media by aligning with one, or more, of the various sportsbooks and, more recently, prediction markets. I've declined to pursue any direct deals, due in large part to the reality that the ease of app-based betting has spawned, and will continue to create, generations of folks who fail to understand that, over time, it's a losing proposition. (And, of course, the small minority who figure out a way to win consistently will inevitably be cut off.) I've used this platform to be candid about the realities of betting, in the hopes of dissuading young men with still-developing brains from thinking it's a path to getting rich quick or, even worse, from believing it's a replacement for the more traditional means for making ends meet. I've previously balanced those concerns with taping weekly podcasts in which Simms and I made picks for every game against the spread. It bugged me. It gnawed at me. Starting this year, I decided to stop doing it. But what about my views on the coming games? Is it possible to pick winners and losers for the sheer fun of it, with no skin in the game — and without sending the message, directly or indirectly, that others should rely on my views when making their wagering decisions? I decided to lay out my weekly picks, for amusement purposes only. "Amusement purposes only" used to be code for "go ahead and bet." Now, it's truly for amusement purposes only. With the addition of a clear caveat that you should only wager what you can afford to lose. Over time, you will. Have a budget. Stick to it. And never, ever chase your losses. The gambling money should come from your entertainment budget. Use only the money you'd otherwise spend for movies, video games, steaming services, books (I've got four you can chose from, with more coming), and do not go beyond that. When the budgeted amount is gone, it's gone. I'll reiterate that message every week, mainly because too few of the people in sports media who are grabbing the bag from sportsbooks and prediction markets will ever bother to tell the members of their audience the truth about gambling. As my dad the bookie started telling me more than 50 years ago, you can't win . With that, here's my own personal look at each of the games. Do not rely on anything I say if you choose to devote any of your entertainment budget to betting on the games. Patriots at Seahawks (Wednesday) For the third time, a Super Bowl rematch happens in Week 1. The Patriots have beefed up the passing game, with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Quarterback Drake Maye and left tackle Will Campbell are healthy. The Seahawks lost Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III to free agency. Rookie Jadarian Price carries the load, with Zach Charbonnet (knee) starting the season on the PUP list. And Seattle has a brand-new, first-time offensive coordinator in Brian Fleury, thanks to Klint Kubiak doing the job well enough in one year to become a head coach. It won't be easy for the Patriots, who were blown out by the Seahawks at a neutral site in February. But they have receivers Brown and Doubs. Maye is healthy. And they seem to be rallying around coach Mike Vrabel, after his eventful offseason. It's a pure hunch. And I'd rather be wrong by being bold than to take the chalk and regret missing the potential signs for an opening-night upset. Patriots 24, Seahawks 21. 49ers vs. Rams in Australia (Thursday) The Rams reacted to a close-but-no-cigar 2025 season by adding defensive end Myles Garrett. Which sparked defensive tackle Aaron Donald's unretirement. And while Donald didn't make the trip to Melbourne, the Rams have enough to overcome a 49ers team that has had one bizarre thing after another happen to it this year. While health will be a key factor as to whether the Rams can get to the Super Bowl and win it, they're healthy for now. And they seem to fully believe in their plan to barnstorm in and out of Australia. Rams 24, 49ers 13. Bills at Texans Few teams have ever faced more pressure than the Bills carry into 2026. The coach was fired after losing in overtime in the divisional round. The G.M. was promoted, as was the offensive coordinator. And the campaign starts with a trip to face the best defense in the NFL, which may be even better in 2026. Yes, the offense is a major question mark for the Texans. They should be able to do enough to hold serve in a home game that could serve as the first step toward winning the top seed in the AFC. Texans 20, Bills 16. Buccaneers at Bengals The Bucs relish the opportunity to get things started on the road, and quarterback Baker Mayfield's new contract removes one significant potential distraction. But the Bengals know the stakes. A fourth straight season without a playoff berth will result in major changes. For now, Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow sees parallels to his 2019 LSU team, which won a national championship. That's enough to get me to give them the edge at home in what could be one of the most exciting games of the first weekend of the season. Bengals 27, Buccaneers 24. Bears at Panthers Carolina won a none-of-the-above division last year, thanks to the Falcons beating the Saints on the final Sunday. The Bears traded to Carolina the pick that became quarterback Bryce Young, and that allowed the Bears (since Carolina bottomed out in 2023) to land MVP contender Caleb Wiliams. It will be a challenging year for the Bears as the hunted in the NFC North. For now, their Week 1 Panther hunt should be successful. Bears 24, Panthers 17. Saints at Lions Lions coach Dan Campbell believes the team's Super Bowl window is still open. They have the talent to justify his faith. Now, they just have to prove it. A strong Week 1 start against a sneaky-good Saints team will help set the tone. Much of it hinges on new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. With running back Jahmyr Gibbs now the centerpiece of the offense, it becomes much easier for any offensive coach to look like Bill Walsh. Lions 34, Saints 24. Ravens at Colts. The team that fled Baltimore in 1984 hosts the team that backfilled the vacancy 12 years later. It's a tough opener for a new coaching staff, but the Ravens have Lamar Jackson — and he seems to be a big believer in the new offense. Ravens 24, Colts 20. Falcons at Steelers The post-Mike Tomlin era begins with what should be an easy win against Tua Tagovailoa, who won the QB1 job by default. The Steelers are 14-2-1 vs. the Falcons since the AFL-NFL merger. A loss would spark widespread panic in Pittsburgh, especially against a quarterback with a reputation for panicking when the first read is covered. Steelers 21, Falcons 10. Jets at Titans Robert Saleh is saying all the right things publicly. Privately, he surely relishes the chance to stick it to the owner who prematurely pulled the plug on what could have been a potential playoff contender in 2024. The question is whether the Titans have enough talent to outscore the Jets. Home team gets the edge. Titans 20, Jets 17. Browns at Jaguars Deshaun Watson gets a two-game audition in Florida, with the goal of doing enough to get the folks in Cleveland to accept him for Week 3 and Week 4. The Jaguars feel disrespected and overlooked; Sunday gives them a chance to put the world on notice that they'll be a force in 2026. Jaguars 28, Browns 14. Commanders at Eagles Before…
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL Kickoff 2026: Seahawks beat Patriots 13-10, but lose Sam Darnold to hip injury
summary: Seattle's defense picked off Drake Maye three times, including late in the fourth quarter to clinch the Week 1 victory.
full_text: The Seahawks beat the Patriots 13-10 after raising the banner for beating the same club in Super Bowl LX. But Seattle’s celebration will likely be a bit muted, as the club has a significant injury concern with its quarterback. Sam Darnold exited the contest after Seattle’s first series of the season with a hip injury and did not return. Darnold was sacked by Dre’Mont Jones on third-and-6 from the New England 46 — Seattle’s sixth play from scrimmage. Darnold came off the field with a noticeable limp. He was examined in the sideline medical tent before going to the locker room for further evaluation, which was when he was announced as questionable. Just before halftime, Seattle downgraded Darnold to out. The quarterback completed one of his two passes for 13 yards, which was a completion to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Drew Lock replaced Darnold on the second drive and played the rest of the game. On the other side, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, the last of which took New England out of the game. With just 26 seconds left in regulation and the Patriots facing third-and-5 from Seattle’s 16-yard line, Maye was flushed out of the pocket to his right and inexplicably threw a poor jump ball to Mack Hollins in the end zone. But Josh Jobe caught the ball instead, effectively ending the contest. The Patriots had taken a conservative offensive approach for most of the game and had a 10-3 lead entering the fourth quarter. But that’s when the meltdown started, as Maye attempted a deep pass to Romeo Doubs that was intercepted by Nathaniel Pritchett on the second play of the period. That led to Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 45-yard touchdown catch-and-run that tied the game at 10-10. On New England’s next possession, Romeo Doubs had a critical drop on a second-and-14 play. Doubs was wide open after Maye was able to evade the pass rush in the backfield and roll to his right. But Doubs was unable to handle the throw as it fell incomplete. On the next play, Maye fired a pass over the middle for DeMario Douglas, but Julian Love read the play perfectly and picked the ball off to give Seattle another opportunity. Seattle took advantage of it with Jason Myers’ 26-yard field goal to go up by three. That’s all the Seahawks needed, as Maye threw his final interception to lose the contest. Maye finished 22-of-33 for 178 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Maye did not have a multi-interception game last year until Super Bowl LX, also against the Seahawks. He also had 47 rushing yards on seven attempts. Lock was 16-of-22 for 187 yards with one touchdown in relief of Darnold. Notably, Patriots receiver A.J. Brown also suffered an ankle injury early in the third quarter and did not return. Now at 1-0, the Seahawks will have a long layoff before facing the division-rival Cardinals on the road in Week 2. The 0-1 Patriots will be at home to face the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Deshaun Watson was cited for speeding on August 26
summary: The eventful month for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson included a speeding ticket, two days after he was named the starter.
full_text: The eventful month for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson included a speeding ticket, two days after he was named the starter. Via Fox 8 in Cleveland, Watson was cited for driving 86 miles per hour in a 60 mph zone on Wednesday, August 26. Watson entered a plea of not guilty in Cleveland municipal court on Wednesday. A bench trial is set for Wednesday, September 23. That's a work day for Watson. It makes sense to just accept the ticket and move on; surely, he won't be missing practice before the team's home opener. The citation also happened four days after the low point of his Cleveland career — a preseason appearance that featured incessant booing, and a regrettable postgame press conference during which he expressed doubt as to whether he could play effectively during a future home game. Whether he plays in the Week 3 home game surely depends largely on how he and the team perform in the first two games of the season, at Jacksonville and at Tampa Bay.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Macdonald: Sam Darnold did not suffer hip fracture, more tests to come
summary: The Seahawks received some positive news on quarterback Sam Darnold, but the extent of his hip injury is still unclear.
full_text: The Seahawks received some positive news on quarterback Sam Darnold, but the extent of his hip injury is still unclear. In his postgame press conference on Wednesday night, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that doctors were able to rule out a fracture. "Let’s say it’s good news right now. I know our thoughts and prayers are with Sam — we love him. The guys really pulled through for him," Macdonald said. "At this point, we were able to rule out a fracture . So, there’s some more tests to be done. But that’s what I’m saying when it’s positive, but I know — we’re still working through all that, but right now a fracture is out, which is great news." Darnold exited the game in the first quarter after he was sacked on third down to end Seattle's first possession. After limping off the field, he was examined in the sideline medical tent before limping back up to the locker room for further examination. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Darnold was transported to Harborview Medical Center to undergo a CT scan on his hip. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noted Darnold received positive news on the CT scan and his X-Ray, indicating that he was able to avoid a major injury. But Darnold is scheduled for an MRI on Thursday to confirm the diagnosis. Given the lack of clarity on the injury, Macdonald said he didn't know what Darnold's status would be for Seattle's Week 2 matchup against Arizona.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Vrabel had no postgame update on A.J. Brown
summary: It's still unclear what kind of injury and recovery Patriots receiver A.J.
full_text: It's still unclear what kind of injury and recovery Patriots receiver A.J. Brown is facing. Brown went down with an ankle injury early in the third quarter of Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks to open the 2026 season and did not return. " I don’t have any update yet ," head coach Mike Vrabel said postgame. "Wasn't able to return, obviously." Brown was injured on an incomplete pass from Drake Maye on third down. title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba 45-yard TD ties Seahawks-Patriots at 10-10 in fourth quarter
summary: The reigning AP offensive player of the year just showed why he earned the honor.
full_text: The reigning AP offensive player of the year just showed why he earned the honor. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored a 45-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter to tie the 2026 season opener at 10-10. After Drake Maye tossed his first interception of the year on a jump ball to Romeo Doubs, the Seahawks didn’t take long to get in the end zone for the first time this season. Facing fourth-and-1 in New England territory, quarterback Drew Lock — playing for the injured Sam Darnold — made a quick fake on a handoff and sent a short pass on the left side to a wide-open Smith-Njigba. But from there, the receiver did the rest, turning on the burners to evade defenders for a 45-yard score. Smith-Njigba gained 41 yards after the catch. title: NFL Kickoff 2026: Patriots lead Seahawks 7-0 at halftime
summary: The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.
full_text: The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold exited the game after the first series with a hip injury. He appeared to suffer it when he was sacked by Dre’Mont Jones on third down, which brought up a punt. Darnold limped to the sideline before he was eventually examined in the medical tent. He then limped off the field up to the locker room for further evaluation. Just before halftime, the Seahawks ruled him out. Backup Drew Lock played the rest of the first half for Seattle. So far, he’s completed 6-of-8 passes for 51 yards. But the Seahawks have also struggled to move the ball, registering six first downs. On the other side, Drake Maye has been a lot more effective than he was against Seattle’s defense in Super Bowl LX back in February. He’s gotten off some quick passes and used his legs effectively to scramble. Though Maye’s most productive pass was one that wasn’t even completed — as newcomer A.J. Brown drew a defensive pass interference penalty that put the Patriots at Seattle’s 2-yard line. On the next play, Maye tossed a 2-yard touchdown to rookie tight end Eli Rairdon for the NFL’s first touchdown of 2026. Maye finished the first half 10-of-12 for 66 yards with a touchdown. The Patriots have 10 first downs, 130 yards, and are 3-of-7 on third down. Seattle has 120 yards and is 1-of-6 on third down. They may want to have a heavy dose of rookie Jadarian Price in the second half, who has 42 yards on his six carries in his debut. The Patriots will receive the second-half kickoff.

title: Kittle, Bosa off the injury report; will play in Week 1 vs. Rams in Australia
summary: Kittle tore his Achilles in the wild card round of last year's playoffs, while Bosa suffered an early-season injury in 2025
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle tore his Achilles tendon during the team's wild card round playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles . That was on Jan. 11, 2026. Almost exactly eight months later, Kittle is back. He's off the injury report for the 49ers' season-opening game against the division rival Los Angeles Rams , and he will play on Thursday night. Defensive end Nick Bosa, who has been recovering from a torn ACL, is also off the injury report and will play in Week 1.
Kittle started training camp on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, then spent about a month ramping up before he officially returned to camp. He was limited in practices throughout the week the 49ers spent in Australia leading up to this game, but he had said earlier this week that he had taken a step toward playing. Now, he will.
It's an extremely welcome development for the 49ers, who dealt with various injury issues both last year and throughout this offseason. Not only did Kittle get hurt during the playoffs, but stars Fred Warner and Nick Bosa didn't play in the postseason at all after suffering early-season injuries that ended their respective years. Those were major contributing factors in their blowout loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in the divisional round.
Bosa, like Kittle, is off the injury report for Week 1 and will play against the Rams in Australia. He's coming off the second torn ACL of his career. Warner almost made it back for the playoffs last year and has been healthy throughout the offseason.
This summer, the 49ers lost wide receiver Ricky Pearsall for the season due to a lingering knee injury. They also saw both Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans miss copious practice time with various ailments (they are both healthy and good to go for Week 1), so they have rarely — if ever — been at full strength in the lead-up to the season opener. Getting Kittle back in the fold is another step in the right direction.
Kittle is heading into his age-33 season. He racked up 57 catches for 628 yards and seven touchdowns in just 11 games last year. He's long been one of the most explosive tight ends in the league in the receiving game, as well as the league's best blocker at that position. It remains to be seen how his power and explosiveness will hold up through this injury, but the fact that he's able to return so soon is an encouraging sign of his progress.
