title: What NFL scouts say about Texas QB Arch Manning ahead of Ohio State test: 'Good's really good, but ...'
summary: Arch Manning led college football in QBR after Halloween last season, but NFL evaluators want to see more refined accuracy and consistency when Texas faces Ohio State on Saturday
full_text:
"He's still got a ways to go."
That's what a high-ranking NFL front office staffer said this summer about Arch Manning's 2025 tape, a common theme when speaking with NFL scouts about the Texas quarterback's future as a draft prospect.
"I think he's an eventual first-round guy, but I don't think the tape from last year says first round yet," that front office staffer told CBS Sports in June. "I view Arch right now as a developmental (NFL) starter that still has a long way to go in terms of touch and processing and seeing the field, but you expect that he's going to get it because he has all the physical tools and the wiring and the pedigree from his family and all that."
Simply put, many NFL personnel and scouting staffers want to see continued growth from Manning this season before being ready to project him as a definite to be one of the top picks in next year's NFL draft if the fourth-year junior decides to turn pro. Manning ranks as the No. 1 player on Mike Renner's Big Board at CBS Sports.
Personnel and scouting staffers saw clear growth throughout last season but there will be a lot of NFL eyeballs on Manning when Texas faces Ohio State on Saturday to see if he's now taken another step forward.
"The good's really good," an NFL college scouting director told CBS Sports. "I think he had severe issues last year with accuracy, ball placement and just anticipation all over the field, but if you just go talent for talent, like he's 1A, 1B with the best guys in the country coming out. It's just really about the nuances of the position. Sometimes he looks like he's skipping rocks. If you watch the Ohio State game (last year), he looked terrible and looked scared and timid but then towards the end of the year, he started playing better."
After the up-and-down start to the season last year, which included losses to two of Texas' first four Power Four opponents and 170 passing yards or fewer from Manning in three of those four games, the former Class of 2023 No. 1 ranked recruit did close his first season as the Longhorns' starting QB with an average of 286 passing yards in the final six games. In those six matchups, four of which were against opponents ranked in the top 20, Manning also accounted for 19 total touchdowns (14 passing and five rushing) with just two interceptions. Nobody in college football had a higher QBR than Manning after Halloween.
"I felt like earlier in the season last year, (Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian) was protecting him with his play-calling comparative with Quinn Ewers because Sark can dial it up with the best of them and I didn't think that they were doing necessarily things to open up the offense," the college scouting director said. "It seemed like it was more to protect the quarterback from himself, but that's just one man's opinion. He's a better athlete than quarterback at this point, but he's got traits to be a really good quarterback. He just needs more time on task. I mean, he played at a 2A high school, where you look at the people that they played, it was nobody. And last year was his first time really being a starter (in college). So I think it was A) Great he came back to school and B) They have a ton of talent out wide. So he has toys, he has a really good play-caller and I expect him to take a natural jump this year."
Manning is indeed off to a good start in 2026.
In two-and-a-half quarters of work during Texas' season-opening 59-7 win over Texas State, Manning threw for 305 yards with four touchdown passes and one interception. Two of the touchdown passes were to star Auburn transfer Cam Coleman , who's a possibility to go in the top 10 of next year's draft. One of the others was a jet sweep to another star junior wide receiver, Ryan Wingo , who also has a shot to go early in next year's draft. Manning hit both Wingo and Coleman on deep shots as well.
It was a nice warmup before this upcoming game against Ohio State on Saturday, a matchup that will provide NFL personnel and scouting staffers with a much better feel for Manning's readiness to be considered a clear-cut top prospect for next year's draft.
"I think he's probably just playing with a little more confidence with it being Year 2 starting for him," Texas State head coach and former NFL QB GJ Kinne told CBS Sports. "I would say that's the biggest thing I saw is he just looks more comfortable. Physically, he's as good as there is in college football.
"He's got everything. He's big. He's athletic. He's got a really strong arm. I think he's also got a couple first rounders at receiver. It kind of reminds me of when Joe Burrow had Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase. He's got elite weapons around him and he's really talented."
author: Matt Zenitz

title: Ranking AFC and NFC championship teams most likely to fall and pick top 10 overall in the draft
summary: New England faces the steepest regression risk due to a brutal schedule, while star-loaded Los Angeles to remain among the elite contenders
full_text:
NFL teams are susceptible to big swings from one year to the next. For dreamers, one popular exercise has been projecting which teams are most likely to go from bottom dweller to Super Bowl contender . The Patriots were an example last season. Alternatively, there is the path that the Commanders took: going from the NFC Championship game during the 2024 season to the No. 7 overall selection in the NFL Draft. The catalyst for that regression was the injury to quarterback Jayden Daniels .
Considering the four teams representing the AFC and NFC in the conference championship and beyond, how would the Patriots, Broncos , Seahawks and Rams rank, from least likely to most likely to pick in top 10 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft ?
No team has improved more than the Rams since last season concluded. They took an NFC title roster and added All-Pros Trent McDuffie , Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald . The secondary has gone from a weakness to a strength, and the unit should benefit from increased pressure from the front.
Los Angeles has one of the oldest rosters in the league, which could make them more susceptible to injuries. General manager Les Snead has done well building contingencies into the roster. They brought back Tutu Atwell at receiver. They used the No. 13 overall selection on Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson rather than attacking a position of greater need this season. If Simpson is forced into action, there is every reason to believe Sean McVay, who got Baker Mayfield ready on a day's notice, will have the rookie up to speed.
The offensive line is a bit of a concern from a talent perspective, but the team has always been able to mitigate a lack of talent through the scheme.
There is a lot of confidence in head coach Mike Macdonald, who reminds me of a young Bill Belichick. Macdonald's defensive accomplishments do not rely solely on a schematic advantage. He has a forward way of thinking that should allow him to remain on the front foot as team personnel and the league evolves around him.
There were key members of that Seattle team who will not be back: cornerback Riq Woolen, running back Kenneth Walker III , edge rusher Boye Mafe and others. However, the lead actors remain intact.
There will always be a portion of NFL fans who are waiting for the other shoe to drop on quarterback Sam Darnold . He has been good for two consecutive seasons, but the image of him seeing ghosts early in his career with the Jets will outlast him.
HBO's 'Hard Knocks' offered a glimpse into what appears to be a very close-knit locker room, and there is a level of expectation fostered in that building. The Seahawks return as one of the favorites to win the Super Bowl.
Denver made one of the best acquisitions of the offseason in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle . Waddle is viewed as the missing piece to Sean Payton's operation. He brings the motion and speed they've sorely lacked. Otherwise, the offseason was more of a net negative for the organization.
The defense is among the best in the league, but edge rusher Jonathon Cooper was placed on the commissioner's exempt list as the league investigates an offseason incident, and defensive tackle John Franklin Myers signed with the Titans in free agency. How many threads in the defense can be pulled before the rug unravels?
Quarterback Bo Nix brings competency to the position but lacks the physical tools to carry the team to victory. Payton is regarded as one of the best in the league, so bottoming out is probably not an option for this team. In a division with the Chiefs , Chargers and what should be an improved Raiders team, the path to the postseason is littered with potholes.
The Patriots, under head coach Mike Vrabel, arrived to the party sooner than anticipated last season. New England's roster was among the worst in the league after the 2024 campaign, but leadership relied upon quarterback Drake Maye and a strong rookie class to propel expectations.
However, several factors make it likely the franchise will go from title contender to a top-10 overall pick in the draft. First and foremost, New England had the fourth-easiest strength of schedule last season. A byproduct of a successful season is that they now have the sixth-hardest schedule based on last season's win totals.
Although the Patriots are No. 1 on this list, the presence of Vrabel creates a high floor that would likely prevent them from picking early in next year's draft. The offensive line has more depth but is still a relative unknown heading into the season. Maye's collection of pass catchers has improved year over year. The offseason drama surrounding Vrabel is in the rearview mirror and likely an afterthought for his players.
In short, there is no strong candidate to mirror the Commanders ' 2025-2026 fall.
author: Josh Edwards

title: 2026 NFL season predictions: CBS Sports experts make Super Bowl, playoff, division champion picks
summary: CBS Sports writers, editors, analysts and on-air talent make their picks
full_text:
For just the second time ever, the season is starting on a Wednesday, with the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks hosting the New England Patriots in a rematch of Super Bowl 60.
The fact that both teams are in this position is something few saw coming entering the 2025 season. The Seahawks had a nice showing in 2024 in their first year under Mike Macdonald, but they moved on from quarterback Geno Smith and offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb for Sam Darnold and Klint Kubiak at their respective positions and also traded away DK Metcalf . It looked more like a team in semi-transition than a team ready to win a Super Bowl. The Patriots, meanwhile, were coming off a 4-13 season and looked years away from contending.
But the NFL is full of surprises, and 2025 proved it. There will be more surprises in 2026, making picking teams both exciting and challenging. Here is how the CBS Sports NFL staff -- writers, editors, analysts and researchers -- envision this season playing out.
Voters: Pete Prisco, Leger Douzable , Emory Hunt, Mike Renner, R.J. White, Ryan Wilson, Jordan Dajani, Josh Edwards, Bryan DeArdo, Tyler Sullivan, Garrett Podell, Jared Dubin, John Breech, Zach Pereles, Doug Clawson
The Eagles became the first team in over 20 years to repeat as NFC East champions, but our voters see a new face emerging atop the division. The Cowboys had a huge offseason adding defensive talent -- both in terms of players and coaches -- to complement a high-flying offense.
The NFC North is the only division that features all four teams getting at least one vote as division champion, and for good reason: All four teams posted winning records last season. There are significant questions for all four teams that prevent them from joining the upper echelon of Super Bowl favorites, but this will be a dogfight.
The Buccaneers' four-year reign atop the division ended last season at the hands of the Panthers , who, eight months later, are the only team in the division not to receive a vote to win it. The Saints' strong finish to 2025 helps them garner significant consideration from our voters.
The Rams are Super Bowl favorites and, in turn, NFC West favorites. The 10 votes they received were tied for second-most among any projected division winner. Seattle received five division nods, while San Francisco somewhat surprisingly gets zero.
Others receiving votes: Rams (5), Cowboys (5), Packers (4), 49ers (4), Vikings (2), Panthers (1), Lions (1)
Cardinals , Commanders received 0 votes.
Last year, Buffalo was the unanimous pick in the AFC East, and that seemed reasonable given the Bills had won the division five straight years and the other three teams were coming off rough seasons. But Drake Maye's superstar rise fueled one of the most remarkable turnarounds in recent memory, and now, it's a hotly contested vote.
The Bengals have missed the playoffs in three straight seasons, with Joe Burrow injuries and a pourous defense being the two major reasons. While Cincinnati can't guarantee Burrow's health, it did invest heavily in the defense to complement the offense, not unlike the Cowboys.
The Texans' 12 AFC South champion votes are the most for any division in this exercise. The defense is excellent, and Houston is hoping an upgraded offensive line and running game can get C.J. Stroud back on track. The Jaguars won't just go away, though: They won eight straight games to finish the 2025 regular season, with Trevor Lawrence finding his stride in Liam Coen's offense.
The Broncos ended the Chiefs' nine-year streak atop the division last season and are now poised to make it back-to-back AFC West crowns, according to our voters. The Chiefs aren't even expected to finish second in the division, with the Chargers earning four nods compared to Kansas City's one.
Others receiving votes: Broncos (4), Bengals (4), Texans (3), Steelers (2), Patriots (2), Jaguars (1)
Browns , Colts , Dolphins , Jets , Raiders , Titans received 0 votes.

title: It wouldn't shock me IF ... for NFL Week 1: Tua one-and-done as QB1, Patrick Mahomes under siege on 'MNF'
summary: Don't be surprised if we see these storylines develop over the course of Week 1
full_text:
We're here. Can you believe it? We finally made it to Week 1, and we have a full regular season in front of us to watch unfold. What a time to be alive! Of course, as we begin the new season, there's an onslaught of predictions that flood in about what folks think will happen between now and when we kick off Super Bowl LXI from SoFi Stadium in February. That ranges from who we think will win their respective division, MVP, the Super Bowl, and everything in between.
But how about we start with Week 1?
Below, we're going to highlight a handful of potential storylines and/or individual results that may sound far-fetched right now as we stand in front of Week 1, but we wouldn't be shocked if they happen over the course of the slate.
All NFL odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.
While David Montgomery has been in the league for quite a bit, he's the shiny new toy in the Texans offense after the franchise struck a trade with the Lions to acquire the runner this offseason. Houston has been desperate for any sort of presence on the ground, especially after a 2025 campaign where they got next to nothing out of the backfield.
Yards per rush after contact
Despite those lackluster numbers, the Texans still ran the football 475 times in 2025, which ranked in the top half of the league. They want to run the ball and now have a back (and a revamped offensive line) capable of doing just that.
Now that we've established Houston's eagerness to run the football, let's look at the matchup, which is tasty for Montgomery. The Bills were horrendous against the run in 2025, ranking at or near the bottom of the league in key metrics.
Rushing yards per game allowed
Rushing touchdowns allowed
While Buffalo did add the likes of Bradley Chubb and T.J. Parker this offseason, those additions are more geared toward pressuring the quarterback than they are at stopping the run. Even the return of defensive tackle Ed Oliver (limited to three games last season) is more a boost to the pass rush, so it stands to wonder if the Bills have actually addressed this glaring hole on defense.
Meanwhile, Josh Allen doesn't have the strongest history against the Texans, and if the Bills offense is stagnant, it'd behoove Houston to lean even more on Montgomery to churn the clock, especially if he's excelling on the ground against an advantageous matchup.
Gambling angle to note : David Montgomery is +670 to rush for 100-plus yards in Week 1.
The Lions are expected to bounce back in a big way in 2026 after missing the playoffs last year, but the secondary still has some questions entering Week 1. Safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are beginning the year on the PUP list, and former first-round corner Terrion Arnold was released this offseason due to off-the-field issues. That leaves a cornerback room consisting of veterans Rock Ya-Sin and D.J. Reed on the boundary, with Roger McCreary and Christian Izien likely manning the slot.
Of course, their attention will mainly be paid to Chris Olave , who is the clear-cut No. 1 option in the Saints passing game, and they may even be eyeing tight end Juwan Johnson after that. However, Devaughn Vele is someone who should be on your radar, whether it be for him to find paydirt (like we believe he will) or simply having a strong outing against a questionable Detroit secondary.
With first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) beginning the year on IR, Vele is the No. 2 receiver for New Orleans, and the 28-year-old did have a solid rapport with Tyler Shough down the stretch last season. After Shough became the starter in Week 9, Vele caught 20 of his 29 targets for 254 yards (42.3 per game) and a touchdown. That includes a Week 13 game where he caught all eight of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown. That's the type of outing we wouldn't be surprised to see him have in Week 1.
Vele is 6-foot-5 and can line up both on the outside and in the slot. Given the finite amount of pass catchers New Orleans has, a big target share could be on deck for him in Week 1, giving him a chance to reach the end zone.
Gambling angle to note : Devaughn Vele is +380 to score a touchdown in Week 1.
Bowers is widely considered to be either at or near the top of the list when it comes to the best tight ends in the NFL. Even after an injury-plagued season in 2025, Bowers ranks third all-time at the position for the most receiving yards (1,874) in the first two years of his career. He now gets an upgrade at quarterback in Kirk Cousins (who'll start the year as QB1 over No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza ) and has a new head coach in Klint Kubiak.
The addition of Kubiak is noteworthy considering how he used wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba last year in Seattle. Smith-Njigba was the clear top option in the passing game for the Seahawks , and Kubiak was not shy about peppering him, as he commanded a 36% target share (first in the NFL). Now, Bowers is that clear top option, so it stands to reason he'll get something close to the JSN treatment. That's especially true given Las Vegas' receiver room isn't bursting with household names.
Bowers had 86 targets last season, which ranked second on the team. The only reason he wasn't No. 1 was that he was limited to 12 games. When he did play, he was averaging 7.1 targets per game. That number should only increase in Year 1 of Kubiak's system. Meanwhile, Bowers will see a Dolphins defense in Week 1 that surrendered the fourth-most receiving yards to tight ends last season.
After notching 103 receiving yards in Week 1 last season, Bowers would become just the third tight end in NFL history to top 100 receiving yards in back-to-back season openers, joining Ben Coates (1994-95) and Julius Thomas (2013-14).
Gambling angle to note : Brock Bowers is +339 to record 100-plus receiving yards in Week 1.
Patrick Mahomes is set to make his return in Week 1 after suffering a torn ACL and LCL in Week 15 last season. While it's a remarkable feat for Mahomes to come back nine months to the day of his injury, facing the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football" probably isn't the welcome-back gift he had in mind.
One question I have about Mahomes as he mounts this comeback is his mobility. His ability to use his legs to extend plays and dance around the pocket is one of the reasons he's already a no-doubt Hall of Famer. That said, I wonder if that piece of his game—his escapeability—is one of the last things to truly come back. If so, that could mean he'll hit the turf more than once in this primetime matchup.
Kansas City has real questions surrounding its offensive tackles entering the season. The Chiefs' 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons has been penciled in as the starter at left tackle, but he may be sidelined for Week 1. Andy Reid told reporters on Tuesday that there's "a good chance" Simmons doesn't play in the opener due to a back injury.
In the event he doesn't play, that'd see undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson elevate to the starting role blocking Mahomes' blindside. Meanwhile, Jaylon Moore is set to start at right tackle after the team parted ways with Jawaan Taylor this offseason. In spot appearances last year (42% of the offensive snaps), Moore gave up three sacks and 23 pressures.
So, the duo of Benson and Moore is what stands between Mahomes and a Denver Broncos pass rush that has been otherworldly over the past two years. In that span, they have tallied 131 sacks, 33 more than the next-closest team. With questions at both tackle spots, this is an opportunity for Nik Bonitto and Co. to tee off.
In 14 games played last season, Mahomes was sacked 34 times. That's the second-highest of his career (36 times in 2024 over 16 games played) and averages out to roughly 2.4 sacks taken per game.
The most times Mahomes has been sacked in a game was six, which came against the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl LIX. The most he's been sacked in his regular-season career is five. That occurred in four different instances, including ... his most recent game played, when he…

title: NFL Week 1 odds, picks: Jags throttle Deshaun Watson-led Browns, plus two underdogs win outright
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 1 schedule, plus five locks against the spread
full_text:
To shamelessly rip off our guy Jim Nantz -- Hello, friends!
It's funny how the NFL season lines up: the start of the new year brings a similar "Back to School" vibe. Unlike when I used to stuff my backpack with fresh notebooks, erasable pens (remember those?) and lunch, I'm not filled with the dread of sitting in a classroom all day. Instead, it's giddiness for what the new season may bring and the twists and turns that we're bound to go through.
Last year was the perfect example of how unpredictable the league can be. Both Seattle and New England had +6000 odds at this time last year to win Super Bowl LX. To put that into perspective, that'd be like if either the Commanders or the Colts (both currently +6000) win Super Bowl LXI this February. Crazy!
Before we get ready to strap in for what should be a heck of a ride this season, I want to pat myself on the back and maybe embolden you to pay even more attention to this little gambling window on the internet this season.
In this very post a year ago , I gave you a future parlay to place before Week 1: the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos to make the playoffs, which paid out +362 at the time. Not only did those two cash that playoff future, but they were the No. 1 seeds in their respective conferences.
The regular season was modest: I went 118-151-3 ATS and 167-104-1 SU, but I was profitable with my Locks of the Week (48-42 ATS). Where I really cooked, however, was in the playoffs, going 9-4 ATS and 11-2 straight-up.
That included an almost perfect assessment of Super Bowl LX . I knew the blowout was coming from Seattle and had them easily covering the 4.5-point spread. I almost even got the final score exactly right, as I predicted a 30-17 win by the Seahawks, and they actually won the Super Bowl, 29-13.
So, here's hoping I carried that strong playoff momentum into the offseason and into the 2026 season. Whether you're fading or following, I'm happy to have you along for the ride.
Oh, and how about we run it back with another future parlay to place before Week 1, shall we? Broncos and Saints to make the playoffs at +386. That's the official play, but if you want to sprinkle something with even more juice, you can go this route too: Broncos and Saints to win their divisions at +1000.
Alright, let's get this thing going with, of course, my five locks of the week.
Locks of the Week ATS : 0-0-0 ATS : 0-0-0 ML : 0-0
Whenever you have a quarterback battle in training camp, you want to enter Week 1 with a firm decision and the confidence that the player selected can get the job done. Does anyone feel confident in Deshaun Watson's ability to keep the offense afloat? Watson didn't look particularly sharp this summer, but beat out Shedeur Sanders anyway, and now he'll face a Jaguars defense that really came on strong down the stretch in 2025, which helped them cover their final eight regular-season games, en route to a league-best 12-5 ATS record.
While Cleveland has a new coach in Todd Monken, the franchise has historically been terrible against the spread on the road over the last two seasons. In that time, they are 4-13 ATS, which ranks as the worst record in the NFL.
I think Cleveland has some solid pieces on the defensive side of the ball, but Trevor Lawrence entering his second year under Liam Coen could make the Jacksonville offense even more high-powered than it was a year ago. If they build up a lead and force Watson into a pass-heavy game script, Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker could feast.
Projected score: Jaguars 30, Browns 17 The pick: Jaguars -7.5
The Laremy Tunsil injury (torn triceps on Aug. 8) was a gut punch to the Commanders, who are hoping to rebound after a disappointing 2025 season that was marred by injury. It looms large in this matchup against Philadelphia, particularly if Jonathan Greenard (who has been dealing with the pec injury) is able to go. When you pair protection issues with a defense that may need a few weeks to fit their new pieces ( Odafe Oweh , K'Lavon Chaisson , and Sonny Styles ) in, there's the possibility that things could get out of hand for Washington as they step into Lincoln Financial Field.
On top of that, Jayden Daniels is 1-7 ATS in his last eight road starts.
The Eagles have routinely started the year off on a strong note, winning five straight Week 1 games entering 2026. They are also 9-1 in their past 10 Week 1 contests. Sure, Philadelphia is dealing with its own set of changes, transitioning to a new offense under OC Sean Mannion and working without A.J. Brown (traded to New England), but this is still a potent group. Most importantly, the offensive line is healthy, which I believe was a key reason for their downfall at the end of last season.
Projected score: Eagles 30, Commanders 20 The pick: Eagles -4.5
I simply don't understand how the books are assessing the Broncos. They are currently looking up at the Chiefs and Chargers to win the AFC West, despite reaching the AFC Championship a year ago. Had it not been for Bo Nix suffering a fractured ankle that booted him from the title game, they could've reached the Super Bowl. To me, they are the most complete team in the division after bringing everyone back from last year, getting Nix healthy, and adding Jayden Waddle to the receiver room.
Something tells me they'll remind the league of their ceiling with a statement road win in Week 1 on the Monday Night Football stage.
I also have some serious questions about the Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes is making his return from a torn ACL and LCL he suffered in Week 15, and I wonder if his escapability will be where it needs to be, considering the shakiness of the offensive line. Specifically, left tackle Josh Simmons is dealing with a back injury, while right tackle Jaylon Moore gave up three sacks and 23 pressures last year despite playing just 42% of the offensive snaps in spot appearances. If Simmons is out, Moore would likely swing to left tackle, which would then elevate undrafted free agent Kahlil Benson to right tackle.
So, if you're scoring at home, Kansas City is starting a quarterback who could have limited mobility in his first game back from a season-ending knee injury and is playing behind an offensive line with clear issues at both starting tackle spots, and they are facing a Broncos defense that has piled up 131 sacks over the last two seasons. That might tell the entire story right there.
Projected score: Broncos 24, Chiefs 20 The pick: Broncos +2.5
I believe DJ Moore being added to the Bills offense will do wonders for Josh Allen this season, but that won't happen in Week 1. I love the Texans as a home dog because they are well-equipped to slow down Buffalo's key offensive pieces. Houston allowed just 17.4 points per game last season (second-fewest in the NFL) and 277.2 yards per game (fewest). Derek Stingley Jr . should help slow down the Bills passing attack; rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald could be a key piece against the run; and, of course, you have Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter both screaming off the edge. That's a lot for Josh Allen to deal with, and Houston has played him well recently.
In his career, Allen is 0-4 on the road against the Texans. In those games, his teams have averaged 17.8 points per game, and he's completed just 52.8% of his passes. Over the past two seasons (no matter the location), here's how Allen has fared against Houston compared to the rest of the league.
All the Texans need from the offense is for C.J. Stroud to protect the football. And they might be able to do that with a stable running game after acquiring David Montgomery this offseason. Buffalo struggled mightily against the run in 2025 and didn't do much this offseason to fix that deficiency. If Houston can get it going on the ground, that should help Stroud immensely in this upset attempt.
Projected score: Texans 26, Bills 23 The pick: Texans +1.5

title: Exactly how this Cardinals’ receiver group is shaping up
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are dotting their “i’s” and crossing all the “t’s” as they prepare to play their first game of the season this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers. This is an exciting time for both the coaching staff, the players, and the Cardinals fanbase.   RELATED: CARDINALS EXTEND MICHAEL WILSON This new offensive […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 10: Marvin Harrison Jr #18 and Michael Wilson #14 of the Arizona Cardinals run up field against the New York Jets at State Farm Stadium on November 10, 2024 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are dotting their “i’s” and crossing all the “t’s” as they prepare to play their first game of the season this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers. This is an exciting time for both the coaching staff, the players, and the Cardinals fanbase. RELATED: CARDINALS EXTEND MICHAEL WILSON This new offensive system is the headline of this year’s team. New head coach Mike LaFleur has taken his experience under similar systems used with the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. Does this mean that the Cardinals will have the offensive firepower of their division foes LA and SF? Yes and no. Yes, it is designed similarly, with a lot of schemes, player personnel, and traits the same. No, in that this doesn’t happen overnight. But this offense is loaded with talent. That is, on paper. It all starts with the offensive line and the talent of the quarterback. We will see if both of these boxes become checked as games fall off the calendar. The true test of the new offense is how the receiver room is utilized. Let’s do a deep dive. “X” receiver The X receiver lines up wide from the offensive line. Back in the day, it was referred to as the “split end.” This position is responsible for running a complete route tree, having good moves, physicality, and the ability to get downfield. Marv Harrison (6’-3”, 220 pounds) is the Cardinals’ X receiver. It is what he played in college, and last year’s coaching staff – along with LaFleur’s guys – have kept him there. Harrison had a ton of success in the X at Ohio State, so why relocate him and attempt to teach him a new job? Just imagine if Harrison can take a huge leap this year. Name a receiver award in college, and that hardware became a fireplace mantelpiece for his household. There are plenty of questions regarding Harrison, and it all begins with his durability. He spent his entire career at all levels without ever having any major injuries, but last year he was in and out of the lineup. If he can remain upright, he can become a very valuable tool in this offense. This position typically remains isolated all game. In LaFleur’s system, Harrison must be highly versatile and will be moved around from side to side quite a bit. This is because of tactical responsibilities. One of these is the ability to absorb and fight off physicality from the outside cornerback, who can jam Harrison as soon as the ball is snapped. His job has no cushion against aggressive press coverage, and he has to be able to beat a jam. The X has the ability to use the sideline to his benefit. The X must be a good downfield blocker. Harrison is considered a willing and capable blocker, although this is not his strongest asset. While this offense will use quite a bit of 12 and 13 personnel, this will often leave the X isolated in man coverage for his number to be called, or simply running the decoy on a clear-out route for another receiver underneath. The main job of the X is to win those isolated man matchups. Harrison showed in college that that is his style of play anyway. “Z” receiver This is where it gets interesting. Last year’s sensation in this offense, Michael Wilson (6’-2”, 213 pounds) is the Z receiver. This position is different from last year’s offensive scheme. Back in the day, this was referred to as the “flanker.” Look at the Los Angeles Rams. The Z is Puka Nacua. Look at the Seattle Seahawks. Their Z is Cooper Kupp. Typically, the Z receiver is the secondary option, but in LaFleur’s offense, it is the engine that sparks the passing game. The Z is a step off the line of scrimmage as another outside receiver and is able to go in motion. Part of the scheme for the Z is that it heavily utilizes play-action concepts that strike the intermediate portions of the field. This helps the offensive line because plays don’t take that long to develop, and the ball is out pretty quickly. Now, it does require a receiver who isn’t afraid to run crossing routes and deal with hard-hitting safeties. As the Z the past three seasons, Nacua had 160, 106, and 166 targets, and 1,486, 990, and 1,715 yards, respectively. And who was Nacua’s coach? LaFleur. Slot receiver This position sits inside its own little pocket outside of either side’s offensive tackle, or if a tight end is lined up. He must be a step off the line and have another receiver on his outside shoulder. He is another guy who will often go into motion and run the ball on the jet sweep. Usually, this is a smaller receiver. For now, Kendrick Bourne (6’-1”, 205 pounds) is playing the slot. Tyreek Hill is a great example who perfectly fills this role by getting up to speed before he turns upfield and has a good running start, often just blowing by his defender. And while Bourne isn’t running in the 4.3 range, his time in the 40 was 4.68, so he doesn’t have that flat-out speed, but he does have quickness. This is a player who rarely gets jammed at the line and doesn’t have the sideline to work with or help him out with bad throws. Bourne is used to the short passing game, which is what the slot was invented for. All it takes is to fool just one defender, and either the center of the field or a soft zone towards the sideline is what he is working for. More than the other two positions, the slot guy must be able to create separation. And after he has gotten some space between himself and the defender, he must be able to defend himself against a head-hunting safety. At times, Bourne will be asked to take it deep, usually in center field. By taking his routes down the middle of the field, he has the advantage of knowing which direction he will break off his route. The depth There will be some four-receiver sets, but only once in a while. But this offense would rather stick another tight end on the field than four pass catchers. When it does happen, most likely you will see Simi Fehoko (6’-4”, 225 pounds), who is the backup to Wilson, as WR4. Two players who should get some snaps are Jalen Brooks (6’-1”, 205 pounds) and the rookie, Reggie Virgil (6’-3”, 187 pounds). Devin Duvernay (5’-10”, 202 pounds) is also listed in the receiver room, but most likely he will be strictly a kickoff and punt returner. Brooks is the guy who might be able to strip away some snaps from Bourne. He has an uncanny ability to get open in deep soft zones and is fearless about being around defenders. He will take hits and secure the catch extremely well. The coaches are very high on the rookie Virgil. But just remember, it is a very deep room. And he is in his first year, so his best friend is patience. This entire group for the past two years pretty much was reliant on the development of Harrison, who was taken with the fourth overall pick and was expected to become the next Jerry Rice and blow up the league. But with the development of Wilson last year, and the experience of Bourne being signed away from the 49ers (who run this same offense) and the preseason success of both Brooks and Virgil, the Cardinals won’t have to rely on Harrison so much this year. If he continues to get injured, the offense is no longer decimated by his absence. There are guys now who can become plug-and-play, and the beat goes on. If Harrison can remain vertical, if Wilson can grow his game even further, and if Bourne can fill his role with his nine years of experience, this will give the Cardinals what they have been missing for many, many years since the glory days of Larry Fitzgerald. A balanced passing attack. The Cardinals open Week 1 on Sunday, September 13, on the road against the Chargers. Kickoff is at 4:25 p.m.(Eastern) and will be broadcast on CBS.

title: Falcons vs. Steelers: What will Week 1’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: We’re at the starting line of yet another NFL season, as the Atlanta Falcons look to fight their way out of the wilderness. The team made headlines this offseason by cleaning house from top to bottom and replacing all of the primary decision makers in Flowery Branch, booting away Raheem Morris, Terry Fontenot and Rich […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re at the starting line of yet another NFL season, as the Atlanta Falcons look to fight their way out of the wilderness. The team made headlines this offseason by cleaning house from top to bottom and replacing all of the primary decision makers in Flowery Branch, booting away Raheem Morris, Terry Fontenot and Rich McKay after another period of failure. Now, with Matt Ryan, Ian Cunningham and Kevin Stefanski at the helm, Atlanta looks to transition into a period of prosperity, something they haven’t had since Ryan himself was operating under center as the team’s quarterback. We will go game by game with the Falcons throughout the season answering two simple questions before each game — what will happen from a scenario perspective if they win this coming week, as well as if they lose. The Falcons are currently in the midst of a nine year playoff draught, the second-longest active streak in the NFL. If they win and are in contention for a post season spot, this series will be looking at possible playoff and division based scenarios. Conversely, if they go the familiar route of losing too much, this will become a series looking at draft based scenarios. Let’s get right into it then for the 2026 season. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win It will be a dream start for Kevin Stefanski, who will become the first non-interim Falcons head coach to start his tenure with a victory since Dan Quinn’s victory on Monday Night Football in 2015. He will do so by beating a team he faced as a division rival the last six seasons, in Cleveland, as well. The Falcons themselves will get off to their first 1-0 start since beating Carolina at home in 2023, and will avenge a 2024 home defeat against the Steelers in that season opener, which was also Raheem Morris’ first game in his new Falcons tenure. This would also be just the second time Atlanta won game one of the season since 2017, which is also the last time they made it to the playoffs. This would not be a victory against just any opponent — it would be just Atlanta’s third triumph over the Steelers in 20 tries, historically. Pittsburgh is the team that has beaten the Falcons more thoroughly than anybody else according to win percentage. This would be the Birds’ first win in this matchup in exactly two decades; it would also be their first victory in Pittsburgh ever. The Falcons have a home game against a Panthers team that’s had their number in recent memory coming up, and going into that game with a 1-0 record will not only increase their confidence but it would relieve any pressure of potentially digging themselves into an 0-2 hole from the jump. If the Falcons lose It will be more of the same historically — another head coach starting his Falcons career off with a defeat, another season starting 0-1, another loss to the Steelers specifically. Following a turbulent training camp and preseason period, the fanbase will likely be a bit more distraught than usual with another poor start. Stefanski’s own personal record against the Steel Curtain will fall to 6-8 (6-7 with Cleveland which, all things considered is pretty good given how bad the Browns have historically been in that matchup since becoming reestablished as a franchise). Atlanta’s schedule this season isn’t what I would consider light. Early on, their upcoming games in the immediate aftermath of this one will be against a Panthers team that swept them last season followed by a Thursday night trip to Lambeau Field to face a very good Packers team. This isn’t even getting to the difficult part of the schedule yet. Things could begin getting a bit dire quickly if they start out with a defeat right from the jump.

title: Atlanta Falcons 2026 game-by-game jersey schedule
summary: The 2026 NFL season is officially here, which means it’s time to look ahead at what the Atlanta Falcons will be wearing every week. With the new uniforms in rotation, they’re going to look good no matter what—but the team does plan to wear their perfect 1966-inspired throwbacks for two games this season. Let’s take […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) The 2026 NFL season is officially here, which means it’s time to look ahead at what the Atlanta Falcons will be wearing every week. With the new uniforms in rotation, they’re going to look good no matter what—but the team does plan to wear their perfect 1966-inspired throwbacks for two games this season. Let’s take a look. Week 1, at Steelers – White Week 2, vs. Panthers – Red Week 3, at Packers – White Week 4, at Saints – Red Week 5, vs. Ravens – Red Week 6, vs. Bears – Red Week 7, vs. 49ers – Throwbacks Week 8, at Buccaneers – White Week 9, vs. Bengals – Red Week 10, vs. Chiefs – Red Week 11, BYE Week 12, at Vikings – White Week 13, vs. Lions – Throwbacks Week 14, at Browns – White Week 15, at Commanders – White Week 16, vs. Buccaneers – White Week 17, vs. Saints – Red Week 18, at Panthers – White It’s a pretty solid jersey schedule overall. The only letdown to me is that the team is going from wearing throwbacks three times in 2025 to only wearing them twice in 2026. But it makes sense considering they likely want to show off their new uniforms. My favorite matchup is going to be the Detroit Lions game in Week 13. Something about that Lions’ Honolulu blue and the Falcons throwbacks is going to make for a nice display on the field. An interesting note is that these are just the tops, we likely won’t know what pants they wear until the week of each game (aside from the throwback games which, will be white pants.) I know some don’t care what they wear, as long as they win, and I get that. But if you’re going to watch 17 games of this team, might as well look nice visually even if their performance doesn’t always back it up.

title: Falcons vs. Steelers Week 1 injuries: Michael Penix Jr. logs full practice
summary: Welcome back, folks! The first official Atlanta Falcons practice report for the regular season is here. If you’re new here, every week we bring the practice reports to you, giving you insight into who is or is not practicing, usually due to injuries. In Week 1 the Falcons will be taking on the Pittsburgh Steelers, […]
full_text: Welcome back, folks! The first official Atlanta Falcons practice report for the regular season is here. If you’re new here, every week we bring the practice reports to you, giving you insight into who is or is not practicing, usually due to injuries. In Week 1 the Falcons will be taking on the Pittsburgh Steelers, and we have a couple of injuries to keep an eye on out of the gate. Let’s take a look! Falcons injury report Full • QB Michael Penix Jr. (knee) Limited • WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) • OL Kyle Hinton (knee) • CB Billy Bowman Jr. (achilles) • DL Brandon Dorlus (groin) • DE Za’Darius Smith (shoulder) Did Not Practice • N/A Steelers injury report Full • N/A Limited • CB Joey Porter Jr. (back) Did Not Practice • N/A As we look at the Falcons first, there’s a few names to keep an eye on. Rookie receiver Zachariah Branch is limited due to a hamstring injury. He’s expected to factor into the offense and special teams, and hamstrings are tricky injuries. Additionally, the team has a few defensive players who have injuries to keep an eye on. It’s only Wednesday though, so I will say please do not panic. Wednesday’s are often not a strong indicator of who may miss that week’s game. The good news is that quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is practicing fully. It’s already been noted that Tua Tagovailoa will serve as the team’s starter as Penix is slowly brought back in when he’s ready, whenever that is. You may be looking at the Steelers report wondering if I missed some names, but I can assure you that I didn’t. The Steelers have one of the lightest injury reports I’ve seen in a very long time, as only corner Joey Porter Jr. is listed, who has a back issue. We will keep an eye on these injuries as we head into Thursday’s practice.

full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up prior to the start of the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Falcons fans and fans across the country. Although Tua Tagovailoa was selected as the starter against Pittsburgh, it’s inevitable that Michael Penix Jr. will take over as the signal caller at some point. Evidence from training camp and preseason suggests Tagovailoa is merely a placeholder as Penix Jr. gets healthy. From his inability to push the ball downfield to maneuver around the pocket, the former Dolphin’s glaring limitations will make it difficult to maintain faith in his ability to maxmize the offense’s capabilities. A daunting road matchup to start the season will only increase the conversations about Penix Jr. taking over. After facing the Panthers in their home opener, a short week to Green Bay may raise the pressure even further among a fan base that has endured incompetent quarterback play for too long. An extended week to prepare to face their biggest rival may be an ideal time to make the switch. Performance will ultimately determine how the coaching staff moves forward, but it’s hard to envision the Falcons getting off to a winning start in September. The schedule and players/coaches available are always subject to change, but on Wednesday we expect to hear from Kevin Stefanski around noon, Bijan Robinson is expected to address the media about an hour later, and then Tua Tagovailoa will take the podium after practice, around 3:55 p.m. We heard from brand-new Falcon Gervon Dexter on Monday, and today’s Opening Drive walks through some of his more interesting comments. In our community spotlight, I’d forgotten all about Dexter’s RAS score , but it’s worth revisiting. And don’t miss today’s Falcoholic Question of the Day : How many games do you think Tua will start this season, and why? Falcons Opening Drive: Grady Jarrett told Gervon Dexter he’s going to love Atlanta I miss Grady Jarrett, and I’m sure I’m not the only one. Well, Grady still loves Atlanta and the Falcons, and he said as much to his now-former Bears teammate Gervon Dexter, who was traded to the Falcons back on Aug. 30, 2026 . Dexter was asked if he got any Atlanta advice from Grady, and he said Grady came to him. “Grady hit me up and told me I was gonna love it here, and the people were great,” Dexter said. Grady Jarrett sounds like he hasn’t changed a bit since signing with the Bears after he was released by the Falcons in 2024 . “Grady’s … a leader, a crazy leader,” Dexter said. “I’d tell a lot of the young guys coming in, if you want to know what to do, look at Grady, ‘cause he’s always in the right place, you know what I mean? He’s always on time. He don’t do a lot of stuff wrong, so Grady’s a great guy. He helped me a lot last year.” Another Bears-Falcons connection for Dexter is general manager Ian Cunningham, who helped build the team the Bears took to the postseason last year. Dexter said it meant a lot, after Cunningham was part of the crew who drafted him, to land here with a familiar face in the front office. And Dexter thinks he’s a great fit for Jeff Ulbrich’s defense, because he’s “big, fast, strong,” and he loves to be able to “just go” out on the field. Dexter joined some fellow former Florida Gators in Atlanta — right tackle Jawaan Taylor, cornerback C.J. Henderson, and obviously Kyle Pitts Jr. are all Florida alums. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) walks onto the field before the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are starting the 2026 season in relatively good health. Cornerback Bilhal Kone and running back Adam Randall, the team’s injured reserve placements during roster cuts, are more like stashes who were not expected to contribute early in the year, if at all. Losing Danny Pinter, who was leading the starting center competition, is certainly a blow, but he was no guarantee to win the job, either. And on the first injury report of the regular season, only four players are listed, all with limited participation. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee) and defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) are still ramping up from the injuries that ended their 2025 season. Playing in Week 1 seems to be within reach, though the team may want them to put in at least one full practice on either Thursday or Friday. Wide receivers Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Devontez Walker (groin) were both listed as limited, though Flowers said after practice that he expects to play on Sunday in Indianapolis. An absence from Walker would give sole possession of the WR3 role to third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane. Fourth-rounder Elijah Sarratt would also take on a game day role. The Colts also reported four players as limited, including two starters: wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) and safety A.J. Haulcy (ankle). Pierce missed all of training camp as he recovered from offseason ankle surgery. He is expected to play against the Ravens, but may do so on a pitch count as he ramps up to 100%. Haulcy, a third-round pick, is listed as the team’s starting strong safety; 2025 seventh-rounder Hunter Wohler would be in line to start if the rookie cannot go. Indianapolis’ other injuries are to backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) and No. 3 blocking tight end Drew Ogletree (neck). Offensive lineman Josh Sills and tight end Pharaoh Brown would likely be elevated from the practice squad as replacements.

title: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills quick passing game will shape Week 1 vs. Texans
summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is known league-wide for creating explosive plays outside the structure of the play call. When mere mortals hold the ball at quarterback, it usually leads to disaster. Late throws over the middle, risky tosses into triple coverage, sacks — you name it — and it often happens with later, off-schedule […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills gestures against the Houston Texans during the fourth quarter at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is known league-wide for creating explosive plays outside the structure of the play call. When mere mortals hold the ball at quarterback, it usually leads to disaster. Late throws over the middle, risky tosses into triple coverage, sacks — you name it — and it often happens with later, off-schedule throws. With Allen, however, those instances are when the magic happens. It’s when he hits Ray Davis fifty yards downfield while Hall of Famer Peyton Manning is yelling to throw it away. It’s when Khalil Shakir finds space between three defenders on a fourth down to catch a touchdown in such a small window that it would make people who suffer from claustrophobia nervous. It’s when Allen is Allen, as he makes us cringe, hold our breath, cover our eyes, and yell excitedly all in the span of three to five seconds. Against the Houston Texans, though, holding the football often leads to disaster. With Allen holding the football, scrambling, and searching for big plays down the field, it hasn’t led to success against Houston in the same way it has against other teams. In fact, Allen’s 1-4 career mark against Houston, including a 22-19 overtime playoff loss in his second season, is the worst head-to-head record he has against any team he’s faced so often. His 74 quarterback rating is significantly lower than his career total (94.4), and he completes just 52% of his passes against Houston compared to nearly 64% overall for his career. Houston has been a house of horrors for Allen and the Bills of late, and one way the team can overcome those struggles is for their top dog to take what the defense gives him in the passing game. What makes Allen great is his ability to break a big play on any given snap, but sometimes, that desire to break the big one leads him to ignore the “easy money” underneath. That puts the Bills in adverse situations offensively, and it allows a defense like Houston’s to do what it does best: hunt quarterbacks. In Allen’s five matchups against the Texans, he’s averaged at least 2.8 seconds to throw in four of those games. Buffalo lost all four of them. The one time Allen and the Bills beat Houston was when his time to throw was the lowest, coming in at 2.62 seconds on average. Granted, that 40-0 victory likely had less to do with Allen’s throw time and more to do with the lack of talent on Houston’s team in what was ultimately a 4-13 debacle of a season, but it definitely sticks out when comparing his struggles in the other four contests. In Allen’s first two matchups with Houston, his desire to create big plays while holding the ball was easy to explain. In his rookie year, he averaged 3.15 seconds per pass in a game where he ultimately left with an elbow injury. In the following season, Allen played one of the most reckless playoff games I can remember, holding the ball for an average of 3.28 seconds per pass in the eventual Wild Card loss. Both of those games were more the product of a young quarterback trying to do too much against a great defense. That can be explained. In the years since Allen has become a star, though, the Texans and head coach DeMeco Ryans have had his number. In Buffalo’s last two losses at Houston, a 23-20 loss in 2024 where Allen completed just 9-of-30 passes and a 23-19 loss last season where he threw two interceptions against zero scores, Allen’s time to throw was on the higher end. In 2024, he had approximately 3.05 seconds to throw on average, and while he took just one sack, he was pressured often. Last season, Allen had an average of 2.79 seconds to throw. The game plan did seem geared towards shorter, higher-efficiency throws, but as the game wore on, Allen kept trying to make plays downfield—plays that just weren’t there. His time-to-throw number was also lowered artificially by the fact that Houston had an absurd 43% pass rush win rate, which led to a career-high eight sacks in the game. Allen’s last two games against Houston have seen him eschew the easy money for deep, lower-percentage throws. In that 2024 matchup, especially, it looked as if Allen wanted to prove to everyone, but particularly Stefon Diggs, he could do plenty of damage without his former teammate. In last year’s matchup, there’s an argument to be made that Buffalo’s lack of receiving talent combined with Houston’s front four forced Allen to make chicken salad out of chicken feces far more often than he should have. In both games, Buffalo continuously — and stubbornly — countered Houston’s seven-man drop coverage with a five-man protection scheme, and Houston’s front four still found space despite playing a man down. Buffalo’s receiving corps was unable to do the same. This week, for better results when trying to solve Buffalo’s Houston problem, the Bills need to rely on quick-game concepts early. Yes, this might mean our favorite bubble screen play call (which, admittedly, did not work at all last November). And while Joe Brady loves the “mesh” concept, running it against what likely will be a zone-heavy Houston defense is not a good idea. Buffalo would be wise to give Allen some easy half-field reads with a built-in checkdown early in the game. It’s been Allen and the Buffalo offense that has been impatient in the recent meetings between these teams; this week, Buffalo needs to keep taking the easy money until Houston’s defense becomes impatient. Using Buffalo’s advantage in the middle of the field should be a priority this week. Khalil Shakir, Dalton Kincaid, and Dawson Knox need to be the focal points of the passing game, and using newly-acquired DJ Moore as a decoy early and often will help to give those other players space. Does that mean Allen should ignore his newest weapon? Of course not. What it does mean, though, is that I’d rather see him take a five-yard chuck against linebacker Aziz Al’Shaiir before he hurls one into double-coverage with Darryl Stingley Jr. sticking to Moore. Those deep shots can happen, and they need to at some point, but they don’t have to happen in ways where Allen is left to fend off unblocked defenders. Buffalo should take those shots off of max-protect looks, especially in early downs with their “12 or “13” personnel groupings. Why not use play-action with James Cook to hit Joshua Palmer on a deep crosser on first down? Why not use Jackson Hawes as a sixth offensive lineman while Dalton Kincaid stretches the seam? There are options, but more than we’re used to seeing, I think those options are going to have to come within the structure of the offense rather than after long scrambles where Allen holds the ball. It might be hard to teach an old dog new tricks, but at 30 years old, Allen still has some time to shift his game depending on the situation in front of him. While the off-schedule big play might be the thing that makes Allen superhuman, in Sunday’s matchup against Houston, Buffalo just needs Allen to be his normal, efficient self. As good as Allen has been when holding the ball for long periods of time, he has become one of the league’s deadliest quarterbacks when the ball comes out quickly, as well. When the ball comes out in under 2.5 seconds, Allen completes nearly 73% of his passes with a 4:1 touchdown to interception ratio. Sure, that total includes screens, swings, slants, and check-downs, but it keeps the chains moving and keeps the ball in Buffalo’s possession. In the last two meetings between Buffalo and Houston, it was the Texans defense forcing Buffalo into losses and errors, negative plays which ultimately prevented the Bills from scoring enough to win. On Sunday, Buffalo can flip the script, and the best way for their offense to do that would be to stick to the one authored by head coach and playcaller Joe Brady.…

title: Is Houston Texans rookie the Key(lan) to victory for Buffalo Bills?
summary: I’ve been doing opponent preview articles for years and you know which ones suck the most to write? Week 1 of any season. I can’t truly rely on stats from last year because there are so many variables that change between years. I could historical matchups, but… see above. Player previews are fun but we’re […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JUNE 04: Keylan Rutledge #66 of the Houston Texans takes the field during OTA Offseason Workouts at Houston Methodist Training Center on June 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve been doing opponent preview articles for years and you know which ones suck the most to write? Week 1 of any season. I can’t truly rely on stats from last year because there are so many variables that change between years. I could historical matchups, but… see above. Player previews are fun but we’re left with one of two choices. Option 1: Players who were on the team before where there’s plenty of footage. It’s not likely I’m sharing anything new and there’s always a chance of change between seasons. Option 2: Rookies where I can give authentic first impressions but it’s based on a very low data set. The title likely gave away I went with option 2 and that’s in large part thanks to some fantastic coverage by the rest of the Buffalo Rumblings team, breaking down hit recent history between the two teams and the ferocity of the Houston defense. Houston’s draft results this year though took me in a different direction. Keylan Rutledge So why Rutledge and why might he actually be the key to victory for Buffalo? If you read this by Chris Trapasso, or this by Rachel Auberger; you likely already know how ferocious the Houston defense has been and how they were the key to the game last year in beating Buffalo. However, if you read closely you likely also noticed that Buffalo’s offensive line was banged up as well as the skill players that day which shouldn’t be the case this time around. If you dive into the box score, you might also have noticed that despite the Texans barrage of sacks, the Bills put up a mostly average number of points and the defense held the Texans to a VERY average scoring output. Enter Keylan Rutledge. The rookie guard is the only member of the Texans’ 2026 draft class currently expected to start Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. If the health of Spencer Brown, Dion Dawkins, Keon Coleman, and Dalton Kincaid will help the offense out, they might be able to normalize the points scored. If the defense can exploit the rookie lineman, that might help knock a few points off the Houston side of the ledger too. So what are we looking at? pic.twitter.com/42qUcYsz29 — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) September 9, 2026 Play notes: I like Rutledge’s fundamentals here. The right hand grabs the shoulder (grab does not equal hold) and moves his feet well to keep the block established. Good awareness of the clutter in front of him prevents Rutledge from tripping, but the defender he’s blocking is able to free themselves relatively easily once they can accelerate. Rutledge’s mechanics fail him here and he goes upright. I point out the feet not because they’re horrible. It’s normal to see them come together and make a short base while moving. That is however, a big reason it’s so dangerous to get stood up like this. If you find yourself upright when your feet are tighter together it’s easy to get rocked. OK fine, I don’t love the feet either. His steps are choppy and at one point he’s pretty close to clicking his heels together. Not his best snap here. I note two things in the clip and both are related. He’s a little too eager on the block and gets ahead of his defender, which risks allowing your opponent to cut in and into the lane you’re, you know, trying to blocking from. Realizing that, Rutledge holds on and twists, and this should have been a holding call. This is a really good rep and shows why he’s the likely starter. Rutledge always finds work and starts off helping his tackle out. He’s quick to respond to the linebacker and gets a good piece of him. The only flaw is that there’s no latch on and the defender can scoot away to get back into the thick of things. What can you say here except that he’s a rookie? This is a good contrast to play 3. Rutledge’s body mechanics are like night and day. Again, rooke. Remember how I said Rutledge always finds work? Yeah, sometimes he shouldn’t. This should have been called as a block in the back and it wasn’t the only one. In summary, Rutledge is a lot of what you’d expect. There are certainly very good traits the Texans should be excited to see develop. They’re interspersed with moments of learning/vulnerability for now. If the Bills can take advantage of his mistakes, it could go a long way in flipping the script from last season.

title: Last time Buffalo Bills won in Houston, the Nintendo Wii had just been released
summary: Buffalo has lost six consecutive games in Houston, including four with Josh Allen behind center. Perhaps it is time to leave this streak in the past. The Buffalo Bills will open the 2026 season on the road against the Houston Texans, giving them an immediate opportunity to end one of the strangest and most stubborn […]
full_text: Buffalo has lost six consecutive games in Houston, including four with Josh Allen behind center. Perhaps it is time to leave this streak in the past. The Buffalo Bills will open the 2026 season on the road against the Houston Texans, giving them an immediate opportunity to end one of the strangest and most stubborn droughts on their schedule. The Bills have not won a game in Houston since November 19, 2006. Yes, 2006. The Nintendo Wii was released in North America that very same day. Twitter had launched publicly just a few months earlier. Hannah Montana had recently finished its first season on Disney Channel. Josh Allen was 10 years old. It has been a while. Remembering the Lee Evans game Both the Bills and the Texans entered that Week 11 matchup with a 3-6 record. Lee Evans made it memorable anyway. On Buffalo’s first possession, Losman found Evans for an 83-yard touchdown. On the Bills’ next possession, they did it again. Another Losman-to-Evans connection. Another 83-yard touchdown. Evans finished the afternoon with 11 receptions for 265 yards, breaking the Bills’ single game receiving record. That franchise record still stands today. Another thing froze in time from that day…It remains the last time Buffalo won in Houston. Six trips, six losses Since that day, the Bills have returned to Houston six times. They have lost all six: 2012: Texans 21, Bills 9 2014: Texans 23, Bills 17 2018: Texans 20, Bills 13 2019 Postseason: Texans 22, Bills 19 in overtime 2024: Texans 23, Bills 20 2025: Texans 23, Bills 19 The last four losses have all come during the Josh Allen era. The first was Allen’s rookie season in 2018, when he suffered an elbow injury and was replaced by Nathan Peterman. Peterman briefly gave Buffalo the lead with a touchdown pass before throwing two interceptions, including the go-ahead pick-six. Then came the 2019 Wild Card game, played in January 2020. Buffalo built a 16-0 lead before Houston came back in the second half and eventually won 22-19 in overtime. In 2024, Buffalo erased a 20-3 deficit only to lose on a Ka’imi Fairbairn 59-yard field goal as time expired. Allen completed just nine of his 30 pass attempts during the 23-20 loss. Buffalo returned to Houston in 2025 and lost again, this time 23-19. Allen was sacked eight times and intercepted twice as the Texans’ defense overwhelmed Buffalo’s offense. Allen is now 0-4 in Houston. Time to end it A season opener already comes with plenty of pressure, excitement and overreaction. This one also carries nearly 20 years of unwanted history. It is time to end the losing streak. The Bills simply need to leave Houston with a win.

title: Buffalo Bills HC Joe Brady taking page out of Sean Payton’s playbook
summary: In recent seasons, people following head coach Sean McDermott had grown accustomed to his podium demeanor. Truthfully, that evolved over time with him becoming far more relaxed as the seasons piled up. Yet still, McDermott kept specific things close to the vest, while talking at length about other aspects of the team, the roster, and […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Head coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills looks on after a weather delay during the first quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images In recent seasons, people following head coach Sean McDermott had grown accustomed to his podium demeanor. Truthfully, that evolved over time with him becoming far more relaxed as the seasons piled up. Yet still, McDermott kept specific things close to the vest, while talking at length about other aspects of the team, the roster, and football 101 in general. No one was entirely certain how Joe Brady would approach those same moments once he was named the new head coach. We’d seen him as generous with his time for reporters in the role as offensive coordinator, but that was a more dialed-in set of responsibilities he discussed. If Brady’s first media availability ahead of Week 1 at the Houston Texans is any indication, prepare yourself for a large serving of tight-lipped nothing. Brady was almost masterful in his ability to avoid answering almost every meaningful question reporters lobbed his way, right down to how he settled in on six captains. Brady was effusive in his praise for defensive back Sam Franklin Jr., tight end Dawson Knox, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. The locker room voted on the team’s captains this season, and it was clear to Brady why each and every guy made the cut. When discussing how things may look against the Texans based on prior matchups, Brady was quick to say that all he cares about is finding a way to win the game, by one point if needed, and in whatever way necessary. It’s clear that Brady won’t covet style points as a rookie head coach. His podium approach is a move expected out of head coaches, done in an effort to avoid giving opponents a leg up, or even just bulletin-board material. Yet Brady seemed poised beyond his years given his ability to deflect away from detail for the better part of 20 minutes in the hot seat. Take, for instance, Brady’s open and the decision to avoid discussing injuries on any level. Instead, Brady chose to lean on the injury report being shared later in the day. McDermott would often begin his pressers with injury updates, while also stating that getting into specifics about them was beyond his scope of knowledge. As for Brady? No comment, essentially. Maybe that changes in time. Or perhaps it’s his go-to, thanks to his roots. An exchange I had with Kyle Trimble ( @BangedUp Bills ) on social media revealed the following after I mentioned it appeared as though Brady talked “in circles at the podium today” — where the esteemed Dr. Trimble noted: “I have someone I speak with frequently about injuries mention that this was similar to what Sean Payton does.” I have someone I speak with frequently about injuries mention that this was similar to what Sean Payton does. Hopefully he’s a little more forthcoming in the future. — Banged Up Bills (@BangedUpBills) September 9, 2026 At that point it made complete sense. I suppose it’s smart to going in expecting less and enjoying when Brady shares more. That said, we know how ruthless Payton can be as a head coach. With Brady having spent years working alongside Payton, it’s easy to see how his podium demeanor may have been shaped by him. He may never show it, but it’s reasonable to expect that Brady is nervous ahead of Week 1, and he’s likely very intentional in making sure secrets stay hidden. Brady was asked about the emotions entering this season, this week, and even how he’s taken things from last season’s playoff exit. For Brady, it’s a new script, a new team, and a new novel whose past is firmly in the rearview mirror. Chapter one begins Sunday in Houston. title: Who’s under the most pressure with the Buffalo Bills in 2026?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills have entered a new era under new, first-time, head coach Joe Brady. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard also joins Brady as a first […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 and offensive coordinator Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills look on during warmups before the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills have entered a new era under new, first-time, head coach Joe Brady. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard also joins Brady as a first time DC in the NFL. that, alone, changes the dynamics at One Bills Drive, ramping up pressure in ways the organization hasn’t seen in nearly a decade. It’s reasonable to expect a regression in year one following Sean McDermott’s dismissal. As a head coach, he ran a tight and successful regular-season ship where playoffs were expected, essentially automatic each season. But it was time for a change, as co-owner Terry Pegula explained. At least in terms of coaching. Quarterback Josh Allen and newly promoted president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane remain, of course, which allows for consistency within some of the most important realms. Allen’s still searching for his first AFC Championship win and Super Bowl appearance (though surely more). It’s true that Beane’s track record isn’t spotless, and many of the roster moves made have played a key role in Buffalo’s premature end during Allen’s tenure. But expecting perfection out of anyone is foolish. That includes Allen, who — fair or otherwise — carries a mountain of weight related to the team’s past shortcomings. Beyond the team, there’s the fan base. It’s a dedicated group unlike any other in American professional sports, and perhaps the one group most deserving of a championship title. It also includes Beane, who cannot control injuries, on-field chemistry, and, ultimately, future ability. Beane simply finds what he and his team observe to be the best people at the right price for the Bills. But is he without fault when things go wrong? They say that hope springs eternal every fall, but it’s also true that beyond hope lies a massive amount of pressure for Beane, for Allen, for Brady, and even Leonhard. Many will point to the playoff losses and lay primary blame on the defense in almost every situation. Winning and losing is more nuanced than a simple explanation like that, but the point remains that Leonhard enters One Bills Drive with some a lot of pressure. If nothing else, the kind of pressure to improve a unit that disappeared too often in big moments under McDermott. Then there’s Brady, whose hire/promotion many balked at simply because it felt like an incomplete overhaul. But how do you part ways with the guy in charge of the league-leading rushing attack who also made the best wide receiver tar tar possible out of something akin to pothole filler? As such, Brady’s still here and the guy Pegula and Beane believe accomplishes what McDermott couldn’t do. You know, the guy they let go who stands behind only Marv Levy as the Bills’ all-time winningest coach. No pressure, Joe! Then there’s Allen, whose career shot clock is beginning to age. Everyone hopes Allen can play into his 40s, and at a high level with the Bills, but nothing is guaranteed. Buffalo has already wasted a lot of Allen’s window, which essentially amounts to the first half of his career in a perfect world. You may look at this season as Josh Allen 2.0, where he ascends to new heights of greatness. But all that’s left for Allen to claim is that AFCC win, a Super Bowl appearance/win, and a Super Bowl MVP award. He’s done everything else and resets the team’s record books almost every week of the season. You can imagine the pressure he feels to begin chipping away at that small NFL bucket list. To be clear, Allen, Beane, Brady, and Leonhard will all feel plenty of pressure this season. No one carries it alone. Yet who among the four is under the most pressure to succeed during the 2026 NFL season? Vote now! Plus, be sure to vote in our first confidence poll of the 2026 season!
