(Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Never in my wildest dreams did I think we would ever have the kind of whirlwind story about a practice-squad-level, developmental tight end as we have with Dae’Quan Wright . If you haven’t been following up on this potential “history” making process , let’s get you caught up real quick: The Cleveland Browns added Wright in mid-August after the Philadelphia Eagles waived him One of our loyal DBN readers was very excited about the Wright addition and shared about it in The Feed: Wright was mostly away from the Browns for the first week he was on the roster, then came news that he was part of a lawsuit attempting to return to college Cleveland then waived Wright , which opened up his chance to return to college Given his plan to return to school, no other NFL team claimed Wright Lawsuits went back and forth , including the SEC making it a rule that schools would face punishment if they rostered players who had declared for and/or signed a professional contract. Another lawsuit said that wasn’t acceptable. Then most of us got lost in the legalese of it all Wright and Zxavian Harris were not placed on LSU’s roster for their game against Clemson , despite reportedly enrolling and practicing The seemingly final update on Wright’s journey with LSU is that he will not have a journey with LSU: NEWS: LSU football is adding two players to the school’s roster, which will complete it at 105 players, per ESPN sources. This will lock LSU’s roster for the rest of the year, which will eliminate the program’s ability to add Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. pic.twitter.com/gLJj7AyvPw — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) September 9, 2026 So, Wright now has two options: Find another school with a scholarship and/or NIL money or seek to return to the NFL, likely on a practice squad. Wright is currently an NFL free agent after clearing waivers, free to sign with any team if they so desired. According to a lawyer (unsurprisingly given all the legal moves involved here) the two would-be LSU players are thinking about their legal options: In response to the news tonight of LSU finalizing its roster without Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, Louisiana plaintiffs attorney Ryan Downton says "players are reviewing legal options." https://t.co/d0Honkz0tb — Ross Dellenger (@RossDellenger) September 9, 2026 Given the Browns flexibility with Wright as he went through his process, including allowing him to be away from the team despite being on the roster, it is at least possible that GM Andrew Berry would look to bring the former Ole Miss tight end back into the fold. We know Berry isn’t afraid of making a few extra roster moves. Cleveland fans, on the other hand, may just be sick of hearing about a player who went undrafted and whose best statistical season included 39 receptions, 635 yards, and five touchdowns. Then again, an athletic 6’4”, 255-pound tight end is always an enticing option. Free-agent TE Dae’Quan Wright still is waiting to hear from the NFL about whether he is eligible to play this season. He never signed with LSU nor joined its roster, and his agent Drew Rosenhaus said multiple teams are now interested in signing him. The preseason is not an exact sign of what the offense will look like with all the most important personnel on the field. This will be the first opportunity to see how Monken plans to attack opposing defenses, how heavily the offense will rely on the run game, which personnel packages it uses most, and what the team’s overall identity will look like. Fans got used to Head Coach Kevin Stefanski’s game plan after several seasons, so this will certainly be a change of pace. When evaluating the run game in Week 1, it will be particularly telling to see how Quinshon Judkins is utilized and the kind of production he provides. The revamped offensive line will obviously be a big part of this discussion as well. Judkins could be gearing up for a really big season in Cleveland. With the questions surrounding Watson’s ability to run this offense, Judkins may have a really big game in week one. summary: Back in March, the Cleveland Browns and DE Myles Garrett agreed to a restructured contract that raised flags for everyone that a trade could happen after June 1st. full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 21: Myles Garrett #95 of the Cleveland Browns rushes against Dion Dawkins #73 of the Buffalo Bills during the fourth quarter at Huntington Bank Field on December 21, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Back in March, the Cleveland Browns and DE Myles Garrett agreed to a restructured contract that raised flags for everyone that a trade could happen after June 1st. Most downplayed that possibility as just talk, saying the move was actually just GM Andrew Berry doing what his mentor, Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman, does with big contracts. On top of that, the Browns put forth a proposal to allow draft picks five years out to be traded , only to find out the NFL had no interest in that idea , but that proposal hinted at the coming trade . We all know the rest of the story. Garrett is now with the Los Angeles Rams, preparing to play the first-ever NFL game in Australia. Garrett could have been preparing for the Buffalo Bills season opener if things had gone a little differently. According to Tom Pelissero’s new notebook on Substack , the Bills were the other suitor to call the Browns on the day the Rams trade was made: But sources say another team called Cleveland on the day the trade leaked: The Bills, who had checked in periodically on Garrett’s availability for the better part of two years. Pelissero noted that there was no chance for Buffalo to match Los Angeles’ offer because they did not have a Jared Vers e-level player to add to the deal. As noted by the Browns GM, Verse was the key to the deal from the Cleveland side . It is likely that the Bills would have offered a more pick-heavy package for Garrett, given that they didn’t have a top young player to add to the deal. Would you have rather have received three first-round picks and a second (an assumed package) from the Bills or the package the Browns got from the Rams for Garrett?

full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 14: The New York Giants line up against the Dallas Cowboys during an NFL football game at AT&T Field on September 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. More important matchup: Cowboys interior defensive line vs Giants offensive line, or Cowboys offensive tackles vs Giants pass rush? MIKE : The matchup that decides the game more is the Cowboys offensive tackles against the Giants pass rush. Dallas’ interior defensive line with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark should absolutely have chances to wreck the Giants’ protection, especially against a young quarterback, but the bigger swing factor is whether Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele can keep the edges clean for Dak Prescott. SEAN : The Giants have been trying to sell their pass rush as their chip to win games forever, and nobody has bought it even once. I’m not about to start now, and even if the Cowboys tackles have their struggles, I think the Dallas offense can have enough quick game options or push in the run game to get by. The Cowboys interior defensive line against the Giants offensive line gets the nod for me here, especially since it’s already a spot many Cowboys fans will be keeping a close eye on, having not seen Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, or Otito Ogbonnia in the preseason. Especially if this group can push the pocket and get pressure on Jaxson Dart, the Cowboys will be in control of this game. TOM : I’ll have to take the opposite position from Sean. As Mickey Spagnola said during a segment on a local radio show, the right tackle and swing tackle situations may be the biggest questions and most likely remaining holes for the team. I do have faith in Dak Prescott and the coaches to come up with a good game plan to attack the Giants, but I am not at all fond of the idea of our quarterback having to always be ducking and dodging. We all know what can happen if he, um, gets hit too much. Conversely, I’m going to put my faith in the middle of the D line. After all, one of the accepted truths is that it is almost impossible for them to be worse than they were last year. Only one way to go. Which young defender needs a big early statement, Caleb Downs, Shavon Revel, Jaishawn Barham, Donovan Ezeiruaku, or Malachi Lawrence? MIKE : The player who needs to make the biggest early statement is Shavon Revel. Caleb Downs, Jaishawn Barham, Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence all have exciting roles, but Revel’s spot feels the most important because cornerback is where one bad day can change the whole game plan. He is another year removed from his ACL injury now, so the excuses are over, and Dallas needs to know whether he can hold up outside without constant safety help. SEAN : I’ll go with the biggest tweener of this group, rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham. Everyone has been impressed by Barham’s combination of being stone cold and focused off the field, but determined like a heat seeking missile on it. How this translates to his first introduction into a regular season game, in primetime, against a rival that was a few plays away from sweeping the Cowboys a year ago, will be fun to watch, as well as just how much the Cowboys throw at him in these circumstances. TOM : Well, this time I have to concur with Sean. There is a certain cyclical nature to the NFL, and we seem to be returning to the time when the middle linebackers are the engines of the defense. I just think Barham (or, as a friend of mine calls him, Barhammer) will have a bigger impact on more plays than any of the others. And if DeMarvion Overshown is healthy and back to his old self, this could be a truly dynamic duo. After last year’s defensive collapse, what would count as real progress in Week 1? MIKE : Real progress in Week 1 would not have to mean a shutout or a dominant stat line; it would mean the defense looks organised, physical, and trustworthy again. After last year’s collapse, Dallas needs to show cleaner communication, fewer busted coverages, better tackling in space, and a front that can stop the run without needing constant safety help. SEAN : Just playing assignment football. Offenses are going to make plays at this level and move the ball, but giving up layup throws like the Cowboys did all the time in 2025 is just too much to overcome. Force Jaxson Dart to think from the pocket by squeezing the Giants run game, don’t give up layups and dunks on the back end, and to pick up with something that was a plus in the preseason – continue defending well in the red zone. TOM : Stop the run and don’t allow Jaxson Dart to convert long third downs. Last year’s edition of the defense failed at those two tasks so often last season. That has to stop, from the jump, for this team to fight its way back into the postseason. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? SEAN: Jake Ferguson TOM: Javonte Williams at the end of a long, workmanlike drive Dak Prescott passing yards, over/under 275.5? SEAN: Under TOM: Under, because I’m expecting them to lean on the ground game CeeDee Lamb receptions, over/under 7.5 SEAN: Over TOM: Under, for all the reasons I listed above Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark combined tackles for loss, over/under 3.5? SEAN: Under TOM: Under, but watch out for Barham Who has the bigger night, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, or Jake Ferguson? SEAN: George Pickens TOM: Pickens. I think he is a man on a mission Bigger defensive key, pressure Jaxson Dart or stop the run early? SEAN: Stop the run early, and often TOM: Definitely stop the run More important, Dallas starts fast on offense or avoids early defensive busts? SEAN: Avoid defensive busts that would instantly give the Giants, and their crowd, a boost of confidence. TOM: Did you watch last season? The defense has to do better, and I expect the offense to take a couple or three series to get their rhythm

title: Cowboys news: George Pickens thinks he and CeeDee Lamb are NFL’s best WR duo
summary: When it comes to wide receiver duos, George Pickens doesn’t feel any pair is better than himself and CeeDee Lamb, and he also had some strong words about the Giants secondary. Terence Steele has been put on notice when it comes to the right tackle spot, but he isn’t phased at all. Cowboys offensive coordinator […]
full_text: When it comes to wide receiver duos, George Pickens doesn’t feel any pair is better than himself and CeeDee Lamb, and he also had some strong words about the Giants secondary. Terence Steele has been put on notice when it comes to the right tackle spot, but he isn’t phased at all. Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams knows how to put a running game together, and now, he’s stepping up in the passing game. Quinnen Williams is a new captain in Dallas, and he’s ready to show why against the Giants by playing bully ball. George Pickens believes he and CeeDee Lamb are ‘the best’ WR duo in the NFL – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Dallas made a major move when they traded for George Pickens last season and paired him with CeeDee Lamb. The former feels they are the league’s best combination at wide receiver. In 2025, the Cowboys’ WR tandem of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 2,506 receiving yards, the second most from a WR duo in the NFL just 12 yards behind Detroit’s Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. On Sunday, Lamb and Pickens kick off their second full season playing next to one another. Pickens, who earned his first career Pro Bowl nod in his first season with Dallas last year, feels he and Lamb are the best duo in the league. “Yeah, we definitely think we’re the best,” Pickens said. “Now, for everybody’s brains and mindsets, I don’t know what they’re going to say. For us, yeah, we’re the best.” Cowboys’ Terence Steele hears criticism going into 2026. He won’t let it shake his confidence – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News Terence Steele has had his ups and downs with the Cowboys, and the team even added veteran Broderick Jones to compete with him at right tackle. However, he still feels he’s the guy for the job. Steele hasn’t let the criticism get to him. He’s remained focused, and it’s shown in practices — that gives the Cowboys confidence he’ll start. “Hasn’t changed at all from his work ethic, his mindset,” Schottenheimer said. “He’ll be the first guy to practice [Wednesday], I’m sure, going through his pre-practice routine. Again, all I can say is he’s done a really good job with the reps that we’ve had. And I was not surprised when I called him and informed him of what we were doing that he didn’t hesitate. He understands the business.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Not just a run game savant, Cowboys offensive coordinator now the full package – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Klayton Adams helped the Cowboys improved in the running game in 2025 as that’s been his area of expertise. During the offseason, he expanded his role to the passing game. This offseason, while Schottenheimer spent a large amount of time reconstructing the defensive side of the ball, Adams took on a bigger leadership role on the offensive side in evolving the unit. “He’s stepped right in and not missed a beat,” Foster said. “He’s taken on that leadership role, he’s a natural leader. His personality fits that room, and it’s cool to see him grow into that role from year one to year two.” Part of that responsibility has been developing a deeper understanding of what the Cowboys try to accomplish in the pass game. In having two weapons like CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, Adams has said that it has opened his offensive mind completely. Qunnien Williams: Captain patch ‘means a lot’, looks to set a physical tone vs. Giants – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys are set to take on their NFC East rivals on Sunday. Defensive tackle and captain, Quinnen Williams, wants to establish the physicality early and often. On paper, this stands to be a test of physicality for Williams and the new-look Cowboys’ defense coordinated by Christian Parker. Cam Skattebo, as one example, is a bruiser of a running back that seeks out contact on a regular basis, but that’s something that, to put it plainly, tickles Williams’ fancy. In other words, Williams can’t wait to unleash on an opposing jersey again, and for a Cowboys’ team he is ecstatic to be a part of. “I enjoy going against [physical players],” he said. “I enjoy playing football. and that’s football — that’s the mindset. Every single week is going to be physical. Every single week is going to be tough. So, like I said, just really focus on our personal craft. getting better and just ready to go to compete.” Cowboys vs Giants: 3 things to love about the matchup in Week 1 – Ben Grimaldi, Cowboys Wire Dallas has had New York’s number over the last decade. As they set to play in the season opener, there’s several things that play in the Cowboys favor. Dak Prescott dominates By now, it should be well-known on both sides just how dominant Prescott has been against the Giants. The record of 14-3 speaks for itself, but Prescott hasn’t lost in a game where he’s started and finished against New York since his rookie year, when he lost both matchups. Since the 2016 season, the Cowboys and Prescott are 14-1 against the Giants, and the lone loss was in last year’s season finale when Prescott only played in the first half and the Cowboys weren’t playing to win. George Pickens respectfully but also brutally slams key Giants player with qoute that adds fuel to Week 1 fire – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Cornerback Greg Newsome said that the Giants have the best cornerback room in the NFL. George Pickens disagrees, and he said so in a straightforward and direct way. Pickens peacefully roasts Giants secondary “That’s definitely how he should feel,” Pickens said of Newsome’s comments via The Athletic’s Jon Machota. “Now, how we should feel, I’d definitely say a completely different story. That’s cool that he thinks that. He should definitely feel like that, but I feel like we’re definitely not thinking the same thing.” Daily discussion question: What did you most enjoy about Seahawks/Patriots?

title: NFL executives high on Brian Schottenheimer, Caleb Downs for 2026
summary: With the latest NFL season kicking off there are people all over the sports world offering their Super Bowl LXI predictions. Perhaps you believe the Dallas Cowboys will wind up there, it is okay to believe if you want, but obviously a lot has to happen on the way to two teams winding up in […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Caleb Downs #13 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the first quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the latest NFL season kicking off there are people all over the sports world offering their Super Bowl LXI predictions. Perhaps you believe the Dallas Cowboys will wind up there, it is okay to believe if you want, but obviously a lot has to happen on the way to two teams winding up in Los Angeles. ESPN curated the opinions of league executives and scout s to figure out some of that in between, and they are very high on two members of the Cowboys picking individual honors: Caleb Downs and Brian Schottenheimer. Defensive Rookie of the Year: Caleb Downs, Dallas Cowboys The Cowboys have big plans for Downs, who instantly becomes one of Dallas’ most versatile players. When I asked head coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp where Downs is best served on the field, he said “anywhere,” then pointed out that he can cover star receiver CeeDee Lamb up the seam. The Cowboys will play Downs primarily in the slot, where he can disrupt in the open field. “He will play in the middle of the defense, so he will probably have some ball production and high tackle numbers,” an AFC executive said. “And if he helps turn around Dallas’ defense, he’ll be looked at as a catalyst.” The last defensive back to win DROY was Sauce Gardner in 2022, when he recorded two interceptions and 20 pass deflections. Ball production is a must to win this award. Also receiving votes: Rueben Bain Jr. (Tampa Bay Buccaneers), Mansoor Delane (Kansas City Chiefs), R Mason Thomas (Chiefs), David Bailey (New York Jets) … Coach of the Year: Brian Schottenheimer, Dallas Cowboys This race featured no runaway favorite. Last year’s prediction was Jim Harbaugh, who could be well-positioned to actually win it this year. But in a tight race, let’s go with a bit of a wild card: Schottenheimer, who has acquitted himself well in Dallas behind the scenes and has most of what he needs to win. “I think Dak [Prescott] will have a big year; we know they can score; and the defense should be much improved,” an NFC scout said. “If they stay healthy, they have a good chance to win the NFC East.” Also receiving votes: Dan Campbell (Detroit Lions), Jim Harbaugh (Los Angeles Chargers), Sean McVay (Los Angeles Rams), Kellen Moore (New Orleans Saints), Jesse Minter (Baltimore Ravens) Let’s start with Caleb Downs. It is fully possible that he could wind up as Defensive Rookie of the Year. He would have to have some sort of statistical data point working to his name as these awards are often low-hanging fruit in that way, and in that sense he is up against the pass rushers who could pick up sack numbers. But given that these awards are often narrative-driven, he could wind up as representing the Cowboys defense to a degree. If the group does have a bit of a turn around then Downs could be seen as a focal point within it and get some hardware as a result. The same sort of conversation is applicable to Schottenheimer. Coach of the Year is often “coach who had an impressive season that we weren’t exactly expecting” and not necessarily a mark of who the best coach in the NFL really is, all due respect to Schotty or whoever. If the Cowboys are a playoff team, maybe even a division winner, then he is the frontman for one of the bigger stories across the league at large. This was sort of the case when Jason Garrett won the award a decade ago. The Cowboys were the top seed in the NFC and were so after winning only four games the year prior. That was the season where Dak Prescott won Offensive Rookie of the Year and Ezekiel Elliott won the rushing title. Some fans believe the aforementioned Prescott also has a chance at MVP this year. As noted, the narrative aspect of these things would really require something special for the team at large as that award is often handed out to the quarterback on the best team, so to speak. What other awards can you see for the Cowboys in 2026?

title: 2026 Week 1 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: We’re so back! And so are you, no doubt delirious with excitement about the start of the 2026 NFL season. As we do annually here at Blogging The Boys, we’ll be helping you prepare for each week with the complete lineup of games and which outcomes you should be rooting for as a Dallas Cowboys […]
full_text: We’re so back! And so are you, no doubt delirious with excitement about the start of the 2026 NFL season. As we do annually here at Blogging The Boys, we’ll be helping you prepare for each week with the complete lineup of games and which outcomes you should be rooting for as a Dallas Cowboys fan. The further along we get into the season, the clearer certain scenarios and impacts from each game will be. But even in Week 1, there are teams we expect to threaten Dallas’ ultimate goals more than others. Some of them will fall flat, and some surprising contenders will emerge. But for now, here’s our take on Week 1 and who can most help the Cowboys by winning (or losing). Obviously, we’re all rooting for Dallas to start the season right with a win over the division-rival Giants. What else would help us get this season off to a good start? NFC East teams Commanders d. Eagles Predictions on who will win the NFC East still come down to Philadelphia or Dallas for most, with the Commanders and Giants well behind them. There’s a lot of angst in Washington right now over some ugly preseason ball, with long-term concerns about their offensive line and defense. So if they go hang a home loss on Philly, that would be a huge gift to the Cowboys. NFC vs. NFC 49ers d. Rams Saints d. Lions Panthers d. Bears Vikings d. Packers These four games all come down to the same thing: which teams are more likely to be in the playoff hunt? Granted, those preseason projections can quickly go out the window. But each of these desired winners is considered an NFC underdog compared to Los Angeles, Detroit, Chicago, and Green Bay. Think of the full course of a season like a road being paved in front of the Cowboys. The less 13 and 12-win teams are out there clogging up the top seeds and playoff spots, the smoother and more open that road becomes for Dallas. We’ve seen the years where winning the NFC East was the only path to the postseason, because too many teams with high win totals were in the wild cards. Naturally, one of those four assumed contenders will probably be thinking about 2027 sooner than we expect. But for now, until we know more about who these teams really are this season, we’re going with the chalk. NFC vs. AFC Patriots d. Seahawks Bengals d. Bucs Falcons d. Steelers Chargers d. Cardinals Generally, we’re going to favor AFC teams to win as they don’t affect the Cowboys’ playoff chances. But sometimes a game comes around, like Atlanta-Pittsburgh, where other factors are at work. Dallas owns the Steelers’ fourth-round pick in 2027 as part of the recent Broderick Jones trade. And the Falcons may be in the NFC, but they’re generally considered one of the least likely teams to contend. We’re almost always going to take a Steelers loss this season, unless they’re playing against a legitimate NFC threat. Right now, Atlanta doesn’t qualify. The rest of the Week 1 games are all AFC vs. AFC matchups with no tangible implications for the Cowboys. Pittsburgh is the only team that owes us a draft pick next year. We’ll likely have more skin in those games at various points in the season, but for now they’re just random contests that will help shape the eventual AFC Champion. For now, we can root for the Cowboys to be among the 1-0 teams next Tuesday, and for other perceived NFC contenders to have less enjoyable starts to their seasons.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 4
summary: It is Day 4 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Butch Johnson (86) dives to make a fingertip catch in the end zone for a 45-yard touchdown reception during the 3rd quarter of the Cowboys 27-10 victory over the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII on January 15, 1978 at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sylvia Allen/Getty Images) *** Local Caption *** It is Day 4 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Here we are on Day 4 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the defensive masterpiece that delivered the second championship in Cowboys history. Dallas forced eight Denver turnovers, controlled the game from the opening quarter and finished its dominant 1977 season by beating the Broncos in Super Bowl XII. Sunday, January 15, 1978 Louisiana Superdome, New Orleans, Louisiana Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Denver Broncos 10 Denver quarterback Craig Morton had previously played for Dallas and started Super Bowl V for the Cowboys. Now he was trying to win a championship against his former team. Instead, the Doomsday Defense made his return miserable, constantly applying pressure and forcing him into one of the toughest performances of his career. Dallas’ defense created the opening touchdown. Randy Hughes intercepted Morton and returned the ball to the Denver 25-yard line. Five plays later, rookie Tony Dorsett scored from three yards out to give the Cowboys a 7-0 lead. Another interception, this time by Aaron Kyle, helped set up Efren Herrera’s 35-yard field goal and made it 10-0 before the opening quarter had finished. The Broncos simply could not protect the football. Morton was intercepted four times during the first half, while Denver also lost three fumbles. Dallas did not take full advantage of every opportunity, missing several field goals and giving the ball away itself, but Herrera eventually connected from 43 yards to send the Cowboys into halftime leading 13-0. Denver had committed seven turnovers before scoring a single point. Denver finally showed some life after halftime. Morton moved the Broncos into Dallas territory and Jim Turner kicked a 47-yard field goal to reduce the deficit to 13-3. For the first time all evening, Denver had a little momentum. Staubach immediately helped take it away. Facing third-and-10, he launched a deep pass toward Butch Johnson, who made a spectacular diving catch in the end zone for a 45-yard touchdown. The play remains one of the most memorable catches in Cowboys Super Bowl history and pushed Dallas comfortably ahead 20-3. Denver responded after Rick Upchurch returned the following kickoff 67 yards. Morton was eventually replaced by Norris Weese, who guided the Broncos to their only touchdown of the game when Rob Lytle scored from one yard out. The Dallas lead was suddenly down to 20-10, but the comeback never went any further. Tom Landry finished the game with one of his trademark creative calls. In the fourth quarter, fullback Robert Newhouse took a pitch as if he were running outside, stopped and threw downfield to Golden Richards. Richards caught the ball for a 29-yard touchdown, giving Dallas a 27-10 advantage and effectively ending the contest. It was Newhouse’s first pass attempt since 1975. The defense remained the story from beginning to end. Dallas intercepted four passes and recovered four Denver fumbles. Morton completed just four of 15 passes for 39 yards with four interceptions before being replaced. The Broncos finished with only 156 net yards of offense as the Cowboys completely controlled the biggest game of the season. Randy White and Harvey Martin were rewarded by becoming the first defensive teammates to share Super Bowl MVP honors. White recorded six tackles, while Martin and the rest of the defensive front repeatedly disrupted Denver’s offense. Their shared award perfectly represented a championship won primarily through defensive dominance rather than one individual offensive performance. This game belongs near the very top of the countdown because it showed Dallas at its most complete. The 1977 Cowboys had opened the season with eight consecutive victories, finished 12-2 and then defeated Chicago and Minnesota by a combined 76-13 in the NFC playoffs. Super Bowl XII completed that run with another controlled performance and gave Tom Landry his second championship. #Cowboys vs #Broncos 1978 Super Bowl XII Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Denver Broncos 10 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/YcqKjghhAg — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 9, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Morton had thrown only eight interceptions during the entire 1977 regular season, then threw four against Dallas in Super Bowl XII. Countdown to kickoff 1 00 , 99 , 98 , 97 , 96 , 95 , 94 , 93 , 92 , 91 , 90 , 89 , 88 , 87 , 86 , 85 , 84 , 83 , 82 , 81 , 80 , 79 , 78 , 77 , 76 , 75 , 74 , 73 , 72 , 71 , 70 , 69 , 68 , 67 , 66 , 65 , 64 , 63 , 62 , 61 , 60 , 59 , 58, 57, 56, 55 , 54 , 53 , 52, 51 , 50 , 49 , 48 , 47 , 46 , 45 , 44 , 43 , 42 , 41 , 40 , 39 , 38 , 37 , 36 , 35 , 34 , 33 , 32, 31 , 30 , 29 , 28 , 27 , 26, 25, 24 , 23 , 22 , 21 , 20 , 19 , 18 , 17 , 16 , 15 , 14 , 13 , 12, 11, 10 , 9 , 8 , 7, 6 , 5

title: Cowboys have plenty working in their favor against the Giants
summary: A new season brings new expectations in Dallas, and with it comes our first Reasons To Be Positive article of 2026. Each week, we are going to forget about the reasons the Cowboys could lose and focus completely on why they can win. Let this be the series that brings you unadulterated optimism for the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys stiff arms Rico Payton #36 of the New York Giants during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images A new season brings new expectations in Dallas, and with it comes our first Reasons To Be Positive article of 2026. Each week, we are going to forget about the reasons the Cowboys could lose and focus completely on why they can win. Let this be the series that brings you unadulterated optimism for the upcoming matchup. The Cowboys begin their season under the lights on Sunday Night Football , travelling to MetLife Stadium to face the New York Giants. New York may have homefield advantage, but history says this is one of the better opening-week matchups Dallas could have been given. Few teams have been controlled by the Cowboys quite like the Giants in recent years. Dallas has won 16 of the last 18 meetings between these teams and leads the all-time series 78-48-2. Even more encouraging is what happens when these two teams meet in Week 1. This will be the 13th time Dallas has opened a season against New York, and the Cowboys are an incredible 11-2 in those games. #Cowboys vs #Giants 2025 Week 2 The @Brandon_Aubrey Double Pressure Kick Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 40, New York Giants 37 (OT) #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/nmzRCsB239 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 21, 2026 MetLife Stadium has hardly been a place Dallas should fear either. Since the beginning of the 2017 season, the Cowboys have played nine road games against the Giants and won seven of them. New York finally stopped that run in last season’s finale, but Dallas has still owned this matchup for nearly a decade. The last time Prescott played a full game against this defense provides a much better example of why Cowboys fans should feel confident. Dallas beat New York 40-37 in Week 2 last year as Prescott completed 73% of his passes for 361 yards and two touchdowns. The Cowboys produced 478 total yards, went a perfect three-for-three in the red zone, and Javonte Williams added 97 rushing yards with a touchdown. CeeDee Lamb finished with 113 receiving yards, while George Pickens and Jake Ferguson were heavily involved as well. This was all happening while the defense was in disarray and producing an extremely lackluster season. #Cowboys Dak Prescott being honest with the offense coming out of the retreat in Utah. “Let’s just keep sticking together, man; let’s keep pushing. We got a good team, we got a good f***ing group right here.” All confidence from the face of the franchise. (🎥: @_CeeDeeThree on… pic.twitter.com/50fnxD3I0M — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) September 1, 2026 Dallas finished last season second in the NFL in total offense and second in passing yards, while its 27 points per game ranked seventh. Prescott threw for 4,552 yards, 30 touchdowns and only 10 interceptions, finishing with a 99.5 passer rating. It means New York begins the year having to defend one of the NFL’s most productive passing attacks rather than an offense still trying to find its identity. The biggest matchup to get excited about, though, may be on the ground. New York’s run defense was one of the worst in football last season. The Giants allowed 2,470 rushing yards, the second-most in the NFL, while opponents averaged 5.3 yards per carry, which ranked dead last. They also surrendered 21 rushing touchdowns. New York has changed coaches and personnel, so the defense will certainly look different, but that weakness gives Dallas a very obvious place to test them immediately. That is excellent news for Williams. His first year in Dallas produced 1,201 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns at 4.8 yards per carry. He isn’t entering 2026 trying to prove whether he can handle the RB1 job anymore. He already did that. If the Cowboys offensive line can get movement against a Giants defense that was routinely pushed around on the ground last year, Williams gives Dallas a way to control the game and take pressure away from Prescott. Javonte Williams is Dallas' bell-cow back, with weekly practice management prioritized over limiting his game-day carries. Brian Schottenheimer: “Javonte is our bell cow. The other guys are certainly gonna play, but Javonte is one of those guys that the stronger he gets is based… pic.twitter.com/Af3D7ogK4e — MicNuggets (@micnuggetsnfl) September 7, 2026 There are reasons for optimism on the other side of the ball as well. The Cowboys defense was the biggest problem on the team last season, so Dallas attacked that unit aggressively. Christian Parker has taken over as defensive coordinator, while the group now includes major additions such as Rashan Gary, Jalen Thompson, P.J. Locke and rookie safety Caleb Downs alongside Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. DaRon Bland and Shavon Revel have also entered camp healthy after Dallas spent much of last season dealing with problems in the secondary. Great view of Caleb Downs’ first interception of Cowboys training camp (Video: jman46401 on TikTok) pic.twitter.com/ZoPeyHNszq — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 26, 2026 The biggest weapon in that Giants offense also isn’t guaranteed to enter Week 1 at full strength. Malik Nabers tore his ACL and suffered meniscus damage last September. John Harbaugh has made it clear that New York hopes Nabers will be ready for Dallas, but his Week 1 status still depends on medical clearance and progressing back to full-speed football. Even if he plays, asking a receiver to immediately look like his old self after such a serious knee injury is a different situation from having a fully healthy Nabers throughout camp. John Harbaugh said that Malik Nabers was in there for “most of the team reps” during practice. The workload plan for Nabers varies “day to day.” https://t.co/HVC4KXiW9H — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) September 1, 2026 The Cowboys have every reason to believe they can walk into MetLife Stadium, spoil the beginning of the John Harbaugh era and fly home 1-0.

title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: Indianapolis Colts
summary: We are down to our last two opponent previews for the Dallas Cowboys 2026 schedule, and they both reside in the AFC South. It’s time now to look at the Indianapolis Colts, who come into 2026 having not made the playoffs since 2020. The pressure is on for both the Colts and Cowboys to get […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - NOVEMBER 30: Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren (84) celebrates his touchdown during and NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts on November 30, 2025 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are down to our last two opponent previews for the Dallas Cowboys 2026 schedule, and they both reside in the AFC South. It’s time now to look at the Indianapolis Colts, who come into 2026 having not made the playoffs since 2020. The pressure is on for both the Colts and Cowboys to get back to the playoffs this year. The Colts have not had the same quarterback start the majority of their games for two consecutive seasons since 2013-14 with Andrew Luck, but will have a chance to do so in 2026 after Daniel Jones started 13 games a year ago. Now, the question is whether or not the Colts will get the version of Jones that got them off to a 8-2 start last season, or the one that lost his next three starts after this before getting injured, leading to the losing streak lasting through the regular season for seven games total. Shane Steichen’s team made a commitment to Jones as their starter with a new contract this offseason, so let’s look now at what else they’ve done to keep things going in a positive direction on both sides of the ball. Colts Key Free Agent Signings/Departures * SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY: DE Michael Clemons LB Akeem Davis-Gaither QB Daniel Jones (Re-signed) DE Arden Key DT Derrick Nnandi WR Keenan Allen SAF Jonathan Owens CB Cam Taylor-Britt TE Mo Alie-Cox (Re-signed) WR Alec Pierce (Re-signed) DT Jerry Tillery SAF Juanyeh Thomas WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine WR Laquon Treadwell (Re-signed) DT Colby Woolen * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY DE Kwity Paye OL Braden Smith SAF Nick Cross DL Neville Gallimore RB Ameer Abdullah LB Buddy Johnson The Cowboys may take the cake when it comes to offensive continuity they’ve retained from 2025 going into the start of this new season, but the Colts are not far behind. The duo of Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor in the backfield is the starting point, but with the exception of trading away Michael Pittman Jr. at wide receiver, the Colts also have returning targets in TE Tyler Warren, WR Josh Downs, and Alec Pierce. The constant QB shuffle has taken former first-round pick Quenton Nelson out of the mainstream conversation for best interior linemen in football, but Taylor matching a career high with 18 touchdowns in 2025 helped revive this, and now Nelson is joined by other experienced players like Bernhard Raimann and Matt Gonclaves. The Cowboys will be no strangers to the style of play the Colts desire under Jones, looking to control the clock, win in the RPO game, and capitalize on field position, much like the best versions of the New York Giants when Jones was the starter there. The Colts are also looking more dangerous on defense as well though, going into year two of having Sauce Gardner at CB who was acquired in a midseason trade last year, Charvarius Ward at the other cornerback spot, loads of new faces at linebacker, and Deforest Buckner and Laiatu Latu going into year two as a formidable interior duo. Indy is also well positioned to take advantage of the boom in tight end usage the league is seeing right now, with last year’s first-round pick Tyler Warren having a strong start to his career as a rookie. The sky is the limit for his potential in the pass game if Jones and the offensive line are healthy and playing in sync this season. This division is no stranger to having teams win games with their defense, something the Titans leaned into by hiring Robert Saleh as head coach this offseason, the Texans are already the leaders of, and now the Colts will be looking to inch closer to if they want to avoid another late season collapse, paired with a strong run game to be an overall tougher outfit in ‘26. Colts 2026 Draft Class Round 2, Pick 21 (53 Overall): LB CJ Allen Round 3, Pick 14 (78 Overall): SAF A.J. Haulcy Round 4, Pick 13 (113 Overall): G Jalen Farmer Round 4, Pick 35 (135 Overall): LB Bryce Boettcher Round 5, Pick 16 (156 Overall): DE George Gumbs Jr. Round 6, Pick 33 (214 Overall): DE Caden Curry Round 7, Pick 21 (237 Overall): RB Seth McGowan Round 7, Pick 38 (254 Overall): WR Deion Burks When it comes to this year’s matchup against the Cowboys, linebacker may be the position to watch the most for both teams when it comes to how much of a makeover both sides have gone through on the second level of their defenses. The Colts brought in Akeem Davis-Gaither in free agency and drafted CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher to remake this group, getting more of a run defender in Allen and a coverage player in Boettcher. This has been a front seven not generally known for being the most physical or intimidating in any recent season, and without the benefit of a first-round pick the Colts did as good of a job as they could adding bodies to change this narrative. George Gumbs Jr. is a very interesting pick in the fifth round, seen as one of the rawest prospects in this class but with high potential for any team that can help him take his game to the next level. The Colts have missed on athletic freaks like this before on defense, but this group has enough experience and talent now to at least be middle of the pack and allow their best overall player in Taylor to have his say in games out of the backfield. 2026 will be year two of the Lou Anarumo defensive system in Indianapolis, coming over from the Bengals where at the end of his tenure he was the face of a Cincy defense that couldn’t stop a cold, but previously had success implementing defenses that could support a high-octane offense like the Bengals. Colts 2026 Coaching Staff * New to staff this season: Defensive Line Marion Hobby Head coach Shane Steichen will go into year four with the same offensive coordinator he started with in Jim Bob Cooter, and like we said a second year for Anarumo as DC. The belief the Colts front office has shown in this coaching staff for some extended period of time is admirable, but the clock is now ticking further on when it will yield better results. Only having one new coach on this list is remarkable, and when the Colts put this to the test against the Cowboys, they’ll be attacking a defense that is the polar opposite from a coaching perspective in Dallas – with lots of new faces. While Cowboys fans are in agreement that all of these changes are for the better, the Colts will be a good test of all aspects of this defense when it comes to interior run, big play potential at RB, and the dual-threat game with Jones. The Cowboys get this game as part of a two-game stretch they will likely need to take advantage of, at home for the Cardinals and then at the Colts. Similarly for the Colts, they come into this game off a divisional test at the Jaguars, then stay home to face the Dolphins, followed by another divisional game at the Texans. Whichever team comes out on top in this Sunday early window game will feel much better at this midpoint junction of the season. Previous 2026 Opponent Previews: Philadelphia Eagles New York Giants Seattle Seahawks Arizona Cardinals Baltimore Ravens Washington Commanders Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans

title: Cowboys discussion: Why optimism feels warranted before Week 1
summary: The long drought is over! Sunday night, the Dallas Cowboys start their 2026 NFL campaign against the New York Giants and their shiny new coach John Harbaugh. It is that magical time when almost every fan base in the NFL (sorry, Jets and Browns) are filled with hope for the revamped rosters.  Of course, all […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants in action during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The New York Giants won 34-17. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images The long drought is over! Sunday night, the Dallas Cowboys start their 2026 NFL campaign against the New York Giants and their shiny new coach John Harbaugh. It is that magical time when almost every fan base in the NFL (sorry, Jets and Browns) are filled with hope for the revamped rosters. Of course, all but one fan base will see their season end without a shiny new Lombardi Trophy to take home. And it has been a long, long time since Dallas fans had a championship to celebrate. But this year has seen a real uptick in optimism about the Cowboys’ chances. Is it justified, however? Our Sean Martin and Tom Ryle take a look at things. TOM : One thing I believe is a truism in the NFL: We don’t know as much as we think we do about the teams. Any team. At this time last year almost no one was looking for Sam Darnold to lead the Seattle Seahawks back to the promised land. Most of the projections are based more on what each team was last year than what they are now. There are just so many changes and variables. Paradoxically, that is one reason I think there are legitimate grounds for optimism about Dallas. The offense is largely the same as last year, and they were very, very good. The 2025 season was a disappointment because the defense was historically bad. The one major move from last year was the controversial Micah Parsons trade, which left a horrible taste in our mouths (although it seems to be looking like a lot better move as the full picture has come into focus.) Over the past seven months, we have seen a major rebuild of the D, starting with new coordinator Christian Parker. And from almost any angle you look at it, the defense almost has to be better. That’s how terrible they were. If they can just be close to middle of the pack, this year should see Dallas back in the playoffs. SEAN: First of all, let me just say as we get both this season and this series started how cool it is to be working with a BTB legend in Tom, and with that said, bring on the season! I am with the fanbase on the optimism, and after months of offseason writing about how the front office has been moving differently, it is fun to flip this around and talk about how it’s felt different as fans too. The biggest difference for me has been not having to artificially hype up players that other team’s fanbases have never heard of, then inevitably asking what were we all thinking just a few games into the season. The Cowboys depth chart is now littered with players with at least some level of proven production you can actually point to in making a case for them, at very least on special teams where they’ll need improvements anyway. The one area I’ll disagree with Tom here is that I’m tired of the “be great on offense, and just average on defense” narrative as good enough for the Cowboys to achieve their goals. We’ve seen plenty of such teams in very recent memory and all of them have fallen way short of breaking the drought. It’s time to hold this defense to a higher standard, and to me that starts with the interior defensive line which is where a lot of my focus will be on Sunday night. TOM: Why, thank you for calling me a legend, which Webster’s defines as meaning “what, he’s still alive?” You also touched on something that I think has been under reported, the different feel to the front office moves. (Although I think OCC, a legit legend, is on the story , and our newest writer Dyllan Rivers also took note in his first article .) The new acquisitions seem better fits. More impressive in my view is how they have finally gotten over the sunk cost fallacy and been much more willing to move on from recent draft picks. As for the defense, I’m really hoping they start out in that mid range but start nudging into top 10 territory soon. We just might have to have a little patience. Meanwhile, we really have to hope they can manage the Tyler Smith injury well. That may be the real measure of the staff’s evolution. SEAN: There’s no denying the Smith injury took a fair amount of wind out of the sails of optimism for this game and the start to the season. We’ve been saying all summer that interior offensive line depth is worrisome outside of T.J. Bass, but one injury is something they can withstand for now. Bass is the most experienced and trustworthy of the backups. We’ve waited patiently to see the Cowboys throw the ball downfield with their full cast of stars out there offensively, and with Bass being even better in pass pro than he is as a run game mauler, I don’t expect those things to completely fall off the game plan. That makes limiting these types of big plays on defense the focus, which like you said almost has to improve by default, and with time could be even more of a strength. TOM: I do think we agree that our optimism has some sound reasons behind it. Now we see how it plays out!

title: How the Broncos can defeat the Chiefs on Monday Night Football
summary: After an impressive 14-win season in 2025, the Denver Broncos are the reigning AFC West champions. They dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs from that spot, who endured their worst season in a decade last year. The Broncos’ quest at a second straight AFC West title and subsequent Super Bowl chase begins on Monday Night Football […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) flexes and yells to celebrate a 9-yard touchdown run in the third quarter of a Christmas Day NFL game between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs on December 25, 2025 at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After an impressive 14-win season in 2025, the Denver Broncos are the reigning AFC West champions. They dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs from that spot, who endured their worst season in a decade last year. The Broncos’ quest at a second straight AFC West title and subsequent Super Bowl chase begins on Monday Night Football at Arrowhead Stadium. The Broncos’ offense has to start off fast There are a lot of reasons to be optimistic about the Broncos in 2026. Nevertheless, one order of business must be achieved. That’s going from a middle-of-the-pack offense to a Top 10-unit in the National Football League. This season will be Bo Nix’s third year leading the offense and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb’s first season calling plays for Denver. I’m bullish on what the two can accomplish and believe Nix is poised for his best year of his career. However, the Broncos must start off fast and forego their early seasons woes that have plagued the group’s efficiency and productivity in the first part of the past two seasons. On the road against the Chiefs, they face a formidable defense coached by Steve Spagnuolo. He does a great job dialing up pressure and confusing opposing quarterbacks. Kansas City used a lot of draft selections to bolster that side of the ball and ended up revamping a good portion of their secondary. With the addition of Jaylen Waddle, the Broncos have a premier playmaker in the mix that was absent from last year’s gridiron campaign. Getting Waddle, the ball and creating some explosive plays through the air will be mission critical to achieve victory. I’m hopeful Denver will be able to get him involved to boost their aerial attack and dial up some big plays against a revamped Chiefs secondary. The Broncos’ defense has to find a way to rattle Patrick Mahomes; slow down Kenneth Walker III Even with Patrick Mahomes coming off a down year that ended prematurely due to an ACL tear, the Broncos defense can’t underestimate his top-notch playmaking ability. In order to defeat the Chiefs, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have to dial up the heat on Mahomes and force him into some bad decisions. Left tackle Josh Simmons may be sidelined from the game due to injury. If that happens, at least one of the Chiefs’ starting tackle spots will be manned by an undrafted rookie free agent. That may be just enough of an opportunity for Nik Bonitto and the rest of Denver’s front seven to feast and cause some havoc. Additionally, the Broncos have to find a way to slow down running back Kenneth Walker III. He is coming off a great season and was the Seattle Seahawks’ Super Bowl MVP last year. Setting the tempo and pace of the game is important, and finding a way to shut down Andy Reid’s ground game plans will be essential to earn a Week 1 win. Play disciplined football and win the turnover battle There were two major issues that were prevalent last year with the Broncos. They were the fourth most penalized team in football and ranked toward the bottom of the league in forcing turnovers. Knowing that, it’s quite impressive they managed to reel off 14 wins and advance to the AFC Championship Game. This season, things have to be different on both fronts. Last year, too many drives on offense stalled or were extended for the opposition with penalties and miscues. If they can cut down on those, the Broncos should be even tougher to defeat in ‘26. The Chiefs are already a tough opponent as is, they can’t make things harder for themselves by shooting themselves in the foot. In ‘25, the Broncos sported a -4 turnover differential. They were one of only a handful of teams to make the playoffs being in the negative. All offseason long, the coaching staff and players emphasized how essential it will be to turn the tides in that regard. Late last season and in the AFC Divisional Playoff victory over the Bills, we saw significant improvement with that. Hopefully, they can find a way to no What do you think, Broncos Country? What things do you believe Denver has to do to come out of Kansas City with a Week 1 victory? Sound off in the comments section and let me know your thoughts.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Sean Payton offers thoughts on what makes the Chiefs defense tough
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. We are just five days away from the Denver Broncos kicking off their regular season against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s a perfect matchup to cap off an intriguing set of Week 1 games across the National Football League. Last night, the NFL’s season began with the Seattle […]
full_text: Good morning, Broncos Country. We are just five days away from the Denver Broncos kicking off their regular season against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s a perfect matchup to cap off an intriguing set of Week 1 games across the National Football League. Last night, the NFL’s season began with the Seattle Seahawks embarking on a comeback victory against the New England Patriots. Drake Maye threw three interceptions and struggled mightily against the Seahawks’ defense. Former Broncos quarterback Drew Lock took the reins early on replacing Sam Darnold [after injury] and helped Seattle earn their first victory of the year. Last night just goes to show how important a great defense can be—especially when your offense wasn’t hitting their stride. In order for the Broncos to achieve a key win on the road in Arrowhead, they’re going to have to perform well against a Chiefs defense that has been one of the best in the NFL the past few seasons. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton offered his thoughts on what makes Kansas City’s defense tough to go up against. “They mix a lot of looks up. The second game, we got a little bit more coverage than we had seen in maybe the game prior or the years prior. It all depends on what they’re trying to take away, but they’re well coached, they tackle well. They can create negative plays in both the run and passing game because of the pressure looks that you get,” stated Payton. “A lot of it is the personnel you’re in and then what they’re trying to take away. They do a good job of keeping the lid on the coverage. They’re near the top of the league in fewest explosives, but each game can kind of take on a shape of its own.” How the Broncos choose to combat the Chiefs’ defense with Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb calling the shots remains to be seen. From my perspective, Denver will need to dial up some big plays through the air against a revamped secondary featuring three new starters. They’ve got the quarterback in Bo Nix to do it and a ton of weapons at skill positions to make that happen. On top of that, they need to be consistent with running the ball. This year’s trio of J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey, and Jonah Coleman should help the Broncos’ running game be a strong point of their offense. Denver has had some modest success rushing the ball against Kansas City last year, but controlling the clock and pace of the game by being efficient in their ground attack will be critical on Monday Night Football . Football is a game of inches and every single one of them will matter in primetime against the Chiefs. We saw that play out on several occasions in the Patriots/Seahawks game. Last night was a good appetizer of what’s to come the rest of the week, but I’m ready for the main course and anxious to see the Broncos feast in just a few days. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Broncos ready to put on a show under Monday Night Football spotlight
summary: There’s opening the NFL season, and then there’s opening on Monday Night Football. Add the fact that the Denver Broncos are doing so on the road against their division rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. Don’t forget Denver won the AFC West, ending the Chiefs’ absurd streak. Plus, two teams that are getting their starting quarterbacks […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s opening the NFL season, and then there’s opening on Monday Night Football. Add the fact that the Denver Broncos are doing so on the road against their division rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. Don’t forget Denver won the AFC West, ending the Chiefs’ absurd streak. Plus, two teams that are getting their starting quarterbacks back from injury. It doesn’t get much better than that for a season opener. When asked if it gets old playing on Monday Night Football, Bo Nix said: “Absolutely, it doesn’t get old. It’s very exciting. It means that you are in a really good spot as an organization, but it’s also a great responsibility. You get put on Monday Night Football in Week 1, it means you have something to go out there and prove. We’re excited as a team. It’s going to be a really big challenge, but one that we are going to respond well to. We just have to go out there and play really hard.” If the Broncos are able to come away with a win on Monday night, that’s the perfect start to the season. That’s especially true considering the sports world will be watching. “Honestly, at the end of the day, it’s exciting to be able to have the opportunity to open up the season, Monday Night Football, all the games are going to be done, college is done, everyone’s played Sunday, Sunday night’s done,” Broncos receiver Courtland Sutton said to the media on Wednesday. “The only game that’s going to be on is Chiefs-Broncos, and that’s what’s exciting. Yes, we have an extra 30 hours, as you would say, to wait to be able to get that first game off, but it’s exciting, though. “It’s exciting. It’s a privilege to be able to open up the season on Monday Night Football. They don’t just hand that out to anybody. I think that it speaks volumes to where our organization is getting back to and where people view the Broncos. I’m looking forward to watching the boys go out there, us and the boys go out there and put on a show for everyone on Monday Night Football.” It's Chiefs Week 💪 pic.twitter.com/uidw39RFWE — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 9, 2026 To make matters even more difficult, Denver is playing at one of the most difficult places to play in the NFL. After a disappointing season, there is the expectation that Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs return to form. So that could lead to a more raucous Chiefs Kingdom than usual. “They have a passionate fan base,” Sutton said when asked what makes Arrowhead Stadium a difficult place to play. “They have a very passionate fan base, and they come, they show up, and they show out, and they lean into what makes them them. They say they have the loudest stadium, and it’s a good environment to be able to go play in. It’s a loud environment, it’s a place where they love their team, and their team has had success. “So, they show up for their team, and you just have to go out there and put your best foot forward. It’s a divisional game. I think everyone’s going to show up for a divisional game, and it’s on us just to go in there and execute one play at a time, one quarter at a time, and see where the chips lie at the end.” Another factor could be the extra day of waiting before playing the opener, plus the fact that it’s at night. “For me, it’s about trusting my training and getting back to having good eyes, having good feet, and having good communication in the huddle and executing at a high level,” Nix said. “Getting the ball out quick, don’t take negative plays and when we get into the red zone, we need to push the ball in and get touchdowns. I know that I just have to do my part, do my role, and we have a lot of guys to where I don’t have to do anything necessarily crazy or special. We just let our guys do their thing. I’m excited. Going there will present different challenges, ones is that we will face then.”

summary: On Christmas Day last year, the Denver Broncos made the typically dreaded trip to Arrowhead for a late December game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Despite Patrick Mahomes being on injured reserve, the Chiefs put up a spirited fight holding Denver without a touchdown until late in the third quarter and held a tie midway […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a rushing touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. And if it means they beat the Chiefs in Arrowhead for the second straight year, then I’m definitely all over it Broncos daily recap Broncos announce they have named 9 team captains Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today and announced that they have named a total of 9 team captains. These captains were voted on by the players and feature veterans and leaders from the offense, defense, and special teams. Broncos Release Unofficial Week 1 Depth Chart ahead of Chiefs showdown The Denver Broncos have released their unofficial Week 1 depth chart ahead of their Monday Night showdown vs. their division rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs. It is an “unofficial depth chart”; Head Coach Sean Payton isn’t giving away everything, but we still can learn a few things about the Broncos roster from this depth chart reveal. Broncos at Chiefs preview: Denver aims for fast start The wait is over. This is true on multiple levels. The Denver Broncos will open the season. And quarterback Bo Nix is set to return to the field after an ankle injury ended his and the Broncos’ season. Potent Quotables Wil Lutz On what it means to be named a team captain “It means a lot. I think when you’re voted as a captain by the guys that you come to work with every day and you spend a lot of time with, I think that’s the ultimate sign of respect and I don’t take it lightly. It’s pretty cool.” On the team’s overall leadership “We have a lot of leadership, and that’s kind of what I said the other night. I think this team is built to lead by committee. It has nothing to do with the ‘C’ [captain’s patch] on our chest. I think we have veterans in the right group. I think as a kicker being a captain, my job is to be a good teammate and make field goals. So that tells me I accomplished that, most of it so far. Yes, we have leadership at every position, and the team feels a lot older than it is, which is a good problem to have.” On the players’ excitement about QB Bo Nix’s return “Yes, I think everybody’s just ready to play. Obviously [QB] Bo [Nix] is one of our leaders, and we know what Bo’s capable of and he’s obviously a super talented quarterback. I think the hardest part about playing on Monday night is we have to wait. So I think everybody’s champing at the bit right now and Monday night will be here before we know it.” On the emotions that go into kicking game-winning field goals “You trust everything you’ve done throughout the season, throughout training camp, throughout the week, that your body knows what to do in every situation. I’m fortunate to have played long enough to have seen every situation, have been in every situation. So I just trust my preparation, trust my routine that when it is tight, when the game is on the line, that your body kind of takes over and what you do works. I think for the most part I’ve been able to do that.” Courtland Sutton On what it means to be named a captain for the sixth consecutive year “I’ll tell you all the same thing I told the team. There’s an immense amount of gratitude that comes from being named captain. To be able to have your peers and the guys that you share work with, locker room, practice, film, games, bus rides, flights, the whole nine, you share those moments with, for them to, not just myself, but the rest of the guys that were named captains, to look at us and say, ‘We trust that you guys are going to help guide us in the right direction and we believe in you guys to be the anchor for us, for the ship to be going into the direction we want to go towards.’ I just have a lot of gratitude and thankfulness that, I know it’s the same, but that comes from being named captain for another season.” On what it says about the team to have so many players as captains “Yes, I think something I was telling the guys after we got done with the dinner, whether you have the ‘C’ [captain’s patch] or don’t have the ‘C,’ everyone has an opportunity to lead. Everyone leads in their own way. You may not have the ‘C’ on your chest, but we all have moments that our leadership shows. I think to answer your question, I think that it speaks volumes of what [Head] Coach [Sean] Payton has done and what Mr. [General Manager] George [Paton] has done in terms of bringing the right guys into the locker room. To be honest with you, we could have 15, 20 guys be captains on this team because we have such… I think there’s such a standard that’s been set amongst the locker room and amongst the guys to understand what it takes to be able to have success and to have productive days at work, whether it’s at practice, whether it’s in the locker room, in the weight room, in the film room. I think we have the right guys in those places, and it allows us to be able to have nine guys named captain. For ‘DK’ (S Devon Key) to be a new member of that group, I speak super highly of him. I probably don’t tell him this enough in person, but I tell all the other young guys to see him come in and to watch his journey, the way that has transpired and for him to never complain. There was one time when I think his rookie year, he was on ‘P’ [practice] squad. I never heard one complaint, he just came to work, got out there and did what he needed to do to be able to have success. Then to watch him grow, and mold into the player that he’s become, and then ultimately into this leadership role, into this captain role it’s truly inspiring to be able to watch that happen. Guys that are undrafted, guys that are drafted in late rounds, guys that get put on ‘P’ squad early on should look at his story and take that and run with it and say, ‘Look, if I keep my nose to the ground and keep working and keep developing myself, the sky’s the limit.’ I’m happy for him to be able to be in that ring and in that realm with us.” On what makes Arrowhead Stadium a difficult environment and the keys to handling that atmosphere “They have a passionate fan base. They have a very passionate fan base, and they come, they show up, and they show out and they lean into what makes them them. They say they have the loudest stadium, and it’s a good environment to be able to go play in. It’s a loud environment, it’s a place where they love their team and their team has had success. So therefore, they show up for their team and you just have to go out there and put your best foot forward. It’s a divisional game. I think everyone’s going to show up for a divisional game, and it’s on us just to go in there and execute one play at a time, one quarter at a time and see where the chips lie at the end.” On opening the season on Monday Night Football “Honestly at the end of the day, it’s exciting to be able to have the opportunity to open up the season, Monday Night Football , all the games are going to be done, college is done, everyone’s played Sunday, Sunday night’s done. The only game that’s going to be on is Chiefs-Broncos, and that’s what’s exciting. Yes, we…

title: Broncos announce they have named 9 team captains
summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today and announced that they have named a total of 9 team captains. These captains were voted on by the players and feature veterans and leaders from the offense, defense, and special teams. The Broncos 9 team captains are quarterback Bo Nix, cornerback Bo Nix, […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 21: Alex Singleton #49 of the Denver Broncos, Talanoa Hufanga #9, Pat Surtain II #2, and Bo Nix #10 stands on the field during the coin toss prior to an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today and announced that they have named a total of 9 team captains. These captains were voted on by the players and feature veterans and leaders from the offense, defense, and special teams. The Broncos 9 team captains are quarterback Bo Nix, cornerback Bo Nix, wide receiver Courtland Sutton, guard Quinn Meinerz, cornerback Pat Surtain II, linebacker Alex Singleton, nose tackle DJ Jones, safety Talanoa Hufanga, safety/special teamer Devon Key, and kicker Wil Lutz. HC Sean Payton has announced our 2026 captains as chosen by the players. ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/0jWwJfHkyB — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 9, 2026 The Broncos have a strong veteran unit that could feature even more team captains, but the players chose these nine players to represent them as captains for the 2026 season. QB Bo Nix – Nix is the Broncos franchise quarterback and is a leader on and off the field. He has been named a team captain all three seasons of his career and clearly has earned the respect of the players. We see his passion and intensity on the field and that same passion and intensity is felt off the field. He’s a true leader and a true franchise quarterback. CB Pat Surtain II – PS2 is an elite player and leads by example. He isn’t known for being a big talker, giving passionate speeches and all that, but for the way he carries himself on and off the field. The former Defensive Player of the Year will once again lead by example and be an elite player on and off the field for the Broncos. WR Courtland Sutton – Sutton is one of the longest tenured Broncos on the team right now (Outside of Bolles, I believe he’s the longest) and provides veteran leadership on and off the field. This is the 6th time that Sutton has been named a captain by the Broncos players. G Quinn Meinerz – The All-Pro guard is one of the best offensive lineman in the entire NFL and is once again, named a team captain by the Broncos players. He is the lone offensive lineman named here and has taken over a key leadership role in that group. LB Alex Singleton – Singleton is beloved by the Broncos players and coaches. He’s the green dot wearer on the field and a truly inspirational leader on and off the field. We saw that strength last season when he battled through a cancer diagnosis, beat cancer, and returned to the field without missing much time at all. He has the respect of the Broncos players and coaches and will be a inspirational leader once again for the Broncos top-ranked defense. NT DJ Jones – Jones is the anchor of the Denver Broncos defense and the leader of the Broncos talented defensive line. He has been part of the Broncos since 2022 and this will be his 10th season in the NFL. Jones provides a valuable veteran and leadership presence in the middle of the Broncos defense. S Talanoa Hufanga – You want that fire and intensity? Hufanga brings that on and off the field. He gives intense and inspirational pre-game speeches, plays with his hair on fire, and is the heart and soul of the Broncos defense. He joined the team last season and quickly became a key part of the defense and the teams success. S/STer Devon Key – Key is a great story. He was viewed as a fringe roster player and someone most fans overlooked or didn’t want on the team. However, Key continued to improve and turned himself into an All-Pro special teams player. He earned the respect around the league, and now, from his teammates. A year later, Key is an All-Pro special teamer, a leader of the Broncos special teams unit, and now, a first-time team captain. K Wil Lutz – Lutz was brought over from New Orleans to Denver during Payton’s first season to help change the losing culture that developed with the Broncos. We have seen the results on and off the field with this culture change that Lutz helped build. He also has become one of the more reliable and clutch kickers in the NFL and will look to do the same this season.

It is an “unofficial depth chart”; Head Coach Sean Payton isn’t giving away everything, but we still can learn a few things about the Broncos roster from this depth chart […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - August 18 : Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix answers questions from reporters at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos have released their unofficial Week 1 depth chart ahead of their Monday Night showdown vs. their division rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs. The Denver Broncos have released their unofficial 2026 Week 1 depth chart Marvin Mims is listed as a starting WR and Jonah Elliss is listed as a starting edge rusher. Pat Bryant is the backup behind Courtland Sutton and is expected to be heavily involved in the Broncos’ offense this season. The other noteworthy tidbit we learned was that Jonah Elliss will be getting the start opposite of Nik Bonitto. This was expected, but the Broncos confirmed as much with this release.
