title: Every Former Packer the Team Will See in the 2026 Season
summary: Last offseason, I ranked the former Green Bay Packers the team would face in the upcoming season based on how much it was gonna hurt to play against them. I specifically ranked them based on pure emotion mixed with how much the Packers could use them at that time. This season, there are a handful […]
full_text: Nov 23, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams (17) acknowledges the crowd after scoring a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last offseason, I ranked the former Green Bay Packers the team would face in the upcoming season based on how much it was gonna hurt to play against them. I specifically ranked them based on pure emotion mixed with how much the Packers could use them at that time. This season, there are a handful more former Packers they’re facing, including some they faced last year and some they haven’t. So this time we’re side-stepping the emotional rankings and looking at every familiar face they’ll see on their schedule. Let’s get to it! Week 1: @ Minnesota Vikings RB Aaron Jones LB Eric Wilson Both of these guys were with the Vikings last year, so it’s nothing new to see them again. Eric Wilson initially signed with the Vikings as a UDFA in 2017, years prior to being one of the only positives on the Packers special teams unit. Aaron Jones was #1 in my ranking last year and would have been high on that list this year taking into account the current Josh Jacobs scenario . Jones will always be the epitome of what the perfect player is: a great player on and off the field. I wish nothing but the best for that man in every facet of his life (except against the Packers). Week 2: @ New York Jets EDGE Kingsley Enagbare C Josh Myers TE/FB Andrew Beck Kingsley Enagbare is a player the team will miss this week after only keeping 4 edge rushers on their final roster due to Micah Parsons and Collin Oliver both starting the season with PUP and IR designations, respectively. Not only are they very thin at the position, but they also have a lot of unproven talent (side-eyeing you , Lukas Van Ness) so it’s not the best timing to face Enagbare, who was a solid backup when injuries piled up. Josh Myers they don’t miss at center, but it’d be nice to have Sean Rhyan as a swing lineman with all the shuffling going on amongst the offensive line due to injuries. Andrew Beck, well, he played 32 snaps for the Packers and I had to Google who he was because I don’t even remember him, so no comment needed there. Week 3: Atlanta Falcons EDGE Za’Darius Smith Za’Darius Smith recently shared that his main reason for retiring so suddenly last season was to spend time with his mother who is battling Alzheimer’s before she passed away, which was shortly followed by the death of his father and grandmother. All of those things are gutting enough on their own, but all of them happening in such a short period of time is heartbreaking. Therefore, despite him consistently taking shots at the Packers, I will not be making fun of him (again) for the captains patch necklace and Lions Super Bowl ring . Thank you. Onto Week 4. Week 4: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles This will be the first week this season Green Bay won’t see a familiar face on the field . However, Bucs head coach Todd Bowles was a member of the team’s player personnel staff in the ‘95-‘96 season, when the Packers won Super Bowl XXXI, so shoutout to him. Week 5: Chicago Bears EDGE Jonathan Garvin (IR) Jonathan Garvin was placed on IR by the Bears in late August and hasn’t played a snap for them. The thing he’s most known for in Green Bay is being cut on his birthday . That’s all I got (plus this terrible meme I made and never got to use, featuring a scene from Role Models ). Week 6: Dallas Cowboys EDGE Rashan Gary DT Kenny Clark ALRIGHT NOW WE’RE TALKING. When I wrote this last season, it was months before the Micah Parsons trade that sent Kenny Clark to the Cowboys, so he wasn’t on that list. This is also the week Parsons is eyeing as his most “optimistic” return to the field, so there’s lots of reunions going on. The Packers faced Kenny Clark last season in their tie at AT&T Stadium, but this marks Clark’s first return to Lambeau as a Cowboy, along with Rashan Gary, who was traded to Dallas for a fourth-round pick earlier this season. If Parsons is back this week, he’ll surely be on a snap count. However, I fully expect him to still make a bigger impact against his former team in limited snaps than we’ll see from Gary, which is nothing new . Week 7: @ Detroit Lions No one, surprisingly! Week 8: Carolina Panthers RB AJ Dillon LT Rasheed Walker AJ Dillon, a fan favorite to some, has already faced the Packers as an opponent during his underwhelming stint with the Eagles last year. Dillon signed with the Panthers this offseason but, like last season, isn’t expected to see the field much unless injuries pile up in that room. Rasheed Walker, however, is facing the Packers for the first time after the team let him walk without a deal this offseason in favor of their former first round pick, Jordan Morgan. Walker signed a one-year, $4 million contract with the Panthers a few days into free agency. The contract, worth up to $10 million with incentives, is likely a lot less than he was expecting which should make Packers fans feel pretty good about the defense lining up against him. Week 9: @ New England Patriots WR Romeo Doubs OL Greg Van Roten (yes, he’s still in the league) First of all, Greg Van Roten is a month older than me so if any of you call him old I am calling the police. Second-of-ly , I wrote in last year’s article about how surprised I was that he was still in the league, then immediately forgot it, I guess because I had the same thought when writing this article. If you can’t tell, I’m stalling so I don’t have to talk about Romeo Doubs. But yeah, Van Roten, that one guy who played for the Packers all those years ago is still in the league at 36 years old (don’t you dare say “old”). He was with the Giants last year, and has been a “just fine” veteran over the last 15 years. PFF ranked him 35th out of 81 guards last season, so, you know, good for him. OKAY FINE! I’ll talk about Romeo Doubs! I hate seeing him for another team. I don’t expect the Packers to miss him on the field despite Doubs being their healthiest WR last season. However, I personally will miss his hilarious and goofy moments the last few years and seeing his comedically giant guardian cap helmet making the most incredible catch you’ve ever seen out of nowhere! Are you happy now?!? Week 10: Minnesota Vikings See Week 1 Week 11: Bye Week (so here’s some Packers free agents still available) C Lucas Patrick CB Corey Ballentine CB Trevon Diggs CB Robert Rochell DT Dean Lowry DT Mike Pennel (lol) EDGE Preston Smith K Brandon McManus TE/FB Josiah Deguara TE John Fitzpatrick TE/QB Taysom Hill (technically, I guess) TE Marcedes Lewis WR Malik Heath WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling Week 12: @ Los Angeles Rams WR Davante Adams WHEW this one’s gonna hurt. The Packers already faced Davante Adams in 2023, when he was in his second season with the Las Vegas Raiders, but this is different. Adams shined last season with a better team and offense than he’s had since being traded from Green Bay ahead of the 2022 season. Davante Adams clearly still cherishes his time with the Packers and even expressed being open to return to the team last offseason before ultimately signing with the Rams. The Rams are a favorite to win it all this year and if the Packers can’t get a ring this season, I hope Adams gets one. Week 13: @ New Orleans Saints DL Colby Wooden Wooden was the guy the Packers traded to the Indianapolis Colts for LB Zaire Franklin, who was recently named a captain by the team. The Colts released Wooden during final roster cutdowns at the end of August and the Saints claimed him on waivers the next day. So, looks like the Packers handled that trade pretty well so far. Week 14: Buffalo Bills None! But shoutout to Micah Hyde anyway. Week 15: Miami Dolphins aka Green Bay South General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan Head Coach Jeff Hafley QB Malik Willis QB Kyle McCord S Zayne Anderson S Jaylin Simpson…

title: Houston Texans stats: Welcome to Week 1 vs. the Bills
summary: Welcome back to another year of football. We at value of things have a tradition that we do every week. You will see two features on a weekly the basis. The first will usually be a post-mortem on the previous’s weeks games. That will come on Monday or Tuesday depending on when the game was […]
full_text: Welcome back to another year of football. We at value of things have a tradition that we do every week. You will see two features on a weekly the basis. The first will usually be a post-mortem on the previous’s weeks games. That will come on Monday or Tuesday depending on when the game was played. We will include the relevant numbers from the game and either a great, good, and bad in victory or good, bad, and ugly in defeat. Then, later in the week you will see “By the numbers.” It is a simple look at the rankings on offense and defense to give us some idea of what each team will try to attack in the upcoming game. Early season games are difficult at best. Small sample sizes are the enemy of good analysis and a look at the previous season’s numbers is often even less significant. However, it is all we got in the early going. Obviously, we could do a huge deep dive into numbers and as much as I love deep dives, we want to keep this relatively simple so that everyone can digest it well. Below is a table of how each team ranked in passing yards, rushing yards, and passing yards defended, and rushing yards defended. It isn’t perfect and I know regular commenters will beg for more. We might get there in subsequent looks, but really this is what we have going in. Texans Bills Rushing Yards 22nd 1st Passing Yards 14th 15th Def Rushing Yards 4th 28th Def Passing Yards 6th 1st Keep in mind that all numbers have a context and they often play against each other in what Bill O’Brien used to lovingly call “complimentary football.” Being in the top of the league or bottom of the league in total yards in rushing or passing is not necessarily an indicator of anything by itself. For instance, the Bills struggled against the run, so teams just didn’t pass as much against them. They didn’t need to. On the flip side, when you are in the top ten in both categories (as the Texans are) then that means you have a really good overall defense. I know I’m not breaking any new ground here. What will the Bills offense try to do? It seems counterintuitive sometimes when you have a former league MVP at quarterback, but the key to the Bills offense is their rushing attack. Obviously, Josh Allen is a huge part of that. Still, if the Bills can run the football without Allen then they will be stay ahead of the sticks and keep the Texans’ pass rush at bay. Obviously, the Texans have been effective at stopping the run and some new defensive additions aim to get even better in that department. Allen has been harassed in two games against the defense and if they have to rely on his right arm to move the football it could be a long day for him again. What will the Bills defense try to do? It’s probably simple enough to say that whichever team runs the football most effectively will win the game. This is the weakness of the Bills’ defense, but it is something they hope they have addressed effectively in the offseason. Historically, the Texans have not been effective running the football, so this is a historical contest between two weak links to see which one has the upper hand. What will the Texans offense try to do? This is simple. They have to run the football effectively. That means converting on third and short and fourth and short to keep the sticks moving. If they are able to do that they will win the time of possession battle and keep their defense fresh. A fresh defense means more harassment and it means a more desperate Bills attack that will take chances. The numbers above don’t really capture the whole truth on the Texans history of running the football. They have been inconsistent from game to game in the past and the preseason didn’t show much as we did not see a lot of the starters. It is the biggest unknown of the entire offseason. What will the Texans defense try to do? This one is also simple. If the Texans can make the Bills one-dimensional then they will have a feast day again. The key is keeping them behind the sticks and keeping Allen bottled up in the pocket. History has shown that he will take chances and sometimes gets burned by those chances. Getting key turnovers in the game obviously feeds right into that offensive philosophy above. In particular, look for J.D. Clowney to play a key role in setting the edge on rushing plays when he is in the game. He gives the Texans a dimension they did not have in the last couple of seasons.

title: It took one series for Anthony Richardson to see his future with the Colts
summary: The first game of the NFL season is special. The NFL diluted it by moving the 22-year standard Thursday opener to Wednesday to fit a Netflix only special in on Thursday to squeeze more money out of its fans, but that’s a story for another time. Regardless, the home opener for the defending Super Bowl champs is […]
full_text: The first game of the NFL season is special. The NFL diluted it by moving the 22-year standard Thursday opener to Wednesday to fit a Netflix only special in on Thursday to squeeze more money out of its fans, but that’s a story for another time. Regardless, the home opener for the defending Super Bowl champs is always electric. With all that energy bouncing around, it didn’t take long for a quiet hush to fall over the festivities. With it, Anthony Richardson saw his future with the Colts. Sam Darnold was the bottom of the barrel until he became the top of the heap. He was a quarterback that the Jets couldn’t wait to unload after a disastrous tenure as the franchise quarterback. Yes, it took him leaving to find his footing, but a resurgence in Minnesota, followed by the greatest achievement in the game with Seattle, found him as the toast of the town and the entire league. On the first drive of the game, Darnold injured his hip and didn’t return to the field. Drew Lock stepped in and led the Seahawks to victory. That is the perfect example of how things can change in the NFL. The MRI for Darnold looks good, but it could have been bad, really bad. While Richardson isn’t rooting for Daniel Jones to get injured, it isn’t out of the realm of possibility that Jones misses time this season. It simply seems to be his M.O. If that happens, Richardson will be thrust into the spotlight with a chance to turn his career around. Darnold lasted one series, so that chance could present itself at any time. That should be enough of a glimpse into his Colts’ future to provide the motivation to be ready at a moment’s notice. Ideally, for the Colts, Anthony Richardson won’t see much time this season. That means Daniel Jones stays healthy and upright. That isn’t guaranteed, however. Sam Darnold lasted five plays. No one saw that coming. Whether one sees it coming or not, Richardson should be ready for that very scenario. Wednesday was the best glimpse he could have into his future with the Colts.

title: Colts receive an encouraging injury update regarding starting rookie safety
summary: The Indianapolis Colts released their Wednesday practice report, and rookie safety AJ Haulcy (ankle) was able to practice on a limited basis. Battling a lingering ankle injury, Haulcy has not been able to practice the past couple of weeks, but he could be trending toward making his professional debut against the Baltimore Ravens for the […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: AJ Haulcy #25 of the Indianapolis Colts runs during an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts released their Wednesday practice report, and rookie safety AJ Haulcy (ankle) was able to practice on a limited basis. Battling a lingering ankle injury, Haulcy has not been able to practice the past couple of weeks, but he could be trending toward making his professional debut against the Baltimore Ravens for the Colts’ regular season opener at Lucas Oil Stadium. Haulcy’s continued status the next few days of team practice will be telling regarding whether the Colts’ 2026 3rd round pick will have his ankle fully healthy to go in time for Week 1. Otherwise, the medical staff may play it careful, as the NFL season is a marathon, not a sprint. If Haulcy cannot go, 2nd-year safety Hunter Wohler would be the projected ‘next man up’ starting alongside veteran safety Cam Bynum in the backend of the Colts secondary. Having suffered a season-ending Lisfranc injury during last year’s preseason, Wohler would also be making his professional football debut in Week 1. Otherwise, tight end Drew Ogletree (neck), wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel), and recently acquired center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) were also all limited participants during Wednesday’s practice, along with Haulcy. It’s worth noting that for the Colts, no one has been ruled out ahead of Sunday’s game, as there theoretically could be players who are injured, but not injured enough yet, to begin the regular season on PUP and miss at least the first 4 games of the upcoming campaign.

title: The Colts’ defense is betting big on its cornerbacks staying healthy
summary: The Colts are going to need their cornerbacks to be one of the best position groups on the team this season. That is not really a preference as much as it is a requirement. This defense has talent, but it also has some obvious questions. The pass rush is nothing to write home about. Laiatu […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 6: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward (7) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts training camp practice on August 6, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Colts are going to need their cornerbacks to be one of the best position groups on the team this season. That is not really a preference as much as it is a requirement. This defense has talent, but it also has some obvious questions. The pass rush is nothing to write home about. Laiatu Latu needs to take another step plus DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart are still high-level interior players, but this does not look like a unit that is going to consistently overwhelm opposing quarterbacks on its own. If the pass rush is closer to average than great, the coverage has to hold up. The corners have to make quarterbacks hesitate, shrink throwing windows and most importantly buy the front extra time. That puts a lot on Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward, Justin Walley and eventually Cam Taylor-Britt. On paper, the top of the group is strong. Gardner is the star and the player this defense should be built around. Ward gives the Colts a proven veteran outside corner opposite him. Walley is expected to handle a major role in the slot and Taylor-Britt will add another experienced body once he returns from his Week 1 suspension. Taylor-Britt also possesses the ability to play outside or inside, which is key. If all of those players are available and playing well, the Colts should feel good about what they have at cornerback. The problem is how much of that last sentence depends on “if.” Ward is a quality corner when he is on the field, but his concussion history makes his availability one of the biggest swing factors on the defense. They need him outside, handling quality players and letting Gardner stay in his role instead of forcing the rest of the secondary to shuffle around him. If Ward misses time, the cornerback room changes quickly. Walley brings talent and long-term upside, but he is also coming off a major injury. Asking him to step into a big role right away is already a lot. Asking him to do it while the team is thin around him adds another layer to the risk. The Colts may believe he is ready, and maybe he is, but corner is not a position where teams usually get a quiet, stress-free season from everyone involved. Even Gardner missed games last season. That does not make him injury-prone, and it does not change the fact that he is the best player in the group, but it is another reminder that cornerback depth usually gets tested. Cornerback is a very demanding position that requires constant cutting, change of direction and full on sprinting; it is the more athletically demanding position in the entire sport. Very few teams get through a season with their top corners completely untouched. That is why the Jaylon Jones move stands out. The Colts waived Jones while signing offensive tackle Luke Tenuta from the practice squad, which may be perfectly defensible on its own. Teams always have to balance the bottom of the roster, and offensive line depth is not something to treat lightly. Still, the move leaves the Colts light at cornerback going into Week 1, especially with Taylor-Britt suspended. Indianapolis did claim Kapena Gushiken, and there are some useful names on the practice squad, but relying on emergency elevations and new additions is not the same as having settled depth. Jones is not some irreplaceable piece, so this is not about making his release bigger than it is. The concern is the overall bet the Colts appear willing to make. They’re asking a group with several health questions to carry a defense that needs strong coverage to function at a high level. That is a lot of pressure for a room that already feels a little thin. The margin becomes even smaller because of what this defense is trying to cover up. If the pass rush does not consistently get home, the corners have to win longer. If the linebackers are young or slow to sort things out, the secondary has to clean up more mistakes underneath. If the safeties are still settling into new roles, communication on the back end becomes even more important. Good cornerback play can hide a lot of issues. Bad or injured cornerback play exposes everything fast. There have been many years with the Colts where the 3rd stringer is getting significant reps by the middle of the season. That is the part that makes the health of this group so important. Gardner can change a defense by himself, but he cannot cover every receiver. Ward can raise the ceiling of the secondary, but only if he is available. Walley can become an important piece, but the Colts need him healthy and comfortable quickly. Taylor-Britt helps once he returns, but he is not available for the opener and still has to earn a role when he gets back. The Colts are not wrong to bet on the top of their cornerback room. There is legitimate talent there, and if the group stays healthy, it should become the strength of the defense and maybe even the strength of the team. The issue is that the whole structure feels fragile. This is not a deep room loaded with proven backups. It is a talented room that needs its best players to stay on the field. For a defense that may not have a dominant pass rush, that is a risky place to be. If the group holds up, the defense has a chance to be much better than it was. If it does not, the Colts may find out quickly that the cornerback room was carrying more of the plan than anyone wanted to admit.

title: Will the Jacksonville Jaguars win their first major NFL award in 2026?
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars don’t get the respect they deserve. Sure, they rank 28th in market size and 30th in winning percentage among active NFL teams, but they were also ridiculed for hosting a Super Bowl and assumed to be London-bound — if not due for extinction. It’s not just that folks don’t care about the […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 23: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills and Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars shake hands after a game at Highmark Stadium on September 23, 2024 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars don’t get the respect they deserve. Sure, they rank 28th in market size and 30th in winning percentage among active NFL teams, but they were also ridiculed for hosting a Super Bowl and assumed to be London-bound — if not due for extinction. It’s not just that folks don’t care about the Jags. For whatever reason, they’re despised. Look no further than the fact that Jacksonville is the ONLY team without a major Associated Press regular-season individual award. NFL teams who have never had a….. pic.twitter.com/KapC7mOvg1 — TB EGO (@TomBradyEgo) September 8, 2026 Obviously, you need talent to win an award, and the Jaguars have struggled to find blue-chip players since the 1995 expansion draft. But you could make the case that Maurice Jones-Drew should’ve won OPOY in 2011. Or that Calais Campbell should’ve won DPOY in 2017. At the very least, Liam Coen should’ve won COTY last year. Jacksonville hasn’t had much to boast about when it comes to the on-field product, but they should have some kind of hardware beyond Walter Payton Man of the Year, right? The good news is the Jaguars finally have some star power. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , four different names have under 50-1 odds to win an award this season. They’re not exactly favorites, but they definitely aren’t longshots, either. Trevor Lawrence has +1800 odds to win MVP Josh Hines-Allen has +4500 odds to win DPOY Travis Hunter has +5500 odds to win CPOY Liam Coen has +2200 odds to win COY Hines-Allen could end up having the best season of that group, though I’d be shocked if national media doesn’t spend all its votes on defenders for the Los Angeles Rams and/or Houston Texans. Similarly, Lawrence could produce more yards and touchdowns than any other passer but still not get the necessary narrative push. For any Jaguar to earn an award, the team would likely need to clinch the AFC No. 1 seed with a no-doubt-about-it performance in the regular season. It’s not very fair, but them’s the rules. For more, check out the most recent episode of the Prowler Podcast with me and John Shipley. If you were to wager on Jacksonville this year, what would be your favorite bet? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Liam Coen’s Jacksonville Jaguars are 8.5-point home favorites against Todd Monken’s Cleveland Browns. It’ll be the latter’s first game as an NFL head coach, and his starting quarterback is a familiar foe for Jaguars faithful. Deshaun Watson, who was at one point the obvious successor to Andrew Luck as the king of the AFC South, has soured into one of the worst players in the National Football League. In 2024, he was the NFL’s least efficient passer through Week 7, when he ruptured his right Achilles tendon. Just a few months after he underwent surgery, he rolled his ankle and re-ruptured the same Achilles tendon. The nasty man turns 31 on Monday. Cleveland’s quarterback sucks. The bigger news is that, for the first time in a decade, reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett will not be wearing orange and brown. The Browns have significant questions across its roster. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see them forecasted for a top-three 2027 draft pick by the middle of the season. The Jaguars ought to take care of business and start the season 1-0. Do you trust Coen and company to get the job done? Is this a trap game? Are you confident in the Jaguars? title: 5 bold Chiefs predictions from the Arrowhead Pride staff
summary: They say fortune favors the bold. The Kansas City Chiefs have certainly been bold through the years, from trading away veteran quarterback Alex Smith to start Patrick Mahomes to trading away All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill in his prime. The organization has three Super Bowl trophies to show for it. So now it’s time for […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 28: A general view of the football field prior to the NFL 2025 game between Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Kansas City, United States. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images They say fortune favors the bold. The Kansas City Chiefs have certainly been bold through the years, from trading away veteran quarterback Alex Smith to start Patrick Mahomes to trading away All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill in his prime. The organization has three Super Bowl trophies to show for it. So now it’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to be bold. Here are five bold predictions about the Chiefs’ 2026 season: Rocky Magana The Chiefs hold opposing teams to under 280 yards from scrimmage per game. For reference, this would put the Chiefs in the echelons of the Denver Broncos and Houston Texans in 2025. But with the addition of a young pass rusher like R Mason Thomas, and a blue chip cornerback in Masoor Delane (who I think will be a multi-time All Pro recipient in his career), along with the return of L’Jarius Sneed and the addition of Alohi Gillman, I think this defense takes the big step from being good, to great this season. I think the Chiefs are going to win a lot of one-score games this year, and the defense slamming the door shut on opponents will be the reason why. Dakota Watson For the first time since 2017, the Chiefs will have a 1,000-yard rusher AND receiver. It is astounding that during the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the Chiefs have never had a 1,000-yard rusher. That streak comes to an end with the signing of running back Kenneth Walker and with Mahomes coming off an injury, a (hopefully) more balanced attack. The last 1,000 yard rusher for the Chiefs was Kareem Hunt in 2017. The bold part of this prediction, is that the Chiefs will also have one wide receiver attain 1,000 yards. The last Chiefs’ receiver to reach 1,000 yards was Tyreek Hill in 2021. It’s time for both these ugly streaks to come to an end. Caleb James The Chiefs will lead the NFL in rushing yards. After multiple seasons of neglecting to develop running backs and putting a stunning lack of resources into acquiring them, the Chiefs signed the best free agent possible this offseason and also drafted a highly touted player. The endgame? Run the damn ball. Kenneth Walker showed the world a glimpse of who he can be in the playoffs this past season, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson has all the skills to develop into a star and to help the team hold a lethal one-two punch. This is what the interior of the offensive line was built for, and even with stability issues at tackle that could hurt the team in pass protection, Andy Reid is still savvy enough to scheme open runs as long as center Creed Humphrey and right guard Trey Smith blow open holes in the middle. Walker should come close to leading the NFL in rushing yards, and Johnson should have a very productive rookie season. Look for Walker to go over 1,300 yards, and Johnson to come close to 800 on the ground. Maurice Elston The Chiefs will finish the season top 5 among NFL teams in interceptions Kansas City recorded only 10 interceptions last season, ranking 22nd in the NFL, but its rebuilt secondary possesses greater ball-production potential. Cornerbacks Nohl Williams and rookie Mansoor Delane have demonstrated strong ball skills. Williams tied for the Chiefs’ lead with seven passes defended as a rookie while earning a 75.6 PFF coverage grade and allowing completions on only 37.1% of his targets. In his final college season, he led the FBS with seven interceptions and recorded 16 passes defended. Delane finished his final season at LSU with 13 passes defended, including 11 breakups and two interceptions, despite opponents rarely challenging him. The addition of safety Alohi Gilman also gives Kansas City a veteran safety with five career interceptions, compared with Bryan Cook’s three, while Chamarri Conner’s move into a more traditional safety role should create further opportunities. Ron Kopp Jr. Two Chiefs will finish in the top 5 of Defensive Rookie of the Year voting In 2025, the Atlanta Falcons had two rookies finish within the top 5 of votes for the NFL AP Defensive Rookie of the Year award: edge rusher James Pearce and defensive back Xavier Watts. I believe the Chiefs will have a similar duo finish within the top 5 this year: edge rusher R Mason Thoma and defensive back Mansoor Delane. This bold prediction could have been centered around Thomas and his sack total. With Kansas City’s ability to stuff the run and set up pass-rush situations, I see Thomas taking advantage of playing with defensive tackle Chris Jones and closing in on 10 sacks in his first year. However, his teammate on the boundary is going to take advantage of the revamped pass rush Thomas is leading. Delane looks the part of a physical cornerback that won’t be giving much room for completions on the outside. If he converts a handful of targets his way into highlight-reel interceptions, he and Thomas will both be vying for the award. What’s your bold Chiefs prediction for the 2026 season? Let us know in the comments!

title: Why the Chiefs are confident in the team’s young backup running backs
summary: After several battles in training camp and preseason to finalize the 53-man roster, the Kansas City Chiefs head into Week 1 of the regular season with three running backs on the active roster. Kenneth Walker, the team’s prize free-agent signing, heads the unit and will take on the majority of snaps this season, but rookie […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs signals first down after a run in the first quarter of an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After several battles in training camp and preseason to finalize the 53-man roster, the Kansas City Chiefs head into Week 1 of the regular season with three running backs on the active roster. Kenneth Walker, the team’s prize free-agent signing, heads the unit and will take on the majority of snaps this season, but rookie Emmett Johnson and second-year back Brashard Smith both had impressive preseasons, instilling enough confidence in the team to part ways with veteran back Emari Demercado on cutdown day. Here’s what to know about the backups in the backfield: Emmett Johnson The Chiefs drafted Johnson in the fifth round of the 2026 Draft, but have wasted no time acclimating him to their system and giving him chances to show his abilities. The Nebraska product worked his way from the bottom of the depth chart to become the Chiefs’ second running back on the roster behind only Walker. In the preseason, Johnson flashed his natural blend of patience and explosion, which helped him find running lanes. Good balance by Johnson to stay on his feet and work through the initial contact to pick up extra yards. pic.twitter.com/iyZbLnK5AQ — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 2, 2026 With good hesitation moves and solid contact balance, Johnson used those tools, along with good vision, to break off decent runs and create plays even when the lane wasn’t there initially. On the snap, the Chiefs go left on a zone run, but there is not a hole for Johnson to hit initially. As Johnson approaches the line of scrimmage, He reads a small crease start to open up, and with a quick jump cut, hits the hole, and shakes off a tackle on his way to the second level. This wasn’t a home-run handoff, but it showed Johnson doesn’t need perfectly blocked looks to find yards. Good run by Johnson. Nygra and Caliendo good combo to the second level. One cut from Johnson and he hits the hole. Breaks a tackle. Might need to be careful spinning into traffic, but a solid run. pic.twitter.com/yvKHhor9Qd — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 29, 2026 Johnson’s quick slashing style and smooth jump cuts make him a natural fit for the Chiefs’ zone run game. The Chiefs run zone right, and on the snap, Johnson heads toward the line of scrimmage, but little opens up on the play side. Johnson recognizes this, and in one smooth motion, he quickly cuts back and finds a nice running lane. Johnson’s sense of timing and how to take advantage of defenses overflowing to hit cutback lanes is not something that can be taught in a classroom, but is a natural trait and ability that comes naturally to only a select few running backs. Brashard Smith Although Smith is seemingly behind Johnson on the depth chart, he still had a productive preseason and showed that he is worth the Chiefs continuing to develop. A seventh-round pick in last season’s NFL Draft, Smith played sparingly in 2025, but when he did find the field, he showed enough flash to make an impact. After playing only one season at running back in college, Smith’s career started slowly in 2025, but this preseason he looked more comfortable carrying the ball after being largely a pass catcher during his rookie season. Where Johnson operates better with quick jump cuts and working “north and south”, Smith uses his speed and quickness to try to create plays to the sideline and uses it to get around would-be tacklers. Smith takes the zone handoff and bounces it outside. The edge defender gets hands on, but Smith runs through the arm tackle and turns the corner for a nice gain. pic.twitter.com/WLoS9QjAt2 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 2, 2026 On the snap, Smith takes a quick peek inside, but elects to bounce the run. The end-of-the-line defender does get a hand on him, but with his quickness, he can turn the corner and pick up a nice gain to the sideline. Like Johnson, Smith showed this preseason that he can find yards even when they aren’t there, and he can create big plays. KC goes Y counter, but nothing opens up on the front side. With good vision and patience, Smith allows the blocks to develop and takes the run to the backside, where he finds a crease. pic.twitter.com/IFXngCMIGZ — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 2, 2026 The Chiefs run counter, but not much opens up on the play side. Smith starts to head to the left to attempt to follow the blocks, but with little movement from the kickout block, there is no lane to run through. While the pullers don’t create much space, the play-side double team does create movement downfield, giving Smith an angle to work off of and helping him find a cutback lane. This play displays Smith’s overall development since his rookie season and that he has the vision needed to play running back in the NFL. The bottom line The Chiefs should plan to use Kenneth Walker as much as possible, especially given what he is being paid, but this preseason showed the team has capable backs behind him. Although Smith is the low man in the running back room, he will likely still find ways to help the team via special teams and other “gadget” looks due to his quickness and ability to run in the open field. Johnson appears poised to be Walker’s direct backup this season, and due to the physicality of the position, he should be poised to carry a decent workload for a rookie headed into the season. Most successful run games in the modern NFL operate with multiple running backs commanding close to equal touches, and while the Chiefs will certainly rely more on Walker, Johnson being able to step up and perform well as a rookie would add another layer to a team that will need to rely on the run game early. With depth issues at offensive tackle, quarterback Patrick Mahomes coming off of an ACL injury, and inconsistency from the pass catchers, the Chiefs will need to lean heavily on Walker, but to ensure that he is still in form for a late-season push, Johnson should look to help shoulder some of the load, especially when the grind fo the season kicks in. The Chiefs have not invested much in running back during the Mahomes era, but this offseason bucked the trend, and the team will be in a better spot if it uses its new talent and builds on its strengths.

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Why Sean Payton put Chiefs’ logo on Broncos’ practice field | Broncos Wire For the first time in the rivalry’s history, the Broncos will open their season at Arrowhead, with both teams looking to bounce back after losing their starting quarterbacks late in their 2025 campaigns. To get Denver ready for the primetime atmosphere and raucous environment, Payton began practice with ESPN’s Monday Night Football theme, and, in an interesting move, painted the Kansas City logo on the 50-yard line of the Broncos’ practice field (something he’s done with opponents’ logos in the past). Life has come quickly at the Chiefs since then. Offensive tackle has to be considered their biggest worry heading into Week 1, and the overall O-line depth also remains a major concern, especially with quarterback Patrick Mahomes returning from December knee surgery. Patrick Mahomes expected to start Chiefs’ opener vs. Broncos on MNF | ESPN Patrick Mahomes is expected to start the Kansas City Chiefs’ season opener Monday against the Denver Broncos, according to coach Andy Reid. Since the Chiefs’ offseason began, Mahomes has made it his mission to be in uniform for Week 1, even though he had surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. Although he was held out of the preseason, Mahomes has not missed any of the Chiefs’ practices since the start of training camp, when he was cleared in late July to participate in all football activities. Kansas City Chiefs release first ‘unofficial’ depth chart ahead of Week 1 tilt vs. Denver Broncos; here’s what stands out | A to Z Sports It should be noted that these depth charts are considered “unofficial,” even though they come from the team. Why is that the case? The team’s PR staff assembles them, not the coaching staff. One reason to take them with a grain of salt: In Week 1 of the 2017 NFL preseason, Tyler Bray was listed ahead of Patrick Mahomes. That said, these aren’t entirely uninformed. They’re often based on what the PR staff observes in practice. Not just a sports mom. Randi Mahomes ‘reintroduces’ herself on social media | The Kansas City Star “Let me introduce myself. I’m Randi. You might know me as a sports mom,” the video’s caption reads. “But that’s only a part of my story. I host. I flow. I live. I’m a Grandi, finding new ways to thrive in my 50s. Come along for this chapter.” In the accompanying post, Randi writes that she is wearing “a lot of different hats these days!” She continued: “Family, football, travel, wellness, being a Grandi, and a whole lot of life in between!! Welcome to my life thriving in my 50s!!” Around the NFL NFL Network: Buccaneers, QB Baker Mayfield agree to three-year, $165 million extension Tampa Bay is signing Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million contract extension, NFL Network Insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo and ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday. Tampa Bay later announced the extension through the 2029 season. The news comes as a surprise after the two sides passed Mayfield’s self-imposed training camp deadline for a deal to get done, leading to the veteran QB to say he felt “disrespected” by the Bucs’ proposals. Roughly six weeks time, however, was enough to bridge whatever gap existed in contract talks, and Mayfield now will make $55 million per year on a new deal struck on the eve of the 2026 season. 49ers lose another key contributor to a season-ending injury | Niners Nation The San Francisco 49ers have another season-ending injury that happened before their season has even started. Defensive tackle Alfred Collins showed up on the injury report this week, and Kyle Shanahan later said it’s a torn patellar tendon suffered Monday . Collins will now be out for the season. This marks another season-ending injury before the season has even started. This certainly doesn’t bode well for the 49ers’ injury concerns and for Collins, who had flashes in 2025 but needed to get some consistency going in his second season as a pro. Rams’ Donald won’t travel to Australia; Garrett ‘ready to go’ | ESPN “He’s doing a great job,” McVay said. “I think he’ll be ready to go sooner rather than later, but we’re making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team. … He’s attacked this the right way, but it would have been a really quick turnaround.” McVay also said defensive end Myles Garrett, who has been dealing with swelling in his knee, will be “ready to go” in Week 1. Garrett, however, did not practice Tuesday, the team said on its official injury report. “He’s looked great,” McVay said. “We’ve been smart with Myles, like I’ve kind of told you guys, but his impact has been tremendous.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride The Chiefs’ offensive line will be ‘the five best guys’ in Week 1 But the bottom line is both options are first-year players, rookies. The rise of Benson as the potential right tackle has not inspired a lot of confidence about Moore, either. There was a lot of conversation this offseason about the Chiefs potentially needing to bolster the offensive tackle position. General manager Brett Veach and the front office did not add to that group in free agency, the draft, or the wave of undrafted free agents to close out draft weekend. Benson, signed after tryouts in rookie minicamp, is one of the Chiefs’ “best five guys” right now after one injury. It remains to be seen if that makes the front office look smart or foolish. title: Drake Maye’s debut reinforces why Matthew Stafford won MVP
summary: Drake Maye could have won last season’s MVP trophy if he had received just one more first place vote, but the Patriots quarterback’s poor play on Wednesday night against the Seahawks only reinforced why he was not in the same class as winner Matthew Stafford. Maye was at his absolute worst in the NFL’s first […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball during the second quarter of the NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Drake Maye could have won last season’s MVP trophy if he had received just one more first place vote, but the Patriots quarterback’s poor play on Wednesday night against the Seahawks only reinforced why he was not in the same class as winner Matthew Stafford. Maye was at his absolute worst in the NFL’s first game of 2026, throwing three fourth quarter interceptions, including the game-loser, as New England left the door open to blow a 10-point lead to Seattle and drop the game 13-10. It would be one thing if this was just one bad start by a great quarterback — Stafford will have bad games too — but it’s really more that Maye was left exposed again and hasn’t really performed at a replacement level since last year’s playoffs began. That’s when the Patriots stopped facing the easiest schedule that any team had faced in over 20 years and had to start putting up points against team that have good defenses. As of Wednesday’s loss, the Patriots are 0-12 with Drake Maye in the regular season against teams that have a winning record. Drake Maye is now 0-12 against teams with a winning record. — Big E (@ian693) September 10, 2026 Again, just a vote separated Maye and Stafford in the MVP race. A vote. After completing over 72% of his passes in the regular season with a 113.5 passer rating, Maye faced four of the best defenses in the NFL in the playoffs: The Chargers, Texans, Broncos, and Seahawks. He completed just 58.3% of his passes and had a passer rating of 82.2. Maye was sacked an NFL playoff record 21 times and threw four interceptions and fumbled seven times. In the Super Bowl, Maye threw for 295 yards, but much of that came in garbage time after Seattle had built a 29-0 lead. He threw two interceptions, lost a fumble, and was sacked six times. Now compare that to Matthew Stafford in three games against the Seahawks last year: 8 touchdowns 0 interceptions Over 9.5 yards per attempt in his most recent two games Facing the Seahawks on Wednesday, a defense that didn’t have star nickel Nick Emmanwori or starting strong safety Ty Okada, Maye went 0-of-4 on passes over 20 yards with three interceptions, and 3/9 passing on throws over 10 yards: Drake Maye on throws 10+ yards downfield 3/9 passing 3 interceptions but 7/8 behind the LOS 🔥 pic.twitter.com/rsUS2jpfid — Underdog (@Underdog) September 10, 2026 He was a check down charlie and this all came after an entire offseason spent by New England of trying to build an offense around Maye that would finally click against better teams, not just the Jets and Dolphins. That included upgrading the offensive line with signings like Alijah Vera-Tucker, and bringing in new weapons like A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. And although Brown did leave the game in the second half with an ankle injury, Maye still wasn’t playing that well before he got hurt. Basically A.J. Brown was the offense prior to his injury, not Drake Maye. It is also true that Doubs dropped an easy pass that should have been a big gain for Maye. But when is Maye going to pick up the offense? He’s supposed to be a dual threat quarterback and an accurate passer with a big arm, that’s why the Patriots drafted him third overall in 2024. At times, he’s even lived up to it. Or appeared to. But at no point last season did it really feel like he belonged in the MVP conversation. Not against the easiest schedule in the NFL. Drake "The Schedule" Maye since last season 2026: DREW LOCK L 2025: G. Smith L T. Tagovailoa W C.Ward W M. Penix W D. Gabriel W S. Rattler W J. Flacco W B. Cook W B. Young W J. Stidham W Q. Ewers W J. Fields W T. Huntley W pic.twitter.com/D5K0OYBh8u — BetMGM 🦁 (@BetMGM) September 10, 2026 Drake Maye's last 5 games: 7 TD : 11 turnovers 7 INTs, 4 fumbles lost 24 sacks taken 143 yards lost on sacks 6.6 yds/att 5.6 net yards/att pic.twitter.com/NdxI32L4Rb — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) September 10, 2026 So it’s fine to say that you like Drake Maye as an up and coming player (I do), or that the Patriots had lesser weapons and offensive support around the quarterback last season than the Rams (they did), but “MVP”? MVP??? Albert Breer voted for him . Gregg Rosenthal said Maye should be the MVP. Field Yates called Maye the MVP, as did most of ESPN. And almost 50% of the AP’s panel of 50 writers who vote for MVP and other awards picked Maye. It’s hard to believe that almost happened and would have been the only reason Stafford didn’t get his only MVP award so far. Because of Drake Maye and the easiest schedule in the NFL. Wednesday just reinforced why the AP and the NFL got so lucky that it didn’t.

title: Rams were lucky to miss out on Maxx Crosby, A.J. Brown trades
summary: The Los Angeles Rams explored trades for both Maxx Crosby and A.J. Brown in the spring, according to Tom Pelissero. Those deals may have improved the team at the time, but by having the ammunition to trade for Myles Garrett in the summer, the Rams were able to get two-for-the-price-of-one when the move compelled Aaron […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams explored trades for both Maxx Crosby and A.J. Brown in the spring, according to Tom Pelissero . Those deals may have improved the team at the time, but by having the ammunition to trade for Myles Garrett in the summer , the Rams were able to get two-for-the-price-of-one when the move compelled Aaron Donald to come out of retirement . Would he have done the same for Crosby? Not even the Las Vegas Raiders are confident yet that Crosby’s knee will hold up for a 17-game season. Pelissero: Rams strongly considered acquiring Maxx Crosby this spring. pic.twitter.com/fHb3tIJeDQ — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 9, 2026 The Raiders traded Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens for two first-round picks, including 14th overall in 2026, but nixed the deal after a physical. By most accounts, Crosby has survived training camp without any health scares and is ready for Week 1, but the team was cautious with him in the preseason as he was the only starter held out of the games entirely. Ironically, Myles Garrett’s knee has been a much bigger story in training camp than Crosby’s. But that’s only as of now and not necessarily the case later. The Rams have to feel great about where their defense is at with Garrett and Donald in the fold, as well as Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Although Watson has just popped up on the injury report too . Offensively, we knew the A.J. Brown story for a long time. The Rams reportedly would have still traded for McDuffie and eventually Garrett, but where would the money come from? L.A. is already tight up against the 2026 salary cap and Brown currently has a $7 million cap hit with the New England Patriots. And it cost New England a 2028 first-round pick to make that deal. Reports had the Rams giving up Davante Adams, which would help offset the money. But no team is trading Brown for Adams straight-up. A first-round pick likely still had to be involved. What would the Rams look like with Crosby, Brown? Matthew Stafford would have Puka Nacua and A.J. Brown as his top targets. The defense would have Crosby starting a defensive line without Aaron Donald (probably) or Myles Garrett. Instead, the Rams have their 2028 first-round pick, which they could still use to entice a team to trade them a wide receiver before the deadline if that’s something that L.A. really wants. Maxx Crosby would have been an interesting acquisition and fans wouldn’t have even been aware of what it would end up costing them in the future. It would just be “The Rams got Maxx Crosby!” and nothing more. No talk of Garrett or Donald. Instead they can look back. Both on who they did get…and who they did not get.

title: Rams-49ers keys to victory: Keep Christian McCaffrey in check
summary: The Rams and 49ers will open the 2026 NFL season against each other in a highly anticipated NFC West showdown. The game is scheduled for Thursday, Sept. 10, at 5:35 p.m. PT (8:35 p.m. ET) at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia, with the matchup streaming on Netflix. The rivalry has been competitive recently. Over the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 09: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers carries the ball against Quentin Lake #37 of the Los Angeles Rams during the second quarter of an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Rams and 49ers will open the 2026 NFL season against each other in a highly anticipated NFC West showdown. The game is scheduled for Thursday, Sept. 10, at 5:35 p.m. PT (8:35 p.m. ET) at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia, with the matchup streaming on Netflix. The rivalry has been competitive recently. Over the past three seasons, the teams have split their six regular-season meetings, with each team going 3-3. Most recently, the Rams dominated San Francisco 42-26 in Week 10 of 2025, after the 49ers had defeated Los Angeles earlier that season. That recent history adds another layer to an already important division matchup. With both teams entering 2026 expecting to compete for the NFC West, the season opener in Melbourne could set the tone for what should be another tightly contested rivalry. Key #1: Rams Offense – Run, Run, Run If the Rams want to put Matthew Stafford and the offense in position to succeed against the 49ers, the formula could be simple: run, run and run some more . San Francisco has a new defensive coordinator in Raheem Morris, who knows Sean McVay extremely well from their time together in Los Angeles and Washington. Morris was the head coach of the Atlanta Falcons last season, and Atlanta handed the Rams an upset loss in Week 17. Stafford struggled in that matchup, throwing three interceptions, although Los Angeles was also missing several key offensive pieces. However, that game also exposed a potential weakness in Morris’ defense. The Rams actually ran the ball extremely well, piling up 115 rushing yards on just 20 attempts. Kyren Williams led the way with 13 carries for 92 yards, averaging an impressive 7.1 yards per attempt. McVay should take notice. Rather than immediately trying to attack through the air, the Rams need to force Morris and San Francisco’s defense to respect the run. Establishing Kyren Williams and Blake Corum could force the 49ers to bring additional defenders toward the line of scrimmage. That, in turn, could create the passing lanes Stafford needs to attack the second and third levels of the defense, where Puka Nacua can make plays. Key #2: Rams Defense – Limit Christian McCaffrey If the Rams want to beat the 49ers, one of their biggest defensive priorities will be limiting Christian McCaffrey. The star running back has proven capable of hurting Los Angeles in multiple ways, particularly as a receiver out of the backfield. That was evident when the teams met in Week 5 last season. McCaffrey gave the Rams’ defense problems through the air, catching eight passes for 82 yards and a touchdown. His ability to create mismatches against linebackers and defensive backs made him difficult to contain and allowed San Francisco to consistently keep the ball in his hands. The Rams had a much better blueprint when the teams met again in Week 10. Los Angeles kept McCaffrey below 100 combined yards despite giving him 20 total touches. He carried the ball 12 times while adding eight receptions, but the Rams prevented him from turning those opportunities into a major impact. Most importantly, McCaffrey failed to find the end zone in that matchup. That performance should serve as a blueprint for the Rams. Completely eliminating McCaffrey is unrealistic, but limiting his explosive plays, particularly in the passing game, could go a long way toward slowing down San Francisco’s offense and giving Los Angeles a chance to win.

title: Super Bowl LXI will be between…
summary: The 2026 NFL season is finally here, and the race to Super Bowl LXI is wide open. While several teams have legitimate championship aspirations, 10 stand out as the strongest contenders in their respective conferences. Here are the top five teams in the AFC and NFC — and why each could make a run to […]
full_text: The 2026 NFL season is finally here, and the race to Super Bowl LXI is wide open. While several teams have legitimate championship aspirations, 10 stand out as the strongest contenders in their respective conferences. Here are the top five teams in the AFC and NFC — and why each could make a run to Los Angeles for Super Bowl LXI. AFC 1. Buffalo Bills The Buffalo Bills remain one of the AFC’s safest championship bets because of Josh Allen. Buffalo has consistently been in the postseason conversation, and Allen gives the Bills the type of elite quarterback play needed to survive the AFC playoff gauntlet. With a roster built to compete on both sides of the football, Buffalo has a strong foundation entering the 2026 season. The biggest question is whether the Bills can finally turn their regular-season success into a Super Bowl appearance. 2. Los Angeles Chargers Justin Herbert enters his age 28 season with sky high expectations. He has Mike McDaniel as his offensive coordinator and Jim Harbaugh as a quarterback whisperer. But will Los Angeles have the defense to get deep into January and February? 3. Cincinnati Bengals Whenever Joe Burrow is healthy, the Bengals have to be considered a championship threat. Cincinnati possesses one of the league’s most dangerous passing attacks, giving the team the ability to win high-scoring games against virtually anyone. The question will be whether the Bengals can consistently complement that offense with enough defense. 4. Baltimore Ravens The Ravens are built for January football. Lamar Jackson gives Baltimore an incredibly difficult quarterback to defend, while the team’s physical identity and ability to control games on the ground make them a dangerous postseason opponent. Baltimore also has plenty of experience playing in meaningful games. If the Ravens can put everything together under their new-look coaching staff, they have the talent to represent the AFC. 5. Jacksonville Jaguars The Jaguars have a budding quarterback in Trevor Lawrence who started to make “MVP rumblings” at the end of the 2025 season if it were not for Matthew Stafford. Travis Hunter enters year 2 as the defense’s main chess piece. NFC 1. Los Angeles Rams The Los Angeles Rams enter the season with the strongest Super Bowl odds in the entire NFL. Matthew Stafford returns to lead Sean McVay’s offense, while the addition of Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald give the defense an extraordinary collection of talent. The Rams are currently among the league’s clear Super Bowl favorites. With Puka Nacua and an offense capable of producing explosive plays, Los Angeles has the balance necessary for a championship run. 2. Seattle Seahawks The defending Super Bowl champions cannot be ignored. Seattle returns with the confidence of having already climbed the mountain, and its defense remains the foundation of the team. The Seahawks also have a balanced roster and an established identity under Mike Macdonald. Repeating is incredibly difficult, but Seattle has earned its place among the NFC favorites. 3. Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles remain one of the NFC’s most talented rosters. Philadelphia has the physicality, offensive weapons and defensive talent necessary to compete with anyone. Saquon Barkley remains a major offensive weapon, while the health of the offensive line could be one of the biggest factors in determining the Eagles’ ceiling. 4. San Francisco 49ers The 49ers have too much talent to overlook. Kyle Shanahan’s offense remains one of the NFL’s most creative systems, and San Francisco has playmakers at virtually every important position. If the 49ers can stay healthy and get consistent quarterback play, they have the roster to make another deep postseason run. 5. Dallas Cowboys The Cowboys enter the season with plenty of pressure but also plenty of talent. Dak Prescott remains capable of leading an explosive offense, while Dallas has the star power necessary to compete in the NFC. The biggest question is whether the Cowboys can finally translate their regular-season potential into postseason success. If they do, they could become a legitimate threat to reach Super Bowl LXI. Pick: Ravens vs. Rams The Super Bowl logo theory tells me to go with the Jaguars. Maybe it’s the thought of general managers James Gladstone and Les Snead bringing their franchises to the title game. Or previous coaches Liam Coen and Sean McVay dialing up their offenses against one another. Jacksonville took the league by surprise last year and nearly advanced to the divisional round after a back and forth with the Buffalo Bills. But the emergence of Baltimore makes too much sense with two-time MVP Lamar Jackson recouping his form while leaning on Derrick Henry. First year head coach Jesse Minter retools the defense to handle quality offenses like the Bills, Chargers, Broncos, and Jaguars. Meanwhile, the Rams have had eyes set on Super Bowl LXI since its loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship this past January. They know its within their grasp again… Score: Baltimore Ravens 23, Los Angeles Rams 29 Super Bowl LXI Champion: Los Angeles Rams. The Rams have been among the most widely backed teams entering the season, and this prediction ultimately comes down to believing their combination of Stafford, McVay, Garrett, Donald and Nacua is too much to overcome when the biggest games arrive.

title: Rams defense gets chance to shine without Aaron Donald
summary: Aaron Donald will not be suiting up in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers and on one hand, that’s disappointing for fans of the Los Angeles Rams. On the other hand, if the Rams can excel or win without Donald, then that bodes even better for his eventual return to the lineup. It’s only […]
full_text: Aaron Donald will not be suiting up in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers and on one hand, that’s disappointing for fans of the Los Angeles Rams. On the other hand, if the Rams can excel or win without Donald, then that bodes even better for his eventual return to the lineup. It’s only one game, but it’s a massive opportunity for L.A. to get a divisional win in an international game and set the stage and show this team has what it takes to compete out of the gate. It’s assumed that this defense should be good with AD, but he won’t be there Thursday so what will this defense be without him? You can bet AD will be watching. What Aaron Donald’s Week 1 Absence Means for the Rams Defense (si.com) “While the Rams will be disappointed to not have Donald available, they are playing the long game and want to ensure he is in game shape before he takes the field. The Rams have been preparing without Donald throughout much of the summer, which won’t change how they approach Thursday’s game against the 49ers. This is also a team that’s uniquely built to manage without Donald. I think what’s cool is you have such confidence in the group that we do have with Kobie, with Fiske, with Poona Ford, with Tyler Davis,” said McVay. “It’ll add value when he’s ready to go, but being two years off retirement, he’s attacked this the right way.” The Rams do have the depth to manage without Donald against the 49ers. Donald would have certainly added a boost, but the Rams had been preparing all offseason to be without him. It wasn’t until they traded for Myles Garrett that Donald’s return became a possibility. Even then, Donald didn’t make it official until two weeks ago.“ Aaron Donald won’t travel with the L.A. Rams to Australia for Week 1 (ktla.com) “Defensive tackle Aaron Donald will not travel to Melbourne, Australia , to play in the Los Angeles Rams’ season opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Donald, who initially retired in March 2024, came out of retirement on Aug. 30 . He signed a one-year deal with the team. While Rams fans will have to wait a bit longer to see Donald back in a Rams uniform, McVay did say that defensive end Myles Garrett, who has been dealing with swelling in his knee, will be “ready to go” in Week 1, according to ESPN. Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year who has the record for most sacks in a season (23), is also considered to be one of the best defensive players of his generation. “ Rams release first injury report of Week 1: 2 starters miss practice (ramswire) “With the Los Angeles Rams playing on Friday morning in Australia, they released their first official injury report of the 2026 season on Tuesday. They practiced in Los Angeles before flying out to Melbourne , and a handful of players were either held out due to injuries or rest. Myles Garrett, who will play against the 49ers in the opener, was listed as a non-participant due to his lingering knee injury. Grant Stuard was limited with a hamstring injury, while Jaylen Watson missed practice because of a toe issue. The severity of Watson’s injury is unclear, but there have been no indications that he’s in danger of missing the opener.“ Raheem Morris used to joke that Aaron Donald would ‘get fat when he retired’ (ramswire) “ ESPN’s Sarah Barshop spoke to Morris, asking if the champion coordinator was surprised by Donald’s return. “No,” said Morris. “I mean, he always stays ready. I used to joke with him and always tell him he’s going to get fat when he retired and he always told me there’s no chance. And he’s right.” Morris’ final game with the Rams was also Donald’s final contest. In their wild-card loss to the Detroit Lions , ending their 2023 season, Morris would go on to become the head coach of the Atlanta Falcons, while Donald opted to retire.“ Sean McVay and Myles Garrett talk Week 1 expectations ahead of Thursday’s matchup against the 49ers (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay and outside linebacker Myles Garrett addressed the media ahead of Thursday’s Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. They discuss expectations around the season opener, maximizing every opportunity & more.” Rams’ Chris Shula names 2nd-year DT who’s been a ‘pleasant surprise’ (ramswire) ““The guy that really stuck out to me was Ty Hamilton,” said Shula on Monday. “I thought he did an awesome job where in camp, it was like Giff (Smith), his position coach, really challenged him to play physical, play fast, play tough. As a rookie, we thought he was kind of thinking and hesitating a little bit too much, and you saw that show up on the tape. He was definitely a pleasant surprise for us, for sure.” Loaded Rams Carry Highest Ceiling, Highest Stakes in the NFL (sports.yahoo) “That talent cuts both ways. Health and chemistry will decide whether the Rams hit their ceiling or floor. Ceiling: 16-1 and Super Bowl Champions Injuries are the Rams’ biggest threat. They strike randomly and have doomed many Super Bowl contenders. Los Angeles does what it can to prevent that, managing practice schedules and giving rest when needed.“ NFL Power Rankings, Week 1: Cowboys rising after defensive makeover; Bears drop out of top 10 (nfl.com) “Am I worried about the statuses of Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua ? Mildly, although Garrett practiced Sunday , and Nacua appears to be on track to play against San Francisco in the opener in Australia. Oh, and Aaron Donald is back on the team now. No movement for the Rams here, but a big test awaits them Down Under.“ Patriots vs. Seahawks: Five must-know storylines for Wednesday’s 2026 NFL Kickoff Game (nfl.com) “Our national nightmare is over. After a 212-day break, the NFL officially returns on Wednesday night, with the New England Patriots visiting the Seattle Seahawks to kick off the 2026 season in an instant rematch of Super Bowl LX . This is the 12th regular-season game between teams that met in the previous Super Bowl, per NFL Research, and the reigning champs are 8-3 in the previous 11 such rematches. Last we saw these two squads on the same field, Seattle’s defense and running game dominated to the tune of a 29-13 victory. Can the Patriots pull off an upset, with marquee offseason acquisition A.J. Brown in tow this time around?“ 49ers catching early breaks — including avoiding Rams’ Aaron Donald (sports.yahoo) “ Kyle Shanahan went out of his way to avoid providing injury updates after the 49ers ‘ first practice in Australia, cleverly pointing out that they were a full day ahead of the Rams . On the flip side, when Aaron Donald was asked about his status after rejoining 11-on-11 practice for the first time this week, all he could muster was a big smile and that he was “feeling good.” Both sides dropped the act Tuesday. And the Niners clearly came out in the more favorable position once the dust of the NFC West rivals’ gamesmanship settled. They’ll have Nick Bosa and George Kittle — and will only have to worry about one future Hall of Famer ( Myles Garrett ) lining up opposite them.“ Comment of the Day: “2 things need to happen for Darnold to maintain his 2025 experience : The O-line needs to keep Darnold upright and clean to make his best reads/throws ( Jared Goff Syndrome) Seattle needs their running game to play to the same levels as 2025, Darnold alone on offense will have dl/dbs with their ears pinned back in mad dog attack ( see Rams/Vikings playoff game )“ -Watcher Of The Skies Fanpost of the Day:

title: Kirk Cousins buys Las Vegas Raiders some, but not much, goodwill in NFL Power rankings heading into 2026 season
summary: Week 1 of the 2026 season is the start of a new era for the Las Vegas Raiders, with Klint Kubiak making his debut as head coach while having a 38-year-old starting quarterback. Of course, we all know that Kirk Cousins is just a placeholder for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. But Cousins’ presence […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 1 of the 2026 season is the start of a new era for the Las Vegas Raiders , with Klint Kubiak making his debut as head coach while having a 38-year-old starting quarterback. Of course, we all know that Kirk Cousins is just a placeholder for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. But Cousins’ presence in Las Vegas is buying the Raiders a little credibility in NFL Power Rankings heading into the campaign. Although not much, since this is widely considered year one of the rebuild in Sin City. Bleacher Report 26. Las Vegas Raiders Coming off a 3-14 campaign, the Las Vegas Raiders should be able to build early momentum in their home opener against the Miami Dolphins, who are also in the early phases of a rebuild. Kirk Cousins played in new head coach Klint Kubiak’s system during his time with the Minnesota Vikings in 2021. He should be solid behind a revamped offensive line that features three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum. While the Raiders’ offense will be much improved, their secondary will be inexperienced and susceptible to big plays. First-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard is a question mark. His ability to put the young defensive backs in spots to succeed could make or break the defense. — Moe Moton As evidence to Moton’s point about Cousins, it was pretty clear in the preseason that the Raiders’ offense functioned more smoothly and efficiently with the veteran behind center. All three of the drives he led last month ended in points: a touchdown and two field goals. Obviously, things will be more difficult now that the games count, but it’s hard to argue that Cousins doesn’t give the team the best chance to win right now. Defensively, yes, Las Vegas does have a lot of young players in the secondary, leading to plenty of question marks. However, several defensive backs were standouts during training camp to provide some optimism heading into the regular season. The Athletic 27. Las Vegas Raiders Mock’s projected win total: 6.2 The past two seasons did not go great for Kirk Cousins after leaving Minnesota, and this is probably his last shot as a starter. In reality, this is about how long he can hold off a switch to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The good news for them after camp is that Ashton Jeanty’s ankle injury wasn’t serious enough to land him on IR, but rookie edge rusher Keyron Crawford is already done for the season due to an ankle injury. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall The projected win total here is interesting because the gambling line has widely been set at 5.5 wins, meaning The Athletic’s model is saying to take the over. Getting the ‘W’ this weekend will be paramount for that, though, because the Raiders’ schedule toughens up with road matchups against the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints over the next two weeks. The Saints are a team to look out for in 2026 after finishing last season strong, winning five out of their last eight games. NFL.com 29. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 31 As expected, Kirk Cousins will begin 2026 as the Raiders’ starter. It’s still safe to assume No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza will see the field before long, though Cousins could delay the passing of the torch by producing quickly. Regardless, I expect Raider Nation to find some joy in the Week 1 meeting with the Dolphins, which would be nice for that fan base. — Nick Shook Expect the Cousins-Mendoza chatter to be a talking point when it comes to the Raiders every week until the switch happens, especially if the team is losing games. As Shook points out, the Silver and Black should be able to get this one, though, because the Dolphins might have the worst roster in the NFL. But if Las Vegas gets upset on Sunday, buckle up because it’s going to be a long 17 weeks to finish out the campaign. ESPN 27. Las Vegas Raiders Post-draft ranking: 28 Milestone to watch: Brock Bowers can surpass Jason Witten (188) for the most receptions by a tight end under the age of 24 in NFL history. Bowers needs only 13 catches to reach this milestone, and it wouldn’t be surprising if he did it in the season opener against the Dolphins. Bowers has recorded at least 10 receptions in a game on five occasions, most recently in Week 9 of 2025 against the Jaguars (12). He also had 13 catches against the Dolphins in Week 11 of 2024. Bowers has been QB Kirk Cousins’ go-to target throughout training camp, so expect the third-year tight end to be targeted often in Week 1. — Ryan McFadden For context, Bowers’ birthday is Dec. 13. So, even if he doesn’t surpass Witten this weekend, the 23-year-old should be able to do it by the end of the month. That’s barring an injury, of course. Expect him to be the focal point of Kubiak’s offense, especially since the Raiders’ receiving corps leaves something to be desired. The Ringer 26. Las Vegas Raiders The Raiders are proof that hiring a new head coach and drafting a quarterback can buy a franchise a healthy amount of goodwill, but I’m not buying into the hope. This roster is in a weird spot, and I don’t think this franchise has as much of a plan as its ownership lets on. Las Vegas spent above market value on multiple free agents, lost expected draft capital in the failed trade of edge rusher Maxx Crosby, and has far-below-average talent at receiver and defensive back entering the season. The only real intrigue I see is Fernando Mendoza’s path to supplanting veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins as starter. If the Raiders are 1-3 or worse after the opening month, will their supposed discipline in letting Mendoza learn from the sideline hold, or will head coach Klint Kubiak want a look at the future of his franchise sooner? — Diante Lee This is an ‘interesting’ way to look at Las Vegas’ offseason… Did John Spytek overspend on a handful of free agents? Sure, but he also had to because no player who was worth bringing in would take anything less than top dollar to sign with an organization that was 3-14 the year before and has had four head coaches in as many years. Also, this wording presents the Crosby trade as if the Raiders are the ones who pulled out of it. I don’t understand how that situation can be held against them. I’ll concede the point that the Silver and Black have an underwhelming receiving corps. That goes without question, and the secondary certainly doesn’t have a lot of proven talent in it. However, the defensive backfield is filled with young players who have enormous potential. Jermod McCoy is a great example of that, and he might not even see the field much to begin the season. I respect Lee and his opinions on the game. But, obviously, we see this situation pretty differently.
