title: Prognosticating the 2026 Jets Pt.2
summary: Last week, I wrote here about the positive story that I thought was plausible for the New York Jets in 2026. The idea was that this young, overhauled roster could overachieve expectations, get some positive regression to the mean with their turnover luck, and have strong offensive line play raise the floor of the entire […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Xavier Newman #65 and Anez Cooper #72 of the New York Jets look on against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, I wrote here about the positive story that I thought was plausible for the New York Jets in 2026. The idea was that this young, overhauled roster could overachieve expectations, get some positive regression to the mean with their turnover luck, and have strong offensive line play raise the floor of the entire offense. I still think that story is very much in play. However, like most things with the Jets, there is always another side to the equation. There is also a pretty easy path to this team going poorly and somehow failing to meet expectations once again. So, like I did last week with the positive spin, I want to lay out the negative story. What does it look like if things go wrong for this team? To me, it starts with three members of the organization: the quarterback, the offensive playcaller, and the defensive playcaller. There is very little optimism surrounding Geno Smith, Frank Reich, and head coach Aaron Glenn, and for good reason. The last time we saw all three in the NFL, they did not just underperform at their respective jobs. They performed horribly. Geno Smith and Frank Reich Let’s start with the quarterback and offensive coordinator duo. Going into the season, I would not blame any media pundit or ranking that had Geno Smith and Frank Reich near the bottom of the league. While I do think there is a positive story you can tell about Geno, it is just as easy to construct a negative one. Geno Smith was simply awful last season. I don’t need to harp on it too much as everyone knows the details, but a 34.1 QBR and 84.7 passer rating are horrible numbers in today’s NFL. He ranked 29th in EPA per play and 27th in Success Rate. Even though his accuracy remained relatively decent from a CPOE perspective, he still threw 17 interceptions in 15 games. The number I have not heard much about that stood out as well, was that his ADOT tanked as well. He ranked 29th in that metric. Now, the surrounding cast in Las Vegas was atrocious. The playcaller was also atrocious. There were plenty of things working against Geno, and the hope is that situation should be significantly better here. But even still, I am not quite sure it is as simple as assuming he will bounce back. The first glimpse we got of Geno this preseason left me cautiously optimistic. His athleticism looked solid and the arm still appeared to be there. But he is also going to turn 36 this year. If Geno were 30 years old, I would be much more willing to chalk up last year’s production to the environment around him and some things that were outside of his control. At 35, though, it is a legitimate question to ask whether Geno simply cannot be a starting quarterback anymore. And then there is Frank Reich. Reich is, by NFL standards, ancient. He is 64 years old and has not called plays at the NFL level in more than three years. And simply put, his last two stops were horrific. In 2022 and 2023, as head coach of the Indianapolis Colts and Carolina Panthers, respectively, Reich was fired midway through both seasons. The talent situation was not great in either place, particularly in Carolina where he was working with an unplayable Bryce Young at the time. But the offenses were still horrific. To Reich’s credit, there was a point in time when he was regarded as one of the better offensive minds in football. His work from 2014 through 2021 with the Chargers, Eagles, and early in his tenure with the Colts was legitimately impressive. The last time we saw him as an NFL offensive coordinator, he helped coordinate a Super Bowl-winning Eagles offense with Carson Wentz and Nick Foles. But that was years ago. It is hard to overlook the possibility that the game has simply moved past him. The one thing that gives me some optimism is that, by all accounts, Reich is a heavy proponent of analytics. That makes me more hopeful that he will be willing to change and adapt than your typical veteran coach who has become stuck in his ways. Still, there is a very real negative scenario here. As fans, we are excited about the young offensive line. We are excited about the young pass catchers. But while we like the idea of some of these players, we still have no idea exactly how good this supporting cast is going to be. It would not stun me at all to look up in late October and realize the Jets offense is once again near the bottom of the league. Put it all together and you have a pretty simple formula for disaster: a bottom-tier quarterback paired with a bottom-tier playcaller, with a young supporting cast that isn’t quite ready to carry the offense. That is absolutely on the table. Aaron Glenn and the Defense Now let’s get to the defense. As I wrote in the positive spin article, I actually like some of the moves the Jets made. This is a completely different unit, and while I am optimistic about the Jets getting some positive regression to the mean from a turnover perspective, it is still hard to overlook just how poor this defense was last year under Aaron Glenn. I’ve defended Glenn before, and I still think there is some truth to the argument that there is only so much a coach can do when the talent is that poor, which it was for stretches last season. But the thing that keeps me up at night is that pretty much from the beginning, the Glenn/Wilks defense was a disaster. It is one thing for a defense to become horrific by the end of the season when you are playing JAGs and half your roster is injured. It is another thing entirely when the defense is struggling mightily even with legitimate talent on the field, including players like Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams. I do think the Jets improved the talent on this unit. But there are still two major questions aside from the coaching. Do some of these older players have anything left in the tank? And how is this secondary going to hold up? Demario Davis, David Onyemata, and Minkah Fitzpatrick were three established veterans brought in to raise the floor of this defense and provide some stability. I personally thought all three moves were relatively fine, particularly because the Jets did not make huge long-term investments in any of them. Having floor stabilizers after what we watched last year was more than needed. But it is certainly not a lock that all three players simply continue playing at their previous level. Then there is the secondary, where there are more questions than answers right now. AZ Thomas is currently one of the starting boundary corners and, frankly, we have no idea how he is going to look this season. There’s hardly any data or film on him at the NFL level due to his injuries and inexperience last year. Brandon Stephens is currently the No. 1, but in an ideal world, given how volatile he can be, he is probably better suited as an average No. 2 corner. At nickel, Jarvis Brownlee and D’Angelo Ponds appear likely to split time. Brownlee has had flashes, but has also been a bit of a mess throughout his career. I loved Ponds as a prospect, but that doesn’t mean he’s going to be a great NFL player. He would be far from the first rookie corner to struggle mightily in his first season. There’s a real scenario here where this secondary is one of the worst in the league again from a coverage perspective. You’ll need David Bailey to be a game-changer from the get-go at Edge. While I think he very well can be, again, it’s far from a guarantee. Where Does This Lead Us Like I said, this is the depressing article. If everything I laid out above, or heck even 75% of it, were to happen this year the Jets will once again be near the bottom of the league. A poor offense led by an overmatched quarterback and play-caller and a defense that cannot hold up in the back end with a lame duck head coach is…

title: Why the Jets’ Addition of Geno Smith Is an Important Test for Aaron Glenn and Darren Mougey
summary: The Jets didn’t quite get Geno Smith for free this offseason, but it was darned close. Gang Green reacquired its once-second round Draft pick in a trade that involved swapping a sixth round pick for a seventh round pick and tacking a $3 million sweetener onto Smith’s contract. It was a long fall for a […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets in action during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets didn’t quite get Geno Smith for free this offseason, but it was darned close. Gang Green reacquired its once-second round Draft pick in a trade that involved swapping a sixth round pick for a seventh round pick and tacking a $3 million sweetener onto Smith’s contract. It was a long fall for a quarterback who just one offseason earlier had been traded for a third round pick. Smith’s year with the Las Vegas Raiders was ugly, and his value fell accordingly. It speaks volumes about how low the regard was for Geno’s Smith’s level of play that the fact the acquisitions required even the seven pick swap and the $3 million contract boost were mild surprises. The Raiders are picking up the tab for most of Smith’s salary. You read that right. When the Raiders take the field to face the Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 1, they for all intents and purposes will be paying Geno Smith to play against them. In this sense, it doesn’t seem like Aaron Glenn and Darren Mougey have much riding on Smith’s play this season. If he bounces back and refinds his Seattle form, the Jets got competency at the quarterback position for the NFL equivalent of pocket change. In the event he fails, few resources were spent. The Jets are sitting on three first round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and should be in great position to land a top quarterback prospect. I do believe quite a bit rides on Smith’s play this season, however, and it has to do both with the past and future of the franchise. A year ago the Jets gave Justin Fields a two year contract with $30 million in guarantees to leave the Pittsburgh Steelers. To say the deal aged poorly would be an understatement. Fields posted a QBR of 38.7 and was benched midseason. Smith himself was the only qualifying quarterback to post a lower QBR in 2025. The Jets dealt Fields to the Kansas City Chiefs in the offseason, and the roles were reversed. The Jets had to accept a late round pick swap and absorb most of the salary to get out of a quarterback mistake. My take on all of this is a bit nuanced so I hope you will stay with me. I don’t blame the Jets for signing Fields. Their options after the Aaron Rodgers experiment failed were limited. Fields was a former first round pick who had shown flashes of high end play. The only other option available to the team who fit that description was Daniel Jones, who likely had no interest in returning to New York after an unsuccessful tenure with the Giants at the start of his career. To an extent, I don’t even blame the Jets for giving Fields the money. Unless you are taking a quarterback off the scrap heap like Smith, a $20 million salary for a veteran quarterback is on the extreme low end in the NFL of today. The $30 million in guarantees were certainly rich for a player with as thin of a resume as Fields. But according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , the Steelers made a push to keep Fields that was in the ballpark of what the Jets offered so it isn’t like they bid against themselves. And contracts are always forward looking. You should never pay a player for what he did in the past. The pay should be for what a player is going to do in the future. This is where it falls apart for me. As we know, Fields failed in New York. Most of the blame has to go to Fields. There is a reason he is now on his fourth team in four years. He simply hasn’t been consistent enough as an NFL quarterback. With that said, I’m not sure how the Jets thought Fields would grow into a $30 million player putting him into the system they eventually ran. At the time of the signing, I figured there was a plan to run an unconventional offense based on Fields’ skills. Fields has been a work in progress as a passer since he stepped onto an NFL field, but he was always one of the most dynamic running quarterbacks in the league. My guess was that they would lean into that, calling designed quarterback runs at a league leading rate. They could also simplify concepts by giving Fields a heavy diet of run pass options and screens. With resources limited, finding quality receivers to put around Garrett Wilson was always going to be a heavy lift. Still maybe they could find some upside plays in free agency, particularly quick separators since Fields is averse to tight window passes. And maybe the coaching staff could get Fields to improve just a little bit playing from the pocket. The odds were never great, but that would have been a legitimate plan to turn Fields into a $30 million quarterback. Instead, we got the opposite . The Jets had Fields run at a lower rate than his previous teams, Chicago and Pittsburgh. They didn’t lean into simplified concepts. And their wide receiver group after Garrett Wilson contained journeymen with no upside like Josh Reynolds, Allen Lazard, and Tyler Johnson. The only young receiver added was Arian Smith, who even at the point he was selected looked like a massive reach in the fourth round. Smith has done little to change that perception. Justin Fields probably wouldn’t have panned out either way. His game as currently constructed is too flawed to have success as an NFL quarterback for the long haul. The suggested steps I mentioned are band aids. There’s only so much you can do to try and work around a quarterback who is fundamentally flawed as a pocket passer. The thing is the Jets didn’t even try to work around Fields’ limitations to get a better result. They took a guy who couldn’t play in a conventional NFL offense and guaranteed him $30 million to play in a conventional NFL offense. If the Jets had given Fields that money and tried to tailor something to him, it probably wouldn’t have worked. It probably would have still been too much money. But there at least would have been some coherence to what they were trying. Fields was never good enough to be a quality starting quarterback in the NFL. Unsurprisingly he regressed under those conditions. This was a massive organizational whiff from top to bottom. Nobody can escape blame from Aaron Glenn to Darren Mougey to Tanner Engstrand (who ultimately did pay for it with his job). A team needs to be able to know what traits are needed from a quarterback to run its system, which quarterbacks have those traits, and how much those traits are worth. The Jets may not have paid much for Geno Smith, but it was clear from the outset of the offseason that he was their top choice. This wasn’t a case of Geno being the last quarterback available when the music stopped. They aggressively pursued him when free agency began, and there was probably a reason for that. The team’s decision makers made it clear to friendly reporters that Smith was definitively their top option. Looking into the not too distant future, the Jets have those three first round picks in 2027. One of those picks is likely to be used on a quarterback. When the Jets make that pick, the ability of their primary decision makers will be tested. Can they find a prospect who has the tools they need? Geno Smith doesn’t need to be great this year. In fact, even a reversion to something resembling his 2024 campaign would give the Jets one of their top quarterback seasons in the last decade and a half. There’s something else on the line. It would be nice to have some evidence going into that 2027 Draft that the people running the Jets actually know how to target a quarterback. What happened with Fields from top to bottom has to provide pause. Smith himself is coming off an awful season in Las Vegas. That’s why he was available at such a cheap price. If the Jets correctly identified that Geno’s 2025 struggles were a matter of infrastructure, and he bounces back it would be very encouraging. If Smith continues on the trajectory of decline he showed with the…

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles were featured in last year’s NFL Kickoff Game as the reigning Super Bowl LIX champions in a win over the Dallas Cowboys. They were not featured in this year’s NFL Kickoff Game as the reigning Super Bowl LX champions in a win over the New England Patriots. But there were two injury […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots reacts after being injured in a play against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles were featured in last year’s NFL Kickoff Game as the reigning Super Bowl LIX champions in a win over the Dallas Cowboys. They were not featured in this year’s NFL Kickoff Game as the reigning Super Bowl LX champions in a win over the New England Patriots. But there were two injury developments from Wednesday night that are relevant to the Eagles. 1) A.J. Brown is hurt The former Eagles wide receiver logged three receptions for 26 yards (plus he drew a defensive pass interference penalty on a bad Drake Maye underthrow that should’ve been a touchdown) against the Seahawks before suffering an ankle injury that ruled him out of the game. Underthrown flea flicker to a wide open AJ Brown Draws a 34-yard PI pic.twitter.com/ydlxjfgDkq — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 10, 2026 The severity of Brown’s injury is currently unclear. His missed time is of interest to the Eagles not only because he used to play for the team … but because, via the Brown trade, Philly owns the most favorable of two 2027 fifth-round picks from either the Pats or the Chicago Bears. If Brown has to miss time and the Patriots struggle further, the Eagles could benefit in the form of improved draft pick compensation. AJ Brown was injured on this play right here. Main concern is mechanism -Eversion of the ankle -Where AJ Brown grabs his ankle (high) The worry would be for a High ankle sprain. Timeline to return is severity dependent Grade I: 2-3 weeks Grade II: 4-6 weeks pic.twitter.com/nHLOjGnU11 — Dr. Evan Jeffries, DPT (@GameInjuryDoc) September 10, 2026 2) The Seahawks might need a quarterback?! Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury early in this game. His backup, Drew Lock, came in and went 16/22 for 187 yards (8.5 average), one touchdown, zero interceptions, and a 113.3 passer rating. Lock also ran for 13 yards. Maybe the Seahawks just ride with Lock if Darnold has to miss a lot of time. But what if they want to add a more proven quarterback — even if just for backup purposes — instead of having the second-year Jalen Milroe serve as QB2? Do you think the Eagles could interest them in a lightly used Andy Dalton or Tanner McKee?! I have my doubts that Seattle is clamoring for one of those two. And it’s not like the Eagles were the only team to keep four quarterbacks; there’s other potential options for Seattle, if they even want to explore the trade market. But, hey, something to keep an eye on. Bonus Eagles connections: Josh Jobe (while covering Mack Hollins!) sealed the Seahawks’ win with a game-ending interception. It would’ve been better for the Eagles if Seattle lost … but it’s hard to be too torn up about a Pats loss. Thus ends the worst game Drake Maye has played since the last game he played pic.twitter.com/fiPKRkX9CL — Shane Haff (@ShaneHaffNFL) September 10, 2026 What an unbelievable catch by Josh Jobe to seal the game. pic.twitter.com/kDy7KNILc6 — Shane Haff (@ShaneHaffNFL) September 10, 2026

title: Eagles Injury Report: Jonathan Greenard and Eli Stowers limited
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week (and first of the 2026 NFL season!) on Wednesday in advance of their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles listed ZERO players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE. Always a good thing to have every player on the roster (and practice squad) […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 27: Jonathan Greenard #52 and Nolan Smith Jr. #3 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on May 27, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week (and first of the 2026 NFL season!) on Wednesday in advance of their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles listed ZERO players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE . Always a good thing to have every player on the roster (and practice squad) available to participate in practice. The Eagles are as close to being as healthy as you could realistically hope them to be entering this year’s campaign. The Eagles listed two players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Jonathan Greenard and Eli Stowers. We previously noted that Greenard returned to practice after missing all of training camp due to a pec strain. The Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reported that the Eagles want to see how Greenard fares in practice this week before determining his availability for Sunday. Even if the veteran edge rusher doesn’t suit up against the Commanders, he figures to be back in game action sooner than later. Good news for the Eagles’ defense. Stowers missed some time late in training camp due to a hamstring injury. Good to see that he’s back in action … but the 2026 second-round pick might very well be a healthy scratch on game day anyway as the fourth tight end behind Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, and E.J. Jenkins. Markel Bell was notably NOT listed on the injury report. The rookie tackle suffered thumb and leg injuries during the Eagles’ second preseason game that kept him out of training camp thereafter. With the Eagles keeping Fred Johnson on the roster, it’s not perfectly clear how the team plans to handle their tackle depth. Is Johnson the swing tackle? Is it Bell, who outperformed the incumbent veteran but lacks experience? Do the Eagles opt to have a different backup at each starting tackle position? We’ll see. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES INJURY REPORT (WEDNESDAY) LIMITED PARTICIPATION EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) WASHINGTON COMMANDERS INJURY REPORT (WEDNESDAY) The Commanders did not have any players on their 53-man roster missing from practice. They do notably have star left tackle Laremy Tunsil and starting cornerback Trey Amos on injured reserve to begin the season. Jer’Zhan Newton and Jeremy McNichols are also on IR while edge rusher Deatrich Wise Jr. is on the reserve/PUP list. And then veteran edge rusher Dorance Armstrong is suspended for the first game of the season. Washington listed three players under limited participation: top running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (his nickname is Bill, isn’t that so interesting, no one ever talks about it) and top edge rushers Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson. There doesn’t seem to be a sense that they’re in jeopardy of not playing. Washington is probably just easing them back in from missing time. We’ll see if that continues to be the case over the next two days. title: Jonathan Greenard injury news: Eagles edge rusher returns to practice ahead of Week 1
summary: Here’s some good news: Jonathan Greenard was spotted warming up for the Philadelphia Eagles’ first regular season practice as the team prepares for their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The team will issue a formal injury report later today but, for now, it’s good to see that Greenard is finally back on the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 27: Jonathan Greenard #52 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on May 27, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here’s some good news: Jonathan Greenard was spotted warming up for the Philadelphia Eagles’ first regular season practice as the team prepares for their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The team will issue a formal injury report later today but, for now, it’s good to see that Greenard is finally back on the field after missing the entirety of training camp due to the pec strain he suffered while while training. The guess here is that Greenard will be listed as a limited participant on his first day back but we’ll see ( UPDATE: Jonathan Greenard was indeed limited ) . The Inquirer’s Jeff McLane says that the team wants to see how he handles this week before determining if he’s ready to suit up on Sunday. Even if Greenard can’t play in Week 1, it seems like his return will be happening sooner than later. That much jibes with the Eagles’ decision to NOT keep him on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list, which would’ve made him ineligible to play in the first four games. It remains to be seen if Greenard, whenever he does play, is hampered by the injury that held him out for a prolonged stretch. If not, well, that’d be a great development for the Eagles’ defense! Greenard has arguably become less important to the team than he was at the time they traded for him. That’s not an indictment of him, to be clear Rather, it’s about feeling more inspired about Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith after watching them look pretty good this summer. A.J. Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie also seem like quality rotational contributors. Put it all together and there’s potential for the Eagles to have one of the stronger pass rushes in the NFL this season. … In other Eagles injury news, rookies Eli Stowers (hamstring) and Markel Bell (thumb/leg) returned to practice in some capacity.

title: Nick Sirianni says Sean Mannion is likely to call plays from the booth
summary: The Eagles are just days away from their first game of the 2026 NFL regular season, and head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters before practice on Wednesday. He talked about DeVonta Smith as a captain, what he likes from OL coach Chris Kuper and what advice he gave to OC Sean Mannion. He is […]
full_text: The Eagles are just days away from their first game of the 2026 NFL regular season, and head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters before practice on Wednesday. He talked about DeVonta Smith as a captain, what he likes from OL coach Chris Kuper and what advice he gave to OC Sean Mannion. He is notorious for keeping any perceived competitive advantage close to the vest, and that continues with him explaining he still has time before he needs to reveal who is QB2 behind Jalen Hurts. Sirianni clarified that just because they aren’t revealing who won the backup job, between Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton, doesn’t mean they haven’t made the decision behind closed doors. Later on, it was brought up that former OC Kevin Patullo shared with Dolphins new head coach Jeff Hafley that the Eagles learned a lot about the Packers defense last season thanks to compiling videos taken from fans at training camp. Sirianni smirked and sarcastically quipped that he was glad that little insight was exposed publicly. “Obviously they’re not doing that this year, or else they wouldn’t have told everybody about it.” While he might not like to give much away, just as the head coach was leaving for practice, he did reveal that OC Sean Mannion will “probably be up” in the booth to call plays for the Eagles offense in Week 1 against the Commanders. Mannion tried play-calling from both the sideline and the booth during the preseason — with the OC noting his career experience from the sideline —, but may have found a new vantage point helpful. Here’s what else Sirianni had to say: On injured players returning Sirianni wouldn’t say if Jonathan Greenard would be available for Sunday’s game, and wouldn’t even say if he would be out on the practice field Wednesday. He did explain that everyone who is trying to come back from an injury have been working their butts off to be ready. “That’s what I always admire about this group, led by our captains and our leaders, is that this team works hard. When you work hard, it’s not just on the practice field, it’s also in the film room, it’s also if you’re having to rehab an injury. [Jonathan Greenard has] worked his butt off — we’ll see where that is by the end of the week.” He was asked if they had seen enough from Makai Lemon during training camp, despite him missing three weeks, for the rookie to play Week 1. Sirianni said that he has a lot of confidence in the WR room, including Lemon, and they’re excited for what that room collectively will do. “Yeah, I think everybody is in a different spot when you go through an injury. Maybe he hasn’t had as many reps. I’m really confident in that room, all the guys in that room, including Makai. And excited about that room and the things that it will bring to our football team. I think we have a number of different guys that can make plays in that room and Makai is definitely one of those guys and looking forward to him having opportunities to be able to do that this Sunday and moving forward.” On Captain DeVonta Smith “DeVonta [Smith] always leads by example.” Sirianni went on to say that whether it’s an a walk-through, a practice, or around the facility, there’s never a moment when he’s not working on something to help him be the best version of himself each week. “I think people notice that. It’s from how [Smith] pre-habs before lifting and before practice, how he rehabs after that, and all the extra things that he does to work his craft of catching the football. He’s just relentless in his approach to getting better and I think that’s so notable.” The head coach noted that people may talk about whether or not he’s a vocal leader, but he always sees the WR grab guys and try to help them. “I know DeVonta [Smith] knows that everyone’s success on this team, equals team success, and he’s not threatened by anything there.” On OL coach Chris Kuper “I just think he’s a really good teacher. He’s had a ton of experience playing the game, and his experience as a coach — starting off at a low lever, working his way up as a coach, I always admire that. I know the guys value his experience and the way he is as a teacher. So, he’s done a nice job — he’s done a really nice job of coaching these guys and getting them all to understand what the job description in for this offense and for the offensive line. I know the guys respect him, and I’m looking forward to that product being shown on the field Sunday.” Other notables Sirianni said that Saquon Barkley is the kind of talent that can and would be successful in any scheme, and he’s confident that he’ll be able to have a good year in the Eagles’ new system. He couldn’t point to one moment in training camp that made him confident, and said it was rather doing things well consistently that showed development. The head coach said his advice to Sean Mannion as he prepares to call plays for the first time in a regular season game, was to have a plan for every situation and be convicted in the decisions he makes on game day. That plan isn’t always perfect and will need adjusted, but the main thing is having a plan for as much as possible. Sirianni said that the pair has been working relentlessly to make sure they’re on the same page and is excited for Mannion’s opportunity.

title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 1 Edition
summary: The 2026 NFL season is HERE! That means it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 15: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up before an NFL preseason football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL season is HERE! That means it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 1 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Seattle Seahawks – I’m big on the concept of benefit of the doubt. The reigning Super Bowl champs deserve the top spot entering the season. Sam Darnold skepticism remains but their defense should still be really good. It wouldn’t be surprising if Mike Macdonald has real staying power as one of the NFL’s top head coaches. Seattle also kind of gets to play up the underdog angle (to themselves, at least) with the Rams getting a lot of hype. 2 – Los Angeles Rams – The Rams have the shortest odds to win Super Bowl LXI. It remain to be seen what Aaron Donald has left in the tank and when he’ll actually play for them. But Myles Garrett is going to be ready to play right away and that makes a big difference. Unless Matthew Stafford just turns out to be way too old and diminished, which isn’t impossible, this team should be a juggernaut. 3 – Kansas City Chiefs – Can’t believe I’m saying this but people are sleeping on the Chiefs. Periphery be damned, this is all about banking on Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes. I really don’t care that the quarterback is coming off injury; this duo will probably find a way to get deep into the playoffs once again. Now is not the time to sell their stock. 4 – Buffalo Bills – Perpetual question: “Is this the year Josh Allen breaks through?” I saw Peter Schrager compare the Bills to the New York Knicks (boo), who were able to finally able to get over the hump after making a coaching change. I was never the biggest Sean McDermott guy, so, I do think they might be better. And I’m willing to believe Allen is going to lead another strong offense. But he really needs to beat the playoffs allegations at some point. 5 – Baltimore Ravens – Speaking of needing to beat playoff allegations, it’s well past time for Lamar Jackson to deliver after getting so much praise for being an awesome regular season player. And, wouldn’t you know it, this is another team moving on from a former Andy Reid disciple at head coach. The Ravens are bound to get some more luck this season after going 2-5 in one-score games last year. 6 – Houston Texans – They had one of the NFL’s best defenses last year and that unit is looking strong again entering 2026. If C.J. Stroud can put it together, you can see why this team is getting some sleeper Super Bowl hype. 7 – Detroit Lions – The Lions are the ultimate positive regression team. They had bad one-score game luck last year. They had bad injury luck last year. And now they get the NFL’s easiest schedule. While their offensive line is a spot to monitor, it wouldn’t be surprising if this team gets back to being one of the top contenders in the NFC. 8 – New England Patriots – The Pats are facing a lot of regression indicators after having such a ridiculously easy schedule in 2025. But while those factors are working against them, New England’s big offseason additions could help them offset those concerns. A.J. Brown looks poised for a massive season and Romeo Doubs is a nice complement for Drake Maye, who appears to be for real. 9 – Philadelphia Eagles – It’s not difficult to feel good about the Eagles’ floor. Jalen Hurts and Nick Sirianni never miss the playoffs. Vic Fangio is overseeing what might be the best defense in the NFL. But it’s hard to know what to expect from this new offense. One would think there’s only room to get better after leading the league in three-and-outs last year. But there are still questions about this passing attack. Perhaps a revamped running game will make a huge difference. 10 – Dallas Cowboys – The Cowboys could be primed to prevent the Eagles from threepeating in the NFC East. Although the Tyler Smith injury hurts them, they should have one of the top offenses in the NFL. And their defense is bound to improve to some extent after being historically bad last year. Maybe it’s even better in a big way after adding Christian Parker and Caleb Downs? I think the NFC East comes down to a photo finish between Philly and Dallas. 11 – Denver Broncos – Between this spot and the next one, here’s a grouping of two teams where it’s easier to believe in the head coach than the quarterback. The bottom won’t drop out entirely on the Broncos but they do have a bit of one-year wonder feel to them (11-2 in one-score games!) and their AFC West rivals all won’t be as bad as they were last season. 12 – Chicago Bears – The Bears seem poised to take a step back this season but Ben Johnson is good and I’m willing to hold space that I might be wrong about Caleb Williams. He’s undoubtedly talented but do you really believe in him deep down going up against some of the other quarterbacks? More likely to win a wild card spot than to win the NFC North. 13 – Cincinnati Bengals – I can’t quit Joe Burrow. If this defense can finally stop letting the Bengals’ offense down, they have something in Cincy. But that’s a big if. 14 – San Francisco 49ers – The Niners are talented but they simply do not have good vibes. Kyle Shanahan’s accident, interminable offseason injuries, tough division … their time in the NFC spotlight has passed. 15 – Los Angeles Chargers – Justin Herbert working with Mike McDaniel is exciting! On paper. Which is fitting because Herbert has largely been an on paper player. Offensive line concerns persist here, even if it’s not quite as dire as last year’s situation. 16 – Green Bay Packers – For years, we’ve talked about the Packers as up-and-comers since they were a young team. Going to need to see them actually establish themselves as a top tier team in the conference first. Their defense should be a major concern after hiring Jonathan Gannon. Not to mention Micah Parsons will be missing time. 17 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers – I dropped the Bucs behind the Packers after seeing that Tampa signed Baker Mayfield to a contract extension. I was actually excited to see Baker go “middle fingers to the world, eff you for not paying me” mode. I think the new deal makes him lose that edge. Still could be the best team in a bad division. 18 – Jacksonville Jaguars – The Jags? More like the Jats. J ust a t eam. Then pluralize that. Yep, definitely makes sense. But, for real, I was tempted to put them 16th because that’s typically what I do with a squad when I don’t really know what to make of them. Then I had to drop them a little lower because I felt slightly better about some other teams. Their lack of narrative juice probably isn’t doing them any favors in terms of perception. Maybe that’ll change if Travis Hunter really goes off. 19 – New Orleans Saints – The Saints are the trendy pick to go from bad-to-good. Kellen Moore’s squad showed improvement down the stretch last year and Tyler Shough seems like he could at least be competent, if not better than that. But there are plenty examples of teams winning late in one season and that momentum not directly carrying over to the next year. So, no need to crown them just yet. 20 – Minnesota Vikings – Never been a big Kyler Murray believer. This team might be able to have some regular season success but no one is losing sleep about them as a postseason threat. 21 – Indianapolis Colts – Pretty weird season last year. The second half version of them is easier to believe than the first half version. 22 – Pittsburgh Steelers – Is this the year the Steelers are finally going to have a losing record? I’ve long been wary of betting on their downfall in that…

title: Eagles News: ESPN picks Philadelphia to return to the Super Bowl against the Chiefs
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! ESPN’s Bill Barnwell is apparently big on the Birds this year. Losing another Super Bowl to the Chiefs by three points sure wouldn’t be fun. I do think it would be cool to see a rubber match between these two teams. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - FEBRUARY 09: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles talks with Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) after Super Bowl LIX at Caesars Superdome on February 9, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! ESPN’s Bill Barnwell is apparently big on the Birds this year. Losing another Super Bowl to the Chiefs by three points sure wouldn’t be fun. I do think it would be cool to see a rubber match between these two teams. Same goes for a potential Super Bowl matchup against the Patriots. Especially cool if the Eagles actually go out and win the game. Predicting the 2026 NFL playoff field, plus Super Bowl pick – ESPN On the NFC side, I’ll pick the Eagles. I really believe in their defense as potentially being the league’s most complete unit, with difference-makers at all three levels and one of the best defensive coaches in Vic Fangio. There’s understandable skepticism about the offense after the Eagles made coaching changes and moved on from legendary offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland, but when Lane Johnson has been on the field, the Eagles have been successful. The star right tackle should be in the lineup more often in 2026, and the Eagles will have more success running the ball than they did a year ago. They’re one of the few teams that can compete with the Rams along the line of scrimmage and hold up in coverage against their playmakers. […] That leaves us with a Super Bowl rubber match. And as you can probably guess, if I believed enough in the Chiefs to pick them to win the AFC, I’ll ride with them to gain a measure of revenge and beat the Eagles in Super Bowl LXI. The added rushing element with Walker will give the Eagles issues they didn’t face when these two teams met in Super Bowl LIX, when the Chiefs basically abandoned the run altogether after the Eagles took an early lead. Without the ability to pin their ears back and strictly go after Mahomes as a passer, the Eagles might not be quite as dominant on defense this time around. Jalen Hurts has been spectacular in the Super Bowl matchups against Mahomes, but his one fumble in Super Bowl LVII helped swing seven points back to the Chiefs in a 38-35 victory. This one wouldn’t be quite as high-scoring, but let’s say that the Chiefs let Kelce (and potentially other members of the organization) ride off into the sunset. My pick: Chiefs 27, Eagles 24. Eagles Film Preview: Commanders could struggle to stop Philadelphia’s rushing attack – BGN Overall, I still favor the Eagles. Washington is installing a complicated new defensive system with a number of new starters, while the Eagles have far more continuity within the roster even if the offensive structure has changed. The obvious concern is that Jones’ entire defensive philosophy is built around making quarterbacks and offensive lines second-guess what they are seeing. That is probably not ideal for an offense playing its first meaningful game under a new coordinator. However, Washington also has to execute all of that complexity, and I’m not convinced the defensive personnel is good enough right now. Every NFL team ranked by their 2027 Super Bowl chances entering Week 1 – SB Nation Tier 1: Super Bowl Contenders. Nobody in our top five should really surprise anyone. These are the teams that are the elite of the elite, the cream of the crop, the organizations that either have everything together they need to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, or have issues so minor they won’t play a major role in their success. These are the teams that would stun us if they missed the playoffs, or got eliminated early. The Rams speak for themselves in this tier. The big question comes at the back end with the Ravens, who perennially get ranked high because they should have all the tools to make it, but end up with a fatal flaw in the playoffs. This year we see new head coach Jesse Minter having the capability to get them over that hump. No. 1: Los Angeles Rams, No. 2: Seattle Seahawks, No. 3: Buffalo Bills, No. 4: Philadelphia Eagles, No. 5: Baltimore Ravens. Season Predictions w/BLG | OTSP #157 – Eagles Pin-Pull Network Shane and Jonny are joined by Brandon Lee Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation to make predictions for the Eagles’ season. Know Your Enemy – Jayden Daniels – Iggles Blitz Daniels having to open the season against a loaded Eagles defense isn’t ideal for Washington, especially behind a questionable OL. The one advantage is that the Eagles won’t have good game tape to study. Washington limited their playbook in the preseason. The Eagles faced the Lions offense last year so they know the basic system, but they don’t know about Blough as a play-caller or how the offense will look with Daniels running it. I think it is fair to say he’s just a tad different from Jared Goff. Why Jalen Hurts will flourish in Sean Mannion’s offense – NBCSP And I don’t see any reason Hurts won’t flourish in this system. For starters, he’s flourished in every system so I can’t come up with a reason this would be any different. But Mannion really seems to have tailored the offense to what Hurts likes to do within the heavy play-action, under-center tenets the scheme is built on. This is a system that is quarterback friendly because the QB doesn’t have to read the whole field, most passes are high-percentage low-risk throws and there’s a heavy emphasis on running the ball and disguising plays pre-snap to keep defenses off balance. If the offensive line can stay healthy – and so far so good – and Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Makai Lemon can help make up for the loss of good ol’ What’s His Name in New England, and Saquon Barkley can run the ball consistently and productively, there’s nothing that can hold this offense back. Will it take a few weeks before it all comes together? Probably. The starting offense hasn’t played one snap of real football with Mannion calling plays, and that’s a little scary. They’ll go into Sunday’s opener vs. Washington without a dry run. But ultimately, this season is going to end the same way as 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. With the Eagles in the playoffs and Hurts as one of the biggest reasons why. Why Eagles OC Sean Mannion’s ‘beautiful mind’ matters more than new scheme – The Athletic The Eagles did not game plan specifically for preseason games, so his first time planning and sequencing the calls comes Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Early feedback on the operation was favorable. Quarterbacks appreciated how quickly they heard the play call. The call sheet appeared organized. Communication remained sound. Substitutions were clean. Mystery still exists. The scheme, which the Eagles consider a competitive advantage, will evolve as Mannion sees how it fits the personnel. But Mannion’s success will depend on more than the binder he put together. It hinges on how he puts those ideas to work. “As the year goes on,” Mailata said, “we get to display what’s in the beautiful mind of his.” ‘It’s his time:’ DeVonta Smith enters 2026 primed to prove the Eagles — and himself — right as the new WR1 – PHLY Eagles Dating back to the spring, there has been palpable internal enthusiasm for what Smith can become in new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s scheme. The 27-year-old has yet to surpass the 100-catch mark in his career mostly spent as the “1B” to Brown’s “1A.” How productive can he be if he starts getting thrown the ball more often? According to TruMedia, Smith ranked 12th in target share last year at 24.4%, while Brown finished 10th at 26.1%. But what if that number were closer to the 30% mark Jaxon Smith-Njigba surpassed last season (35.8%) and Puka Nacua approached (28.5%) in similar schemes geared around a play-action passing game that funnels targets to versatile pass catchers. Those close to Smith believe he’s ready for that workload. Actually, those close to…

title: Steelers Week 1 power rankings roundup: Does the national media have faith in Mike McCarthy?
summary: The NFL is back, and the Pittsburgh Steelers open up their 2026 regular season on Sunday afternoon at Acrisure Stadium when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. The game will mark an entirely new era of Steelers football, as Mike McCarthy is set to enter his first season as head coach of the franchise. McCarthy […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is back, and the Pittsburgh Steelers open up their 2026 regular season on Sunday afternoon at Acrisure Stadium when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. The game will mark an entirely new era of Steelers football, as Mike McCarthy is set to enter his first season as head coach of the franchise. McCarthy is, of course, reunited with his former quarterback from his time with the Green Bay Packers, Aaron Rodgers. The legendary quarterback returns for his second season with the black and gold and is looking for a storybook ending to an already illustrious career. After going 10-7 and winning the AFC North last season, the Steelers are returning much of the talent that earned them a playoff spot. Is that enough to earn them some respect among the national media in the Week 1 power rankings? Let’s take a look at where the Steelers rank among the rest of the league in our weekly power rankings roundup. SB Nation: No.18 “Hitting Tier 4 we have the teams that have the pieces to make the playoffs, and that’s more or less their ceiling. There’s a mixture of lacking top-end talent, one side of the ball which is highly problematic, or simply being too young to really believe they can put a run together.” – James Dator and Mark Schofield The Athletic: No.18 “The Steelers haven’t had a losing season since 2003, so maybe it’s unwise to predict only eight wins. They boast the league’s highest-paid defense, but the big question is how good the offense can be with 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers reuniting with Mike McCarthy.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk: No. 18 “They need to get off to a fast start; there are plenty of tough games after the Week 9 bye.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.21 “While I expect the Steelers to prove their superiority against the Falcons in Week 1, I’m more interested in seeing how this offense operates under the direction of new head coach Mike McCarthy. The new-look receiving corps could produce some highlights to start the season and alter expectations quickly.” – Nick Shook USA Today: No.21 Another squad facing so many questions in 2027, particularly on the offensive side, probably should think long and hard before dumping more money into this defense” – Nate Davis ESPN: No. 21 “This season is a success if … the Steelers win a playoff game in coach Mike McCarthy’s first season. Yes, the organization sets its eyes on adding another Vince Lombardi Trophy to the case every season, but the first step is winning the team’s first playoff game in a decade.” – Brooke Pryor Seeing Pittsburgh placed in the middle of the pack was to be expected, but it is hilarious that, of the publications featured, all of them rank the Steelers either 18th or 21st. Given the fact that Week 1 is always undpredictable, it will be interesting to see how much we see the Steelers rise or fall in the power rankings after their date with Atlanta. title: Steelers 2026 season predictions: Record, award winners, and more
summary: The NFL’s 2026 season gets underway tonight with a Super Bowl matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots. The Steelers season won’t be long behind, with Pittsburgh set to face off against the Falcons during the early slate of games this Sunday (1 p.m. EST). With anticipation mounting, we at BTSC decided […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s 2026 season gets underway tonight with a Super Bowl matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots. The Steelers season won’t be long behind, with Pittsburgh set to face off against the Falcons during the early slate of games this Sunday (1 p.m. EST). With anticipation mounting, we at BTSC decided to bring back our staff roundtable and discuss what we’ll be watching this season with the Steelers, and what else we’re thinking about the rest of the NFL. While we’re certain to be surprised by some outcomes of this season — this is why you play the games! — it’s always fun to look back at the end of the season on how we thought the season would go, and see where we were on the right track and where we were hilariously off base. After you’ve read our selections, be sure to sound off in our comments with your takes! We look forward to reading your thoughts about the upcoming seasons and talking ball with the BTSC community. Here we go Steelers! Which Steeler are you most excited to watch this season? Mike Nicastro: Call me crazy, but my choice is Aaron Rodgers. How often will we get the chance to watch a top-five quarterback of all time have his swan song with the team you root for? I’m excited about the additions to the offense, as well as reuniting with his former coach, Mike McCarthy. It will be entertaining – for better or for worse. Joey Bray: I am very much looking forward to seeing Nick Herbig in what should be an expanded role. Every season Herbig has been in the league, his sack total has increased. This season should be no exception, given the fact that Herbig signed a massive extension in the offseason. I would not be shocked if Herbig leads the Steelers in sacks this season. Ryland Bickley: Jaylen Warren. He’s long been one of the league’s most underrated running backs, in my eyes, and I’m excited to see what he can do in Mike McCarthy’s offense. Ryan Parish : I will echo this answer a little further on in this exercise, but the Steelers selected the exact two players I wanted them to in this year’s draft when they took Max Iheanachor and Germie Bernard with their first two picks. I think both will eventually take over important roles for the team during the season, and I will eagerly await their debuts. Jarrett Bailey: I look forward to Aaron Rodgers shutting up a lot of people again. Not projecting a top-10 quarterback season by any means, but he’s still a top-20 guy. What is the most interesting storyline for this year’s team? Ryland Bickley: It’s abstract, but can the new coaching staff finally give the Steelers the jolt the team has seemingly been missing the past several seasons? In more concrete terms, that’s innovation on both sides of the ball and maybe some rising stars on the coaching staff. It’s also the roster’s most highly-paid position groups actually living up to their potential. And most importantly, will the team look like it’s actually building towards eventual Super Bowl contention, not floating in a perpetual state of wild card losses? Ryan Parish : The Steelers are a team trying to straddle two different timelines. They want to “win now” for their older core (Rodgers, Heyward, Watt, Ramsey), but they’re also keeping 11 rookies and have several other young players we’d like to see make the leap this year: Derrick Harmon, Yahya Black, Troy Fautanu, Roman Wilson, Payton Wilson, Mason McCormick, Jack Sawyer, Carson Brueneer. Nick Herbig and Keeanu Benton just got large extensions — and Joey Porter Jr. will either get one just under the wire before Sunday or potentially be a franchise tag candidate next year — can they continue to get better and pay off those deals? While the Steelers may have the “ oldest roster ” on average in the NFL (27.1 years old), that list of players I reeled off is a significant chunk of the roster. How many of those players can take a major step forward in their development this year? The answer will tell us how viable this roster’s construction is as the team enters the post-Rodgers era in 2027. Jarrett Bailey: If the Steelers are a playoff team again, the best storyline will be how everyone who swore Mike Tomlin was the only thing good about the Steelers and the only reason they win games will have egg on their face. Defensively, they’ll be better. Offensively, they should be better. This is a team that has all the tools to make it to the postseason. Mike Nicastro: The Rodgers-McCarthy reunion is intriguing, of course, but I’ll go with the aging defense. When will Father Time find them? Cam Heyward and Jalen Ramsey will eventually hit a wall – and TJ Watt isn’t getting any younger. Do they have a stellar year left in them collectively? Joey Bray: How different does this team look under Mike McCarthy? While the Steelers return much of the same talent that won them the division last season, how differently will the team perform week-to-week and respond to adversity under a new head coach? I am very intrigued to see a new era of Steelers football under Mike McCarthy. Who will be the Steelers team MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, and Offensive Player of the Year? Jarrett Bailey: Team MVP: Aaron Rodgers DPOY: Nick Herbig OPOY: Jaylen Warren Ryland Bickley: Team MVP: Troy Fautanu DPOY: TJ Watt OPOY: Jaylen Warren Mike Nicastro: Team MVP: Aaron Rodgers DPOY: TJ Watt OPOY: DK Metcalf Joey Bray: Team MVP: Nick Herbig DPOY: Cam Heyward OPOY: Zach Frazier Ryan Parish: Team MVP: Zach Fraizer DPOY: Cam Heyward OPOY: Michael Pittman Jr. 11 rookies made the roster. Who is the Steelers Rookie of the Year? Ryan Parish : Anyone who followed my draft coverage knows I was a big fan of both the players the Steelers selected with their first two picks: Max Iheanachor and Germie Bernard. Iheanachor likely won’t start for the first part of the season, but I believe Bernard is already putting pressure on the coaching staff to play him with how he looked in the preseason. His ability to get open quickly underneath, as well as create yards after the catch, pairs well with the type of quarterback Aaron Rodgers is at this point in his career. That’s why I have Bernard eeking out this honor. Joey Bray: One of the biggest surprises of the 53-man roster was the Steelers keeping Eli Heidenreich as the team’s RB3. Not only will Heidenreich be the team’s third running back, but he will also be the personal protector on special teams. I would not be shocked to see Heidenreich get some runs as a return man this season as well. It’s pretty obvious that the Steelers coaching staff sees Heidenreich as someone who can play anywhere on the field, and it would be silly to keep him on the roster and not put the ball in his hands. Despite being a seventh-round pick, he has one of the clearest paths to immediate production of any Steelers rookie. I think he is an underrated pick for Steelers rookie of the year. Mike Nicastro: I think Max Iheanachor will take over the starting right tackle spot early and won’t let it go. Germie Bernard will come on late, but “IMax” will have the biggest impact. Ryland Bickley: It appears Max Iheanachor is on the fastest track to a starting gig this season of the team’s rookie class, and if he continues on what has been a promising trajectory this summer, he should quickly establish himself as the roster’s top right tackle. If the Steelers hit on the Iheanachor selection, it’s an easy pick for this award. Jarrett Bailey: Germie Bernard. He’ll get quality snaps very early on and be an important part of the passing game. title: Steelers’ secondary concerns and other storylines to follow in Week 1 vs. Falcons
summary: The 2026 NFL season is on the horizon. And after weeks of discussions, predictions and analysis, we’ll finally get to see some of the year’s biggest Steelers stories thus far finally play out on the football field as Pittsburgh hosts the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. With that in mind, here are some of the biggest […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker (3( participates in training camp drills at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 NFL season is on the horizon. And after weeks of discussions, predictions and analysis, we’ll finally get to see some of the year’s biggest Steelers stories thus far finally play out on the football field as Pittsburgh hosts the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. With that in mind, here are some of the biggest narratives Read & React will be monitoring this weekend: How will the new-look secondary perform? RB : There is a lot we still don’t know about the 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers, but the secondary might be where the most uncertainty lies. When I predicted which Steelers units would be most likely to finish in the NFL’s top 10 in the upcoming season, the pass defense was the hardest to get a read on. With a cornerback room made up of Joey Porter Jr., Jalen Ramsey, Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr., Brandin Echols and Daylen Everette, there’s a legitimate argument that this group could be elite. But at the same time, it isn’t difficult to imagine scenarios that result in the Steelers dropping closer to their 29th-in-the-NFL ranking in passing yards allowed per game in 2025. There’s a lot that can go wrong, especially early in the season. Starting with Porter, who is expected to be the top name in the secondary this year, there’s a chance he doesn’t even play if he doesn’t receive an extension by kickoff. But assuming he does suit up, it’s worth noting Porter missed the bulk of summer on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a reported back injury, and never took a rep in the preseason as a result. Rust could be a factor early-on in his game. Most of my concern regards the safety room, however, which will be especially undermanned early in the season with starter DeShon Elliott opening the year on injured reserve. Veteran Rayshawn Jenkins is expected to start alongside Jaquan Brisker, but I’d expect a short leash and Ramsey to rotate in at safety as well sometimes to give the group some needed extra range. We haven’t seen much of free agent signing Jamel Dean this offseason, who has flown under the radar a bit this offseason despite having the makings of a high-end CB2. He wasn’t far behind Porter in most metrics in 2025, allowing a 63.1 passer rating when targeted and a 49.2% completion percentage for Tampa Bay. Rewatching the tape from last night, and already impressed with #Steelers CB Jamel Dean GB got the ball out fast, but Dean had a number of strong man reps against Packers WR Matthew Golden, his primary opponent Showed off his physical press and mirrored well too pic.twitter.com/wrjlz8ilmU — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) August 14, 2026 Dean will turn 30 this season, meaning age is a concern but a Darius Slay-esque drop off in play isn’t expected this season. However, Dean’s availability is a minor question; he’s averaged four missed games per season in the last three years. But the arguable biggest piece of the puzzle is how that assortment of names will mesh with the scheme of new coordinator Patrick Graham. Graham is seen as a highly-adaptable defensive mind, but if the looks he did show in the preseason are any indicator, he isn’t afraid to use a number of coverage concepts in one game — or blitz. Graham sent a heavy dose of pressures in Pittsburgh’s slate of August games, putting the team’s secondary (that was missing names such as Porter, Ramsey and Brisker, to be fair) in tough spots where they didn’t always succeed. Now up to almost-full strength, we’ll get to see how Pittsburgh’s defensive backs mesh with Graham’s coaching in a real game. It’ll also be interesting to see how Porter’s speciality in press-man coverage fits into a more diverse scheme. The good news is that while the Falcons boast a talented group of offensive weapons, starting quarterback Tua Tagovailoa shouldn’t present a massive challenge for the defense in Week 1. But if things go poorly against Tagovailoa, who was benched by the Dolphins late last year, it could be time to worry a little bit. How soon can top rookies make an impact? RP : As Week 1 gets closer, the team is letting out more info about how head coach Mike McCarthey sees the roster at this early stage of the season. The team has put out its first depth chart of the season Tuesday, which came with some items to ponder. While it’s wise to remember a depth chart is ultimately just a list of names that a coaching staff can quickly pivot from on game day, it is also useful for setting initial expectations. It isn’t shocking that the Steelers top two rookies, first-round selection Max Iheanachor and second-rounder Germie Bernard, are absent from the list of starters. McCarthy and the Steelers’ brass have been telegraphing that for most of August, even with the two youngsters giving plenty of reason for optimism this summer. But how long can we expect either rookie to remain sidelined? We’ll start with Iheanachor, the team’s top pick. The Arizona State product was the talk of Steelers camp in the early days of training camp, and might have had a legitimate shot to start in Week 1 if he hadn’t suffered an untimely shoulder injury that sidelined him through the first two preseason games. With that amount of time missed, it was going to be next to impossible for him to earn a starting spot with a viable alternative at the Steelers disposal. The Steelers believe Dylan Cook is just that. “We feel really good about Dylan,” McCarthy told the media Monday, when he said that Cook was taking most of the reps at right tackle this week. I think it’s safe to pencil Cook in as the starter for Week 1, but I also think McCarthy’s comments are telling. Cook was taking the majority of the snaps, but not all. McCarthy also declined to outright name Cook the starter when he was asked. This, paired with other comments from the head coach, as well as from the team’s offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio , should make it clear that Iheanachor taking over this season is a matter of when and not if , as long as health allows. Mike McCarthy says Max Iheneachor has been 'impressive' but because he has missed so much time, it is tough to throw him into the starting role right away. Added the ability has been there when he's out there. "Make no mistake about it, he can play." — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) September 7, 2026 Projecting when Iheanachor might take over is trickier. He was healthy enough to play in the final preseason game, so I have to believe he is physically capable of going now. You wouldn’t want to see it go down this way, but like most NFL backups, he’s realistically just one injury away from entering the lineup. But barring that, I’m eyeing Week 5 and October 11 as a possible entry date. That would give him another month to ramp up, and the Colts have one of the least intimidating pass rushes in the NFL. If they feel like that start date is still too soon, then perhaps coming out of their bye week against the Bengals in Week 10 might be another alternative. McCarthy wasn’t just playing coy about the right tackle position, though. Instead, he said he wouldn’t discuss the starters, citing it as an attempt to keep the Falcons off balance heading into the matchup. While I ultimately don’t believe that will have much impact on the game one way or the other, it’s a long-held tactic by many football coaches I’ve met across all levels of football, so it shouldn’t be that surprising. Mike McCarthy said he doesn't want to give definitive declarations on who will start and what the rotations will be to keep the Falcons off balance for now. So, no sure fire answer on who will be WR3, starting RT, etc. — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) September 7, 2026 But unlike Iheanachor, I’m having a hard time believing the Steelers will keep Bernard sidelined for long. For one thing, Roman Wilson barely has any more…

title: Ian Rapoport tells Steelers fans not to give up hope on Joey Porter deal
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. is the lone cornerback remaining on contract extension island. The New England Patriots signed All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez to a four-year, $135 million extension early Tuesday. Gonzalez will receive $102 million guaranteed. Porter Jr. now stands as the last young corner still looking for a new deal before kickoff […]
full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. is the lone cornerback remaining on contract extension island. The New England Patriots signed All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez to a four-year, $135 million extension early Tuesday. Gonzalez will receive $102 million guaranteed. Porter Jr. now stands as the last young corner still looking for a new deal before kickoff on Sunday afternoon. NFL Network/ESPN insider Ian Rapoport isn’t closing the door on a new deal being completed yet. “I would say, ‘the season has not started yet,’” Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show Tuesday . “Until the season starts, I will not give up hope that this could get done.” Play begins in five days and marks the unofficial official deadline for negotiations, as the Steelers don’t negotiate during the season due to a team policy established in the 1990s. A trade doesn’t seem likely, either. That means Porter would make just under $4 million on the last year of his rookie contract and stay with the Steelers. “There’s been a lot of trade rumors with Joey Porter Jr.,” Rapoport said. “I’m not sure at this point whether or not those are going to come to fruition.” NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo reported Tuesday that the Steelers made an offer to Porter, but extension talks remained far from close. “There’ve been some conversations, but (it) doesn’t seem like they are far along contract-wise,” Rapoport said. “You get Christian Gonzalez done; that’s come in as the highest-paid. The more information there is, the more the market is built, the easier it is to get deals done.” In 14 games last year, Porter recorded 52 tackles, 14 passes defended, one sack, and one interception. He didn’t allow a touchdown in man coverage and began following the opponent’s top receiver more often later in the season. The Steelers listed their starting cornerbacks as Joey Porter Jr. OR Asante Samuel Jr. in their updated depth chart on Tuesday, opposite Jamel Dean. It feels like a clear message to Porter Jr. to suit up and play against the Falcons and get the contract negotiations all sorted. Let us know what you think in the comments . From there, Coach Macdonald ratcheted up the Darkside and put enough pressure on the Pats to force Maye and Mike Vrabel into some bad decisions. One Drew Lock postgame interview later, and we are still the toast of the town. How did you enjoy the game? How happy are you that our squad is back at it again? Was the game ever in doubt for you? title: Mike Macdonald makes NFL history with Seahawks win over Patriots
summary: It was not remotely as easy as Super Bowl 60, but the Seattle Seahawks once again beat the New England Patriots, this time rallying from a 10-0 2nd half deficit to prevail 13-10 on opening night of the 2026 NFL season. On a night of mixed emotions ranging from the joy of unveiling another Super […]
full_text: Feb 8, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel and Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike MacDonald shake hands after Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was not remotely as easy as Super Bowl 60, but the Seattle Seahawks once again beat the New England Patriots, this time rallying from a 10-0 2nd half deficit to prevail 13-10 on opening night of the 2026 NFL season . On a night of mixed emotions ranging from the joy of unveiling another Super Bowl banner to the dread after Sam Darnold’s injury , fans left Lumen Field happy after Josh Jobe’s game-clinching interception on a truly puzzling Drake Maye decision . Dating back to last season, the Seahawks have won 11 consecutive games when including the playoffs. That not only ties a franchise record set by the 2005 NFC champion squad led by Mike Holmgren, it’s also a historic moment for head coach Mike Macdonald. Hired two seasons ago as the youngest coach in the NFL (which he’s no longer, thanks to Kellen Moore and Joe Brady), the 39-year-old Macdonald is now the youngest coach in NFL history to win 11 in a row. Mike Macdonald is the first head coach to win more than 10 straight games prior to turning 40 years old (including playoffs) in the Super Bowl Era 🔥 @Seahawks | #GoHawks pic.twitter.com/urcoiTnjyH — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) September 10, 2026 The Seattle Seahawks enjoyed a whole lot of success and a Super Bowl under Pete Carroll, whom by the end of his Seahawks career was the oldest coach in the league but has the seemingly eternal youthfulness of someone half his age. His successor has already brought Seattle a second Super Bowl to go along with the one Pete captured over a decade ago. The hope is that Macdonald keeps the winning ways and is here for decades to come.

title: Seahawks’ Josh Jobe pulled off a game-winning pick not seen in NFL since 2021
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks lost to the San Francisco 49ers last season, Riq Woolen infamously looked to be in position to intercept Brock Purdy and seal a win up 13-10. The ball, of course, ended up in the hands of Jake Tonges for the game-winning touchdown, and it marked the shift of Woolen having to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after intercepting a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Seattle Seahawks lost to the San Francisco 49ers last season, Riq Woolen infamously looked to be in position to intercept Brock Purdy and seal a win up 13-10. The ball, of course, ended up in the hands of Jake Tonges for the game-winning touchdown, and it marked the shift of Woolen having to effectively share snaps with Josh Jobe instead of be the unquestioned second corner. Fast forward to opening night against the New England Patriots, and the Seahawks are once again up 13-10 and needing to defend a red zone throw into the end zone that could win the game. Josh Jobe was in position to make a play, and boy did he make one hell of a play. JOSH JOBE TOE TAP INT NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MrmQx0a3fo — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 It goes without saying that this is a horrible, panicked decision by Drake Maye. In tying field goal range, only a turnover loses you the game, so any throw made into the end zone has to be out of harm’s way and preferably to a wide open receiver. Jobe still made a terrific play on the ball, and the replay shows his nifty toe-tapping ways to secure the W. Called game and kept his feet in pic.twitter.com/SunasYF0Zr — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 The context of this interception is relevant because, well, you don’t normally see a team in position to tie end up losing the game because they threw a pick with this type of field position. We needn’t look beyond the NFC West for the last time this type of ending happened. Per ESPN Stats and Info, the last QB to throw a pick… …down by 3 …with less than a minute left …inside of the 20 …was Kyler Murray on Week 8 of 2021. It's been almost five years since we've seen a pick this egregious situationally. https://t.co/X2m0eaTQPj — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 10, 2026 this was that play, lmao https://t.co/VsuDFpM9CJ — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 10, 2026 This might be an oddly specific stat but it also underscores how rare it is to see a team in position to tie with a field goal end up losing because they threw a red zone interception in the dying seconds of regulation. That’s how you defend home field and “Run it forward” toward another Super Bowl run.

title: Vinod Khosla has priceless reaction to first win as Seahawks owner
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may not have done any ceremonial passing of the torch with their 12 Flag raise on opening night against the New England Patriots, but this was nevertheless the start of the Khosla era of Seahawks ownership, and what a way to start. What could’ve been a disastrous night for the Super Bowl […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: (L-R) Owner Vinod Khosla of the Seattle Seahawks talks with general manager John Schneider prior to the game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks may not have done any ceremonial passing of the torch with their 12 Flag raise on opening night against the New England Patriots, but this was nevertheless the start of the Khosla era of Seahawks ownership, and what a way to start. What could’ve been a disastrous night for the Super Bowl champions after losing Sam Darnold on the first drive of the season turned into a 13-10 win in front of a raucous Lumen Field crowd. Drake Maye went from no sacks and no turnovers through three quarters to taking three sacks and throwing three interceptions in the fourth quarter, including the game-clincher to Josh Jobe when they were comfortably in tying field goal range. Vinod Khosla, the venture capitalist billionaire who bought the Seahawks for $9.612 billion, was in attendance after he and his family held an introductory press conference earlier in the day. As someone who admitted to becoming an NFL fan through the 1970s Pittsburgh Steelers, then a fan (and minority stakeholder) of the San Francisco 49ers for several decades, this was Khosla’s first foray into Seahawks fandom as an owner. I think Khosla can relate to every Seahawks fan after tweeting this out after the game. I’m going to get a cardiac test before the next @Seahawks game. The team and 12s won it tonight. Hard to imagine a better roller coaster — Vinod Khosla (@vkhosla) September 10, 2026 Get used to it, Vinod. This is the Seahawks way no matter who’s on the field.
