title: Winners and Losers from the Seahawks’ dramatic, gutsy win over the Patriots
summary: The Seattle Seahawks unveiled a new Super Bowl banner, welcomed a new ownership group, and that’s could’ve easily been the high point of the night. If the Seahawks’ 2025 season was a dream come true, the start to the 2026 season was shaping up to be a Nightmare on Occidental Street. Sam Darnold left early […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass in the end zone intended for Mack Hollins #13 of the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks unveiled a new Super Bowl banner, welcomed a new ownership group, and that’s could’ve easily been the high point of the night. If the Seahawks’ 2025 season was a dream come true, the start to the 2026 season was shaping up to be a Nightmare on Occidental Street. Sam Darnold left early with a hip injury, the Seahawks fell behind to the New England Patriots and were shut out at halftime, and things were looking bleak. But these are Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks, and they will find a way even when they’re down key players in the secondary and their star QB. Let’s get to the Winners and Losers for Seahawks 13, Patriots 10 . Seattle Seahawks Winners The secondary shows up and stands out Riq Woolen and Coby Bryant are on other teams. Ty Okada and Nick Emmanwori are out injured. Rodney Thomas II was elevated from the practice squad, Nehemiah Pritchett hadn’t had a start since his rookie season. Thomas and Pritchett combined for a huge interception at 10-3, then Julian Love did a Super Bowl redux for another interception that resulted in the go-ahead field goal, and Josh Jobe called game with a toe-tapping pick in the final minute. Love was phenomenal and played down in the box more than he usually does, while Pritchett had a PBU outside of the INT and Thomas looked like a quality veteran option. Three picks, all from the secondary, and all led to points or the end of the game. Outside of Mack Hollins, the Patriots receivers were relative non-factors. A.J. Brown did beat Jobe and drew a pass interference, but that was the only really bad play all night. Uchenna Nwosu is a beast What a superb game by Chenna. His run defense was outstanding and he was flying all over the place at the line of scrimmage. I think he was the best defensive lineman on the team, with Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams not too far behind. This is a contract year for Chenna and we’ll worry about that later, but a healthy Nwosu—he did leave for a concussion check—changes so much for Seattle’s front. Drew Lock to the rescue again Lock was admittedly shaky to start the game, but he is a backup quarterback who is dealing with his own offensive coordinator change. I think that partially explains the late huddle breaks and delay of game penalties when communicating with Brian Fleury, in which case that can be cleaned up during practice. In the second half, Lock was 10/14 for 136 yards, a touchdown, and a 15-yard scramble that was straight out of the Russell Wilson playbook. Overall, Lock finished 16/22 for 187 yards and a TD, outplaying the 2025 MVP runner-up. I was really harsh on Lock as an NFL QB during the whole Geno Smith competition back in 2022, but over the years I’ve learned to tone it down when warranted. Lock may not be a franchise QB but he can win you games, and he was a big help once he settled into the game. Brian Fleury adjusts on the fly and succeeds This was a tough spot for the new OC. You prepare all camp and preseason with your starters and then your QB goes out on the fifth play. Fleury did not panic when Lock was subbed in, and the second half saw a lot cleaner execution (as long as the plays were actually snapped on time). The 4th and 1 call to JSN was a Big Balls Brian moment that was beautifully designed. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is still the best in the business When Sam Darnold went out, JSN had the one catch for 13 yards. When he was with Drew Lock, he had 7 catches for 109 yards and a game-tying touchdown. It helps that Lock already has chemistry with JSN as far back as his rookie season, but unless you have an all-time bad QB under center then JSN is going to feast. What a player, what a superstar, what a way to start a season. Jadarian Price showcases his skills in a solid debut I will take 10 carries for 52 yards and a couple of catches if that’s the appetizer for a long career in Seattle for the first-round running back. He looked fast, he slipped out of tackles, and there will be home run opportunities in the future. Unfortunately, the game plan got thrown out of whack and that limited his touches. Cooper Kupp still got it Seattle’s first points came courtesy of a one-handed Cooper Kupp effort 24 yards down the field, while his other catch helped put the ‘Hawks in the red zone for the would-be winning field goal. He had a touchdown taken away due to an illegal shift, but Seattle committed a clear delay of game that somehow was missed. Kupp is still WR2 until further notice. Jason Myers bounces back from tough preseason I wouldn’t ordinarily celebrate making three kicks all no further out than 32 yards, but the way Jason Myers was in shank mode throughout August had me worried. We’ll see what happens when the kicks are longer later on this season, but he didn’t miss his cues this time. Michael Dickson is the best punter who’s ever lived Slight exaggeration but tell me I’m wrong. Mike Macdonald has his guys ready for anything Key players hurt before the game? Quarterback injured during the game? A shit ton of penalties that gift the other team points? No problem. Seahawks still win. That’s the hallmark of a great coach who has his squad connected. This was the most adversity the Seahawks have faced since the Los Angeles Rams Thursday night thriller and Seattle pulled it out of the fire. This isn’t to say we haven’t seen Pete Carroll teams pull off games (well, not with Russ out) where they’re beaten up and far from their best—there’s a deep collection in the LOB catalogue of “how did they win that?” performances—but something about the way Macdonald has got this level of buy-in from the roster is downright admirable. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Seattle Seahawks Losers Sloppy penalties all night The starters didn’t play in the preseason and the Seahawks’ reserves were sloppy. We saw some sloppiness with operation issues in training camp, some of which was documented on Hard Knocks. Well, the starters played in this game and were very undisciplined. Chazz Surratt committed a roughing the punter penalty that turned into a field goal. Josh Jobe’s pass interference might have saved an A.J. Brown touchdown but it led to an Eli Raridon touchdown anyway. There were false starts, blown blocking assignments on offense, it all just felt out of sync. If Sam Darnold didn’t get hurt then there would be less reason to panic. He is hurt, and the Seahawks’ margin for error is a fair bit smaller. Too many George Holani touches, but maybe this will soon be phased out I like George Holani, whom despite Mike Tirico’s insistence, is not Brady Russell. He’s a good special teams player, great pass protector, solid receiving back. Holani had eight carries for 29 yards but outside of his first carry it felt like the drives were dying with his touches. Holani had three “successful runs” and none in the second half. He just doesn’t have that extra burst or strength to barrel over first-team caliber defenders, and he’s not very fast. I get why Holani had to play quite a bit tonight, but we’re now at 40 career NFL carries and he still doesn’t have an explosive run. I’m also puzzled as to why Emanuel Wilson only had two carries. Not too worried yet. Holani will still be a part of this offense, but when Jadarian Price is more up to a heavier workload + Zach Charbonnet comes back his touches should be reduced. Abe Lucas was not at his best It felt like there was constant pressure coming from the right side of the line, and Lucas looked to be struggling more than any Seahawks offensive lineman. Not Abe’s…

title: Seahawks-Patriots score: Seahawks lose Sam Darnold, still rally to beat the Patriots
summary: The bad news for the Seattle Seahawks is that they have lost quarterback Sam Darnold for an undetermined length of time. The good news is the Super Bowl champions started the season in the win column with a 13-10 comeback over the New England Patriots (0-1). Despite having a banged up secondary missing Nick Emmanwori […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Julian Love #20 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after interception against New England Patriots during the fourth quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The bad news for the Seattle Seahawks is that they have lost quarterback Sam Darnold for an undetermined length of time. The good news is the Super Bowl champions started the season in the win column with a 13-10 comeback over the New England Patriots (0-1). Despite having a banged up secondary missing Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada, the Seahawks defense still produced three Drake Maye interceptions in the final quarter, including a game-winning pick by Josh Jobe on a ball Maye should’ve never thrown. Drew Lock once again has a game-winning drive in primetime, while “The Dark Side” once again reminded everyone of how dominant they are even when undermanned. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored Seattle’s only touchdown on a 4th-and-1 throw from Lock, and even without Darnold for almost the whole game he still had 8 catches for 122 yards and a score. Seahawks-Patriots 1st half recap The first play-call of the season and therefore of Brian Fleury’s career as offensive coordinator was a 13-yard run by rookie running back Jadarian Price. Sam Darnold’s first pass was an over the middle throw to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for another 13 yards. An Eric Saubert false start penalty put them behind the sticks, and then a worrisome sight happened when Sam Darnold was sacked by former Seahawk Dre’Mont Jones and he limped off the field with a hip injury. Dre'Mont Jones gets home to end the drive 💪 NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OWqNvAEY81 — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 New England’s opening drive ended in a punt but nevertheless was briefly extended after Derick Hall committed a personal foul penalty by shoving Drake Maye when he was already out of bounds. Sending the house on Maye led to a throwaway on the next third down. Drew Lock came in for Darnold but was predominantly handing the ball off, and nearly got intercepted by Christian Gonzalez early in the second quarter on an underthrown ball to Cooper Kupp. The Patriots finally opened the scoring with a methodical 10-play, 77-yard drive. Multiple third-down conversions, including a pass interference on Josh Jobe when he was beaten on a flea-flicker by A.J. Brown. Drake Maye found a wide open Eli Raridon for the first touchdown of the season. The rookie tight end has his big moment. Hard to start your NFL career better than Eli Raridon just did NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/BBOHTP6VEW — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 Seattle’s sloppy penalties persisted on offense, pushing them into 3rd and 22. Drew Lock still threw a dime to JSN for 21.5 yards, setting up the Barnyard shove with A.J. Barner. The conversion was successful, but a mysterious offside penalty on the offense negated the conversion and led to another punt. No further scoring happened in the half, but Darnold was ruled out with a hip injury. Seahawks-Patriots 2nd half recap The Patriots’ opening drive stalled out in Seahawks territory, but a Chazz Surratt roughing the punter infraction not only gifted New England a new set of downs, it set up an Andy Borregales 50-yard field goal to extend the lead to 10-0 Patriots . Another Seahawks drive with Lock ended in a punt, but the Pats were backed up and went three-and-out. Jay Harbaugh forced a delay of game through showing punt block and limiting the number of gunners the Patriots could send down the field. He showed the same look again and Rashid Shaheed was able to at least get into New England territory on his return. Faced with 3rd and short and maybe thinking about a long field goal or having to go for it on 4th, Drew Lock lofted a long throw to Cooper Kupp, who made a remarkable one-handed diving catch to set Seattle up in the red zone. What a grab by Cooper Kupp 🙌 NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R92aA9SXng — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 A touchdown to Kupp was taken away due to an illegal shift penalty, but it looked like Seattle also got away with a delay of game penalty so it shouldn’t have counted either way. Lock’s back-foot throw to JSN in the end zone was too long and Jason Myers had to come on for a 30-yard field goal. First attempt after a rough preseason? No problem. 10-3 Patriots . Seattle could’ve used a stop when the Patriots were faced with 2nd and 19. A checkdown to Rhamondre Stevenson got a good chunk of yards, and a blitz by Mike Macdonald was burned when Pop Douglas caught a screen and gained 9 on 3rd and 8. Tough way to end the third quarter. Great way to start the fourth, though! Rodney Thomas II and Nehemiah Pritchett combined for a huge turnover, with Thomas on the tip drill and Pritchett snagging his first career interception. Tipped and intercepted by Nehemiah Pritchett! NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MbMdmJBzfE — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 When Seattle was stuffed on 3rd and 1 with Emanuel Wilson, the Seahawks went for it on 4th and 1. Barnyard? Nope. Play-action pass to Smith-Njigba, who caught it and took off for the end zone. How about a 45-yard game-tying touchdown for Seattle’s first of the season? 10-10. THERE GOES JSN NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SIt21pDRO8 — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 The Pats were backed up after a block in the back penalty on the rookie Gabe Jacas. Romeo Doubs had a huge play laid on a platter and he dropped the ball. That proved costly, as Drake Maye’s over the middle shot on 3rd and long was picked off by Julian Love! He was touched down at the Patriot 47, so no yardage on the return. JULIAN LOVE WITH ANOTHER SEAHAWKS INT NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gj5YJDH3hT — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 Drew Lock led Seattle into the red zone, but after scrambling for 14 yards on 2nd and 15 he committed a costly delay of game penalty. Back-to-back incomplete passes meant Jason Myers was tasked with another short field goal, which he converted from 26. 13-10 Seahawks with 5:50 to go. Following a holding penalty, Leonard Williams sacked Drake Maye after initial pressure from Byron Murphy II. A long play to Mack Hollins turned 2nd and 21 into 3rd and 2. In a big decision, Mike Vrabel went for it on 4th and 2 and Maye scrambled for a first down. An ineligible man downfield was induced thanks to Dante Fowler Jr blowing up an Eli Raridon screen. A throw out to Lan Larison went for a loss of two thanks to Josh Jobe. After the two-minute warning and a 10-yard gain by Hunter Henry, the Pats went for it on 4th and 9 in Seattle territory. Mack Hollins was wide open for a first down as Ernest Jones IV was late on the rotation. On 3rd and 1 with :44 left, the Patriots called timeout to talk it over. Drake Maye converted on the naked bootleg for another first down. Derick Hall pressured Maye, who was sacked by DeMarcus Lawrence and Byron Murphy II. Maye with another completion to set up 3rd and manageable. Just don’t throw it in harm’s way and a field goal attempt is secured…. DRAKE MAYE JUST THREW THE GAME AWAY TO JOSH JOBE! SEAHAWKS WIN! 13-10 Seahawks FINAL. JOSH JOBE TOE TAP INT NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MrmQx0a3fo — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 Seahawks injury report QB Sam Darnold injured his hip in the first quarter and was ruled out before halftime. Drew Lock replaced him for the rest of the night. EDGE Uchenna Nwosu was pulled out of the game for a possible concussion while chasing down Drake Maye in the fourth quarter. title: Seahawks Reacts results: Fans enter 2026 season with high expectations
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seattle Seahawks fans and fans across the country. The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks certainly made their fans happy last season, taking home the team’s second Lombardi Trophy. However, expectations seem to follow success, and […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seattle Seahawks fans and fans across the country. The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks certainly made their fans happy last season, taking home the team’s second Lombardi Trophy. However, expectations seem to follow success, and the Seahawks’ fan base has set the bar high for their team entering the 2026 season. At least according to those who answered our Fan Reacts Survey, with over 52% of fans expecting the Seahawks to make it past the Wild Card Round and 29% projecting a second straight appearance in the NFC Championship. Here are the full results: Making the playoffs isn’t enough for some, with 13% saying that the team winning the Super Bowl for the second year in a row would be the minimum. That’s a near-impossible bar to reach, as only eight teams have repeated as Super Bowl champions, but Seahawks fans have become accustomed to winning and might not be ready to give it up yet. This question was asked before quarterback Sam Darnold left the game against the New England Patriots, so there very well might need to be a reset depending on the severity of Darnold’s injury. Setting expectations wasn’t the only question that fans were asked, as they were asked if they thought the Seahawks were heading in the right direction. The results may not shock you. Yup, fans feel their team, fresh off a Super Bowl, is heading in the right direction. Despite several losses in the offseason, including the Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, fans’ trust in general manager John Schneider has never been higher. They’re pretty fond of their head coach Mike Macdonald as well, making this a fairly obvious ‘Yes’ for nearly every fan. That’s it for this week! Make sure to stay tapped in for the next SBNation Reacts Survey and let us know in the comments if you agree with your fellow fans. Check out FanDuel , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.

title: 49ers vs. Rams injury report: George Kittle and Nick Bosa have no designations
summary: Ahead of Thursday night’s game (Friday local time) against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, the San Francisco 49ers released their injury report, and it’s got some good news. George Kittle and Nick Bosa are both off the injury report entirely, which bodes well for their Week 1 statuses. The only player out on the […]
full_text: Ahead of Thursday night’s game (Friday local time) against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, the San Francisco 49ers released their injury report, and it’s got some good news. George Kittle and Nick Bosa are both off the injury report entirely, which bodes well for their Week 1 statuses. The only player out on the injury report is Alfred Collins, who tore his patellar tendon in practice last week and is now expected to miss the season. He could be placed on Injured Reserve this week, with the 49ers likely making a corresponding move for the game. Undrafted rookie James Thompson Jr. is the only player questionable for the 49ers with a hamstring injury. While Wednesday’s practice was a walkthrough for the 49ers, they did list several players as limited: Nick Bosa, George Kittle, Luke Gifford, Renardo Green, Dre Greenlaw, Gracen Halton, Romello Height, Kyle Juszczyk, and James Thompson Jr. On the Rams side, they’ll only be without Aaron Donald, who was ruled out for Week 1 earlier in the week and did not make the trip to Australia. They only had one limited player on Wednesday, cornerback Jaylen Watson, but he’s a full go for Thursday evening. While Bosa and Kittle are full go’s, Shanahan acknowledged they’ll look to be smart with both coming off major injuries. “Yeah, we’ve got to be smart with that,” Shanahan said. “Bosa not practicing as much. Kittle, he’s had this whole week, but they both look great and stuff. But we also definitely have got to be smart with that.” On Wednesday morning, reporting that Kittle is back and good to go for Week 1, Ian Rapoport did share that he’ll likely be on a pitch count for the game, so that’ll be something to monitor as well. “George Kittle, who tore his Achilles on January 11th and is attempting an improbable comeback much earlier than he ever should be back, is also off the [injury] report and will play,” Rapoport said. “How much will Kittle play? That remains to be seen. I would expect him to be on a pitch count, but a pretty dramatic return for one of the NFL’s best tight ends. George Kittle is back.”

title: 49ers News: At long last, it’s Game Day!
summary: This has felt like the longest offseason ever. Partially out of excitement and partially out of frustration. I’m so curious to see how this offense works with such different pieces. Lotta different faces since the last time they played.  Seattle’s defense looks as good as ever. It reinforced my prediction that they’re gonna be such […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - October 30: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey, #23, throws a touchdown pass to wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk in the second quarter. McCaffrey threw for a touchdown, caught a touchdown pass and ran for a touchdown as the 49ers beat the Rams 31-14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood Sunday, Oct. 30, 2022. Christian McCaffrey becomes the first player since 2005 to throw a TD pass, rush for a TD and catch a TD in the same game. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) This has felt like the longest offseason ever. Partially out of excitement and partially out of frustration. I’m so curious to see how this offense works with such different pieces. Lotta different faces since the last time they played. Seattle’s defense looks as good as ever. It reinforced my prediction that they’re gonna be such a problem for us if we don’t make a move. The Rams will be tough but at least their linebackers aren’t monsters like Seattle’s. Let’s get this W and make it back in one piece. Go Niners!!! Kyle Shanahan, 49ers eye more explosive Christian McCaffrey plays this season “Shanahan said Black is fully capable of doing all the things McCaffrey is able to execute in the run game. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel also is capable of lining up in the backfield, too. The problem arises when the 49ers take McCaffrey off the field on passing downs. “There are things you’re only going to ask Christian to do,” Shanahan said. “And when he’s out, you got to change that stuff up, and the threat of that stuff gets changed, too, for the defense.” Five 49ers players to watch in Week 1 international game vs. Rams in Australia “The 49ers are expected to go with Connor Colby, a second-year player who started six games a year ago. Colby, rookie Carver Willis, and veterans Robert Jones and Austen Pleasants all got their turns at winning the job. Willis also could see action on Friday against the Rams. The 49ers released Jones, and Pleasants begins the season on injured reserve. While Colby will not face Donald, he still will face stiff challenges from interior defensive linemen Braden Fiske and Poona Ford.” Walking in faith, slinging f-bombs, Brock Purdy redefines leadership for 49ers (paywall) “ So what are Purdy’s awful sins? He paused and considered the question. He admitted to judgmental thoughts and getting caught up in living comfortably. He sometimes catches himself staring at his phone when he could be helping his wife, Jenna, clean the post-dinner dishes. He wants to do a better job of maximizing his time with their 13-month-old daughter, Millie. ….“He’s the same guy now as he was when we were rookies,” Zakelj said. “None of this has changed him.”…. But Purdy is as intense as he is empathetic. On Aug. 8, Purdy screamed a decidedly unchurchlike word while hollering at Jordan Watkins after the second-year wide receiver failed to come back aggressively for a pass that was intercepted during a training-camp practice. Purdy was apoplectic: “Attack! Attack!” On Aug. 23, with trash-talking linebacker Fred Warner giving the offense an earful, Purdy bellowed at Warner after floating a completion over him. He barked two words. They weren’t “Bless you.” Purdy isn’t proud of sporadically sounding like a sailor. But he once struggled to reconcile that language with his faith. Purdy said he has habitually asked himself: How can I honor God with what He’s given me? He’s often thought about that in terms of his influence and resources. But he’s fully embraced maximizing his gift as one of the world’s best QBs. And part of being great at his job is inspiring men to follow him. Sometimes that requires a four-letter correction to a young wide receiver. “I think that’s stewarding the job God has given me well,” Purdy said. “Rather than saying, ‘Hey, I’m going to be this perfect, nice guy and not say anything and let things slide by.’ It’s like, ‘No, I’m called to hold my guys accountable and hold myself accountable.’ … When guys saw me do that (to Watkins), I think they had a lot of respect for it. And, honestly, they might want a little bit more of it.” 49ers vs. Rams: The Standard’s 5 fast predictions (paywall) “Kawakami: 49ers 24, Rams 20. In the middle parts of this game, I expect Matthew Stafford to move the ball and the Rams’ defense to look good. But the 49ers’ Melbourne mojo should allow them to jump out ahead in the first 10 minutes and give them fresh legs to close well in the last 10. Also, the Rams gave themselves an excuse to lose this game by traveling so late (and by keeping Donald home), and if you’ve got an excuse against a good team, you usually end up having to use it afterward.” 49ers work out Australian rugby player Ben Te Kura “Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports that Te Kura has aspirations of becoming an NFL offensive tackle.” Weighing on the pros and cons of 49ers’, Rams’ Melbourne travel “ According to Mah, who has worked with NFL teams on their sleep methods and spoke at the player health and safety summit in the spring about how to travel smarter, the Niners will at least be able to recover from travel fatigue and jet lag, even if body clocks aren’t fully calibrated. “I think it’s helpful that they’ve given themselves a cushion to do that because regardless of the jet lag, there’s also travel fatigue [from] this 16-hour flight that they’re taking,” Mah said. “That’s a long time on a flight. And being able to recover from the travel fatigue is a separate issue than just how the body clock is adjusted and how that can affect your sleep and daytime functioning….. “They will have had three or four days to shift their time a couple hours forward,” Wright said. “They will have slept; they will have eaten. Will they be totally acclimated? Nope. But they will have had two or three days to get [a] solid eight [to] 10 hours of sleep in.” Both Wright and Mah noted that another benefit of early arrival is the chance to get and stay hydrated (the Niners gave each player a specific amount of water to consume on the plane ride based on their size and needs) as well as get sunlight at the proper times of the day. ….San Francisco will have a few extra days off upon returning to the West Coast, but it will still take careful planning to get back on Pacific time before returning to practice. “Their reacclimating coming east may be more difficult,” Wright said. “Afterward, they may need to have a tight schedule of light and dark and on the way back feed the guys as they would be on the West Coast and taking short naps and just trying to reacclimate them.” …”Every [Rams] player’s going to walk off the plane stiff, every joint’s going to be aching, and it’s going to take the rehab team a lot of work just to get some fluid back in those joints,” Wright said. “But it’s not just a tired leg problem. Less than 24 hours after getting off a plane, you’ve got a whole body timing problem. And both things are happening at once for them. “The travel fatigue from the journey itself, cramped up, no sleep. And the dehydration is real on a long flight like that. So, you’ve got the physical tiredness and then the time zone, the jet lag, which is the mismatch between body clock and local times.”

It won’t be easy for the Seahawks to repeat, as they’ll need to outlast the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams. We’ll see both teams in action in about 24 hours. Until then, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots is sacked by Rylie Mills #98 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. It won’t be easy for the Seahawks to repeat, as they’ll need to outlast the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams. We’ll see both teams in action in about 24 hours. Until then, here’s what to expect from a rematch of the Super Bowl. It’ll look a bit different for the hosts in this one, with Nick Emmanwori out with an injury. Seattle will also be without starter Ty Okada, meaning a pair of backups will start in the secondary. New England upgraded their receiving core, perhaps more than any team in the league. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs take over as Drake Maye’s top targets. Brown is a WR1, no matter how you slice it for any team. Doubs will be a good fit and should thrive playing off Brown. Tonight, I’d expect Rhamondre Stevenson to get plenty of looks in the passing game underneath. Drake Maye takes what the defense gives him, and the Patriots should have far more success through the air. What will Sam Darnold look like in his second season as a starter? I think tonight looks good for him, and he might not even rely on Jaxson Smith-Njigba in the same manner as last year. Tonight feels like a Cooper Kupp game, with Rashid Shaeed taking advantage of being defended by the “other” cornerback. I think we see a high-scoring game, relative to the market. And wouldn’t be surprised to see the Patriots sneak out of here with a victory. Tonight should give us an idea of what to expect when the 49ers run into the Seahawks.

title: 3 biggest questions for the 49ers in Week 1: Who will step up at DL?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are inching closer to their Week 1 Australia game against the Los Angeles Rams, as both teams look to debut their prized additions from the offseason. San Francisco is a 2.5-point underdog heading into kickoff, while the projected total of 48.5 points indicates this should be one of the higher-scoring games […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Colton McKivitz #68, Matt Hennessy #61 and Connor Colby #75 of the San Francisco 49ers block during the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Falcons 20-10. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are inching closer to their Week 1 Australia game against the Los Angeles Rams, as both teams look to debut their prized additions from the offseason. San Francisco is a 2.5-point underdog heading into kickoff, while the projected total of 48.5 points indicates this should be one of the higher-scoring games of the Week 1 slate. The 49ers return a ton of star pieces, and they made several key additions this offseason, including wide receiver Mike Evans, who is all good to go for Week 1 after dealing with a minor injury in training camp. But there are a couple of questions surrounding this team for the opener, especially after starting defensive lineman Alfred Collins tore his patellar tendon is and out for the year. What are the biggest questions we want to see answers from in Week 1? Who will step up on the defensive line? Even before Collins’s injury, there were some questions about the 49ers defensive line this offseason. Without Nick Bosa, this unit ranked 32nd in sacks last year and was inconsistent against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in yards per carry allowed. Now, Bosa’s return and the addition of Osa Odighizuwa should help the 49ers pass rush in a key way. But behind them, there were a ton of questions about the defensive line, and now their 2025 second-round rookie is out for the year. San Francisco also won’t have Sam Okuayinonu, who broke his foot and will miss substantial time, and Mykel Williams, who remains on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list after his ACL tear last year. Collins and C.J. West were both inconsistent against the run in the preseason as well, which could be an underrated issue this team faces. And Romello Height is also dealing with a minor injury ahead of Week 1. There’s a lot of questions the 49ers have on the defensive line, and that’s tough to deal with against arguably the best team in football. What will the RB split look like? The 49ers have said they want to maintain Christian McCaffrey this season, and we already saw that in training camp with him being held out of practice for soreness. But will that carry over to gamedays? We all know how vital Christian McCaffrey is on offense and how much he changes both the run and the pass game. But the 49ers have started to invest draft capital into the position, and have two players they seem high on in the backfield behind McCaffrey. So, against the Rams, what will the split look like, if there is any at all, and who will the 49ers trust to put on the field? Kaelon Black has received a lot of praise after a quality training camp and preseason, while Jordan James is now back and healthy. How will left guard play out? It’s looking likely that the 49ers will try to rotate players at left guard without a clear solution at the position. Many could see this playing out after the team elected not to invest much in the offseason, and none of the options have looked like a true starter so far through the preseason. Carver Willis seems primed for snaps, but there likely will be a rotation to figure out the team’s best option at the position. That’s not ideal, and could end up being the top factor setting this team back on offense.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 3 things to watch for in 49ers-Rams: Get the ball out quickly, Brock Purdy
summary: Folks, we made it. The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams will do battle in Australia on Thursday night. While the warm-up is the Super Bowl rematch tonight, the rumble down under feels like the official season opener, with the matchup getting more attention after an offseason of adding Myles Garrett and two new […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 20: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers throws a pass against the Los Angeles Chargers during the first quarter in a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Folks, we made it. The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams will do battle in Australia on Thursday night. While the warm-up is the Super Bowl rematch tonight, the rumble down under feels like the official season opener, with the matchup getting more attention after an offseason of adding Myles Garrett and two new secondary members, plus the return of Aaron Donald, who is inactive tomorrow. As for the 49ers, the team feels overlooked and disrespected. All the talk surrounds the defending Super Bowl champs and the excitement over the “super team” Rams. The 49ers have heard the chatter, and I’m fairly certain Kyle Shanahan will use the talk as extra motivation for himself and his team. Here are three things to watch on Thursday night: Quick game throws for Brock Purdy In the 49ers’ “upset” victory over the Rams with Mac Jones under center, the 49ers took what the Rams gave them and got the ball out quickly, leading to YAC opportunities. Now, that was with Demarcus Robinson, Kendrick Bourne, and Jake Tonges as the leading targets. The 49ers will have Mike Evans, George Kittle (in some capacity), Christian McCaffrey, and Purdy leading the offense. In 2025, the 49ers ranked 12th in the NFL with a 68.4% short-throw rate. The Rams also ranked 12th, facing 67.8% short throws. Now, adding Myles Garrett, the 49ers will likely lean toward heavier personnel and try to get the ball out quickly, forcing the Rams’ cornerbacks to tackle in the open field. Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie are two of the better tackling cornerbacks, which proves the Rams understand how they will be attacked in 2026. Stay ahead of the sticks, stay away from third-and-long situations, and run the football enough to keep play action in the arsenal has to be the goal. The Rams’ defense could shift personnel styles in 2026 Last season, the Rams played base defense 26.7% of the time, ranking 21st in the NFL. As far as nickel goes, their 41.6% was 29th in the NFL. This season, the front four and back end are the Rams’ strengths. However, the linebackers are a soft spot for the defense, and Shanahan has been known to put linebackers in a blender in coverage. You have to imagine the Rams understand that and could lean into more “dime” looks. Bringing more defensive backs on the field would make second-level coverage less of a concern. The 49ers’ advantage in this situation would be to run the football against a lighter defensive look. The Rams ranked fourth in the NFL with a 53.6% light box percentage. The chess match between Shanahan and Chris Shula is going to be primetime television. The 49ers run defense The loss of Alfred Collins is such a brutal way to lose another defensive tackle. Regardless of your thoughts on his play, the 49ers are down bodies in the middle of the defensive line. Osa Odighizuwa improves one spot, but essentially a rotation of C.J. West, Kevin Givens, and James Thompson, Jr., is what the 49ers will be working with. Sean McVay spams “duo” runs and will likely double that rate knowing the 49ers are down at defensive tackle. With the fourth-highest EPA/rush of 0.03 last season, the Rams will look to continue that efficiency. Essentially, their only hope is to hold blocks in place and hope Dre Greenlaw and Fred Warner can fly into run gaps to slow Los Angeles’s rushing attack.
author: Jason Aponte

title: 4 bold predictions for the 49ers this season: Perfection, career-highs, and splash trades
summary: Let’s get bold.  The San Francisco 49ers kick off the 2026 season with a matchup against the Los Angeles in Melbourne, Australia on Thursday. The time for predictions is now. But my favorite type of prediction is the bold one. I get to say outlandish things, and when I am wrong, I can hide behind […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get bold. The San Francisco 49ers kick off the 2026 season with a matchup against the Los Angeles in Melbourne, Australia on Thursday. The time for predictions is now. But my favorite type of prediction is the bold one. I get to say outlandish things, and when I am wrong, I can hide behind that “bold” word. It’s always something fun to do. So here are my four bold predictions for the 2026 San Francisco 49ers: The 49ers go 6-0 against the NFC West A third of this shouldn’t be an issue, with the Arizona Cardinals assumed to be looking forward to 2027 and beyond. The other two-thirds is what makes this bold. Last season, the 49ers finished 12-5, a record that would have won every other division in the NFC other than the NFC West. Unfortunately, San Francisco plays in the NFC West, and those 12 wins were only good enough for third place, behind the two teams that met in the NFC Championship Game. And with how both the Rams and Seahawks improved, the competition at the top isn’t going to be any easier in 2026. The 49ers split the season series against the Seahawks and the Rams, winning both the first games against each before falling to both in the latter half, with the Week 18 loss to Seattle giving the Seahawks the NFC West crown. A 6-0 divisional record would obviously be huge for the 49ers, where the margins are so thin in the NFC West. It’s a tough mountain to climb, but anything is possible in divisional matchups. Mike Evans sets a career-high in receptions Quick, without looking it up: what is Mike Evans’ career-high in receptions? When researching for this post, I assumed it was much higher than it actually was. But Evans’ career-high in receptions sits at 96 receptions back in 2016 (on a whopping league-high 173 receptions). Evans has been one of the better receivers in the NFL for the better part of a decade, but he’s somehow never eclipsed the century mark in receptions. That changes in 2026. After a season of a rotating door at wide receiver, the 49ers signed Evans in hopes to give the position some stability. And in terms of overall talent, Evans might just be the best receiver to don the red and gold since the days of Jerry Rice and Terrell Owens. Brock Purdy is a gunslinger, and he certainly has the “I have a receiver down there somewhere” trait, and Evans fits that perfectly. It would be very easy to see Purdy falling in love with his newest target and searching for Evans often. It also helps that there are plenty of question marks for the pass-catchers, with Evans topping the depth chart, with only De’Zhaun Stribling and George Kittle as the only threats to take targets away from Evans. This is also a double-whammy bold prediction, as no 49ers receiver in the Kyle Shanahan era has eclipsed 100 receptions in a season (Christian McCaffrey became the first 49er to eclipse 100 receptions, but he’s a running back). Evans can kill two birds with one stone with a 100-catch season. Jack Jones leads the 49ers in interceptions Outside of Stribling, no 49er impressed quite like Jones. Jones earned his spot on the 49ers’ 53-man roster with his stellar play in the preseason, showing he has a nose for the ball with three pass breakups. He was nearly rewarded with a pick-six against the Raiders but couldn’t quite haul in the interception. But what Jones showed is that he has a nose for the ball, something the 49ers severely lacked in 2025. It took until Week 8 for the 49ers to record their first interception of the season, and because of it, the 49ers tied for 29th with just six interceptions. Jones entered the NFL in 2022 but has recorded eight career interceptions, matching Deommodore Lenoir’s career total with one fewer season, for most interceptions by a cornerback on the 49ers roster. Jones’s three interceptions in 2024 also match Lenoir’s single-season high for the most by a 49er in a season. He’s just as prolific an interceptor as the 49ers’ best corner. The 49ers need a cornerback to force some turnovers at some point. Why can’t it be Jones? Maxx Crosby will be a 49er at some point It’s pretty silly that the Raiders traded Crosby, the trade was voided, and all of a sudden Crosby is happy to be a Raider again. There’s a good chance Crosby gets floated out for a trade once again. Why not the 49ers? There are two paths for the 49ers to go after Crosby, and both are contingent on Nick Bosa. It’s either: Bosa doesn’t quite recover from his knee injury last season, and the 49ers need to add a pass rusher or Bosa stays healthy, but the 49ers’ lack of depth on the edges forces the 49ers to make a Christian McCaffrey-esque superstar trade to get over the hump. The 49ers largely ignored the massive need at defensive end, only adding Romello Height via the draft; after the pass rush sans Bosa, they recorded a league-low 20 sacks. That is simply not enough. The addition of Osa Odighizuwa will help on the interior of the line, but with an unknown timeline for Mykel Williams, it’s tough to see the defensive line being effective, even if Bosa stays healthy. Crosby would help both the pass rush and the run defense on the line and would be a huge swing for a team whose defense is lacking. The fit is there; the 49ers just have to make it all work.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: 2026 49ers Season Preview: Predicting every game using croissants from every city
summary: I gotta be honest with y’all. There was a day last summer that I would have picked the apple pie croissant from Butter and Crumble over the San Francisco 49ers winning the Super Bowl. In fact, I got up at 6 AM, stood in line for hours, got the last one, and then had to […]
full_text: A man carries a large tray of pastries on his head on a street near Franso Hariri Stadium during a football match in Erbil, Iraq's Kurdistan region, on May 2, 2026. Erbil SC defeated Al-Karkh SC 1-0 during an Iraq Stars League match at Franso Hariri Stadium, a victory that moves Erbil closer to the top of the league table, in front of 25,000 fans. (Photo by Sabur Rashid / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images) I gotta be honest with y’all. There was a day last summer that I would have picked the apple pie croissant from Butter and Crumble over the San Francisco 49ers winning the Super Bowl. In fact, I got up at 6 AM, stood in line for hours, got the last one, and then had to carefully transport my hot, flaky treasure from San Francisco to Sunnyvale by train, scooter, and car. Ninety minutes later, I breathed a sigh of relief when I arrived at my parents’ front door with the apple pie croissant intact. I opened it and walked in to the sound of my mom throwing up. She had good days and bad days when it came to keeping food down, and the day before was the rare good day. I so badly wanted her to keep the streak going, so she could try this mash-up of her two favorite foods. Her cancer made sure that she never had a good day again. She was gone by October. I’ve written before about how she fell in love with the 49ers shortly before I was born, a consequence of her moving to the Bay Area during Steve Young’s prime. My first conscious memory was waking up from a nap because my parents were losing their minds when Terrell Owens caught The Catch II. This will be my first full season without her. My mom and I bickered a lot when I was younger. 49ers football was our sanctuary. The game would come on, and instead of yelling at each other, we yelled together at the TV. Whatever we were arguing about would shrink down to something so insignificant that we found our way back to each other. Football was her love language, often reconciling an argument by randomly bringing up something she heard on sports radio that morning. Her other love language was food. Butter and Crumble opened up a few blocks from my apartment in 2023, and that became our local bakery. It opened our eyes to a new type of pastry — not the traditional croissants you can get at an Arsicault but something more new-age, more Shanahan-esque: chimichurri short rib croissants, eggplant parm danishes, chorizo tater tot cro-quiches, banana foster bread pudding. Every month’s menu reveal kept us on our toes. We started seeking out what we called a “WTF is That” pastry whenever we traveled to a new city. It evolved from my designated role on family trips: the food-finder who had to scour Reddit threads, Instagram pages, and Google reviews to figure out where to eat in a city none of us had been to before. Where’s that town’s version of Butter and Crumble, churning out flavor combinations in their carby monstrosities that would offend the purists? The only thing less realistic than wishing for one more game and one more pastry to share with my mom is wishing for a fully healthy 49ers team. For the purpose of this season preview, I’m trying to assess this team at its full potential, even though there’s obviously major questions about critical pieces of the puzzle. I went through every game on the schedule, analyzed each matchup through the lens of how I see football, and scouted the opponent city to find the local Butter-and-Crumble-style “WTF is That” pastry I would have shown my mom. Hours of screen time later, this is the article I wish I could send her. It has everything she would have loved: my thoughts on how the 49ers season will go and zany specialty croissants in random American cities we could have visited… all wrapped up in a very long read for her to fire up on the iPad during her morning coffee on game day. As a fan, I hope to have the problem of missing her extra if they win the Super Bowl rather than feeling relieved that she couldn’t feel the pain of her beloved 49ers falling short, yet again. The last time I felt that sense of relief was during the playoff loss to Seattle, seeing how the trenches completely collapsed for the 49ers on both sides of the ball. On one side of the ball, the 49ers offense couldn’t get a play off because Seattle just kept disrupting the 49ers at the point of attack. All of Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey’s heroics crumble to dust when the play gets snuffed before it has a chance. On the other side of the ball, Seattle’s offensive line was imposing its will and moving around the 49ers’ defenders wherever they wanted. It only took a couple drives before I mentally checked out to the offseason, scrolling mock drafts and free-agency lists at halftime. Now that we’re finally on the cusp of the regular season, did the 49ers do enough on the offensive and defensive lines to clear the bar set by the Seahawks? I don’t buy that they did enough to challenge for the #1 seed confidently, but I do buy that they’re capable of winning ~13 games and getting a wild-card spot. So much of their ceiling depends on two bets going right (beyond the implied bet on health): Bet #1: The offensive line won’t matter, because Kyle Shanahan will be able to create enough spacing by targeting linebackers in the passing game. The 49ers took care to invest in the make-the-linebackers-lives-hell department in the draft and free agency. De’Zhaun Stribling, Mike Evans, and Kaelon Black all add completely new elements to the offense: real downfield speed and physicality, a legit red-zone + boundary target, and compelling running back options that can keep Christian McCaffrey fresh. Linebackers across the league aren’t as good as defensive linemen; their coverage skills are frequently the vulnerability for even the elite defenses. There are only a few linebackers in the league not named Fred Warner that can keep up with CMC and George Kittle. I would have preferred more investment at left guard, but who cares about DJ Jones and Zach Allen barreling down the pocket if Brock is getting it out immediately to his star players on a quick pass against Alex Singleton? If this bet goes right, I think that means they will beat the teams that don’t have good enough coverage linebackers. That means Denver, the Rams, the Chiefs, and the Cowboys are all much more beatable than they seem, as long as the 49ers offensive skill players bring their A-games. Good coverage linebackers can’t offset huge flaws elsewhere in the defense — take the New York Giants, who have such a bad interior defensive line that their run defense would shatter like a flaky croissant shell. But for those teams that do have good coverage linebackers on top of a more balanced roster, the 49ers will need a different plan than “outlast them in a shoot-out”. Which brings me to the defense… Bet #2 : With Osa Odighizuwa taking up the offensive line’s attention, the pass rush roars to life because all four of the following happen: Nick Bosa’s knee holds up Mykel Williams comes back from his ACL tear and keeps improving Romello Height adapts quickly and thrives in the NFL as a speed rusher At least one of the unproven young guys makes a major leap (CJ West, James Thompson Jr, Gracen Halton). As of now, with Odighizuwa and a healthy Fred Warner in front of a solid yet unspectacular secondary, I’m confident the defense will go from “mediocre” to “competent”. If one or two of that four-leg parley hit, I would be shocked if they can’t handle the rebuilding teams (Cardinals, Raiders, Dolphins), the decent teams with bad quarterbacks (Falcons), and the decent teams with uniquely bad interior offensive lines (Vikings, Commanders). Once you get to the Seahawks, the Chargers, and the Eagles, you need the 49ers defense to make game-altering plays. The 49ers’ offensive line isn’t equipped to handle those teams’ combination of a monster defensive line, the best non-Warner coverage linebackers in the game, and shutdown cornerbacks/safeties. Their…

title: 5 Questions with Turf Show times ahead of 49ers-Rams opener
summary: The 49ers kick off their regular season with a mouthwatering Week 1 clash with their division rivals, the Los Angeles Rams in a historic clash at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground. The first regular-season game to be held in Australia will be a key one in the fight for supremacy in the NFC West, with […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 49ers kick off their regular season with a mouthwatering Week 1 clash with their division rivals, the Los Angeles Rams in a historic clash at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground. The first regular-season game to be held in Australia will be a key one in the fight for supremacy in the NFC West, with both the 49ers and Rams expected to be in a tight fight for the division title with the Seattle Seahawks. Encounters between the Niners and Rams have typically been close and very entertaining affairs in recent years, though an offseason of blockbuster moves for Los Angeles has Sean McVay’s team as the favorites for this game and to go all the way and lift the Lombardi Trophy at SoFi Stadium in February. But how are Rams fans feeling about a roster that has been dubbed a ‘super team’ heading into the new campaign? SB Nation’s new app is perfect for game day! SB Nation’s NEW game chat feature in the app is perfect for keeping the latest 49ers updates and conversations at your fingertips. Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . I caught up with Evan Craig of Turf Show Times to find out. 1. The Rams have received the ‘super team’ billing after an offseason of spectacular moves. It’s exhausting for 49ers fans to see a rival stack so much talent, but what have you made of LA’s overall roster construction this offseason? Do you see any major holes? First off, I love when a team gets aggressive like this. Yeah, it can be costly and reckless regarding future roster construction. If you believe blockbuster moves will beef up your roster and put it over the edge, why not? You’ll never know if you don’t try. Whether or not this pans out for the Rams, I can respect them for making the moves they felt were necessary, even if it annoys the rest of the division. It was great seeing General Manager Les Snead make several splashes after holding off on them the last few offseasons. Signing Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson gave the secondary, which was a weakness last season, and made it a strength. Myles Garrett was certainly a luxury addition, yet the Rams needed juice in the pass rushing department and got it and then some. Those moves helped make them a Super Bowl favorite; championships obviously aren’t won in the offseason, so each one will have sky-high expectations to live up to. Given how the roster’s built, it’s very top-heavy, which could pose a problem should the injury bug bite. If that happens, then Snead will figure something out well ahead of the trade deadline. Wide receiver outside of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams is unproven. The Rams traded for Tutu Atwell after letting him go to the Dolphins, yet that’s not enough. LA barely used him when he was on the roster before, so I highly doubt anything changes here. Several young guys could be very exciting; only they need to be broken in gradually as they earn more playing time. Outside of WR3, that’s the main roster hole that I see. 2. Aaron Donald won’t play Week 1. What can we realistically expect from the returning three-time DPOY? Do you think he and Myles Garrett will immediately form a devastating duo, or will Rams fans have to be a little patient? Rams fans should be a little patient, because anyone expecting Aaron Donald to return to his old ways right off the bat is kooky. It might be somewhat easier for a defensive player to return to the field after time away. Still, as great as Donald is, he’s still two full seasons removed from NFL gameplay, even if he’s kept himself in shape during that time. I expect him to be on a snap count early into the season before the coaching staff gradually increases it throughout the season as he proves he can handle it. Eventually, Myles Garrett and AD will form a dynamic duo, but it’ll take time. I would say that with opposing offenses concentrating on them, it will pave the way for other players like Kobie Turner and Byron Young to take advantage. So, assuming the Garrett-Donald pairing works as anticipated, it could be more beneficial to other young pass rushers on the team. I’m glad the Donald “will he or won’t he” saga is finally over since it was getting pretty tiring over here. It was also too distracting as the team got ready for the season. I speak for all Rams fans when I say the noise better be worth it. 3. Away from the superstars, who are some players that have stood out for the Rams in training camp and preseason that could make an impact in Week 1? Rookie wide receiver CJ Daniels really stood out in the preseason and could have a sizable impact as the season progresses. In his final two preseason games against the Saints and Chargers, Daniels had 13 receptions for 110 yards on 19 targets, becoming a reliable target for fellow rookie Ty Simpson. He has plenty of growing to do, yet I believe he can form a nice rapport with Matthew Stafford as he earns more playing time throughout the season. Plus, with the Rams unsettled at the WR3 spot, it only boosts his chances of seeing more snaps. Keep an eye on second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson as well. The Rams love their tight ends (who doesn’t) and have no shortage of them, so mark my words, Ferguson will be on the field a bunch this year. 4. The Rams have long since been considered Super Bowl favorites, but how do you expect the season to pan out? Do you think they have enough to dethrone a still very good Seahawks team? As long as they stay healthy and things work out as fans expect, the Rams should finish with the top overall seed in the conference. On paper, they truly have the best team, and that’s not the biased Rams writer in me saying it. I’d say the same thing about the Niners if they constructed a team like this. I believe they have more than enough to dethrone the Seahawks this season, but will they? That remains to be seen. Seattle is still the team to beat until proven otherwise. It’s easy to pick the Rams because, again, they have the best team on paper, yet they seemed like the beat last season until the Seahawks upended them twice to end the year. Of course LA has the talent to win and unseat Seattle. It’s a matter of whether they can win the big games and actually beat the Seachickens. Until that happens, they haven’t proved a darn thing just yet. 5. Los Angeles is a 3.5-point favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook. Which way do you think the game will pan out and why? LA traveling to Australia right before the game is quite a bold, extremely risky strategy. If it pans out, then it might change how teams handle international travel moving forward. Personally, I’m in the crowd that the Rams’ travel plan isn’t the wisest. Fans will point to a similar plan the team had before their game in London last season. But this is a much different beast. When I went to Hawaii a few years ago, I was very jet-lagged after an eight-hour flight, so I cannot imagine how off these players are going to feel. I won’t be surprised if the 49ers win this one. The Rams have a far superior team, but between the long flight and all the new pieces that need to gel, I expect LA will be sluggish coming out. They’ll close the gap after a slow start. However, it won’t be enough in the end as they fall short. 49ers 27 Rams 24

title: Titans’ 1st impression vs. the Jets will say a lot
summary: Many reporters on the Tennessee Titans beat are calling Sunday’s Week 1 matchup versus the New York Jets a “must-win” opener. That is obviously ridiculous on the surface, but there’s some merit to those claims given the context. No team’s season was ever decided in Week 1, but these Titans are attempting to recapture this […]
full_text: (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Many reporters on the Tennessee Titans beat are calling Sunday’s Week 1 matchup versus the New York Jets a “must-win” opener . That is obviously ridiculous on the surface, but there’s some merit to those claims given the context. No team’s season was ever decided in Week 1, but these Titans are attempting to recapture this fanbase’s trust. The Titans endured consecutive 3-14 seasons in 2024 and 2025. This small-market fanbase hasn’t exactly been forgiving (understandably so). Many late-season games at Nissan Stadium have recently been played in front of meager crowds. The Titans underwent significant changes this offseason, both on and off the field. While general manager Mike Borgonzi continued rebuilding the roster, a rebranding also occurred. The Titans have three new uniforms, a new logo, and are preparing to open a new stadium in 2027. For Titans fans to maintain excitement over all the off-field developments, the on-field product needs to warrant it. The Jets have been considered a laughing stock of the NFL (the Titans, too). If Tennessee loses in Week 1 to the Jets, it wouldn’t be shocking if large portions of this fanbase snickered, said “same ole Titans,” before finding other ways to fill their Sundays. There’s also the revenge element. Head coach Robert Saleh used to coach these Jets. John Franklin-Myers, Jermaine Johnson II, Tony Adams, Solomon Thomas, and Jacob Martin are among those who played for them. Everyone involved wants to prove they’ve moved onto bigger and better things, with Saleh proving he was never the problem. Realistically, the Titans don’t need to qualify for the playoffs to convince this fanbase they’re on the right track. Fielding a competitive squad that doubles their 2024/2025 win total by finishing 6-11 would highlight direction and growth. Beginning the campaign by beating the Jets would be considered a good-faith gesture.

title: How Commanders QB Jayden Daniels shut out noise, prepped for Year 3
summary: Jayden Daniels essentially put a moratorium on discussing 2025 during Washington’s offseason program. The Commanders quarterback was done rehashing a sophomore season where he missed 10 games and finished only four, a disappointing encore to his NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign in 2024.   While he has long-since been done with it, the […]
full_text: Jayden Daniels essentially put a moratorium on discussing 2025 during Washington’s offseason program. The Commanders quarterback was done rehashing a sophomore season where he missed 10 games and finished only four , a disappointing encore to his NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign in 2024. While he has long-since been done with it, the page is formally turning. All focus is on its follow-up, which begins on Sunday against the Eagles in Philadelphia. “What I did in Year 1 and what I did in Year 2 doesn’t matter,” Daniels told on-site reporters during a press conference after Wednesday’s practice. “That’s what people are going to talk about – recency bias and all that – Year 2 is what it is. Now we’re on to Year 3. Whatever happens on Sunday will be what people talk about more than Year 2.” The criticism Daniels faced was more about availability than talent or performance, with the same pre-draft detractors wondering if his frame plus playing style could regularly weather the rigors of an NFL campaign. There’s little doubting Daniels’ passing accuracy or anticipation or scrambling/rushing ability. He has proved adept at those things in NFL games. Observers have also lauded Daniels’ ability to execute David Blough’s new offense and its pro-style, under-center requirements over the course of training camp. So many of these national season previews are questioning whether Daniels can be a top NFL quarterback, especially if Washington struggles to protect him. Daniels understands that previous success and talent brings heightened scrutiny when things don’t go right. “It comes with the territory,” Daniels said. “I was blessed enough to be a starting quarterback in the NFL. As a kid you dream of that but you know what actually comes with it. Having some success in this league brings more attention and you stay grounded, protect your peace of mind and focus on one-day-at-a-time.” That approach has led to an excellent summer. The Commanders know that. The coaching staff knows that, too. Few others have seen it live, which leads to an unevenness with how Washington’s perceived from the outside. There are fair questions about the state of the offensive line after Laremy Tunsil’s injury. We still haven’t seen the Commanders run – Bill Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White didn’t play in the preseason – and there’s little known about how Blough will call a game. Daniels understands his role on this particular team, with a deep receiver corps and tight end room, perfectly explained with a basketball analogy. “It’s about being a point guard, getting the ball to the playmakers in space and letting them do their thing,” Daniels said. “When it’s time for me to go get a bucket, I’ll go do that sometimes. That’s how I look at it.” It’s now time to play it out, starting in Week 1 and against a quality Eagles team while playing on the road. We’ve all talked enough. It’s time to go play. “It’s an exciting time,” Daniels said. “Football is back. … Just go out there and try to execute at a high level. They’ve got really good players over there. We’ve got good players over here, too. It’s going to be a hard-fought game.”

He’s still not ready to play so we won’t see him for a few weeks at least. That leaves Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson as the projected starting cornerback pairing. Both are undersized corners that profiled more as slot cornerbacks rather than outside cornerbacks due to their size. Sainristil has had some ups and downs over the past two years while Robertson is coming off a down year too. Behind them, Rasul Douglas and Fabian Moreau are two solid veterans, but neither were on the roster prior to training camp, so clearly they weren’t part of the initial plan at the cornerback position. So it’s fair for fans to have some concerns regarding this unit as we enter the regular season. It could potentially hold back a defense that is extremely promising up front. So what can new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones do to help mask those weaknesses in the secondary? To find that out, first we must take a quick look back at last season, where the play in the secondary was terrible, but also not helped much by the coaching staff. New defensive coordinator Daronte Jones is coming from a system in Minnesota where they also didn’t have big names in the secondary, but they produced one of the best defenses in the NFL. So what did they do in Minnesota that helped cover up the secondary? Well let’s start with the Cover-0 scheme. In preseason, we’ve already seen signs that Daronte Jones can dial up these pressures in Washington. In yesterday's The District Film Room session, @nick_akridge and I broke down one of the more exotice looks he showed pic.twitter.com/nNZalhQD1L — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 26, 2026 ESPN NFC East: Sizing up the Cowboys, Eagles, Giants and Commanders Expectation for quarterbacks Commanders Very high. Daniels has always been an accurate passer, but he looked even sharper throughout training camp. Offensive coordinator David Blough said he’s as “accurate as he’s ever been.” But his quick command of a new offense — how he handles the huddle, what he’s telling teammates as they break it or walk to the line — has also been impressive. He remains a dynamic playmaker, capable of turning bad plays into explosive ones. Washington has surrounded him with his strongest cast of passing targets — having added tight end Chig Okonkwo and receivers Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams to pair with Terry McLaurin — in his three seasons with the team. — John Keim How each team can win the division Commanders Daniels tops his rookie season and the defense takes a major step forward. Washington’s main offseason focus was improving arguably the NFL’s worst defense in 2025, adding high-profile pass rusher Odafe Oweh and drafting linebacker Sonny Styles among other moves. The Commanders are longer and faster in the front seven. Also, Daniels is coming off his best camp of his three seasons. It’s not far-fetched to see him topping his rookie year. But, of course, he must stay healthy. — Keim Don’t be surprised if … Commanders Daniels reminds everyone he’s capable of being a top-five quarterback and Washington is much better than people think. Of course, many think they will be one of the worst teams in the NFL. The Commanders have holes. The offensive line is a question after losing All-Pro left tackle Laremy Tunsil. If the line can be at least average — as it was two years ago en route to the NFC Championship Game — then the Commanders can surprise. An improved defense, especially the pass rush, needs to take a big leap to make the postseason. If Commanders don’t have a good one, they won’t surprise anybody. — Keim To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Why this season will get serious fast for the Commanders General manager Adam Peters had this to say about Sunday’s opener at Philadelphia: “We couldn’t be more thrilled than to start our season where we’re starting it,” Peters said after he and coach Dan Quinn finalized their third roster together. “It’s gonna be a great challenge, and we’re looking forward to it.” Might be an odd way to think about playing an Eagles franchise that has won back-to-back NFC East titles and been to the playoffs in all five seasons of coach Nick Sirianni’s tenure. But if Washington’s season is going to be a success — and a success means returning to the playoffs after last year’s 5-12 disaster — then it says here the Commanders are going to have to figure out a way to win at least one of their first two games, which are at Philly and at Dallas. Consider that in the last 20 NFL seasons, only 65 teams have opened with back-to-back divisional games. Of those teams, just 10 went 0-2. Of that group, just one — last year’s Chicago Bears — managed to put behind the miserable start against its biggest rivals and reach the playoffs. Even more ominous: Of those 10 teams to start 0-2 with both losses coming against divisional opponents, five fired their coaches, four in midseason. Five of the Commanders’ first eight games come against 2025 playoff teams, including the home opener against the Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Week 3. The second half — with just two playoff teams (Houston and Jacksonville) in nine games — might provide a chance to go on a run. Resources have not been put into running back The Commanders actually ran the ball fairly effectively in 2025, ranking fourth in the league in yards per game and fifth in yards per attempt. But 1,478 of their 2,290 yards on the ground last season came from players who are either on IR (McNichols), no longer play in Washington (Chris Rodriguez, Deebo Samuel, Austin Ekeler, Chris Moore), play quarterback (Daniels, Marcus Mariota) or some combination of those factors (Josh Johnson). To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Wire Commanders vs. Eagles: 5 things to know for Week 1 Opening the season in Philadelphia The Commanders and Eagles have opened the season in Philadelphia five previous times. Washington holds a 3-2 edge in those five previous road Week 1 meetings in Philly. The last time the Commanders opened a season in Philadelphia was in 2019. The Eagles won, 32-27, but that was Terry McLaurin’s first career NFL game, when he caught five passes for 125 yards and a touchdown. Quarterback Case Keenum missed a wide-open McLaurin on another potential touchdown. 11 total Week 1 meetings Sunday’s game will be the 12th time that Philadelphia and Washington meet in Week 1. The Commanders hold a 6-5 edge, including winning the last meeting in 2020, 27-17. Dwayne Haskins started under center for Washington and completed 17 of 31 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown. Peyton Barber scored two rushing touchdowns on that day, while McLaurin led the team with five receptions for 61 yards. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Week 1 should reveal how David Blough plans to divide the carries, passing-down work and short-yardage snaps…
