title: Hogs Haven 2026 season predictions – readers make the picks
summary: Something old; something new Something oldFor 14 years, Hogs Haven has published an annual article in which the site’s writers/contributors predict team and individual award winners for the upcoming season. This year’s edition of that prediction article was published earlier today. Something newThis year, for the first time ever, Hogs Haven invited members to participate […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 15: Jayden Daniels #5 and Terry McLaurin #17 of the Washington Commanders celebrate during a NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on December 15, 2024 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Something old; something new Something old For 14 years, Hogs Haven has published an annual article in which the site’s writers/contributors predict team and individual award winners for the upcoming season. This year’s edition of that prediction article was published earlier today. Something new This year, for the first time ever, Hogs Haven invited members to participate in the fun by formally submitting your predictions. In total, 51 readers took up the challenge, making predictions on the exact same questions as the writers/contributors. Hopefully, you participated in the fun. If not, you can still get your picks on record in the comments section. To view the predictions of all participating Hogs Haven members (listed in alphabetical order), CLICK THIS LINK Not unbiased, but still useful No one is suggesting that this is a scientific survey; members of Hogs Haven are passionate about the burgundy & gold. The predictions have more than the usual number of predictions that the Commanders will win the division, the NFC championship, and even the Super Bowl, and Washington players are heavily represented in predictions of Comeback Player of the Year, Offensive Player of the Year, Defensive Rookie of the Year, and League MVP. There’s nothing wrong with a bit of rooting for the home team — and, who knows? You may be right. I’ll summarize the broad strokes below, but if you want to hold yourself or your Hogs Haven nemesis accountable for his or her preseason optimism or pessimism, bookmark this link where 51 brave souls put their reputations on the line by signing their (user)names to predictions written in blood before the first snap of the 2026 season. The NFC East champion The Eagles were the most popular pick here, with 43% of the vote, but the Cowboys were surprisingly strong at 35%. It says something that 78% of readers on Hogs Haven picked Dallas or Philly to win the division. I’m not sure what it says, but something, anyway. About 20% of participants stayed true to the burgundy & gold, which is a bit less than I might’ve expected on a site full of passionate fans, but far beyond the national perception of Washington’s chances this year. Most popular picks for division champs in the 7 other divisions: When it comes to the AFC, where passions may not run as high, only 7 teams got more than 20% of the vote for regular season champs across the 4 divisions, and one team in each division got a clear majority of the vote. In the NFC, the Rams are the clear favorite in the West; the Bucs only slightly less so in the South, but the picture in the NFC North is muddled, with the only agreement being that the Vikings won’t be in contention. NFC NFC West – Rams (92%) NFC South – Buccaneers (64%), Saints (21%) NFC North – Lions (48%), Bears (29%), Packers (21%) AFC AFC East – Bills (87%) AFC North – Ravens (67%), Bengals (29%) AFC South – Texans (64%), Jaguars (27%) AFC West – Broncos (52%), Chiefs (31%), Wildcard Teams Voting for the AFC was consistent, with none of the top-3 teams in the wildcard vote showing up as divisional champs. Not surprisingly, the only division where things are a bit non-rational in this prediction exercise is the NFC East. The Eagles, who got the most votes for division champion (but not a majority) got picked as a wildcard team by pretty much everyone who didn’t pick them as division champs. Obviously, Philly can’t be both division champ and a wildcard team, so… If we assign the NFC East championship to the Eagles, then these results would put Washington into the playoffs as a wildcard team If we assume the Eagles get into the playoffs as a wildcard team, then the implication is that the Cowboys would be the division champs and the Commanders would be out of the playoffs. For my projected playoff seedings below (based on % of vote received), I assumed the scenario where the Eagles win the division, the Commanders qualify as a wildcard team, and the Cowboys watch the playoffs from their sofas. NFC Seahawks 73% Eagles 40% Bears 31% Commanders 29% 49ers 29% Lions 27% AFC Patriots 48% Chiefs 48% Chargers 44% Ravens 29% Bengals 29% Broncos 23% Based on these results, playoff seedings would be: Conference Champions There’s a lot of optimism being shown here by about 1 in 5 Hogs Haven readers. The consensus picks of Rams-Bills seem to be in line with national expectations and betting odds. NFC – Rams (60%), Commanders (19%) AFC – Bills (54%), Ravens (17%) Super Bowl Champions Rams 41% Bills 23% Commanders 15% Again, some real die-hard fans of the burgundy & gold are carrying the banner here. Also, I suspect that the Rams getting something like 2:1 odds (or is it 1:2?) of beating Buffalo in February is not far astray from national sentiment. First pick in the 2027 Draft Dolphins 40% Cardinals 25% Jets 14% Browns 8% This list appears to be close to the consensus of the 4 worst teams in the NFL as we approach the start of the season, which probably guarantees that at least one of them will make the playoffs. Awards I’ve listed the most popular pick in each category, except OPOY, where Josh Allen received 1 more vote than Jahmyr Gibbs. There was a clear favorite in every other prediction (though that does not mean a majority, just a clear separation from the #2 vote-getter). Comeback Player of the Year Jayden Daniels Coach of the Year Sean McVay Offensive Rookie of the Year Jeremiyah Love Defensive Rookie of the Year Sonny Styles Offensive Player of the Year Josh Allen Jahmyr Gibbs Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett League MVP Josh Allen Predict the Commanders regular season record 10-7 (21%) 8-9 (14%) 5-12 (14%) 7-10 (12%) 6-11 (10%) 9-8 (10%) These 6 outcomes accounted for 81% of the vote. You can see that, among these predictions, there are a lot more people expecting a losing record than a winning one. Count me among the optimists. I predicted 9-8 with a playoff win. title: Can Washington Commanders survive, thrive with Nick Allegretti at center?
summary: With the season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles less than a week away, the angst about the Commanders’ starting center position has reached obsessional levels.  The level of concern about a single roster position may have even surpassed the anxiety about the offensive tackle situation which gripped the fanbase ahead of the 2024 season. And […]
full_text: With the season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles less than a week away, the angst about the Commanders’ starting center position has reached obsessional levels. The level of concern about a single roster position may have even surpassed the anxiety about the offensive tackle situation which gripped the fanbase ahead of the 2024 season. And just look how that turned out. The makeshift duo of rookie third-round pick Brandon Coleman and fringe starter/reliable backup Andrew Wylie, whom many predicted would get the Commanders rookie quarterback killed, actually held up well enough for Jayden Daniels to have the best rookie debut of any QB in the modern era, leading the Commanders to within one game of the Super Bowl. The truth is nearly every NFL team has a few weak links on the roster, even those that make it to the Super Bowl. Sometimes that is the result of attrition through the season, with backups replacing starters. And in other cases, it is the result of situations like the Commanders found themselves in this offseason, when luck didn’t go their way in free agency or the draft. To illustrate what I mean, and hopefully put the Commanders’ center situation in perspective, I had a look at the starting offensive lines of teams that played in the Super Bowl over the past six NFL seasons. After missing out on Tyler Linderbaum in free agency, and failing to find value at center in the draft until Day 3, the Commanders are set to face the Eagles on opening day with Nick Allegretti snapping to Jayden Daniels. Allegretti is no All-Pro, but is he really bad enough to single-handedly prevent his team from making it to the playoffs? To answer that question, we’ll take a tour of the weakest links along the interior offensive lines of the last 12 Super Bowl teams. But before we do, let’s take a close-up look at the player at the center of attention. The Next Man Up G/C Nick Allegretti, 8 th year, age 30 6’ 4” | 310 lbs | 32.25” arms | RAS: 7.6 | 2026 cap number: $3.84 million 2025 Stats: 16 games | 4 starts | 260 snaps | 1 sack | 2 QB hits | 8 total pressures | 5.7% pressure rate | 45.1 run block grade | 3 penalties Allegretti has been a career backup with occasional stints as a starter, playing his first five seasons with the Chiefs and his last two with the Commanders. In his second season with the Chiefs, he started nine games at left guard, including two playoff games and Super Bowl LV. In 2024, he started all 17 regular season games and three playoff games for the Commanders at left guard. Throughout his career, Allegretti has played predominantly at left guard, but has also started three games at center and four at right guard. The Commanders like Allegretti’s toughness, reliability, intelligence and ability to play all three positions on the interior. Performance-wise, he is a replacement-level player at this point in his career, meaning that he is about what you’d expect from a veteran free agent on an inexpensive contract. Allegretti’s 5.7% pressure rate allowed in pass protection in just four starts in 2025 would have placed him at the 21 st percentile of starting iOL (approximated by the 96 centers and guards with the highest snap counts), if he had maintained that rate for a full season. Median for “starting” iOL was 4.6%. However, that is a very small sample to draw conclusions from blocking metrics, which are subject to considerable game-to-game variability. I would usually like to have at least twice as many games played. The figures from his most recent full season starting might be more representative of his abilities. In 2024 he allowed a pressure rate of 4.99%, which is at the 40 th percentile using last season’s figures. That year he allowed three sacks and one QB hit in 650 true pass blocking snaps. Unless he’s had a dramatic decline at age 30, he is probably somewhere between a below average starter and a bottom 20% starter in pass protection. Allegretti’s run blocking grades peaked at 71.3 in his sophomore season and have held steady in the low 60’s through 2024, before cratering to 45.1 last season. That might indicate a sudden drop off, but is more likely an artifact of having only played four games. His 63.9 run blocking grade from 20 games in 2024 ranked 57 th among the 96 most active iOL (41 st percentile). Unless he really fell off the cliff in 2025, his run blocking is probably a little below average for a staring interior offensive lineman. Overall, Allegretti’s performance in his most recent full season profiles in the below-average starting range. The numbers from 2025 are much worse. But it is dangerous to draw conclusions from a 4 game sample due to game to game variability. Comparable or Worse iOL Who Have Started in Super Bowls Now that we have a handle on the Commanders’ 2026 starting center, let’s see how he stacks up against the weakest links on the interior offensive lines of Super Bowl teams over the past 6 NFL seasons. Super Bowl LIX (2025) – Seattle Seahawks 29, New England Patriots 13 RG Anthony Bradford, Seahawks 6’ 4” | 335 lbs | 33.5” arms | RAS 9.78 | 3 rd year | age 24 2025 Stats: 20 starts | 1,037 snaps | 3 sacks | 5 QB hits | 28 total pressures | 6.1% pressure rate | 55.4 run block grade | 4 penalties I’ll kick this off with the player who inspired this article. Some Seahawks fans believe that their Super Bowl champion right guard is the worst player in football. Bradford started all 20 games at RG for the Seahawks last season and earned a Super Bowl ring in the blowout victory over the Patriots. His performance in the big game was not wonderful, with three QB hurries allowed and a pressure rate of 7.5%. But it was hardly his worst game of the season. Bradford is a physically imposing blocker with freakish athleticism, who has become legendary on the internet for his frequent mental gaffes and lapses of awareness. Let’s take a look at some of his work: TRENDING: #SEAHAWKS GUARD ANTHONY BRADFORD CONTINUES TO GO VIRAL EVERY WEEK. Bradford is one of the worst players in the league. Every week, Bradford figures out a way to get worse — it is truly a spectacle to watch. pic.twitter.com/wtLwm7qNME https://t.co/zXfJRUwqNr — MLFootball (@MLFootball) December 15, 2025 In an otherwise great season for the Seahawks, he was the one player who managed to stand out for the wrong reasons. His 6.1% pressure rate in pass protection ranked 83 rd out of 96 starting iOL in 2025. His numbers were worse than Allegretti’s last season and well below Allegretti’s level in 2024. Bradford’s 2025 run blocking grade ranked 74 th out of 96 iOL (23 rd percentile). The frustrating thing for Seahawks fans is that Bradford is wildly inconsistent. Plays where he is completely lost or whiffs are interspersed with dominant blocking efforts. Overall, his play is worse than Allegretti’s, but not bad enough to keep the Seahawks from taking home the Lombardi. Super Bowl LIX (2024) – Philadelphia Eagles 40, Kansas City Chiefs 22 LG Mike Caliendo, Chiefs 6’4” | 301 lbs | 30.9” arms | RAS 6.91 | 3 rd year | age 27 2024 Stats: 20 games | 6 starts | 410 snaps | 2 sacks | 3 QB hits | 15 total pressures | 6.2% pressure rate | 45.6 run block grade | 1 penalty Caliendo is a backup guard for the Chiefs. He got an opportunity to start 6 games at LG late in the regular season and the playoffs, when Andy Reid moved starting LG Joe Thuney to LT to replace struggling starter Wanya Morris. His numbers in pass protection and run blocking are even worse than Bradford’s and Allegretti’s. Nevertheless, the Chiefs won three regular season games and two playoff games with Caliendo starting at left guard. Super Bowl LVIII (2023) – Kansas City Chiefs 25, San Francisco 49ers 22 LG Nick Allegretti, Chiefs 2023 Stats: 21 games | 3 starts | 253 snaps | 2 sacks | 1 QB hit | 12 total pressures | 7.8% pressure rate | 59.6 run block grade | 1 penalty The weakest link on the Super Bowl LVIII champions’ iOL was none other than the man himself, Nick Allegretti. He was…

title: NFL Week 1 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips
summary: What should we expect from Patrick Mahomes? How will the Raiders handle their QB situation? Which receivers could break out? Our insiders have Week 1 intel.
full_text:
As we hit Week 1 of the  2026 NFL season , league insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 What should we expect from Patrick Mahomes and other players returning from significant injuries in the early parts of the season? Which teams might be flying under the radar and could surprise? Where are the most interesting and uncertain quarterback situations around the NFL? And for all those fantasy football managers out there, which players might come out of nowhere in Week 1?

 It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions and empty their reporting notebooks with everything they are hearing heading into the 2026 campaign.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Injury comebacks | Playoff sleepers 
 QB situations to watch | Breakouts 
 More notes, intel entering Week 1 

 
 

 Which player returning from a significant injury is best set up for a strong comeback? 
 Graziano: Let's start with the biggest name: Mahomes. He tore his ACL late enough last season that many wondered if he'd play at all in the early part of the 2026 season. But it was clear early in camp that he attacked his rehab and would be ready to go in Week 1. We should see him Monday night against the Broncos, and though the injury to left tackle Josh Simmons does give me a little pause, I think there's reason to believe the Chiefs' offense will be better around Mahomes.

 

 They replaced Matt Nagy with Eric Bieniemy at offensive coordinator, which doesn't seem like a big change given Bieniemy's history there, but they also changed out several other offensive assistants. And they are counting on a fully healthy Xavier Worthy , a ( hopefully ) fully healthy and engaged Rashee Rice and newly signed running back Kenneth Walker III to make them more explosive. I have the Chiefs bouncing back and reclaiming the AFC West title.

 Fowler: What helps Mahomes is a supporting cast that seems improved, especially if rookies Emmett Johnson and Cyrus Allen ascend, but Simmons' injury also gives me pause. But Mahomes is well-positioned to win Comeback Player of the Year. He hears the noise, the hint of doubt about his place in the QB pantheon for the first time in his career. I expect him to respond accordingly -- with a big season.

 But he isn't the only QB on the comeback trail. Jayden Daniels can reclaim his place as a premier quarterback, and there's considerable hype in league circles that Daniels will get back on track and be a problem for the rest of the NFC East. Kyler Murray has everything he needs in Minnesota to succeed if he can maximize Kevin O'Connell's offense.

 Graziano: I believe Daniels is a fantastic player and will play well as long as he's healthy. I have significant concerns about the group around him, particularly his offensive line, capping his (and the team's) performance ceiling this season. Hopefully for their sake I'm wrong.

 Some guys who I think are good enough to win Comeback Player of the Year if they come back healthy and play are:

 
 Giants wide receiver  Malik Nabers  if he helps to elevate Jaxson Dart and the Giants to playoff contender status 
 Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons if Green Bay makes a second-half defensive turnaround and a playoff run once he returns 
 Jaguars receiver/cornerback  Travis Hunter  if he plays like a lockdown corner and catches, say, three touchdown passes on offense. The Jags playing well again also would help. 
 
 Fowler: Parsons could provide a timely October lift for the Packers to contend. And the way Jacksonville plans to use Hunter -- as a primary zone corner and a "package" receiver -- will showcase his splash-play ability.

 And let's not forget about 35-year-old Aaron Donald . No, he's not returning from an injury, but he is unretiring -- and he will be a major force if he can get to 80% of his previous play. Interior rushers have proved they can play well into their mid-30s (see  Cameron Heyward  and Calais Campbell ). The sheer talent around Donald should free up rushing lanes and one-on-one opportunities. Still, the ramp-up will take some time. The Rams are sitting him this week , and returning after two-plus years out of football is no small feat. Part of the Rams' plan will be to keep Donald fresh for December and January snaps. That's the right strategy -- even if that sacrifices early-season sack numbers.

 

 

 
 Based on your preseason conversations, which team could be a real playoff sleeper? 
 Fowler: Sleepers are harder to find because of the league's deep parity, but let's go with the Giants, who won only four games last season. An NFL truism remains that you win with line play, and the Giants have that. They finally found an offensive line combination that works, resulting in a top-five rushing offense last season. The defensive line is well-stocked, even without defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II . Dart is widely viewed as a quarterback with an upward trajectory. Add the John Harbaugh confidence boost and Nabers' imminent return , and New York might have something. So, give me the Giants as a sneaky NFC playoff team.

 Graziano: The people I talk to seem to agree with you somewhat on the Giants. Those who buy into Dart as a real NFL starting QB point out how good they look up front on defense and that the offense has plenty to work with if Nabers is truly healthy. Those who doubt Dart are obviously more hesitant to back the Giants as sleepers.

 But, in general, I agree with you in that it's tough to find many true "sleepers" -- as in, teams most people don't think will be good but could end up being good. I keep talking myself into the Jets having a passable offense and maybe even a good one, but I don't expect them to contend with Buffalo and New England in the AFC East. I do think we will be talking about them as a potentially good spot for a rookie QB to land next spring.

 I'm going to stretch the definition a bit: I think people are sleeping on just how good the Jaguars can be. Jacksonville was 13-4 last season, won nine of its final 10 regular-season games and ended up winning the AFC South. It seems as if a lot of people have already conceded that division to the Texans, but it wouldn't surprise me to see Jacksonville build on last season's progress under Liam Coen, repeat as division champs and make a playoff run.

 Fowler: The Jaguars are deep and will be able to move the ball. Their three-man receiving corps is among the league's best. The offensive line faces questions -- it's lacking ideal size and has had some injuries. But Coen made it work with that group last season and should again.

 

 Your point on the Jets is a fair one -- I was there for camp and the roster is better. But the Jets haven't won eight or more games since 2015, so it's tough to bank on them until they show it. But here's a snoozefest of a sleeper, if we're going that deep: the Browns.

 I'm not declaring that Cleveland will make the playoffs just yet, but there's legitimate talent on both sides of the ball. The defense has a chance to be stout. Resources were spent to replenish the line. The offense is well-stocked with intriguing young talent. If Deshaun Watson 's play graduates from poor to passable, Cleveland might be in decent shape in Todd Monken's first season .

 Graziano: If Watson had played passably in 2022, 2023 or 2024, Monken probably wouldn't be there, because Kevin Stefanski probably would have kept his job. We haven't seen Watson play well since 2020, so I'm going to have to see a lot of success from Watson/Cleveland before I believe it.

 I also need to point out that while many seem to see the NFC West as a two-team race (or even a one-team race!), the 49ers should be a threat to win that division if they can keep everyone healthy ( I know, I know ). They were still in the hunt for the division title and the NFC's No. 1 seed in Week 18 last season despite their injury issues. If San Francisco starts the season by beating the…

title: Springboks captaincy aside, RGR series proves Siya Kolisi is an all-time flanker great
summary: Siya Kolisi has not unanimously been recognised as a top-tier loose forward in the history of the game. If there was any doubt remaining, this series should have put that to bed.
full_text:
Siya Kolisi broke the record for Test wins as South Africa captain in Saturday's 29-24 win over New Zealand, but the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry (RGR) series has proven he is not only one of the greatest captains ever, but also one of the top flankers.

 Kolisi's 55th Test win as captain saw him officially surpass John Smit's 54 for the Springboks, but realistically, he cemented his legacy as the greatest Bok captain to date when he became the first to lift a second successive Rugby World Cup in 2023.

 Still, he has not unanimously been recognised as a top-tier loose forward in the history of the game. If there was any doubt remaining, this series should have put that to bed, and will be cemented in Baltimore on Saturday.

 

 Leadership aside, the difference between a Springbok side with and without Kolisi has been absolutely visible in pure rugby terms.

 In the first Test, the Boks started with a loose trio of Paul de Villiers, Pieter-Steph du Toit, and Jasper Wiese.

 They fared well in the first half, but Wiese aside, lost control in the second. Marco van Staden - who came on for de Villiers after the hour-mark - was yellow-carded late on, doing little to help the cause.

 Kolisi returned to the fold from injury for the second Test in Cape Town, scoring a crucial try and drawing a roar from the crowd with a huge hit on Ardie Savea as the latter received the ball at the back of a lineout.

 He made a huge contribution in the third Test, too - particularly on defence when the Boks were under the cosh during periods of the first half.

 

 On For the Love of Rugby , injury-embattled veteran Springbok prop Trevor Nyakane said: "If you sleep at a breakdown and Siya is around it, you best know he is going to put you on your back.

 "If you really understand the game that we play, things like that - donkey work - it's invaluable.

 "Most people don't see. You always see the guys that are scoring the tries, but you don't ask yourself: 'How did that space open up?'

 "It comes from guys like Siya who will be selfless in the team, in the structure - understanding that it's not him. We all drink from the same cup. When we win, it's not one person that won; it's South Africa that won."

 

 It is true that much of what Kolisi does goes unseen. However, the stats alone are increasingly beginning to favour the argument for the 35-year-old going down as one of the game's all-time greats in his position.

 Only seven players playing predominantly as flankers have ever reached 110 Test caps: Richie McCaw, Pablo Matera, Michael Hooper, Alessandro Zanni, Peter O'Mahony, Ardie Savea, and George Smith.

 Kolisi (currently on 106) is on course to become the eighth by the end of this year if he stays fit. McCaw is the only one among the seven flankers with 110 caps to have ever won a World Cup - captaining the All Blacks to victory in 2011 and 2015.

 For a flanker to have the consistency of Kolisi in an elite team puts him in almost unparallelled territory. Being drafted into a series against the All Blacks after missing the first Test through injury and having such a clear impact aged 35 should see him honoured as world class in pure rugby terms alone.

 He may have avoided placing himself among the game's all-time greats when he discussed the topic in his 2021 autobiography "Rise". However, much has changed since then.

 Kolisi won a second World Cup. Then, he endured a difficult 2023-24 season with Racing 92 and announced later in 2024 that he would be getting divorced - but still won Rugby Championship titles in 2024 and 2025 even amid the personal turmoil.

 In November 2025, he made it to 100 Springbok caps, and in 2026, he has played an instrumental role in salvaging the RGR series - which will either end in a draw or a Springbok win.

 Kolisi will undoubtedly be honoured alongside McCaw as one of the game's greatest ever captains. When its greatest ever flankers are listed, both belong at the top.

title: Predicting the 2026 NFL playoff field, plus Super Bowl pick
summary: Which teams from last season's playoffs will return -- and which ones will miss out? Who will be the surprises in the bracket? And who will win the Super Bowl?
full_text:
It's postseason projection time. With hours to go before the first game of the 2026 NFL season , I'm picking the 14 teams that will be celebrating after the league plays 272 regular-season games. There's so much football to come and so many unexpected things we'll see along the way, but like anyone else, I want to lay out the playoff field I expect to see in January before the games kick off in mid-September.

 Of course, that would be too easy. If you've read this column over the past couple of years , you'll remember that there's a twist. One of the most common mistakes we make as football fans -- myself included -- is overconfidence in the teams we saw excel last year. We're collectively too inclined to pick teams that made the playoffs a year ago to make it back in the current season. Ask me to pick 2026 playoff teams without any constraints and I'd pick at least nine of the 14 teams that made it in 2025.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 History tells us that's underestimating the chaos and variance that comes with 17-game NFL seasons. The league has been using the 14-team playoff format for only a few years now, but if we go back to 2002 and treat the seventh-best team in each conference as a playoff team, about 56% of teams that make it to the postseason in any given season make it back the following year. That's just under eight teams per campaign.

 Eight teams in, six teams out. There's no guarantee that 2026 will play out like an average season in terms of playoff returnees, but the evidence says our playoff predictions should start there. I'll take things a step further by looking at division champions and teams with losing records in 2025 to tailor the field even closer to what a historic playoff field typically looks like by the end of the regular season. I'll detail how those play out along the way. And at the end, I'll make my Super Bowl pick for the upcoming season.

 

 
 Jump to a section: 
 2025 division champions 
 2025 wild-card berths 
 From out to in 
 Barnwell's Super Bowl pick 

 
 

 Which 2025 division champions will return to the playoffs? 
 Let's start by splitting last season's playoff teams into two groups. Since 2002, just under 60% of teams that won their division in a given year have made it back to the playoffs the following season. That's 4.8 teams per year, which we'll round up to five. So, of the eight division winners from 2025, I have to pick five to return to the playoffs in 2026.

 We can split that even further. About 43% of division winners repeat as champs the following season, with teams such as the Tom Brady-era Patriots and the  Patrick Mahomes -era Chiefs as near-perennial favorites to finish first. If we remove the Patriots and Chiefs from the data set, the rate of repeating divisional winners drops to 36%. That's an average of about three division winners retaining their titles each season.

 

 One of the weirdest things about the 2025 season factors in here. In 2024, six of the eight teams that won their division the prior year retained their crowns, which was just the third time that has happened in the eight-division era. In 2025, everything went in the opposite direction. Just one of the eight reigning champs held on to its division title for another year. The one team that did so was the Philadelphia Eagles , who became the first team to win back-to-back titles in the NFC East in more than two decades. Four 2024 division champs -- the Chiefs, Ravens, Lions and Buccaneers -- missed the postseason outright in 2025.

 History tells us to pick three division winners to repeat as champions, with two more making it back to the postseason as wild cards. I'll then be left with three division winners from 2025 that I'll need to pick to miss the playoffs entirely. I'm sure that won't upset anyone ...

 Running through my options, I'm already beginning to squirm. I'm not sure there are three division winners with good chances of repeating in 2026. I like some of last season's wild-card teams more than the division winners. If this were just "pick eight playoff teams to repeat," I might have five division winners missing the playoffs. This is why I like doing this column in this very particular way -- it forces me to think about choices I don't necessarily love but that might turn out to be more realistic as the season plays out in the months to come.

 
 

 Seattle Seahawks 
 My pick for 2026 : In the playoffs (NFC West champions)

 It feels almost controversial to pick the defending Super Bowl champions to stay atop the NFC West for another year. It's easy to understand why the Rams are favorites to top the Seahawks and return to the top of the division; they added Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald , Trent McDuffie  and Jaylen Watson to their roster this offseason.

 But the Seahawks did beat the Rams twice in three tries last season. They went 14-3, finishing two games ahead of Los Angeles in the race for the NFC West, and led the league in DVOA. Sure, the Seahawks were one of the league's healthier teams, especially on offense, but they also outscored opposing teams by more than 11 points per game and went a sustainable 4-3 in games decided by seven points or less.

 The champs lost several players on defense ( Coby Bryant , Riq Woolen  and Boye Mafe among them), but coach Mike Macdonald has a significant track record of developing both young players and underappreciated veterans into useful contributors on the defensive side of the ball. And virtually everybody of note beyond Super Bowl MVP  Kenneth Walker III is back on offense. It would be a surprise if the Seahawks weren't competing for a division title this season.

 

 
 

 Philadelphia Eagles 
 My pick for 2026 : In the playoffs (NFC East champions)

 If the Eagles were able to overcome what had been a multi-decade run of new champions in the NFC East to finally hold on to their division crown, I'm willing to back Jalen Hurts & Co. to make it three straight in 2026. Things didn't end well for the Eagles in 2025, as they lost four of their final seven games before being bounced out of the playoffs by the 49ers , but you might remember the Eagles going through a similar scenario in 2023. They started 10-1, lost five of their last six games and were then blown out by the Bucs in the wild-card round. Yet Philly won the division the following season -- and also won the Super Bowl.

 The Eagles weren't great on offense, but things really began to crater once they lost star right tackle   Lane Johnson in November. The 36-year-old is back as part of what should be a healthier offensive line. Vic Fangio fielded the youngest defense in the league last season, and that unit could be even more productive after adding Riq Woolen and Jonathan Greenard to the mix during the offseason. Sean Mannion's new under-center offensive scheme creates some uncertainty, but the Eagles have one of the highest floors of any team in the NFL.

 
 

 New England Patriots 
 My pick for 2026 : In the playoffs (AFC East champions)

 I've already written about why I don't expect the Patriots to win 14 games again, which shouldn't be any sort of significant surprise. (It's hard to win 14 games twice in a row!) Even with a bit of a step backward, though, the Patriots could still hold on to their AFC East title with something like an 11-win campaign.

 Their schedule is tougher, but it's still the 11th-easiest slate in the league per ESPN's Football Power Index . They'll probably suffer more injuries after being one of the healthiest teams a year ago, but unless stars such as  Drake Maye , Christian Gonzalez  and A.J. Brown miss significant time, the Patriots should still have plenty of talent. And if the blitz-happy defensive scheme that helped sustain the Patriots as their offense struggled during the AFC playoffs carries over into 2026, the Pats might actually be a better team on a snap-by-snap basis than they were in 2025 -- even if that doesn't produce a similar…

title: What's got Bills coach Joe Brady's energy up?
summary: The highly caffeinated 36-year-old is the youngest head coach in the NFL while he oversees a contending Buffalo team.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Sleep, in Joe Brady's mind, is overrated.

 No, wait. Scratch that. 

 He reconsiders. It's not that it is overrated. Instead, it's the most important thing.

 But, Brady asserts, that he has tried to "convince" his brain that he can operate without it.

 During seasons past, Brady -- before becoming a head coach for the Buffalo Bills -- would sleep no more than three or four hours a night. 

 Brady can sustain such a schedule with the help of caffeine, which plays an important role in his life, but declares caffeine is just an assist. 

 His brain doesn't stop either way.

 

 The first-time head coach made it clear that he's "not living on caffeine." Yet on the morning of a sitdown with ESPN in June, he was on his second Gatorade Fast Twitch of the day. He's an espresso guy, not coffee. On the road for games and in the summer it's café con leche when it can be found on a food delivery app.

 Brady's consistent energy has been noted by staff and coaches over the years, even in the early hours of the morning. Quarterback Josh Allen noted Brady's fast-talking nature pops up when he's wired for team meetings in the morning, espresso in tow.

 Now that ever-moving brain has a tall task on its hands in leading the Bills and continuing to call offensive plays.

 The highly caffeinated but light on sleep 36-year-old is the youngest head coach in the NFL, and over a team that is listed for the second-highest odds of winning Super Bowl LXI (10-1), per DraftKings Sportsbook. 

 Brady has worked this offseason to put his own stamp on the Bills. Now the time has arrived to see how his high-energy iteration of the Bills translates on the field as Buffalo plays at the Houston Texans in Week 1 ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 "This is Year 1 in the Joe Brady era," said Allen. "What he's doing it's gonna take the conviction to buy in, in order to achieve what we want to achieve. And it's going to take everybody in this locker room to do it."

 

 CHANGE IS A visual thing in Orchard Park.

 As the leaves begin to turn, the new Highmark Stadium has transformed the landscape and can be seen from different vantage points around Western New York.

 It's audible, too.

 At an arbitrary Bills practice, the music blasting throughout the session stands out. Not the fact that it's playing itself, but that this music contains significantly more expletives. There's no censoring this practice unlike what the previous coaching regime did.

 The change was something the players requested in which Brady obliged. It is one of many changes that he has brought to the team after coach Sean McDermott's nine-year tenure ended on Jan. 19 when he was fired .

 "Right, wrong or indifferent. I want the guys, this is their safe space," Brady told ESPN. "... I don't want them to have to think about the music."

 Training camp practices were moved earlier in the day in part to embody Brady's "put the ball down mantra" -- that the team can play whenever and wherever. Therefore, less practices were held at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York than in years past. The choice was to encourage players to spend time together as opposed to going back-and-forth to Buffalo, and to simulate game-like weeks.

 Offense and defense switched practice jersey colors.

 "[There's a] new energy in the building and he wants us to be well conditioned," right tackle Spencer Brown said of Brady's changes. " He's letting guys be themselves, trying to get the ball in everybody's hands and stay together."

 

 For every change, there are also consistencies.

 General manager Brandon Beane is still in charge, but now with more power as the president of football operations with Brady now reporting to Beane as opposed to separately to owner Terry Pegula. Much of the support staff has stayed in place. But the coaches are new, notably the coordinators, namely defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard and offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. 

 When Beane described the process of hiring Brady, a focus was put on having a "CEO-type of head coach" who brought alignment and his own "strong culture."

 "From a staff point of view and from a player point of view, there's still a lot of familiar faces. Gives me the vibe that they probably didn't want to blow it up for that very reason," long-snapper Reid Ferguson , one of the team's longest tenured players said. "... We were having a lot of success over the last decade."

 Many of the tweaks Brady has made are done with the players in mind. A big one for the season is changing practice to later in the day so players can eat lunch before and then have dinner at a more standard time.

 "There is a lot of support for that," Ferguson said. "We used to practice ... 12:30 to 2:30, and I would eat lunch after practice at 3 or 3:30 and I would go home, and my wife would have dinner, and I would basically just sit there with her and the kids and I'd be like, 'I just ate two hours ago. I'm not hungry.'"

 On his side, Brady emphasized during his introductory news conference that he needs to have his "uninew energy" every day, while acknowledging assists from espresso or Fast Twitch.

 "I believe people are going to feed off [my energy]," Brady said. "I truly believe in being the temperature. I'm the weather, and they're going to feel it every single day, a mentality."

 

 EXPLAINING THE WHY is important to Brady -- so people in the building understand the reasons behind something being done.

 "Why are we calling this? Why are we doing this? Whether they need to hear it or not," Brady said. "It's important, because then it allows guys to at least have an understanding of it."

 DJ Mangas, now the Bills pass game specialist, has known Brady since they were teammates, and roommates for a time, at William & Mary. He joined his friend at LSU, then for a season with the Carolina Panthers , where Brady was offensive coordinator in 2020 and for most of 2021 before being fired, and since 2023 with the Bills.

 He thinks the desire to explain the why comes from Brady, as a player and coach, not understanding why things were done himself. Understanding, in turn, brought energy.

 "When he finally figured out the why to why we're doing something, it clicked," Mangas said. "It's almost energizing and it makes you a better player or it makes you a better coach."

 

 Learning is a theme of Brady's coaching career. He has publicly discussed the lessons taken from his stretch as the Panthers coordinator. In hiring his coaching staff, Brady brought in coaches who have plenty of experience in former head coach John Fox and Carmichael. 

 Brady has changed over the years to get here, too. "The Carolina thing I think was, I know he's been pretty open about it, it's been one of the best things that's happened to him. He's learned so much, I think, from that experience," Mangas said.

 "... He felt like he just didn't, not that he didn't care for the players, but he spent too much time in the X's and O's, this is his words, as opposed to I think communicating and connecting with the players. And obviously I have definitely seen a change in that."

 Quarterback Kyle Allen saw Brady through the ranks to elevate at One Bills Drive from quarterbacks coach to interim offensive coordinator to offensive coordinator to head coach, however, note the consistency he's shown.

 "He's the same guy though as a head coach, which is awesome to see," Allen said. "And he's in the quarterback room all the time, too and it hasn't changed. Hasn't got an ego. We still give him some s---, and he won't get mad about it."

 Lessons come on a daily basis for Brady, who repeatedly emphasizes a focus on where he is in that moment. Some of that comes in the form of internal feedback, including asking for coaches to anonymously send him what they would change, things that they think should be emphasized and answering, "If you were head coach right now, what's one thing you would change?" 

 "I think there's…

title: Commanders' crab stuffed pretzel headlines new NFL 2026 foods
summary: The latest NFL season has no shortage of unique concession items that will debut across stadiums.
full_text:
When it comes to the NFL, the league seems to level up each season. The same applies to foods debuting at league stadiums.

 

 Arguably the best from any team is a crab stuffed pretzel sold at Northwest Stadium, home of the Washington Commanders . The crab-shaped pretzel is filled with lemon tarragon crab dip topped with garlic butter and grated parmesan cheese created by Levy Restaurants.

 

 Here's a look at some of the top new foods at NFL stadiums this season.

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers : Black N' Gold Chicken and Waffle 

 The iconic colors of the Steelers are represented in a classic Southern meal that includes fried chicken, coleslaw, bacon jam, sweet potato fries and hot honey.

 

 

 Philadelphia Eagles : Tush Push Taters 

 Philadelphia fans have seen their share of success with the tush push in recent years. Now, the play has a meal named after it. The item consists of a deep-fried potato with a fried chicken cutlet, mac and cheese, bacon hot honey jam, scallions and 215 sauce.

 

 

 Eagles: Broad Street Beast 

 Now available at Lincoln Financial Field is an 18-inch chalupa shell that includes wagyu beef shank, fried jalapeno poppers, tomatillo avocado salsa, Oaxaca queso, shallots and cilantro.

 

 

 Cincinnati Bengals : Who Dey Sausage 

 The Bengals' "Who Dey" chant is the namesake for a 24-inch BBQ cheddar pork sausage served on a bun with pickled red onions, jalapeno and BBQ sauce.

 

 

 Carolina Panthers : The Big 'Dilla 

 The two-foot smoked adobo chicken quesadilla includes a cheddar and jack cheese seared tortilla plus cilantro, pico de gallo and chipotle crema.

 

 

 Denver Broncos : Beast in a Blanket 

 Denver's take on a two-foot item is a hot dog with brisket burnt ends, cheddar and goat cheese wrapped in a puff pastry. It's topped with secret sauce, avocado cream, pickled onions and jalapeno.

 

 

 Houston Texans : Battle Red Berry Bird 

 Houston rocks battle red uniforms, therefore, it's only right that a concession item named after the threads is created. Fried chicken breast is tossed in a strawberry buffalo sauce and topped with coleslaw, pickles and Cajun cheese curds on a challah bun.

title: One thing Deshaun Watson has to improve to remain Browns' starter
summary: Whether the veteran passer can regain dominance over this particular skill will help determine his role in 2026.
full_text:
When Deshaun Watson takes the field as the Cleveland Browns ' starting quarterback during Sunday's Week 1 game (1 p.m. ET, CBS) at the Jacksonville Jaguars , it will likely mark the beginning of his final opportunity to salvage his tenure in Cleveland -- and possibly his NFL career.

 Whether Watson can do so hinges on him recapturing a semblance of his Pro Bowl form with the Houston Texans , a player for which the Browns were willing to trade three first-round picks and give a fully guaranteed $230 million contract in March 2022 after more than two dozen women accused him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during massage sessions.

 

 Suspension- and injury-related layoffs have been the story of Watson's time in Cleveland. His latest physical setback: two Achilles surgeries that cost him all of the 2025 season and 22 months between live game action. Watson acknowledged that, at the age of 30 and after multiple significant injuries, his style of play might not resemble that of his peak dual-threat capabilities in Houston.

 However, his accuracy on downfield passing and willingness to push the ball -- once a strength -- is an area of his game that has declined in recent years and will need to improve if he wants to keep his job as QB1.

 When Watson was named to three consecutive Pro Bowls as a member of the Texans, he wasn't just one of the league's premier mobile quarterbacks but a pinpoint passer able to stretch the field.

 In 2018, Watson ranked third among 34 qualifying quarterbacks in completion rate (58.8%) on downfield passes (attempts that traveled at least 10 air yards), according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Watson led the NFL in passing yards in 2020, and he only trailed then-Saints QB Drew Brees in completion rate on downfield pass attempts at 59.9%. Even in Watson's six-game run in his first year in Cleveland after sitting out the 2021 season and serving an 11-game suspension, he completed 53.1% of his downfield passes, which would have ranked sixth.

 

 That mark has declined in recent years. In 2023, Watson completed 39.3% of his downfield attempts, which would have ranked as the worst rate in the league if he qualified. His 33.3% off-target rate on such passes only trailed Panthers QB Bryce Young for the worst in the league. Watson's stat worsened in 2024, as he completed a career-low 37.9% of downfield attempts before his Achilles tear sidelined for the final 10 games of the season.

 Compounding Watson's struggles is an aversion to attempting to push the ball downfield. Watson's average depth of target has dropped significantly, from 9 yards in his final Pro Bowl season in 2020 to a career-low 7.1 in his most recent season in 2024, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Watson threw downfield on a career-low 26.9% of his passes in 2024, his second career season with a rate below 30%, including his 28.8% mark in his 2022 debut season with the Browns.

 The struggles coincide with a right, throwing shoulder injury that Watson originally sustained against the Tennessee Titans in Week 3 of the 2023 season. He ultimately underwent season-ending surgery for a fractured glenoid after a Week 10 road win against the Baltimore Ravens .

 Watson returned for the start of the 2024 season but never looked comfortable before his season-ending Achilles injury in October 2024.

 In his first news conference since rupturing his Achilles, he said in June this was the first time he felt 100% healthy since initially injuring his shoulder against the Titans.

 Despite confidence in his physical state, Watson's passing was inconsistent in training camp, and he struggled to push the ball downfield in the preseason. In two preseason games, he was 1-of-6 for 20 yards and an interception on downfield passes; such attempts made up just 22.2% of his passes in the preseason.

 

 "That's something I've always been pretty good at, especially in the past," Watson said Aug. 19. "But those looks and opportunities got to come up. Whatever coach is calling, I try to execute as much as possible, keep the chains moving. Especially early on, it's hard to really start taking shots when the defense is sitting back on that. Especially with Chicago [first preseason game], they were playing a lot of two-wide shells, so a lot of underneath things were right there. But that's something I definitely want to continue to work on, and when those opportunities come, take advantage of it."

 Explosive plays are a priority in first-year head coach Todd Monken's offense. In a 2023 presentation at The Harbaugh Academy, Monken listed explosive plays as one of six figures that best explain how teams win games.

 After Watson was named the Browns' starting quarterback on Aug. 24 despite struggles in the second preseason game, questions surfaced on how much leeway he would have as QB1. If he's unable to generate the explosive plays Monken desires, Watson's backup, Shedeur Sanders , could provide a more aggressive option.

 Though Sanders struggled as a rookie in 2025, his downfield passing -- and willingness to do so -- have been one of his greatest assets. During his seven starts last season, Sanders completed 15 passes on downfield attempts, tied for 19th most among quarterbacks during that span; his 58 downfield attempts were 17th most. Sanders was even better in this year's preseason, completing 5 of 8 of his downfield attempts for 106 yards with a touchdown and an interception (36.4% of his attempts were downfield passes).

 Adherence to one of Monken's core tenets could define Watson's 2026 season. Watson's first test comes against a Jaguars defense that allowed a 42.8% completion percentage on downfield throws last season, the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL.

 "Everyone's chasing explosives and trying to not to turn it over," Monken said last week. "And that's what you're trying to do. What's the defense trying to do? Turn you over and not allow explosives. That's really the big chess match, is that. The ways that you win.

 "Obviously having explosive players helps that. Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I'm confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn't be starting him."

title: Respectful Lions eager to tangle with Saints in opener
summary: Campbell spent five seasons as an assistant to Sean Payton and credits the former Saints coach as the reason he was hired in Detroit.
full_text:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- Dan Campbell began his pre-practice speech on Tuesday morning by highlighting his longtime adoration for the New Orleans Saints organization.

 Campbell expressed his respect for the way they've built the program -- and doesn't want his team overlooking the Week 1 opponent -- as the Detroit Lions prepare to kick off the 2026 season against the Saints on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

 "He opened this morning by talking about how not only have they had this mindset there that the defensive football and grind-it-out football is big-time in their mentality," said Scottie Montgomery, Lions associate HC/wide receivers coach. "But, also, the personnel that they have that's been set by players that have been there before and that are there now and they continue that grit."

 Campbell's thoughts and coaching DNA were shaped throughout his time within the Saints organization, which he often references.

 Campbell spent five seasons with the Saints (2016-20) as an assistant head coach/tight ends coach before being hired as head coach of the Lions in 2021.

 He won his only previous game versus the Saints as Lions head coach at New Orleans' Caesars Superdome in 2023.

 In New Orleans, Campbell benefited from the tutelage of former head coach Sean Payton with Mickey Loomis, serving as the executive vice president/general manager, where they captured four NFC South division titles during that span.

 "It means a lot. Had it not been for my time there with that organization, it's a class act and a class organization and being with Sean Payton, obviously, I wouldn't have gotten this opportunity," Campbell said. "So, it means a ton and the environment's got to be right.

 "It's got to be the right conditions and we had the right conditions, and you don't forget those and you try to carry over the things that you feel like are done right that you do right and take them to where you go, and there's a lot of similarities in that regard."

 The Week 1 contest at Ford Field will mark his second time facing the Saints, and Campbell says, "they have got some potency" on this year's roster despite coming off a 6-11 season.

 After starting with a 2-10 record last year, the Saints went 4-1 in their final five games as the defense allowed 17.6 points per game in Weeks 14-18, which was tied for the fifth fewest in the NFL with the Los Angeles Chargers during that span.

 Detroit is also looking to bounce back from a disappointing 2025 season where they finished 9-8 while failing to reach the postseason for the first time since 2022.

 

 The Lions enter 2026 with high expectations, including a 40% chance to win the NFC North, per ESPN Analytics, which is the highest of any team in the division, despite finishing last in the NFC North last season.

 Lions assistant head coach/safeties Jim O'Neil described the team's level of excitement as being extremely high for the opening week, notably after completing "as hard of a camp as I've been around."

 "We got after it, and I feel that everybody got better," O'Neil said.

 For Campbell, it goes without saying that this Saints game means a lot. Although he's respectful of the opponent, he's done everything throughout training camp to make sure "we'll be ready to go" at kickoff.

 Nobody within the organization wants to let him down while going against his former team, either.

 "There is a certain level of heightening of awareness from assistants to make sure we give our head football coach the best opportunity we can and our program and the organization the best chance we have to go win this game," Montgomery said.

title: Jalen Brunson becomes the latest notable athlete to host 'Saturday Night Live'
summary: There have been 35 athletes to host the sketch comedy staple, including greats such as Peyton Manning, Derek Jeter and LeBron James.
full_text:
Fresh off delivering the New York Knicks the franchise's first NBA title in a half-century, Jalen Brunson 's tour de force in the Big Apple is set to continue under a different primetime spotlight: that of Studio 8H.

 

 On Wednesday, "Saturday Night Live" revealed the first four hosts and musical guests of the show's upcoming 52nd season. Leading things off on Sept. 26? Brunson, who will be accompanied by musical guest Katseye.

 

 Brunson will be far from the first athlete to host the show. The first to do it was then- Minnesota Vikings quarterback Fran Tarkenton, who was the guest host on the 13th episode of the second season, with many more coming afterward -- including most notably Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, who has hosted the show five times, more than any other athlete, his first turn coming in 2000.

 Ahead of Brunson's appearance, we look at some notable sketches from sports figures who have appeared on the show.

 

 John Madden |  Sept. 7, 1982 

 Long before the Madden Cruiser ferried the famously aerophobic Madden between games, he traveled by train. Look for how many times the late, great broadcaster tries to tell the story about leaving a player behind after a game.

 

 

 Marvin Hagler |  May 17, 1986 

 Just two months after defending his middleweight title with a win over John Mugabi, Hagler co-hosted the show with journalist Jimmy Breslin. In this sketch, Hagler, who won 52 fights by knockout in his career, gives viewers advice on how to get knocked out.

 

 

 Wayne Gretzky |  May 13, 1989 

 The hockey legend hosted the show fresh off his first season with the Los Angeles Kings , following "The Trade" the offseason prior. Among other skits, Gretzky played himself as the guest host of a call-in show -- fielding a number of questions that had no relation to hockey.

 

 

 Chris Evert |  Nov. 11, 1989 

 The 18-time Grand Slam winner was the first female athlete to host the show. She was joined by musical guest the Eurythmics. This is Evert's historic monologue:

 

 

 Michael Jordan |  Sept. 28, 1991 

 Just months after winning his first NBA title, Jordan hosted the premier episode of SNL's 17th season. The GOAT gave an all-time showing in "Daily Affirmations with Stuart Smalley." Jordan, who was on the show with Public Enemy, has yet to host again.

 

 

 Charles Barkley |  Sept. 25, 1993 

 After winning NBA MVP and reaching the NBA Finals, Barkley hosted the Season 19 premiere. Barkley has hosted three other times since then. He did his own "Daily Affirmation" in his first episode. However, one of the best moments was unintended and came from a promo shoot with Nirvana, that episode's musical guest.

 

 

 Deion Sanders |  Feb. 18, 1995 

 Just weeks after winning his first Super Bowl with the San Francisco 49ers , Prime Time took over Studio 8H. He had one notable NSFW sketch that showed a little too much of Chris Farley and, in a peak-1990s moment, Sanders joined Tim Meadows and Adam Sandler as a rap trio short on bars. 

 

 "Peace, we outta here."

 

 Derek Jeter |  Dec. 1, 2001 

 The New York Yankees captain went from the Bronx to midtown Manhattan for his performance with musical guests Bubba Sparxxx and Shakira. On "Weekend Update," Jeter debated noted Boston Red Sox fan Seth Meyers.

 

 

 Tom Brady |  April 16, 2005 

 Four Super Bowl wins, three NFL MVPs and two retirements ago, Brady, then just a three-time champion, took on hosting duties. He came near a funnel cake in this sketch with Maya Rudolph, Rachel Dratch and Rob Riggle. Those cakes probably aren't allowed in the TB12 diet, but that didn't exist in 2005.

 

 

 Peyton Manning |  March 24, 2007 

 Manning hosted on his birthday, and his parents and brothers were in attendance. Manning, who had just won his first Super Bowl with the Indianapolis Colts in February 2007, turned in an all-time great performance, highlighted by his spoof of NFL United Way commercials.

 

 

 Manning has yet to host the show again, but he did return in January 2022 for a passionate breakdown of the Netflix series "Emily in Paris" on Weekend Update.

 

 

 Ronda Rousey  |  Jan. 23, 2016 

 Rousey hosted just two months after losing her bantamweight title to Holly Holm in UFC 193. Rousey became the first female combat athlete to host the show and just the third female athlete ever to take on hosting duties.

 

 

 Travis Kelce  | March 4, 2023 

 From the rousing success of his and brother Jason's "New Heights" podcast  to hosting SNL, the star Kansas City Chiefs tight end has displayed quite a penchant for media off the gridiron. He'd also make a guest appearance later in 2023 in a skit referencing his highly publicized relationship with Taylor Swift.

title: Travis Hunter, wife give gifts to nurses who helped with birth of their child
summary: The nurses who helped care for the couple's son's while he was in the Wolfson Children's Hospital neonatal ICU left a lasting impression.
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter and his wife, Leanna Lenee, were understandably overwhelmed when their son was born nearly eight weeks premature in August 2025.

 The support they received from multiple nurses while their son spent weeks in the Wolfson Children's Hospital neonatal ICU left a lasting impression on the couple, which is why they surprised those nurses with lunch and scrubs Tuesday.

 "They treated us very well, took care of us, and I saw the work that they did for everybody else," Hunter said. "They took care of us just like they took care of everyone else here. So it was definitely really, really special to come back and give back to them.

 "Being first-time parents, you need all the help you can get going through the experience."

 And while they were thankful for all the nurses who helped, they were especially appreciative of Rebekah Davis. They saved her scrubs for last, and when she came up to get them she got a tearful hug from Leanna.

 

 "Being first-time parents, we prepared for a lot," Leanna said. "We prepared for the nursery and bottles and all that stuff, but something you can't prepare for is your son being born almost eight weeks early and him being in the NICU. And it was really hard for both of us, and we didn't know what to do. It was something unexpected. Rebekah was somebody who was very calming to us. I remember I tried to stay at the hospital every single night, and she was like, 'Go home, please. We got it. We'll take care of him.' And she celebrated with us all the wins, all the little milestones. She kept both of us grounded because it was really scary seeing your child just in all these little tubes and stuff. And she was amazing.

 "All the nurses here were amazing to us. So Wolfson will always hold a special place in our hearts."

 Travis Hunter, who was going through training camp and the beginning of the 2025 NFL season while his son was still in the hospital, tried to get to Wolfson whenever he could. Sometimes that meant coming over at night after a full day of practices and meetings, and he was grateful the hospital was willing to accommodate him.

 "I [didn't] speak a lot when I came in the building, but y'all made me feel comfortable being able to come here and stay," Hunter told the nurses. "Y'all make me feel very special and I really appreciate it."

 The scrub giveaway is part of Create Amor's Healthcare Heroes Initiative, which Create Amor founder and CEO Matthew Vuckovich was a personal mission.

 "My mom was an ER nurse, so I grew up seeing the heart, sacrifice and commitment that healthcare professionals bring to their work," Vuckovich said. "When someone like Travis uses his platform to recognize nurses it gives these healthcare heroes a moment they'll remember long after today. Our mission is to bring this platform to hospitals across the country, creating a national movement around celebrating the heart behind healthcare."

title: How to bet 49ers-Rams on 'TNF': Analysis, tips and favorite plays
summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet 49ers-Rams on "Thursday Night Football."
full_text:
The "Thursday Night Football" slate gets going with a matchup of NFC West rivals, as the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers kick off the international series at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia.

 

 The most important matchup is the Rams' offense against San Francisco's defensive front. Sean McVay's expected use of multiple-TE formations could force the 49ers to make a choice: stay lighter and risk getting run on, or bring in heavier personnel and become more vulnerable to play-action. The Rams can run or pass from the same formations without tipping off the defense.

 That versatility matters only if the protection holds up. Offensive tackle is my biggest concern entering the season. Matthew Stafford is 38 with a history of back trouble, and the Rams have questions on both edges. San Francisco finished last in sacks last season, so its pass rush remains a projection. But if Nick Bosa and that defensive front can generate pressure without blitzing, the 49ers can force Stafford into obvious passing situations and make the Rams much easier to defend.

 San Francisco can use motion and personnel changes to create openings in the Rams' rebuilt secondary. The question is whether the 49ers can turn those opportunities into explosive plays and touchdowns enough to stay in contention.

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 The market is pricing the Rams' ceiling more heavily than the uncertainty attached to it. Los Angeles has more stars, added Myles Garrett and upgraded its secondary with  Trent McDuffie , while San Francisco enters with another uncomfortable injury list on top of off-field narratives. That makes the Rams an understandable favorite, but four points on a neutral field requires more than believing they have the better roster.

 Week 1 makes uncertainty especially important. The Rams are introducing new starters on the offensive line and in the secondary, while their special teams get a refresh. San Francisco has questions of its own, but Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy and the core offensive system provide continuity.

 The handicap is about whether the Rams should be rated above San Francisco before their new pieces have played together. I view these teams as being part of the same tier.

 

 Notable player props, bets 
 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 49ers +3.5 (-108) 

 

 Maldonado: This is a bet on the number, not a declaration that the 49ers are necessarily the better team. Pricing the Rams as four points better without any home-field advantage is an overreaction to both the Rams' loaded roster, especially the high-end receiving talent, and the Niners' preseason woes.

 San Francisco won 12 games last season despite major injuries, while its offense still ranked top 10 in points per drive and yards per drive. That's not a team I want to treat as a sizable neutral-field underdog.

 The Rams may be slightly better overall, but San Francisco has the returning chemistry within its system, while Los Angeles is asking several new pieces to hold up immediately. That makes the points more valuable than simply deciding which team has the better stars.

 

 

 Colby Parkinson receiving yards OVER 19.5 (-110) 

 Matt Bowen: The Rams' heavy usage of two- and three-tight-end sets opens the door to more opportunities for Parkinson in the pass game. Parkinson averaged 27.2 receiving yards per game last season, and the Rams boot tendencies -- they led the NFL in designed rollouts in 2025 -- will create catch-and-run targets for the tight end.

title: How NFL brought 49ers-Rams to 'sports mad' Australia
summary: The NFL's latest and farthest international venture is to Melbourne, Australia. How did the 49ers and Rams fit into those plans?
full_text:
MELBOURNE, Australia -- By the time San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan had a chance to publicly discuss playing the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, 53 days had passed since the NFL announced the matchup.

 Speaking at league meetings on March 31, a reporter had barely finished the question when Shanahan made his feelings clear. Though the 46-year-old coach said he understands it's "cool" for the league to expand globally, he doesn't see any "pro" for a team to take a 16-hour flight across the international dateline.

 The next day, Shanahan told PFT Live that he knew "for a fact" the Rams had pushed to play San Francisco to prevent 49ers fans from taking over SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. That theory gained steam in the Bay Area and had the backing of Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur, but it was ultimately not the reason the Rams and Niners are set to meet at Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) on Thursday ( 8:35 p.m. ET, Netflix ).

 "We did not select the Niners at all," said Kevin Demoff, the Rams' team president. "I know they would love to think of themselves highly enough to say that, but that was not the case at all."

 

 In reality, the Melbourne opener is the culmination of the NFL's four-year journey to deliver a marquee matchup that can ensure its first foray into the region will leave fans in this part of the world yearning for more. The record-setting travel (roughly 8,000 miles) also requires the toughest test yet of compromise between the league's global ambition and the comfort of its teams.

 For the Rams, it's a trip to the Eastern Hemisphere more than a decade in the making. In 2016, they looked into playing a regular-season game in China. As the NFL closed in on plans for a game in Australia in 2024, the Rams immediately volunteered to host it. Doing so quickly allowed Los Angeles to be designated as the home team when the announcement was made, which no team had really ever done, Demoff said.

 The league then turned its attention to the Niners -- Australia's most popular team by total fans, according to league data -- in an effort to create a blockbuster debut. It's a strategic pairing designed to unlock a massive new sports market while satisfying the league's ever-growing list of deep-pocketed broadcast partners.

 "We knew that we had an amazing opportunity in Week 1 on Friday morning in Australia to create what feels like a major event, which I know is a priority for Netflix and a focus overall," said Matt Shapiro, the NFL's senior vice president of global events and market strategy. "It really does feel like we are creating a global moment, a global stage between the Rams, the 49ers, Netflix and one of the most iconic stadiums in the world."

 
 WHILE THE NFL  is constantly collecting statistics on how people consume its games globally, the league does not have specific benchmarks in place that trigger any new country getting a game.

 It's why Charlotte Offord, the NFL's general manager of Australia and New Zealand, had no expectations on when the first contest Down Under would take place after helping open the Australian league office in 2022. At the time, the league had noticed sizable growth in the fanbase despite minimal investments in the market.

 According to NFL data, Australians who identified as NFL fans grew from 5.7 million to 8.8 million between 2022 and 2025, a 54% jump that included more than 1.3 million people declaring themselves NFL fans in the past year. The league also has initiatives through the NFL Academy, which opened in 2024, and an active NFL flag football program in all 16 Australian states and territories.

 "What I learned through the journey of that was this market is sports mad," Offord said. "There's two markets in the world that I think are sports mad: Australians and Americans."

 With that in mind, the NFL solicited bids from Australian cities to host. Sydney (where an exhibition  was played between the Broncos and Chargers in 1999), Perth and Melbourne provided submissions. But Melbourne stood out for two primary reasons: its walkability and the MCG, which is the largest stadium in the Southern Hemisphere with a capacity of more than 100,000 fans.

 

 The decision to pick the Rams as the home team was easier, Offord said.

 Australia is one of the Rams' seven chosen markets (along with China, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand and the United Arab Emirates) in the league's Global Markets Program. The GMP is a league initiative that began in January 2022, granting teams international marketing rights outside of the United States. Teams choose the markets and must invest resources in growing their brands and the game to maintain those rights. Despite their popularity in Australia, the 49ers' three GMP countries are Mexico, United Kingdom and UAE.

 The Rams have made 15 visits to Australia since the GMP launched, sending current and former players, cheerleaders and team mascot Rampage Down Under. Their first visit came after winning Super Bowl LVI, when they brought the Lombardi Trophy to the country.

 Los Angeles had initially hoped to wait until Week 1 of the 2028 season to give up a home game for an international contest, roughly two months after the end of the LA 2028 Olympics, Demoff said, but the team felt there was the "unique opportunity" once the league put Australia on the table for 2026. Having Demoff and the Rams on board allowed the NFL to move quickly to put the other pieces in place.

 "We definitely wanted to do it with a club who was going to be that pioneer with us," Shapiro said. "The Rams have certainly been an incredibly progressive and pioneering club on the international front and their willingness to take this journey with us was a critical piece of it overall."

 The Rams had not given up a home game to play internationally since the $5.5 billion SoFi Stadium opened in September 2020, so they knew the assignment was coming. In December 2023, the NFL voted that each team has to "host" an international game every four years.

 While the Rams did not choose to protect any teams on their home schedule, Demoff acknowledged that they originally wanted to play their game against the Kansas City Chiefs at SoFi Stadium. But after Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL in mid-December, Demoff said the Rams asked the NFL to play Kansas City in Week 1. The league said no.

 Instead, the league eliminated the Rams' East Coast opponents for travel purposes. The Seattle Seahawks were not an option because they won the Super Bowl and the right to host the opener. That left the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals as the only teams under consideration, Demoff said.

 

 And while the Cardinals, who have won 19 games over the past four seasons and don't rank among the 10 most popular teams in Australia, would have made sense geographically, they offered neither the global brand nor the competitive verve of the Cowboys and 49ers.

 Ultimately, the league opted for the prime NFC West matchup by sending the 49ers to Melbourne while the Cowboys became the designated home team in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in Week 3 against the Ravens. It will be Dallas' first international game as the home team and the NFL debut in Rio de Janeiro.

 
 THE GAME IN  Melbourne is not the 49ers' only international trip in 2026. With Estadio Azteca fresh off renovations in advance of this summer's men's FIFA World Cup, the Niners lobbied hard to return, according to 49ers CEO Al Guido.

 San Francisco was overdue to give up a home game after not hosting one since 2010. The last time the Niners played an international game was as the visitors in Mexico City in 2022.

 As the Niners submitted their requests, the league broached the idea of sending them to Melbourne as the Rams' opponent.

summary: The 2026 NFL season opened with a rematch between last year's Super Bowl teams, the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots. Here are all the highlights from the first game of the new season.
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks stormed back to defeat the New England Patriots 13-10 Wednesday night in the NFL's 2026 season opener.

 

 The game seemed destined for overtime as the Patriots drove down the field and set up at the Seahawks' 16-yard line with 26 seconds left in the game. However, New England quarterback Drake Maye threw a costly interception, and Seattle held on to win -- no different than Super Bowl LX against the Patriots months earlier.

 The Seahawks had an inauspicious start with starting quarterback Sam Darnold injured on the last play of its opening drive. Seattle then went scoreless in the first half, becoming the third defending Super Bowl champion to be shut out in the first half of their season opener and first since 1984, according to ESPN Research.

 The momentum shifted late in the second half, however. New England went up 10-0, and Seattle responded with 13 straight points, including a 45-yard touchdown from wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The Seahawks picked off Maye on consecutive possessions in the fourth quarter, setting up scores.

 Stepping in for Darnold, Seattle quarterback Drew Lock threw for 187 yards and one touchdown, while Smith-Njigba had eight receptions for 122 yards. Maye had 178 passing yards and one score, but three interceptions.

 Here are the top moments from Seattle's opening-game win.

title: Seahawks open season with win over Pats in Super Bowl rematch
