title: Seahawks take Week 1 win over Patriots, lose QB Darnold early
summary: In a Super Bowl LX rematch, the Seahawks kicked off the NFL season with a win but lost QB Sam Darnold to a hip injury.
full_text:
SEATTLE -- In one way, this NFL season began the same way the last one ended, with the  Seattle Seahawks ' defense making life miserable for Drake Maye . This time, though, it was Drew Lock leading the Seahawks to a 13-10 win over the  New England Patriots  Wednesday night at Lumen Field in a rematch of Super Bowl LX.

 After Sam Darnold went down on the opening possession with a right hip injury, the Seahawks' QB2 stepped up. Lock threw a 45-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba to tie the game in the fourth quarter. Jason Myers followed with a go-ahead field goal and Mike Macdonald's defense slammed the door, with cornerback Josh Jobe picking off Maye in the end zone -- as New England was in position to kick the tying field goal -- for Seattle's third interception of the night.

 Macdonald said postgame that the Seahawks got "great news" on Darnold, who appears to have avoided a fracture. Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Darnold was at Harborview Medical Center in Seattle undergoing a CT scan on his hip. The initial test was encouraging but inconclusive, and Darnold now is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Thursday.

 Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

 

 

 

 Seattle Seahawks (1-0) 

 What to make of Drew Lock's performance: Lock   went 16-of-22 for 187 yards and one TD. He   played as well as the Seahawks could have expected -- maybe better -- considering he was pressed into action early. He kept the ball out of harm's way and made big-time throws, including a 21-yard strike to Jaxon Smith-Njigba that nearly converted a third-and-22. New coordinator Brian Fleury showed faith in his backup quarterback by opting against a tush push with tight end AJ Barner on the fourth-and-1 play that resulted in Lock's touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba. The Seahawks did not help Lock out with three false-start penalties.

 

 Trend to watch: As expected, the Seahawks went with a committee approach in their backfield. Rookie first-round pick  Jadarian Price led the way, flashing explosiveness while gaining 52 yards on 10 carries. He might have gotten more work if not for the offensive penalties that forced Seattle into passing situations. George Holani gained 29 yards on eight carries, and  Emanuel Wilson added 3 yards on two attempts. This is how the work figures to be split for at least the first four games while Zach Charbonnet begins the season on the physically unable to perform list .

 Most surprising performance:  Cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett 's fourth-quarter interception on a tipped pass got the Seahawks the ball for what would be their tying touchdown drive. He had an earlier pass breakup as well. The third-year pro is serving as the Seahawks' No. 3 corner, which has looked like the biggest question mark on a defense that allowed the fewest points in the NFL last season. He'll face competition for that job from Trevon Diggs and potentially Terrion Arnold (who's on the commissioner's exempt list ) as well. But plays like that one will keep him in the starting lineup.

 Next game: at Arizona Cardinals (Sunday, Sept. 20, at 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 New England Patriots (0-1) 
 Wide receiver A.J. Brown was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a right ankle injury, taking away quarterback Drake Maye's No. 1 option and creating uncertainty about how long the team might be without him.

 Maye missed him greatly, with the Patriots losing a 10-0 lead as the Seahawks fed off two Maye interceptions and then sealed the game with a third. The first pick came when Maye threw downfield to Romeo Doubs  while giving the receiver a chance to climb the ladder, something he had shown a knack for in training camp. Doubs later had a costly drop on a play that would have gone for a first down but instead was followed by Maye's second interception when he was looking for receiver Pop Douglas over the middle on third-and-14.

 The Seahawks scored on the ensuing drive both times -- with a touchdown and a field goal. Then they closed out the game with the final pick.

 What to make of Maye's performance:  He threw multiple interceptions, which is rare. He had only one game last season (including playoffs) in which he threw two interceptions -- the Super Bowl vs. the Seahawks. The Patriots played it conservatively early, as he had just one pass traveling more than 10 air yards in the first half, according to ESPN Analytics tracking. Maye's other 11 throws traveled a combined 15 air yards. That might have been designed, in part, to protect the offensive line. Two of Maye's interceptions in the second half were on downfield throws.

 Most surprising performance: Doubs. The Patriots signed the former Packers receiver to a four-year, $68 million contract as a free agent in the offseason, and he was involved in two critical plays that hurt the team -- Maye's first interception and a dropped pass when he was open to convert a first down that preceded the second pick. The Patriots needed Doubs to deliver after Brown left the game with a right ankle injury early in the third quarter.

 Stat to know:  Rookie tight end Eli Raridon , who scored the opening touchdown of the NFL season on a 2-yard pass from Maye, did not score a TD in 12 games with Notre Dame last season.

 Next game: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (Sunday, Sept. 20, at 1 p.m. ET)

title: Cam Skattebo has potential to receive the 'Jonas blessing'
summary: First, it was Cody Bellinger. Then it was Patrick Mahomes and Lewis Hamilton. Is the New York Giants running back next?
full_text:
What do Dodgers OF  Cody Bellinger , Chiefs QB  Patrick Mahomes and F1 driver Lewis Hamilton all have in common? They accomplished major feats in their respective sports immediately after attending a Jonas Brothers concert.

 Nick Jonas coined the phrase "Jonas blessing" on "The Tonight Show" in 2021.

 "The first was Cody Bellinger, who then went on to win the [2020] World Series with the Dodgers," the singer explained. "We had Patrick Mahomes, who in the 2020 Super Bowl won the Super Bowl with the Kansas City Chiefs . He came to a show in K.C. And then Lewis Hamilton, who surpassed the all-time [Formula 1] record, he went on to, after he came to a show, to do that.

 "I was saying, 'We're going to have to start charging these athletes,'" he joked.

 According to Nick, the Jonas blessing could possibly live on in 2026.

 

 The Jonas Brothers are set to headline the halftime show for the Week 1 matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia. Those two teams will be the latest to receive the honor -- sort of. But the youngest of the Jonas Brothers, a lead talent alongside comedian Kevin Hart in DraftKings' "Take Your Game Anywhere" campaign that launched on Sept. 2, told ESPN he has identified the next athlete to potentially receive the honor.

 " [Cam] Skattebo came to our show in Newark," Jonas told ESPN. "He and his buddies came out and had a great time and [my brother] Kevin [Jonas] played golf with him the other day and was actually at the [NBA] Finals with [quarterback] Jaxson Dart and Skattebo. So I'm hoping that we'll get some of that for the Giants this year."

 For Skattebo, the second-year New York Giants  running back, had his 2025 season cut short due to a dislocated right ankle -- a bounce-back in 2026 seems to be the goal that Jonas and the Giants are hoping for.

 Before Skattebo's injury, he played a big role in New York's offense. In eight games, Skattebo picked up 410 rushing yards on 101 carries with five touchdowns. He also had 207 receiving yards with two touchdown receptions.

 Jonas, a lifelong Giants fan, is excited about the upcoming season.

 "There's a lot of great storylines this year and I feel like there's a lot of young talent that's going to be fun to watch. ... I'm obviously biased, but Jaxson Dart is doing his thing," he said.

title: Big things expected from John Harbaugh's Giants
summary: Harbaugh comes to New York as the Giants' fifth head coach in the past 10 years -- with a different set of expectations.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- John Harbaugh comes to New York as the  Giants ' fifth head coach in the past 10 years. He arrives with a different set of expectations. 

 Unlike the rest of the bunch, Harbaugh brings a track record of success. He made the postseason in 15 of his 18 seasons with the Baltimore Ravens . The previous four head coaches in the post-Tom Coughlin era (Ben McAdoo, Pat Shurmur, Joe Judge and Brian Daboll) had zero playoff appearances combined as a head coach. Only Shurmur even had NFL head coaching experience. 

 It has the Giants and the fanbase feeling a different type of way entering this season and for the future. 

 "The way I look at it is we've used the word 'hope' in the last 10 or 12 years or whatever it might be," owner Chris Mara said recently during an interview with Gary Myers on 880 ESPN New York. "The hope now has turned into expectations. At least for me it has. I don't hope we win this year. I expect it. And I think everybody else does, too."

 The reality is that McAdoo and Daboll both reached the playoffs in their first season as head coach of the Giants (2016 and 2022, respectively). They failed to match that success at any other point, and New York owns a .336 winning percentage since Coughlin was pushed out the door in January 2016.

 Only the New York Jets , with a .297 win percentage from 2016 until now, have lost more than the Giants during that span.

 Harbaugh was brought to New York to change that. It begins Sunday night when the Giants host the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium (8:20 p.m. ET, CBS).

 Presumably, the Giants should be better prepared for the season opener after what one veteran player described as the "hardest training camp of my life." Harbaugh held more practices, and they were consistently longer and tougher than Daboll's.

 The Giants had 23 practices through Labor Day. They had 19 last year despite starting almost a week earlier. The team was in full pads a lot more this year under Harbaugh, as well.

 

 Tight end Isaiah Likely is used to this kind of workload, having come with Harbaugh from Baltimore this offseason. He said it was "mind-boggling" to hear from his new teammates how training camp was in the past.

 This is Harbaugh's program. He's hoping building a bigger, more physical team pays immediate dividends because the schedule doesn't let Harbaugh's Giants ease into the flow. The Giants face an unusually big game in Week 1 considering they get the Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams on the road next Monday night. It makes their matchup in Week 1 with a division rival that has owned them for years that much more critical.

 Dallas has won 16 of its past 18 games against the Giants. New York's only two wins in that stretch have been in Week 18 games.

 But nobody seems to be giving Harbaugh the sort of grace period new head coaches generally receive. Instead, the rhetoric is to turn it around immediately, even though the Giants won seven games combined the past two seasons.

 "I get it from the standpoint of expectations, but of course we expect to win," Harbaugh said. "How do you go out there and compete at this level if you don't expect to win? If you don't expect to win, you certainly aren't going to. I've said this before, we expect and we plan to and we'll be playing to win every single one of our games this year. That's our expectation, that's our plan, that's what we'll be striving for. 

 "We think we can [win], we believe we can [win], wholeheartedly."

 When Harbaugh took the job, he said the expectation was to make the playoffs this year. Now, the pressure is on to at least compete for a spot in the postseason. Anything else would seem like a disappointment.

 The Giants' over/under is 7.5 games, according to DraftKings.

 "I feel good about the group that we have and expect us to be competitive week in and week out," general manager Joe Schoen said. "I really like the group, both sides of the ball, special teams. ... And now, really, we just got to go out and do it. But I do like the roster, I like where we are. We had a competitive camp. And I'm looking forward to seeing how things go Sunday vs. the Cowboys."

 Schoen mentioned that this team has a young quarterback in  Jaxson Dart , who's in his second year. It has a No. 1 receiver in  Malik Nabers , a strong offensive line and a potentially scary pass rush. All that combined with Harbaugh perhaps makes the idea of a quick turnaround feasible.

 The players expect improvement. They know the only way to accomplish that is by improving in the win column, finishing with a winning record. Anything else is insufficient.

 "I would say it always starts with winning. I have a really hard time being able to look back at something and find something that is a successful product that didn't win," Dart said. "So from a perspective of always putting the team first, winning comes first and I want to be able to see that growth from what our team was last year to this year. ... I think that this team is shaking out to be wanting to do something special. So that's what I'm excited to try to build on."

 Dart flashed enough in his rookie year to provide hope. He accounted for 24 touchdowns and seven turnovers as a rookie. If he can stay on the field, there is enough tangible evidence to believe he can be a high-level quarterback.

 Harbaugh has already proved he can be a high-level coach. He has a Super Bowl win on his résumé. When you have a high-level quarterback and coach, it gives you a chance. When you have a No. 1 receiver like Nabers returning from injury it helps.

 Cornerback Greg Newsome II even boasted that he believes the Giants have the "best cornerback room in the league" despite almost the entire group coming off down seasons. That is when you realize it's time to show it on the field.

 "I feel like this is a great, talented roster from all points -- from the offensive line, skill positions, from defense to offense, and I feel like every day we get each other better," Likely said. "I can come here and gloat as much as I want to about the team, but like you said, Week 1 is next week. We've got to prove it."

title: Baker Mayfield learned about contract while watching 'Cars'
summary: The 31-year-old quarterback was watching a classic Disney film when he agreed to his contract.
full_text:
TAMPA, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' contract talks with quarterback Baker Mayfield's agent were shrouded in such secrecy last week that not even he knew about them until the day before agreeing to terms on a three-year deal worth $165 million. 
 
 

 "Apparently they engaged in talks last week that I did not know about until Monday about 6 p.m.," said Mayfield, who told his agent, Tom Mills, and general manager Jason Licht that once he reported to training camp, he was "done talking about it" until after the season.

 But there was one small exception. Mayfield told Mills: "Unless something really changes -- you can bring that to my attention. If you think I'll actually be willing to agree to it, then bring it to my attention."

 Licht respected Mayfield's wishes. But having secured Vita Vea after the defensive tackle had requested a trade and was a training camp hold-in, he thought it was worth one last-gasp effort before the start of the season. Licht, assistant GM Mike Greenberg and vice president of football research Jacqueline Davidson got to work and gave Mills a buzz.

 Mayfield and Mills believed the Bucs' initial offers didn't reflect his value. But the Bucs thought their last offer before training camp -- for two years and just north of $50 million, according to sources -- wasn't far off. As talks broke off, Mayfield and Mills made it clear what they were seeking, and when the Bucs reached back out, they offered something more competitive, according to a source.

 On Monday night, while Mayfield and his wife, Emily, were eating dinner, Mills texted Mayfield: "Hey, I think I need to give you a call. I need to update you on something."

 Mills would call him again with what would be the final terms of the agreement while Mayfield was at the movie theater with teammates and their children watching the 20th anniversary release of the movie "Cars."

 "That was fun," Mayfield said. "Step away from Lightning McQueen for a second to agree to that."

 Things weren't always agreeable. The Bucs have not typically had players express their contract grievances publicly -- with the exception of former wide receiver Mike Evans in 2023 -- and Mayfield broke form by not only speaking about it but getting into numbers.

 Though it caused friction inside the building at One Buc, Licht praised Mayfield's authenticity and passion. Mayfield said many times that he has achieved his greatest professional and personal success in Tampa because "they've let me be myself."

 "One of the things I love the most about Baker is you never have to question or wonder how he feels," Licht said. "We got an example of that last month, but it's that passion that he has that makes him tick and what he is as a player. And we're just so excited that he's going to be here in the future for as long as we can."

 Licht even joked that some of their back-and-forth exchanges during the heat of negotiation were "not safe for work."

 But Licht attested, "We knew deep down that at some point we'd get something done." 
 
 

 Mayfield nodded in agreement.

 "Like I said before, we know Baker and we know that he likes to tell you how he feels, and that's what we love about him, so that's not going to change," Licht said. "So you always kind of like to know where you stand, have that relationship both ways."

 "It's also fun when you learn that somebody's pretty easy to get stirred up," Mayfield joked.

 Licht laughed, "Just don't do it on vacation."

 Mayfield was then asked if it's safe to assume that the deal's completion keeps Licht off "the list" of his personal grievances with doubters and others. Mayfield created the list back in high school and had updated it throughout college as a source of motivation. He even added media members and stored screenshots of offending tweets on his phone.

 "Haven't updated that thing in a long time. There was a time and point where I used a lot of that negative stuff to fuel me, but I've found the fire within," Mayfield said. "I still have so much to prove. This isn't, 'I've made it.' This is life-changing money and this is stuff that for us is unbelievable, but it's an opportunity to help the community to continue to progress and move forward. Main goal is still a Super Bowl, and I don't have one of those."

 Mayfield said the new deal -- the richest in the franchise's history -- won't change his approach to the season, although his teammates cracked jokes at his expense.

 Left tackle Tristan Wirfs , who was among the teammates with Mayfield when he got the call asked, "Baker, now that you've done your deal, the O-line is wondering what the Christmas gifts are going to be?"

 Wirfs, left guard Ben Bredeson , center Graham Barton and right guard Cody Mauch all stood in the back of the room watching Mayfield revel in the moment. Baker and Emily invited them up on stage. They each took turns greeting his 2-year-old daughter, Kova -- who donned a No. 6 jersey and uttered "Dadda" several times -- and their 5-month-old son, Maverick.

 "A lot of the guys are making jokes, but it's all fun and whatnot, but for me, I'm going to lead," Mayfield said. "It doesn't matter what the contract is, doesn't matter what the outside thinks. I'm going to lead the best way I can and just be myself and play with fire and passion and try and be the best quarterback on the field."
